# Specification — rebase-plan-guard

Status: normative definition (Path B). Author: definition agent.

Input of record: `.tpatch/features/rebase-plan-guard/analysis.md` (approved, normative),
`.tpatch/features/rebase-plan-guard/request.md`,
`.tpatch/features/rebase-plan-guard/status.json`, `AGENTS.md`,
`docs/engineering-workflow.md`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `.tpatch/steering/local.md`,
`.claude/skills/tessera-patch/SKILL.md`, and the hard-parent artefacts of `sync-modes`,
`stack-status` and `amend-aware-rebase`.

This document settles **every** genuinely open numbered decision of analysis §19 (items 1–29).
Nothing is left to implementer discretion; there is no "TBD", no alternative left standing, and no
"either is acceptable". Where this specification refines an analysis *recommendation* rather than
adopting it verbatim, the refinement is recorded in §25 with its justification. §26 maps every §19
item to its resolution.

## Normative vocabulary

**MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **REQUIRED**, **MAY** and **REFUSE** are binding.

- **REFUSE** means: return a Cobra `RunE` error and exit `1`, performing — **from the point of
  refusal onwards** — **no** Git mutation, **no** fetch, **no** state/lock/sentinel/transaction
  write, **no** guard claim or reclaim and **no** push. It never means "print a warning and
  continue". It has exactly two shapes, and no text in this specification, in a message, in
  documentation or in a skill may conflate them:
  - **Early REFUSE (no document, nothing done).** The refusal is decided before the route performs
    any work: §3.3 steps 1–5, every §3.4 row, the I8/I19/I20 gates, and the shipped continuation
    gates that precede the fetch. Nothing was fetched, probed or written by this invocation at
    all, so the **absolute** claim "this invocation performed no fetch" holds and is asserted.
  - **Post-fetch REFUSE.** The refusal is decided after the described route already performed its
    own policy fetch — every guarded seam of §12.2b/§12.3 (where the fetch deliberately sits
    **above** the guard seam), the post-claim seam of §12.2c, and every JIT seam. The guarantee
    there is that no *further* Git mutation, fetch, state write, claim or push follows; it is
    **not** that nothing happened. Remote-tracking refs, `FETCH_HEAD`, tags and covered local
    branches may already have moved, and the refusal text MUST NOT imply otherwise. The
    `state-preserved: ` prefix (§6.4) is about on-disk tws residue, never about the fetch.
- **Document-level refusal** is **not** a REFUSE. A plan-only route that produced a document
  publishes `refusal.kind` *inside* it and exits `0` (§3.6), whether or not that route already
  performed its policy fetch. Only the four §3.6 causes that leave **no document to publish** — a
  control-flag error, an unresolvable subject or a security refusal, an encoding failure and a
  writer failure — exit `1` on the plan route. An unreadable `stack.yaml`, an unsortable stack, a
  refused selection and every projected gate are **not** among them: they publish a document,
  rows-less where the subject could not be read (§3.6 rows 2–3, §4.3).
- **Frozen** means: byte-identical stdout, byte-identical stderr, identical exit code, identical
  Git argv sequence (including order, cwd and environment), and identical state-file shape,
  asserted by the existing immutable goldens.
- **Plan-only route** — an invocation carrying `--plan`. It emits a document, and it is
  non-mutating **only in the scoped sense defined below**. It is Git-write-free only under an
  effective `no-fetch` policy. A plan-only invocation **MAY perform exactly the policy fetch of the
  route it describes** — the external legacy fetch, an external `--fetch` fetch, and (per §13.7) a
  checkout `--fetch` fetch — at most once per invocation. **No text in this specification, in any
  help string, in any document field, or in any skill may call the plan-only route "non-mutating",
  "read-only" or "side-effect free" without naming that scope**; the unqualified claim is reserved
  for an explicit new-mode `--no-fetch` plan.
- **Guarded execution route** — an executing invocation carrying at least one of
  `--max-replay-per-entry`, `--max-replay-total`, `--approve-plan`, and **not** `--plan`.
- **Guarded state envelope** — the recovery state a *guarded execution* writes: a
  `state_version: 3` external payload (`.sync-state.v2.yaml`) beside its sentinel and run guard, or
  a `state_version: 3` checkout transaction. Version `3` exists for exactly one reason — an older
  binary MUST refuse to resume it rather than resume it unguarded (§13.6). Plan-only writes none of
  it; an unguarded run writes exactly the shipped shape.
- **Unguarded route** — an executing invocation carrying none of the five control flags. The
  no-flag cell of this route is the frozen path.
- **Mode triggers** — exactly the six shipped flags of `syncTriggerFlags`
  (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:31`): `--fetch`, `--no-fetch`, `--full`, `--local-only`, `--only`,
  `--from`. They alone set `newMode`.
- **Control flags** — `--plan`, `--json`, `--max-replay-per-entry`, `--max-replay-total`,
  `--approve-plan`. They are **not** mode triggers and never change which underlying route runs.
- **Legacy route / new-mode route** — as defined by analysis §0.2. For a fresh run the route is
  trigger-derived; for a continuation it is **state-derived**: a `state_version: 2`
  `SyncRunState`, a `state_version: 3` payload whose persisted `route` is `new-mode`, or a
  `CheckoutTransaction` whose effective route is `new-mode` (§13.6) ⇒ new-mode; a legacy
  `.sync-state.yaml`, a pre-v2 transaction, or any `state_version: 3` envelope whose persisted
  `route` is `legacy` ⇒ legacy.
- **"Mutates nothing"** is always scoped, never global: HEAD, the index, the working tree,
  `stack.yaml`, every runtime state/lock/sentinel/transaction file, and every `refs/heads/**` ref
  outside the described fetch's own local-branch destinations are byte-identical afterwards. Only
  an explicit new-mode `--no-fetch` plan carries the unqualified claim that no Git process writes
  anything at all.
- **Candidate** — a member of the topological source range `<upstream>..<git_branch>` with merges
  excluded. A candidate is an **upper bound** on what Git will consider, never a commit Git
  promises to apply.
- **Signalable** — `pid > 0 && pid != os.Getpid() && isProcessAlive(pid)`, where liveness is the
  shipped `Signal(0)` probe. It is never spelled "definitely running": `EPERM` can make a foreign
  owner look dead and PID reuse can make a dead owner look alive.
- **Owner-signalling artefact** — exactly `.checkout-sync.lock` and `.sync-run.lock`. A checkout
  transaction's `lock_pid` is recovery data and is **never** an owner signal.

## 1. Problem statement

`tws sync <feature>` rewrites local branches before it says what it is about to rewrite. In both
workspace modes the operator learns the destination, the replay boundary and the replay size only
from the rebase output — that is, after the first branch has already moved.

Three facts exist before the first mutation and are never published:

1. the **destination** the replay lands on (`--onto` target, or the resolved base ref Git will
   re-resolve);
2. the **old cutoff** (`StackEntry.LastBaseSHA`, `internal/stack.go:19`), which decides the
   `--onto` arm and pins the source range;
3. the **candidate count and identity** of the commits inside `<upstream>..<branch>`.

The customer topology that motivates the feature is `master = A-B'-D` with `pr2 = A-B-C` and a
recorded cutoff of `B`: before any ref moves, the operator must be shown new base `D`, old cutoff
`B` and first candidate `C`, and must be able to stop a run whose replay is wider than expected.

This feature ships:

- a **shared, executor-owned rebase planner** in `internal/`, consumed by both executors, so the
  plan and the run cannot disagree;
- an explicit **plan surface** (`--plan`, `--plan --json`) that mutates no branch, working tree or
  tws state, and that still fetches wherever the route it describes fetches;
- an **opt-in guard** (`--max-replay-per-entry`, `--max-replay-total`) with a fingerprint-based
  `--approve-plan`;

and leaves the no-control no-flag path byte-, argv- and process-identical in both modes.

---

## 2. Non-goals

Binding. Each is a REFUSE-to-implement boundary for this feature.

1. No safe reparent/restack mutation. This feature never edits `base` or `last_base_sha`.
2. No patch-id, `git cherry`, or tpatch change-equivalence inference; no prediction of which
   commits Git will drop.
3. No multi-parent composition and no implicit merges.
4. No PR/remote retargeting and no provider API calls.
5. No general Git simulation. No dry-run `read-tree`, no scratch worktree replay, no
   untracked-overwrite prediction.
6. No hidden fetch and no extra denied fetch: fetch follows the executor's policy exactly, with
   only the closed six suppression causes of §11.2.
7. No destructive recovery: no `git reset --hard`, no force push beyond the shipped
   `--force-with-lease`, no abort of a foreign rebase.
8. No change to conflict handling, validation semantics, or push semantics.
9. No new workspace mode and no change to external multi-worktree behaviour.
10. No applied-commit count anywhere. `replay.applied_count` MUST NOT exist as a key.
11. No unbounded commit listing.
12. No change to the mode-trigger set, the I8 operand set, or the frozen-axis decision of
    `sync-modes`. The I20 gate and the deferred half of I7 keep their exact sentences and their
    exact outcomes for **every** state a shipped binary can have written; the single declared
    refinement is that both ask "is the persisted run a *new-mode* run?" through the route
    derivation of §13.6 rule 4 instead of through a bare `state_version`/artefact-presence
    comparison, which changes the answer only for the `state_version: 3`, `route: legacy` envelope
    this feature introduces — where I20 refusing and I7 *not* refusing are what preserve legacy
    semantics (§13.6 rule 4a).
13. No `TopoSort` ordering change. Plan row order is not execution order. The controlled-path
    *position* of the sort does move in checkout mode — it is hoisted above the lock and the fetch
    on the plan and guarded routes, and only there (§13.7, §17.2, §25.35) — but the order it
    produces, the entries it yields and the executor's iteration over it are untouched, and the
    unguarded checkout route sorts where it sorts today, inside `BuildCheckoutPlan`.
14. No unguarded rebase argv change: no injected `--no-update-refs`, no injected `--no-autostash`,
    and no destination pinning on any golden-covered path.
15. No v1 configuration surface. No `sync.plan_guard.*` key of any name; `internal/config.go` is
    untouched.
16. No structured output from an executing invocation. `--json` REQUIRES `--plan`.
17. No fix to the cwd-scoped `IsPrunableWorktree` (`internal/exec.go:199-221`); it is mirrored and
    disclosed, not corrected.
18. No refusal kind outside the closed enum of §7 and no second precedence order.
19. No restoration of the operator's original branch in external mode.
20. No repair of the checkout `restoring` push loss; it is published, not fixed.
21. No fix to new-mode fetch-context nondeterminism: `selectedRealEntries` is not sorted,
    `UniqueRepos` is not changed, `TopoSort` is not made deterministic.
22. No new exit code. The alphabet stays `{0, 1}`.
23. No TTY prompt and no interactive confirmation.

## 3. CLI contract

### 3.1 Flag inventory (exact and complete)

Registered on `syncCmd` in `internal/cli/sync.go` beside the eleven shipped flags. No other flag
is added, removed or reworded.

| Flag | Registration | Default | Help text (exact) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--plan` | `cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&plan, "plan", false, …)` | `false` | `Describe the rebase this invocation would perform, then exit; moves no branch, working tree or tws state, but still fetches wherever the route it describes fetches (see --no-fetch)` |
| `--json` | `cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&planJSON, "json", false, …)` | `false` | `Emit the plan document as JSON on stdout (requires --plan)` |
| `--max-replay-per-entry` | `cmd.Flags().IntVar(&maxPerEntry, "max-replay-per-entry", 0, …)` | `0`, presence-sensitive | `Refuse before rebasing if any entry of this invocation replays more than N candidates (this invocation only; a guarded run records its limits in recovery state older tws releases refuse to resume)` |
| `--max-replay-total` | `cmd.Flags().IntVar(&maxTotal, "max-replay-total", 0, …)` | `0`, presence-sensitive | `Refuse before rebasing if this invocation replays more than N candidates in total (this invocation only; a guarded run records its limits in recovery state older tws releases refuse to resume)` |
| `--approve-plan` | `cmd.Flags().StringVar(&approve, "approve-plan", "", …)` | `""` | `Approve the exact plan with the fingerprint printed by --plan (requires a replay limit)` |

Binding rules:

1. `0` is a **legal, meaningful** limit and MUST be distinguishable from absence. Presence is read
   from `cmd.Flags().Changed`, never from the zero value.
2. `--approve-plan` takes a token matching exactly `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`. Comparison against the
   computed fingerprint is **bytewise**. Surrounding ASCII whitespace in the supplied value is
   trimmed before validation; nothing else is normalised.
3. No flag registers a shell-completion function. Integers and a 64-hex digest have no completable
   domain (see §21).
4. **No help string may claim unqualified non-mutation.** The withdrawn wording
   `Describe the rebase this invocation would perform and exit without mutating anything` is false
   on the route it describes most often: a bare external `--plan` fetches. The concise flag help
   above carries the qualified claim; the full disclosure is the command `Long` of §3.1a, which is
   the single normative home of the six required disclosures (non-mutation scope, external fetch by
   default and checkout's local default, per-invocation limits, the distinct `--plan --no-fetch`
   route, the guarded run's `state_version: 3` recovery state, and the guarded refusal contract).

### 3.1a Command `Long` (exact, normative)

`syncCmd` gains a `Long` — it has none today — set to exactly this text. `Short` is unchanged
(`Rebase branches in dependency order`).

```text
Rebase the feature's branches in dependency order.

--plan describes the rebase this invocation would perform and then exits. It moves
no branch, rewrites no working tree, and writes no tws runtime state. It is not
Git-write-free: a plan fetches exactly where the run it describes fetches — an
external plan fetches by default, a checkout plan only with --fetch — and may
update remote-tracking refs, FETCH_HEAD, tags and covered local branches. Add
--no-fetch for a fully local preview — that previews a different, new-mode route,
not the route a bare "tws sync <feature>" takes.

--max-replay-per-entry and --max-replay-total bound the work of this invocation
only — the whole plan on a fresh run, the remaining work on --continue — and are
never cumulative across resumes. --approve-plan takes the fingerprint printed by
--plan and requires at least one of those limits.

A guarded run — one carrying a replay limit or --approve-plan — records its limits
in state_version 3 recovery state, so an older tws release refuses to resume it
instead of resuming it without the guard. When the guard itself refuses, the run
exits 1 and writes one "plan-guard: <kind>: <detail>" line on stderr, before any
branch has moved unless that line says "state-preserved:". Refusals tws already
performs — a dirty tree, a held lock, a base that does not resolve locally, an
incomplete previous run — keep their own wording, exit 1 without that line, and
are never marked.
```

The marker sentence is scoped deliberately: the anchored line belongs to
**guard-owned** refusals (§6.4, "marker by origin, never by rank"), and every native refusal the
shipped binary already raises stays marker-free. Help text that promised a marker for *any* guarded
invocation's failure would teach consumers to treat its absence as success.

`Long` reaches only `tws sync --help`; Cobra's usage template (printed beside a `RunE` error)
renders `Short`, the use line and the flag help, never `Long`, so no refusal's bytes change beyond
the five new flag lines. **Snapshot obligations:** no shipped artefact captures `tws sync` help or
usage output — `internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag/**` (126 files) and
`internal/cli/testdata/existing_commands/**` contain none — so **no existing snapshot is
rebaselined**. A **new** help snapshot artefact capturing `tws sync --help` (the `Long` plus every
registered flag line) is added under `internal/cli/testdata/` and asserted through production
`Execute()`, and it is the single place the exact strings of §3.1/§3.1a are enforced.

### 3.2 Orthogonality — the control flags are not route axes

MUST NOT add any control flag to `syncTriggerFlags` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:31`),
`syncPresenceFlags` (`:34`), or `CheckoutSyncOpts.Changed` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:559`).

- `syncTriggerFlags` stays exactly six members; `syncPresenceFlags` stays exactly seven;
  `CheckoutSyncOpts.Changed` stays exactly seven keys.
- `newMode` stays computed from `syncTriggerFlags` alone.
- `syncContinueMismatches` and `syncChangedTriggerList` MUST NOT observe control-flag presence. A
  `--plan` on a previous invocation can never become a frozen-axis mismatch.

A new resolver owns the control flags:

```go
// internal/cli/sync_plan_guard.go
type planGuardOptions struct {
    Plan        bool
    JSON        bool
    MaxPerEntry *int   // nil == absent; *v == 0 is a real limit
    MaxTotal    *int
    Approve     string
    Present     map[string]bool // "plan","json","max-replay-per-entry","max-replay-total","approve-plan"
}

func resolvePlanGuardOptions(cmd *cobra.Command) (planGuardOptions, error)
func (o planGuardOptions) checkoutGuard() internal.CheckoutPlanGuard
```

The value the checkout executor receives is the **`internal`-owned** type, so no `cli` type crosses
the package boundary and `internal` never imports Cobra (§19.1, §19.2):

```go
// internal/rebase_plan_guard.go — package internal
type CheckoutPlanGuard struct {
    Plan        bool
    JSON        bool
    MaxPerEntry *int
    MaxTotal    *int
    Approve     string
    Present     map[string]bool
    // PersistedGuarded is NOT a control flag: it is set only by the checkout
    // --continue dispatch, from internal.TransactionGuarded(tx), so a guarded
    // run's persisted limits stay load-bearing on a flagless resume (§13.6
    // rule 4d). checkoutGuard() always leaves it false, and no external route
    // and no fresh run ever sets it.
    PersistedGuarded bool
}

func (g CheckoutPlanGuard) Armed() bool   // at least one limit present, or a token supplied
func (g CheckoutPlanGuard) Guarded() bool // (Armed() || PersistedGuarded) && !Plan
```

`CheckoutSyncOpts` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:545-560`) gains exactly one field,
`PlanGuard CheckoutPlanGuard`, beside `Policy`/`NewMode`/`Continue`/`Abort`/`Changed`. It is a
**separate** field: it is never merged into `Changed`, never consulted by
`checkoutContinueMismatch`, and its zero value is the unguarded route.

### 3.3 Validation order — zero side effects before step 7

Identical in both workspace modes. Steps 1–6 perform no fetch, no lock, no state write, no probe
of repository content, and no network I/O.

1. `RequireTool("git")` and `RequireWorkspace()` (external) / `RequireWorkspace()` (checkout).
2. `resolveSyncPolicy(cmd, mode)` — shipped trigger validation I1–I8, unchanged.
3. `resolvePlanGuardOptions(cmd)` — control-flag validation of §3.4. Runs **after**
   `resolveSyncPolicy` and **before** mode dispatch, identically for both modes. It reads the five
   control flags plus `cmd.Flags().Changed("continue")` and `("abort")`, which it needs for the
   §3.4 rows; it reads no state, no stack and no repository, and `Present` still carries exactly
   the five control-flag keys.
4. Feature subject resolution: external `GuardFeatureName(twsRoot, feature)` then
   `resolveExternalSyncLayout(ws, twsRoot, feature)`; checkout `internal.RequireFeaturePath(feature)`.
5. External only: shipped `classifySyncState(layout.FeaturePath, newMode)` probe. Its symlink
   refusal (`refusing to use %s: runtime state path is a symlink`) stays a hard error on every
   route including `--plan`.
6. Plan-only dispatch (§3.6). External: below `classifySyncState`, above deferred I7 (which a
   `--plan` can never reach, since §3.4 refuses `--plan` with `--abort` at step 3 — §13.7a rule 7),
   abort/continue
   routing, `syncCellRefusal`, I20, the previous-incomplete refusal, `runScopedSync` and
   `syncFeature`. Checkout: below step 4 **and below the hoisted `opts.FeaturePath`/`opts.RepoDir`
   assignment** (§13.7 step 0, §19.2), above the I19 containment refusal, abort/continue routing,
   I20, the previous transaction refusal and `internal.RunCheckoutSync`.
7. Only now may any route take the pre-acquisition snapshot, load and sort the stack, resolve
   selection, enumerate fetch contexts, or fetch.

### 3.4 Incompatibility matrix (checked at step 3, before any side effect)

Every row is an **early REFUSE** (Normative vocabulary): no document, no fetch, no state, exit `1`.
Because step 3 precedes subject resolution and every route decision, the "no fetch" claim here is
absolute and is asserted as such. Messages are new; they MUST name the flags involved and MUST NOT
reword any shipped message.

| Input | Result | Message (exact) |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` without `--plan` | REFUSE | `--json requires --plan` |
| `--plan` with `--abort` | REFUSE | `--plan cannot be combined with --abort` |
| `--max-replay-per-entry` with `--abort` | REFUSE | `--max-replay-per-entry cannot be combined with --abort` |
| `--max-replay-total` with `--abort` | REFUSE | `--max-replay-total cannot be combined with --abort` |
| `--approve-plan` with `--abort` | REFUSE | `--approve-plan cannot be combined with --abort` |
| `--json` with `--abort` | REFUSE | `--json requires --plan` (the `--json` rule is evaluated first) |
| `--max-replay-per-entry` < 0 | REFUSE | `--max-replay-per-entry must be zero or greater` |
| `--max-replay-total` < 0 | REFUSE | `--max-replay-total must be zero or greater` |
| non-integer limit | REFUSE | pflag's own parse error, unchanged |
| `--approve-plan ""` | REFUSE | `--approve-plan requires a 64-character lowercase hex fingerprint` |
| `--approve-plan` value not `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` | REFUSE | `--approve-plan requires a 64-character lowercase hex fingerprint` |
| `--approve-plan` **without `--continue`** and with neither limit flag — **with or without `--plan`** | REFUSE | `--approve-plan requires --max-replay-per-entry or --max-replay-total` |

The last row is decided from the command line alone at step 3, where "fresh" is exactly "no
`--continue`", so it is decidable before any subject resolution or state read. `--plan` is **not**
an exemption: an approval with no limit authorizes nothing on any route, and a document minted
under it could never be usable (§8.4 clause 2), so publishing one would teach a workflow that
cannot execute. A `--continue` invocation is excluded here because its limits may come from
persisted state; when no limit is effective **there**, the fact is rank 7.5
`approval-without-limits` (§7), not a flag error.

Shipped wording that MUST remain byte-identical: the I8 operand error
`--abort cannot be combined with %s` (its operand list is unchanged because the trigger set is
unchanged), I20's `cannot use sync mode flags on --continue without v2 state; continue without them
or abort and start a new run`, I14's `base %q for stack entry %q does not resolve locally; drop
--no-fetch or fetch manually first`, and the symlink refusal above.

Legal combinations, all REQUIRED to work:

| Combination | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `--plan` + any trigger | Describes that new-mode route |
| `--plan` alone | Describes the **legacy** route (the run a bare `tws sync <f>` performs) |
| `--plan --continue` | Describes remaining work only; never fetches; route is state-derived |
| `--plan --push` | Projects `intent.push`, `push.targets[]`, `push.executable`, `push.blocked_by[]`; pushes nothing |
| `--plan --approve-plan <fp>` **with at least one effective limit** | Legal plan-only token validation: publishes `approval.supplied`/`accepted`, waives covered rows, and mutates nothing **in the scoped sense of the Normative vocabulary** — it still performs the policy fetch of the route it describes |
| `--plan --approve-plan <fp>` with no limit flag and no `--continue` | REFUSE at step 3 (`--approve-plan requires --max-replay-per-entry or --max-replay-total`) |
| `--plan --json` | Document on stdout only |
| limits and/or `--approve-plan` without `--plan` | Guarded execution |
| `--approve-plan` on a continuation with no effective limit | Not a flag error; rank 7.5 `approval-without-limits` (§7) |

### 3.5 Route matrix

| Invocation | `route` | `policy.fetch` | Fetches? | Emits document? | Exit on refusal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tws sync <f>` | legacy | external `fetch`, checkout `no-fetch` | per route | no | 1 (shipped) |
| `tws sync <f> --plan` | legacy | external `fetch`, checkout `no-fetch` | per route, unless suppressed | yes | 0 |
| `tws sync <f> --plan --no-fetch` | new-mode | `no-fetch` | never | yes | 0 |
| `tws sync <f> --plan <trigger>` | new-mode | resolved | per policy | yes | 0 |
| `tws sync <f> --plan --continue` | state-derived | state-derived | **never** | yes | 0 |
| `tws sync <f> <limits> [--approve-plan]` | trigger/state-derived | per route | per route | no | 1 |

`requested_route` is published only when the command line requests a route that differs from the
effective (state-derived) continuation route; otherwise it is `null`.

A **checkout** plan fetches only where the described checkout route fetches — that is, under an
effective `--fetch` policy, never on the default `no-fetch` legacy route, never on a continuation,
and never when a pre-fetch gate the executor would have raised first refuses (§11.2 cause 2). Its
ordering, its gates, its writers and its "exactly one fetch" bound are §13.7; the external twin,
with the same gate-then-fetch rule, is §13.7a.

### 3.6 Exit codes and stream discipline (§19.14 resolved)

**The exit contract is total, and one question decides the plan-only half: was a document
produced?** Every fact the planner can *describe* is published inside the document at exit `0`;
only a failure that leaves **no document to publish** exits `1`. The table below is exhaustive —
every row of §7.1, every projected gate of §13.5/§13.7/§13.7a and every rows-less profile of §4.3
lands in exactly one of its cells.

| # | Outcome | Exit | stdout | stderr |
|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Plan-only, any document produced — including `runnable: false`, `guard.would_refuse: true`, `approval.accepted: false`, `refusal.kind != null` | `0` | the document (human) or exactly one JSON value followed by one `\n` and no other byte (`--json`, §22.9) | plan/fetch operational prose, `Sync mode:` header, verbose child fetch stdout+stderr |
| 2 | Plan-only, **unreadable `stack.yaml`** (rank 1 `plan-unavailable`) or **cyclic stack** (rank 1 `stack-unsortable`) | `0` | the rows-less `summary.plannability: unavailable` document of §4.3, carrying that `refusal.kind` | prose only |
| 3 | Plan-only, a selection, state, preflight, continuation-gate, I14, fetch-context or limit/approval fact (ranks 2–12) | `0` | the document, with rows where §13.7/§13.7a established them and rows-less otherwise | prose only |
| 4 | Plan-only, control-flag validation failure (§3.4) | `1` | nothing | the §3.4 sentence; **early REFUSE**, decided at step 3 before any subject resolution. `tws sync <f> --json` with no `--plan` is a member of **this** row and of no other: it is an early control error (`--json requires --plan`), not a plan-only route that failed to produce a document, and no taxonomy anywhere may file it under rows 5–7 |
| 5 | Plan-only, subject or security failure (§3.3 steps 1–5: `RequireTool`/`RequireWorkspace`, feature resolution, `RequireFeaturePath`, the shipped runtime-state **symlink refusal**) | `1` | nothing; **never** a partial JSON object | the shipped error, marker-free |
| 6 | Plan-only, the document could not be **encoded** (`MarshalRebasePlan` failure) | `1` | nothing under `--json`: the renderer returns `(nil, err)` and `renderPlanDocumentTo` therefore issues **no** `Write` at all, so **zero** bytes reach stdout | the encode error, marker-free |
| 7 | Plan-only, an `io.Writer` failure while emitting the document or the prose (`renderPlanDocumentTo`'s single document `Write`, or a prose write, returns an error) | `1` | **zero** bytes where that `Write` accepted none (`(0, err)`), and exactly the `n` bytes the writer itself reported accepting where it returned a short write (`(n < len(buf), err)`). The document is offered in **one** `Write` of a complete in-memory buffer (rule 1), is never retried and is never written to another stream, so this feature produces no partial document in any cell | the write error, marker-free; no `plan-guard:` line, because no guard refused |
| 8 | Guarded execution, success | shipped | shipped route prose, byte-identical to the unguarded twin | shipped |
| 9 | Guarded execution, guard-owned refusal | `1` | nothing added | shipped prose plus exactly one anchored guard marker line (§6.4). This is a **post-fetch REFUSE**: the route's own policy fetch has already run above the guard seam (§12.2b, §12.3), so neither the marker nor any documentation may describe it as "nothing happened" |
| 10 | Guarded execution, shipped-check refusal | `1` | shipped | shipped, **marker-free** |

Rows 4–7 are the **complete** list of plan-only exit-`1` causes, and they are exactly **four cause
classes** covering **five** distinct assertable cells:

| Cause class | Row | Cells | Trigger |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Control-flag error | 4 | 1 — `control-flag` | any §3.4 row, including `--json` without `--plan` |
| Subject or security failure | 5 | 2 — `subject-unresolvable` and `security-symlink` | `RequireTool`/`RequireWorkspace`, feature resolution, `RequireFeaturePath`; and the shipped runtime-state symlink refusal |
| Encoding failure | 6 | 1 — `encode-failure` | `MarshalRebasePlan` fails; it returns no buffer, so no `Write` is issued and zero bytes reach stdout |
| Writer failure | 7 | 1 — `writer-failure` | the single document `Write`, or a prose write, returns an error |

**No `stack.yaml`-class failure is a member.** Any statement anywhere that an unreadable stack, an
unsortable stack, a refused selection or a refusing gate leaves the plan route with "no document to
publish" is **withdrawn**; those are rows 2 and 3, they publish the rows-less document of §4.3, and
§22.15/§22.16 assert exactly that. Neither is a fetch failure, a probe failure, a refused
continuation gate, an exceeded limit, an approval mismatch or a controlled-path blocker a member:
each of those is describable, so each is published inside a document at exit `0`. Rows 4–7 are also
the only cells where a plan-only invocation returns a non-`nil` error, and that error is always an
ordinary untyped error — never `*PlanGuardRefusalError`, never marker-carrying (§13.7, §13.7a).
§22.12a asserts the four classes through their five cells and fails on a sixth cell or a fifth
class.

Binding: there is **no** exit code `2`. Consumers MUST branch on `runnable`,
`guard.would_refuse`, `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` and `refusal.kind`, never on the exit status of
a plan-only invocation. Under `--plan --json` no byte other than the JSON document may reach
stdout; the `Sync mode:` header and every fetch/progress line move to `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` on the
plan route only. Under human `--plan` the document blocks go to stdout and the same operational
prose goes to stderr. `--plan --verbose --json` keeps verbose child fetch output — on stderr.
Shipped non-plan streams (`fetchQuiet`, `printSyncModeHeader` on executing routes, status lines)
are untouched.

**Stream plumbing (normative, and the only mechanism).** The discipline above is implemented by
explicit writers, never by process-global redirection and never by swapping `os.Stdout`:

1. **Every document renderer produces a complete `[]byte` in memory and holds no writer at all:**
   `internal.FormatRebasePlan(plan RebasePlan) ([]byte, error)` and
   `internal.MarshalRebasePlan(plan RebasePlan) ([]byte, error)` (§19.1). Each either returns the
   **whole** document — every block and the byte-exact four-part tail for the human renderer; the
   canonical JSON object **plus its single trailing `\n`** (§22.9) for the JSON renderer, so the
   value and its newline are one slice — or returns `(nil, err)` and no bytes at all. They take no
   `io.Writer`, write to no stream, use no `fmt.Print*` family call, and are the sole producers of
   document bytes. A renderer that streamed into a writer, or that returned a buffer missing the
   JSON newline, is a specification violation: partial-document questions exist only where a
   document is emitted in more than one write, and this feature has no such cell.
2. The package-`cli` render dispatch is writer-taking, is the only caller of the two renderers, and
   is the only function that binds document bytes to a stream:

   ```go
   // internal/cli/sync_plan_guard.go
   func renderPlanDocumentTo(stdout, stderr io.Writer, plan internal.RebasePlan, jsonMode bool) error
   func renderPlanDocument(cmd *cobra.Command, plan internal.RebasePlan, jsonMode bool) error
   ```

   `renderPlanDocument` is a one-line wrapper that passes `cmd.OutOrStdout()` and
   `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`. `renderPlanDocumentTo` calls the renderer selected by `jsonMode`, returns
   its error **without writing anything** when the encode/format failed (§3.6 row 6), and otherwise
   performs **exactly one** `stdout.Write(buf)` — one call, the complete buffer, no second write,
   no retry, no fallback stream — returning that call's error unchanged (§3.6 row 7). It writes the
   **document** to `stdout` and nothing else to it; under `jsonMode` that one write is exactly one
   JSON object and a single trailing `\n`. Any operational byte it emits goes to `stderr`. Tests
   assert both halves with two distinct non-`os.Stdout` buffers, and count the document writes at
   exactly one. **`renderPlanDocumentTo` is the sole document writer in the tree**: no
   other function in either package writes a document byte to any stream, and no `internal` entry
   point is given a document writer at all (rule 5, §13.7 rule 9).
3. **Operational prose has exactly one implementation per printer, and the shipped symbol is a
   wrapper.** Each shipped printer's body moves **verbatim** into a writer-taking twin, and the
   shipped symbol becomes a one-line wrapper passing the writers it wrote to today. No format
   string of this feature's prose is implemented twice anywhere in the tree, in either package:

   | Shipped symbol | Package | Twin (the single body) | Shipped wrapper becomes |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `printSyncModeHeader(p internal.SyncRunPolicy)` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:500-504`) | `cli` | `printSyncModeHeaderTo(w io.Writer, p internal.SyncRunPolicy)` | `printSyncModeHeaderTo(os.Stdout, p)` |
   | `printSyncModeHeader(p SyncRunPolicy)` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:519-521`) | `internal` | `printSyncModeHeaderTo(w io.Writer, p SyncRunPolicy)` | `printSyncModeHeaderTo(os.Stdout, p)` |
   | `fetchQuiet(repo, wtPath string, verbose bool)` (`internal/cli/sync.go:604-635`) | `cli` | `fetchQuietTo(out, errw io.Writer, repo, wtPath string, verbose bool, ctx internal.PlanFetchContext) internal.PlanFetchRepoResult` | `_ = fetchQuietTo(os.Stdout, os.Stderr, repo, wtPath, verbose, internal.PlanFetchContext{})` |
   | the inline checkout fetch block of `RunCheckoutSync` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:618-625`, the `if opts.Policy.Fetch == SyncFetchEnabled` block only — `:617` is the header call) | `internal` | `fetchCheckoutRepoTo(w io.Writer, ctx PlanFetchContext) PlanFetchOutcome` | `fetchCheckoutRepo(repoDir)`, itself `_ = fetchCheckoutRepoTo(os.Stdout, PlanFetchContext{Root: repoDir, Source: "workspace-repo-root"})`, called from `RunCheckoutSync` at the shipped point inside the shipped `opts.NewMode` / `SyncFetchEnabled` conditions |

   - **Two writers exist exactly where the shipped body writes to two streams.** `fetchQuiet`'s
     verbose arm runs the child through `internal.RunDir`/`internal.Run`, which wire
     `cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout` **and** `cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr` (`internal/exec.go:117-134`), so its
     twin takes `out` and `errw` and the shipped wrapper passes `os.Stdout, os.Stderr`. Collapsing
     the pair into one writer would send child stderr to stdout on the shipped path and move
     golden-covered bytes. The plan route passes the **same** prose writer for both, which is how
     `--plan --verbose` keeps child output on stderr (rule 4).
   - The two header twins and `fetchCheckoutRepoTo` take **one** writer, because their shipped
     bodies write to stdout only: the header is a single `fmt.Printf`, and the checkout fetch block
     silences its child through `RunSilentDir` (`internal/exec.go:193-197`), which leaves
     `cmd.Stdout`/`cmd.Stderr` nil. Neither has a shipped stderr byte to preserve, and neither may
     invent one. `fetchCheckoutRepoTo` additionally takes the **pre-computed** fetch context of
     §13.7 and returns a whole `PlanFetchOutcome` rather than a bare row, because the checkout
     route has exactly one context: it copies that context's already-measured `Effect` into the row
     it returns and re-probes nothing after the fetch (§13.7 rule 6a).
   - The fetch twins **return what they observed** — never `void`, never a bare `bool` — so the
     document's `fetch.*` facts describe this invocation's own fetch instead of a re-derivation
     (§13.7, §13.7a). Every shipped wrapper discards the returned value, which cannot move a byte.
   - Because each body exists once, an executing route and its plan twin are byte-identical **by
     construction** rather than by review. Enforcement: the 126 `sync_noflag` goldens (§17.1), plus
     a wrapper test per row asserting the wrapper's bytes equal the pre-change bytes, plus a source
     assertion that neither `"Sync mode: fetch=%s propagation=%s scope=%s\n"` nor
     `"Fetching %s... "` appears in more than one function per package.
4. **Child-process output needs writer-taking exec helpers, added in `internal/exec.go`:**

   ```go
   // internal/exec.go — additive; the shipped helpers are untouched
   func RunTo(stdout, stderr io.Writer, name string, args ...string) error
   func RunDirTo(stdout, stderr io.Writer, dir, name string, args ...string) error
   ```

   Each is the body of its shipped twin (`Run`, `RunDir`) with `cmd.Stdout`/`cmd.Stderr` taken
   from the parameters; `cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin` and `cmd.Dir` are unchanged, and no filtering,
   buffering or reordering is added. They are called **only** from `fetchQuietTo`'s verbose arm,
   which MUST pass through the **two writers it received** — `RunDirTo(out, errw, …)` /
   `RunTo(out, errw, …)` — and record the child's exit status in the `PlanFetchRepoResult` it
   returns. Under the shipped wrapper those writers are exactly `os.Stdout` and `os.Stderr`, i.e.
   `RunDir`'s and `Run`'s shipped wiring, and the returned value is discarded exactly as the
   shipped body discards the error today; under the plan route both are the single prose writer,
   which is what puts verbose child stdout **and** stderr on stderr. §13.7's checkout plan fetch
   uses `RunSilentDir` and reaches these helpers only if a verbose arm is ever added there. `Run`,
   `RunDir`, `RunDirClean`, `runWithFilteredStderr`, `RunSilent` and `RunSilentDir` keep
   byte-identical bodies and are **not** rewritten as wrappers, so no executing route's process
   wiring changes; a test asserts `RunDirTo(os.Stdout, os.Stderr, dir, …)` is observationally
   identical to `RunDir(dir, …)`.
5. **`internal` writes no byte to a process-global stream on a plan route, and holds no document
   writer.** The claim is about *streams*, not about bytes as such: `FormatRebasePlan` and
   `MarshalRebasePlan` live in `internal` and legitimately **produce** document bytes — as the
   complete `[]byte` they return to their caller, which on the plan route is always package `cli`.
   What `internal` never does on that route is write to `os.Stdout`, `os.Stderr` or any other
   process-global stream, and it never receives a document writer to write to either:
   `PlanCheckoutRebase` receives only the **prose** writer (§13.7),
   the document value travels back to `cli` as a return value, and `renderPlanDocumentTo` is the
   only function that binds it to a real stream. `internal.RunCheckoutSync`, `ContinueCheckoutSync`
   and `internal.printSyncModeHeader` keep their shipped **output** on executing routes — the
   header and the checkout fetch block reach `os.Stdout` through the one-line wrappers of rule 3,
   which is the same bytes in the same order — and the checkout plan route never enters those
   executors (§3.3 step 6, §13.7), so no `internal` executor learns a writer and `internal` still
   imports no Cobra package. The previous revision's phrasing "`internal` prints no plan byte at
   all" is **withdrawn**: it contradicted `FormatRebasePlan`/`MarshalRebasePlan` living in
   `internal`.
6. Unguarded and guarded **executing** routes keep the shipped direct-output calls unchanged. The
   goldens under `internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag/` are the enforcement of that claim (§17.1).
