## 4. Plan document model and JSON schema

`schema_version` is the integer constant **`1`**, spelled exactly `schema_version` (never
`plan_schema_version`). It is document-scoped and is **not** the fingerprint tuple schema version.

### 4.1 Top-level key order and totality

Emitted in exactly this order:

```text
schema_version, route, requested_route, route_triggers, invocation, workspace, feature, policy,
intent, push, restore, fetch, freshness, repositories, state, runnable, blockers, warnings,
encoding_issues, config_issues, entries, summary, guard, refusal, approval
```

| Key | Type | Nullability | Domain / rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | int | never | `1` |
| `route` | string | never | `legacy` \| `new-mode`; effective route |
| `requested_route` | string | nullable | `null` when equal to `route` |
| `route_triggers[]` | array | never null | trigger names sorted **bytewise lexical**, de-duplicated; `[]` on legacy (§4.8) |
| `invocation` | string | never | `plan-only` (v1 publishes no other value) |
| `workspace` | object | never | `{mode, stable_id, repo_root}`; `stable_id` nullable; `repo_root` is sanitized, **display-only**, and is never a join, sort or fingerprint input (§8.3) |
| `feature` | string | never | resolved feature name |
| `policy` | object | never | `{fetch, propagation, scope_kind, selector, fetch_default_applied}` (see below) |
| `intent` | object | never | closed shape of §4.6 |
| `push` | object | never | closed shape of §4.4a |
| `restore` | object | never | closed shape of §14.4 |
| `fetch` | object | never | closed shape of §4.4a |
| `repositories[]` | array | never null | closed row shape of §4.4 |
| `state` | object | never | closed shape of §4.5 |
| `blockers[]` / `warnings[]` | arrays | never null | `{kind, entry, detail}` rows of §4.6 |
| `encoding_issues[]` / `config_issues[]` | arrays | never null | closed row shapes of §4.4 |
| `entries[]` | array | never null | closed row shape of §4.2 |
| `summary` | object | never | closed shape of §4.3 |
| `guard` | object | never | closed shape of §4.6 |
| `refusal` | object | never | `{kind, detail}`; `kind: null` when nothing refuses |
| `approval` | object | never | closed shape of §4.6 |
| `runnable` | bool | never | see §7 |
| `freshness` | string | never | closed twelve-value enum of §11.3 |

The table above is **total**: the **twenty-five** keys of the order list at the top of this section
are exactly the keys the document has — two rows above group two keys of identical shape, and the
emission order is the order list, not the table order. The §23 schema test asserts the emitted key
set and key order against this list and against the nested closed tables it points to — including
`fetch` and `push`, whose complete field tables are §4.4a, and `restore`, whose complete field table
is §14.4 — so a field added anywhere without amending its table fails. **The descent is
bidirectional and does not stop at the top level**: it recurses into `fetch.repos[]` rows,
`push.targets[]` rows and each row's nested `lease` object, asserting in both directions — every
declared member present in the emitted object, and every emitted member declared — so neither an
added nor a removed nested member can pass (§22.33b).

**Scope vocabulary (one closed enum, one shipped label).** `policy.scope_kind` is the **closed
three-value enum `all` \| `one` \| `subtree`**, taken verbatim from the shipped
`internal.SyncScopeKind` constants (`internal/sync_selection.go:32-38`). `policy.selector` is a
**separate**, nullable string carrying the logical `StackEntry.Name` — `null` exactly for
`scope_kind: all`, non-null for `one` and `subtree`. The two are never fused into one token in
JSON. The human `Policy:` line renders the shipped `SyncRunPolicy.ScopeLabel()`
(`internal/sync_selection.go:148-157`) verbatim — `all`, `only:<selector>`, `subtree:<selector>`
(§6). **The token `from` never appears in either surface**: `--from` is a *flag* that selects
`scope_kind: subtree`, and publishing it as a scope value would name a state the executor does not
have. `route_triggers[]` is where the flag spelling `from` legitimately appears.

**Legacy-continuation totality (§19.8 resolved).** A legacy `.sync-state.yaml` continuation
persists no policy, no selection and no limits. The document MUST publish those keys with explicit
absence values, never omit them: `policy.fetch`/`propagation`/`scope_kind` carry the legacy
defaults the executor really uses (`fetch`/`full`/`all` external, `no-fetch`/`full`/`all`
checkout), `policy.selector` is `null`, `policy.fetch_default_applied` is `true`, `route_triggers`
is `[]`, and `guard.limits.<key>` is `{value: null, origin: none}` or
`{value: <n>, origin: flags-legacy-continuation}` when armed by this invocation's flags. Omission
is never used to express "this route has no such fact".

A **legacy-route `state_version: 3` envelope** (§13.6) is a different cell of the same `route:
legacy` document: it publishes the identical legacy policy values and `route_triggers: []`, and it
publishes `guard.limits.<key>` as `{value: <n>, origin: persisted-payload}` for every key its
envelope carries — written at birth by a guarded legacy fresh run, or by the §13.2a upgrade of an
armed `.sync-state.yaml` continuation — exactly as a new-mode payload does. The **cell-4 recovery
arm** (§12.8b, §13.6 rule 2c) publishes the same `origin: persisted-payload`, because its intent
block *is* the payload the interrupted setup had already committed to; the enum stays closed at six
members and gains none. `origin: flags-legacy-continuation` therefore names only the real
`.sync-state.yaml` cell, which is where the value came from **for that document**: the same
invocation makes it persistent below its guard seam, and the run's next continuation is the
envelope cell above (or, after a crash inside the setup, the recovery cell).

### 4.2 `entries[]` — per-row fields

Rows are sorted by logical `name`. Row position is semantically inert; dependency travels in
`destination.depends_on`.

**Identity and context**

| Field | Type | Nullability | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | never | logical `StackEntry.Name` |
| `git_branch` | string | never | `StackEntry.GitBranch()` (`internal/stack.go:22-27`) |
| `repo` | string | never | `StackEntry.Repo`; `""` is a value, not absence |
| `role` | enum | never | `anchor` \| `propagated` |
| `materialization` | enum | never | `materialized` \| `archived-metadata` \| `worktree-missing` \| `prunable` |
| `base_context` | object | never | `{context_id, repo_root, source}` |
| `execution_context` | object | never | same shape |
| `*.context_id` | 64-lower-hex | nullable | `null` iff the context could not be established or `source: not-applicable`; **the only join key** |
| `*.repo_root` | string | nullable | sanitized display path, `null` exactly with its `context_id`; never a join, sort or fingerprint input |
| `*.source` | enum | never | `entry-repo` \| `worktree` \| `process-cwd` \| `workspace-repo-root` \| `not-applicable` |

Context-source assignment is total:

| Arm | `base_context.source` | `execution_context.source` |
|---|---|---|
| External pass 1, `Repo != ""` | `entry-repo` | `worktree` |
| External pass 1, `Repo == ""` | `worktree` | `worktree` |
| External pass 2, `Repo != ""` | `entry-repo` | `entry-repo` |
| External pass 2, `Repo == ""` | `process-cwd` | `process-cwd` |
| Checkout (any) | `workspace-repo-root` | `workspace-repo-root` |
| `skipped-updated-ref` | real preflight base context only on new-mode `--no-fetch`, else `not-applicable` | real external pass-2 execution context |
| `skipped-anchor`, `skipped-archived`, `skipped-no-base` | `not-applicable` | `not-applicable` |

- A context that fails to establish is rank 5.1 `repo-unavailable`, blocking, and nulls only that
  context's `context_id`/`repo_root`. `not-applicable` is **not** `repo-unavailable`, is
  non-blocking, and cites no `repositories[]` row.
- Contexts are compared by measured canonical top level and measured canonical `--git-common-dir`.
  Equal `context_id` ⇒ same context. Equal common dirs ⇒ same object store; a store fact MAY be
  shared only after that measurement.
- Two distinct contexts sharing one common dir emit the non-blocking warning
  `base-execution-context-split`. Divergent measured common dirs on one row are rank 5.15
  `base-execution-store-divergent` (external only), blocking.
- An external pass-1 row with empty `Repo` whose worktree fails a non-`IsNotExist` stat produces
  **no** strategy row; it survives only as a rank 4 `preflight-refused` row that MAY carry the
  new-mode `--no-fetch` preflight's process-cwd base context.

**Base, destination, head**

| Field | Type | Nullability | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base.name` | string | `null` iff configured base is empty | verbatim `StackEntry.Base` |
| `base.kind` | enum | never | `stack-entry` \| `literal-ref` \| `none` |
| `base.ref` | string | nullable | ref the executor passes to Git; `null` for unset base, failed resolution, or `not-applicable` context |
| `base.decision_sha` | SHA | nullable | `GetBranchSHA(base.ref)` in **`base_context`**; selects the arm only. `null` for unset/unresolvable/not-applicable/repo-unavailable base, a deferred destination, and every `skipped-updated-ref` row |
| `destination.sha` | SHA | nullable | commit the replay lands on, resolved in `execution_context`; `null` for missing ref, deferred destination, every `skipped-*` row |
| `destination.deferred` | bool | never | true iff the resolved `base.ref` will be rewritten by an entry this route executes **earlier** |
| `destination.depends_on` | string | `null` iff not deferred | the earlier executor row, not merely `entry.Base` |
| `destination.snapshot_sha` | SHA | nullable | current resolution of a deferred `base.ref`; explicitly a snapshot |
| `head.state` | enum | nullable | `present` \| `missing` \| `unresolvable`; `null` only for `repo-unavailable` or a `not-applicable` execution context |
| `head.sha` / `head.short` | SHA / string | `null` unless `head.state == present` | `refs/heads/<git_branch>` tip in `execution_context` |

**Cutoff, strategy, argv**

| Field | Type | Nullability | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cutoff.recorded_sha` | SHA | `null` iff no recorded value | verbatim `StackEntry.LastBaseSHA`; never inferred from a merge base |
| `cutoff.state` | enum | nullable | `absent` \| `present` \| `unresolvable`; `null` only when the recorded SHA was not probed (context unavailable/not-applicable, or a `skipped-updated-ref` row) |
| `cutoff.provenance` | enum | never | `recorded-by-sync` \| `none` |
| `cutoff.resolved_sha` | SHA | `null` unless `cutoff.state == present` | peeled cutoff |
| `cutoff.usage` | enum | never | `used` \| `not_used`; external pass 2 is always `not_used` |
| `cutoff.write` | enum | never | `per-entry` (external pass 1) \| `at-finalization` (checkout) \| `never` (external pass 2, all skips) |
| `strategy` | enum | never | `onto` \| `plain` \| `plain-explicit-branch` \| `conditional` \| `skipped-updated-ref` \| `skipped-anchor` \| `skipped-archived` \| `skipped-no-base` \| `unknown` |
| `strategy_condition` | string | `null` unless `conditional` | literal predicate, e.g. `onto unless post-rebase(pr1) == <cutoff> or post-rebase(pr1) is unreadable` (external) / `onto unless post-rebase(pr1) == <cutoff>` (checkout) |
| `argv[]` | array of strings | `null` **iff** `strategy ∈ {conditional, unknown}` | exact tokenized Git argv; every `skipped-*` row is `[]` |
| `argv_alternatives` | 2 argv arrays | REQUIRED iff `conditional`; `null` for every other strategy including `unknown` | both possible shapes |
| `effective_backend` | enum | nullable | `merge` \| `apply`, by the total table of §11.7; `null` **exactly** in that table's two unestablished cells — the context's config inventory could not be read, or the 2.26 default-backend capability is unknown — and only when the published argv forces neither |

**Replay**

| Field | Type | Nullability | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `replay.upstream_ref` | string | nullable | cutoff for `onto`, `base.ref` for plain; `null` for `conditional`/unresolved |
| `replay.upstream_sha` | SHA | `null` iff determinacy is `unknown` or `not-applicable` | effective source boundary |
| `replay.upstream_provenance` | enum | never | `recorded-cutoff` \| `base-ref-snapshot` \| `base-ref-deferred` \| `unknown` |
| `replay.determinacy` | enum | never | `exact` \| `snapshot` \| `unknown` \| `not-applicable` |
| `replay.reason` | enum | `null` iff `exact` | first satisfied member of the precedence list below |
| `replay.range` | string | nullable | `<full-upstream-sha>..<git_branch>` — the **full** hex `replay.upstream_sha`, never an abbreviation and never a ref name; `null` **exactly when** `replay.upstream_sha` is `null` (deferred, unresolvable and every `not-applicable` skip) |
| `replay.candidate_count` | int | `null` iff `unknown` | `0` for `not-applicable` rows, **without probing** |
| `replay.first_candidate` | object | nullable | `{sha, short, subject}`; `null` for unknown or known-empty ranges |
| `replay.commits[]` | array of full SHAs | `null` iff the range is unknown | oldest-first, capped at **50** (§5); `[]` for a known-empty range including skips |
| `replay.commits_listed` | int | `null` exactly with `commits` | count actually listed |
| `replay.commits_truncated` | bool | `null` exactly with `commits` | derived from `candidate_count > 50`; no cap-plus-one probe |
| `replay.candidate_digest` | 64-lower-hex | `null` exactly with `commits` | SHA-256 over the **complete uncapped** oldest-first sequence (§5) |
| `replay.may_drop_patch_equivalent` | bool | nullable | arm- and range-derived (§4.6) |
| `replay.may_drop_becomes_empty` | bool | never | always `true` (Git default `--empty=drop`) |

`replay.reason` precedence, evaluated top-down:

| Order | Token | Condition | Determinacy |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 0 | `not-executed` | any `skipped-*` row | `not-applicable` |
| 1 | `merge-recreation` | effective `rebase.rebaseMerges` resolves true **and** `effective_backend == merge` — the backend being decided by §11.7's table, in which `rebase.rebaseMerges` itself is **not** an input | `unknown` |
| 2a | `repo-unavailable` | required context unavailable | `unknown` |
| 2b | `head-ref-missing` | `head.state != present` | `unknown` |
| 2c | `base-unset` | executable external row with `base.kind: none` | `unknown` |
| 2d | `base-ref-missing` | required base ref unresolvable | `unknown` |
| 2e | `cutoff-unresolvable` | required recorded cutoff unresolvable | `unknown` |
| 2f | `probe-failed` | replay-critical probe failed | `unknown` |
| 3 | `upstream-deferred` | plain upstream depends on an earlier post-rebase result | `unknown` |
| 4a | `no-recorded-cutoff` | no cutoff recorded | `snapshot` |
| 4b | `cutoff-not-used-on-arm` | cutoff exists but the arm never reads it (external pass 2) | `snapshot` or `unknown` |
| 5 | `null` | — | `exact` |

Rank 2a–2f outrank `merge-recreation` when the config read itself did not succeed.
**The backend conjunct is load-bearing.** `rebase.rebaseMerges` recreates merges only where the
merge backend runs the rebase: under `effective_backend: apply` the range's merges are dropped
exactly as the `--no-merges` bound models them, so the row keeps its ordinary determinacy, its
`candidate_count` stays a valid upper bound, and it is **not** rank 10 `indeterminate-entry`
(§5 rule 2, §10.4, §11.7). Where `rebase_merges.interpretation` is `true` and `effective_backend`
is `null` — no forcing argv and an unestablished backend — the conjunct cannot be evaluated at all,
so rank 2f `probe-failed` applies by the precedence above; the row never silently assumes a
backend in either direction.
`merge-recreation-unknown` and `cross-repo-unsupported` are **not** members;
cross-repo status lives only under `ancestry`.

**Collateral, mutation, preconditions, ancestry**

| Field | Type | Nullability | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collateral_refs[]` | array of `{repo, ref, sha, stack_owned}` | nullable | upper bound; local branch refs in `execution_context` whose tips lie inside the candidate range, minus every worktree-held ref; sorted `(repo, ref)`; `null` when range/config/branch/worktree probing failed |
| `collateral_exposed` | bool | nullable | this row's tip is inside an earlier row's `collateral_refs`; independently computed even for skip rows |
| `collateral_mechanism` | enum | nullable | `argv` \| `config` \| `none` |
| `mutation.will_switch_head` | bool | never | `true` for external pass 2 and for every checkout row whose arm runs a standalone `git checkout` (§13.3b); `false` for external pass 1, for the checkout `switched` continuation arm — which switches nothing, because HEAD is already on the branch (§13.3a) — and for all skips |
| `mutation.will_leave_head_on` | string | `null` iff not switching | branch HEAD rests on after the arm returns, including after an arm-local `git rebase --abort` |
| `mutation.head_restored_by_run` | bool | never | `true` checkout, `false` external |
| `context.dirty` | bool | nullable | tracked-only, submodule-ignoring; probe of §18.3 |
| `context.autostash` | bool | nullable | effective `rebase.autoStash` in `execution_context` |
| `context.autostash_applies_to_this_arm` | bool | nullable | true exactly where this arm's own `git rebase` is the next command that reads the dirty tree: external pass 1 (in place), external pass 2 (across the implicit switch), and the checkout **continuation** arms of §13.3b; `false` on a fresh checkout row, which the shipped whole-repo dirty gate refuses before any rebase |
| `context.autostash_reapply_may_conflict` | bool | `null` exactly with the field above | equals applicability; the plan never claims a rescue |
| `context.rebase_in_progress` | bool | nullable | external-only existence of `$GIT_DIR/rebase-merge` or `$GIT_DIR/rebase-apply` in this row's execution directory |
| `context.untracked_present` | bool | nullable | any untracked non-ignored file under the canonical worktree top level |
| `context.overwrite_risk` | enum | `null` iff `untracked_present` is `null` | `none-known` \| `unknown`; never a prediction |
| `branch_checked_out_at` | string | nullable | canonical holder path, from this row's execution context's entry in the §14.4 holder index; holders are the **four** `BranchHoldMechanism` values — an attached `checked-out` HEAD plus the detached `rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply` and `bisect` holders |
| `prunability.probe_context` | string | never | constant `cwd` |
| `blocking` | bool | never | true iff this row independently makes the described run unrunnable |
| `ancestry` | shipped `StackEdge.Status` + `Reason` | status `null` when unevaluated | consumed verbatim from `internal/stack_ancestry.go:174-178`; no new enum |
| `notes[]` | array | `[]` when none | evaluator identity notes, verbatim |

`replay.applied_count`, `context.untracked_overwrite_paths[]` and `snapshot_candidate_count`
MUST NOT exist (§19.15: no snapshot estimate is published — the row publishes `null` plus its
`reason` and nothing else).

**Skip-row contract (total)**

| Field | Mandatory value |
|---|---|
| `argv` | `[]` |
| `replay.determinacy` | `not-applicable` |
| `replay.reason` | `not-executed` |
| `replay.candidate_count` | `0` |
| `replay.commits` / `commits_listed` / `commits_truncated` | `[]` / `0` / `false` |
| `replay.candidate_digest` | digest of the empty sequence (SHA-256 of zero bytes) |
| `replay.range` / `upstream_ref` / `upstream_sha` / `first_candidate` / `may_drop_patch_equivalent` | `null` |
| `replay.upstream_provenance` | `unknown` |
| `collateral_refs` | known `[]` |
| `mutation.will_switch_head` / `head_restored_by_run` | `false` / `false` |
| `mutation.will_leave_head_on` | `null` |

`collateral_exposed` stays independently computed on a skip row (`true`, `false` or `null`). Skip
rows never produce rank 10 `indeterminate-entry`. A `skipped-updated-ref` row has a real execution
context and real head facts, never calls `GetBranchSHA`, and keeps `base.decision_sha: null`. An
external unset base is **not** `skipped-no-base`: it stays an executable `plain` /
`plain-explicit-branch` row with `reason: base-unset` over the quoted empty token `''`.

**`strategy: unknown` contract (total).** An `unknown` row is an **executable** row whose argv the
planner cannot state, because the arm's own inputs did not resolve: per §9.3 it is reached only by a
**checkout** row — one whose destination is unresolvable (eager base failure) or whose head is
missing or unresolvable. No external arm produces it; external keeps its normal arm and publishes
the corresponding rank-5 blocker instead. It is *not* a skip and *not* `conditional`:

| Field | Mandatory value |
|---|---|
| `argv` | `null` — the planner MUST NOT publish a guessed shape, and MUST NOT publish `[]`, which means "this row runs no Git command" |
| `argv_alternatives` | `null` — two shapes are known only on a `conditional` row |
| `strategy_condition` | `null` — it is non-`null` only on a `conditional` row |
| `replay.determinacy` | `unknown` |
| `replay.reason` | the first satisfied member of the **single, complete** §4.2 precedence list — no mini-enum applies here (see the totality rule below the table) |
| `replay.candidate_count` / `commits` / `commits_listed` / `commits_truncated` / `candidate_digest` | `null` (the range is unknown, so §4.7's `unknown ⇒ null` applies to all five) |
| `replay.range` / `upstream_ref` / `upstream_sha` / `first_candidate` | `null` |
| `replay.upstream_provenance` | `unknown` |
| `mutation.will_switch_head` | `true` for every checkout row whose arm runs a standalone `git checkout`; `false` on the `switched` continuation arm, which switches nothing (§13.3a, §13.3b) |
| `blocking` | `true` — every route into `unknown` carries its own rank-5 blocker |
| `guard.evaluation[]` row | `value: null`, `verdict: unknown`, `unknown_kind: not-resolvable` |

**`replay.reason` is total, and there is exactly **one** precedence list (§19.15).** No row shape —
`unknown`, `conditional`, skip or ordinary — gets a private sub-enum of reasons. Every row's
`replay.reason` is the first satisfied member of the §4.2 list, evaluated top-down in its published
order: rank 0 `not-executed`, rank 1 `merge-recreation`, ranks 2a–2f (`repo-unavailable`,
`head-ref-missing`, `base-unset`, `base-ref-missing`, `cutoff-unresolvable`, `probe-failed`), rank 3
`upstream-deferred`, ranks 4a–4b (`no-recorded-cutoff`, `cutoff-not-used-on-arm`) and rank 5 `null`.
On a `strategy: unknown` row that resolves as follows, and the reachability of each rank is a
consequence of the list, never a second rule:

| Rank | Reachable on a `strategy: unknown` row? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 0 `not-executed` | **no** | reserved for `skipped-*` rows; an `unknown` row is executable |
| 1 `merge-recreation` | **yes** | a checkout row whose head or destination did not resolve can still sit in a context with `rebase_merges.interpretation: true` and `effective_backend: merge`. It **outranks** the row's own missing-input reason, exactly as it does on every other row — the earlier five-token enumeration that omitted it is withdrawn |
| 2a–2f | **yes** | these are the reasons that make the row `unknown` in the first place |
| 3 `upstream-deferred` | **yes** | a row whose upstream depends on an earlier post-rebase result and whose own head/destination is separately unresolvable publishes the higher-ranked 2x reason; where only the deferral holds and the arm's argv is still unstatable, rank 3 is the reason |
| 4a–4b | **no** | both imply `determinacy: snapshot` over a resolvable range, which contradicts `unknown`; a row that would otherwise reach them has already matched a rank 1–3 member |
| 5 `null` | **no** | `null` is `determinacy: exact` only |

The same totality holds in the other direction: a `conditional` row takes its reason from the same
list (typically rank 3), and a `skipped-*` row always matches rank 0 first. `argv` is `null` for
`conditional` **and** `unknown` and `[]` for every skip (§4.2), independently of the reason.
Tests (§22.25a, §23): an `unknown` row in a `rebaseMerges`-true merge-backend context publishes
`merge-recreation`; the same fixture with `effective_backend: apply` publishes its 2x reason; and a
table test asserts every emitted `replay.reason` is a member of the one list with no row-shape
exception.

`effective_backend` still publishes what the config inventory established, because it does not
depend on the argv the planner could not build; it is `null` only under §4.2's own rule.

### 4.3 `summary` and the two rows-less profiles

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `summary.plannability` | enum, never null | `rows` \| `empty` \| `unavailable` |
| `summary.entries` | int, never null | published row count |
| `summary.deferred_destinations` | int, never null | over published rows |
| `summary.conditional_strategies` | int, never null | over published rows |
| `summary.max_entry_candidates` | int, nullable | `null` when every candidate count is `null` |
| `summary.total_candidates` | int, nullable | the exact total; non-`null` **iff** `summary.plannability ∈ {rows, empty}` **and** `summary.entries_with_unknown_candidates == 0`, in which case it equals `summary.total_candidates_lower_bound`; `not-applicable` rows contribute `0`. The plannability conjunct is **not** redundant: an `unavailable` document publishes `entries_with_unknown_candidates: 0` because it has no rows at all, and a rule reading the unknown count alone would then require a non-`null` total for a document that measured nothing (§4.3's second table, §25.43) |
| `summary.total_candidates_lower_bound` | int, nullable | sum of countable rows; `null` only for `plannability: unavailable` |
| `summary.entries_with_unknown_candidates` | int, never null | `determinacy == unknown` rows; excludes `not-applicable` |
| `summary.collateral_exposed_entries` | int, never null | known-exposed rows |
| `summary.entries_with_unknown_collateral` | int, never null | rows with null collateral facts |
| `summary.collateral_refs` | tuple array, nullable | union of known at-risk refs, sorted `(repo, ref)` |
| `summary.collateral_bound` | `upper` or `null` | `upper` iff `summary.collateral_refs` is non-null |
| `summary.collateral_refs_unowned` | int, nullable | count with `stack_owned: false`; `null` iff aggregate is `null` |

| Field | `plannability: empty` | `plannability: unavailable` |
|---|---|---|
| `entries[]` | `[]` | `[]` |
| `entries` / deferred / conditional counts | `0` | `0` |
| unknown-candidate / unknown-collateral counts | `0` | `0` |
| `max_entry_candidates` | `null` | `null` |
| `total_candidates` | `0` | `null` |
| `total_candidates_lower_bound` | `0` | `null` |
| `collateral_refs` | `[]` | `null` |
| `collateral_bound` | `upper` | `null` |
| `collateral_refs_unowned` | `0` | `null` |
| `guard.evaluation[]` | one `basis: total`, `value: 0`, `within-limit` row iff a total limit is effective; no per-entry rows | `[]` — always, even with effective limits (§4.6) |
| `guard.would_refuse*` | `false` | `false` |
| `repositories[]` | `[]` unless a context was cited | `[]` unless a safe context was already established |

The two `total_candidates` cells above are the **only** reading of the row rule: `empty` is a
measured zero (rows were plannable and there were none), `unavailable` is an unmeasured nothing.
Both carry `entries_with_unknown_candidates: 0`, so plannability — not the unknown count — is what
separates them (§25.43).

**Rows-less runnability is decided by the general rule of §7.3, never by an enumeration of the
ranks a rows-less document happens to reach.** A `plannability: empty` document is
`runnable: true` **iff** it carries **no** *independent* blocking fact: no effective, unwaived
blocker of ranks 1–5 (**every** sub-rank of rank 5 included — 5.0, 5.05, 5.06, 5.07, 5.08, 5.1,
5.15, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.45, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9) and no rank 6 `selection-hazard` under its v1
blocking rendering (§7.1, §7.3). *Independent* means the fact is not attached to a published row,
because there are none: on a rows-less document the qualifying facts are its document-level
(`entry: null`) blockers plus any fact a projected arm attributes to a transaction or payload entry
the document publishes **no** row for (§13.3's `restoring`/`completed` stages). Ranks 7–12 never
move it, exactly as on a document with rows.

The earlier reading — "`runnable: true` **only** when it carries no independent rank 3, 4, 4.5, 6
fact and no document-level rank 5.05 `fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate` (checkout route only)"
— is **withdrawn**, and no text may restore it: it was a list of the cells then in view rather than
a rule, and it would have published `runnable: true` for a rows-less run that a hard blocker really
stops. The following are therefore explicitly, and non-exhaustively, `runnable: false` on a
rows-less document:

- document-level rank 5.05 `fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate` and rank 5.06
  `fetch-local-branch-checked-out` — both are facts of the *fetch*, need no row at all, and are
  reachable in both modes (§11.2, §11.5, §11.6);
- **route-applicable** rank 5.07 `invalid-git-config` — a rows-less run that still fetches,
  restores or pushes really hands the offending key to Git, and the row-lessness of the document
  does not make the key harmless (§7.1 rank 5.07, §11.7);
- **conditional** rank 5.08 `identity-not-utf8` — emitted exactly where the document would mint or
  was given a token; a limitless rows-less plan publishes `encoding_issues[]`, emits no such
  blocker and stays runnable, which is the same rule, not an exception (§7.1 rank 5.08);
- rank 5.0 `fetch-context-indeterminate`, rank 5.1 `repo-unavailable`, rank 5.15
  `base-execution-store-divergent` and rank 5.9 `probe-failed` measured for a fetch, restore or
  **push** context rather than for a row — including the unreadable push mapping of a rows-less
  push-only continuation (§14.1a rule 5a);
- rank 4 `preflight-refused` from the external completion gate on that same rows-less push-only
  continuation (§7.1's rank-4 rule), rank 4.5 `restore-blocked` and rank 3 `state-refused`.

A `plannability: unavailable` document is `runnable: false` in every reachable cell — not by a
separate axiom but by the same rule, because whatever prevented rows from being established is
itself an effective rank 1–5 blocker (rank 1 `plan-unavailable`/`stack-unsortable`, rank 2
`selection-refused`, or a rank 3–5 state/context fact, §10.2, §13.7, §13.7a).

### 4.4 `repositories[]` and configuration evidence

```text
{repo, context_id, repo_root, root_source,
 config: {update_refs, rebase_merges, backend, auto_stash}}
```

- One row **iff** the context was established and is cited by an entry `base_context` /
  `execution_context`, a `push.targets[].context_id`, a `config_issues[].context_id`, or the
  restore context. A fetch-only context emits no row. `source: not-applicable` never emits a row.
- Sorted `(repo, context_id)`; empty `repo` sorts first.
- `context_id` = SHA-256 over the length-framed raw tuple
  `("config-context/v1", canonical raw repo root, root_source, canonical raw common dir)`,
  produced by **one** generic context-identity function that is never execution-scoped and has no
  empty-string fallback. It is the sole join key, in both directions, and stays total across a
  partial context failure: a surviving ref keeps its citation.
- `root_source` ∈ `worktree` \| `entry-repo` \| `process-cwd` \| `workspace-repo-root`
  (`not-applicable` excluded).
- `repo_root` is sanitized, display-only, may collide, and is never a join, sort or fingerprint key.

Config slots are total over `{status, value, source}` (`rebase_merges` adds `interpretation` — the
one declared arity exception):

| `status` | `value` | `source` |
|---|---|---|
| `valid` | the effective typed value | `probed` |
| `absent` | `null` | `null` |
| `not-evaluated` | `null` | `null` |
| `probe-failed` | `null` | `null` |
| `invalid` | `null` | the offending occurrence's Git **scope** |

`rebase_merges.interpretation` ∈ `true` \| `false` \| `unknown` \| `invalid`, never `null`:
`valid`⇒`true`/`false`, `absent`⇒`false`, `not-evaluated`/`probe-failed`⇒`unknown`,
`invalid`⇒`invalid`. It is fingerprint material. `unset` is not a status member.

`config_issues[]` rows are closed at eleven members:

```text
{issue_id, context_id, repo_root, key, source, route_command, error_kind,
 raw_value_present, raw_value_base64, raw_value_sha256, sanitized_value}
```

- `source` ∈ Git's own seven `--show-scope` names (`system`, `global`, `local`, `worktree`,
  `command`, `submodule`, `unknown`) plus `gitmodules`. `command` means *inherited* command-scope
  configuration; this feature never adds a `-c`.
- `route_command` ∈ `fetch` \| `checkout` \| `push` \| `rebase`.
- `error_kind` ∈ `bad-boolean` \| `bad-fetch-recurse` \| `unknown-rebase-merges-mode` \|
  `missing-backend-value` \| `unknown-rebase-backend` \| `bad-numeric`.
- Exactly one row per route-fatal `(context_id, key)`, one-to-one with a rank 5.07
  `invalid-git-config` blocker; sorted and de-duplicated on `issue_id` (64-lower-hex) alone.
- `raw_value_present: false` (a valueless occurrence) differs from an explicitly empty value;
  `raw_value_base64` / `raw_value_sha256` / `sanitized_value` are `null` iff no raw value exists.
- Raw bytes never appear in any `detail`, human line, or warning.

`encoding_issues[]` rows are closed at six ASCII-only members:

```text
{field_id, path_label_ascii, owner_entry_ascii_or_null, byte_length, raw_base64, sha256}
```

sorted by `(field_id, path_label_ascii, owner_entry_ascii_or_null [null first], sha256)` with exact
duplicate rows removed. The array is never `null`.

### 4.4a `fetch` and `push` — complete top-level schemas

Both objects are **fixed-domain and closed**: no key is ever omitted, no key is ever added without
amending this section, and the §4.1 key-set test descends into both tables. Every enum below is
closed; `null` always means *unknown*, per §4.7.

**`fetch` (7 members)**

| Field | Type | Nullability | Domain / rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fetch.attempted` | bool | never | at least one `repos[]` row ran a `git fetch`; `false` for every suppression cause of §11.2 and for `local-only` |
| `fetch.outcome` | enum | never | `ok` (every attempted row succeeded) \| `failed` (every attempted row failed) \| `partial` \| `skipped` (nothing attempted) |
| `fetch.policy_source` | enum | never | `route-default` \| `flag` \| `persisted-payload` \| `persisted-transaction`; the provenance of the effective fetch policy, never a second policy value |
| `fetch.suppression_cause` | enum | nullable | `null` iff nothing suppressed the fetch; else **the `freshness` token of the single satisfied §11.2 cause**, in that section's precedence order: `not-refreshed-continuation` \| `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` \| `not-refreshed-live-run` \| `not-refreshed-context-indeterminate` \| `not-refreshed-submodule-reach-indeterminate` \| `not-refreshed-local-branch-checked-out`. It introduces **no** second vocabulary: it is exactly the six-member suppression subset of the twelve `freshness` values (§11.3). "Policy says no fetch" is not a suppression: it is `attempted: false` with `null` here and `freshness: local-only` |
| `fetch.mutated_remote_tracking_refs` | bool | **tri-state** (nullable) | `true` when a successful attempted row has a known contacting, ref-writing effect; `null` when a relevant effect/reach is unknown or a contacting fetch failed and may have partially written; `false` otherwise, including every suppressed fetch (§11.3) |
| `fetch.mutated_local_branches` | bool | **tri-state** (nullable) | same three-valued rule over `fetch_effect.may_update_local_branches` / `may_delete_local_branches` of the attempted rows; `false` when no covering positive `refs/heads/**` destination exists |
| `fetch.repos[]` | array | never null | the row shape below. It is `[]` **exactly** in three cases: suppression causes **1–3** (nothing was ever resolved for this invocation), the `local-only` policy, and `not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets` (zero resolved targets). Causes **4–6** publish their resolved rows with `attempted: false` — cause 4 with the known tokens and candidates only, causes **5 and 6** with the **whole** resolved row (`context_root`, `context_common_dir`, `context_source`, `fetch_effect`, `context_candidates[]`), because the route measured all of it *before* deciding not to fetch (§11.1, §11.2, §13.7 step 1.5). A cause-5 or cause-6 document whose `fetch.repos[]` is `[]` is a schema failure (§22.13g) |

`freshness` is **not** a member of this object: it is the document-level key of §4.1, computed by
the total table of §11.3 from these fields.

**`fetch.repos[]` row (8 members, closed)** — the §11.4 shape, restated here as the normative
field table:

| Field | Type | Nullability | Domain / rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo_token` | string | never | the `StackEntry.Repo` token this context was resolved for; `""` is a value, not absence; the checkout route emits exactly one row with `""` |
| `context_root` | string | nullable | sanitized display path of the directory the fetch child ran in (or would have run in); `null` under suppression cause 4, and `null` on causes 1–3, where no row exists at all |
| `context_common_dir` | string | nullable | sanitized measured `--git-common-dir`. `null` under suppression cause 4 and `null` when the measurement itself failed — the same failure that forces `fetch_effect: null` and `freshness: unknown-fetch-effect`. It is **never omitted**: the checkout route's single row always carries this member, measured before its fetch (§11.1, §13.7 rule 6a) |
| `context_source` | enum | nullable | `worktree` \| `entry-repo` \| `process-cwd` \| `workspace-repo-root`; `null` under suppression cause 4 |
| `fetch_effect` | object | nullable | the closed §11.4 effect object (`all`, `contacted`, `head_branch`, `may_delete_refs`, `may_delete_tags`, `may_clobber_tags`, `may_update_local_branches`, `may_delete_local_branches`, `local_branch_destinations`, `remotes[]`, `submodule_recursion`); `null` exactly when the effect could not be established |
| `context_candidates[]` | array | never null | `{context_root, context_source, first_entry}` rows, sorted per §4.8; the disclosure that makes rank 5.0 auditable. It is `[]`, never `null`, wherever the row exists — including the checkout route, whose single row always carries exactly **one** candidate (`{repo root, workspace-repo-root, null}`), and including a cause-5/6 row |
| `attempted` | bool | never | this row ran `git fetch`; `false` on every suppressed row |
| `ok` | bool | nullable | `null` **iff** `attempted: false`; else the child's exit status |

**Go ↔ schema mapping for one row (fixed, total, no third spelling).** The row is produced by
`internal.PlanFetchRepoResult` (§13.7) and by nothing else; the builder copies, never re-derives:

| JSON member | Go field | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `repo_token` | `RepoToken string` | verbatim |
| `context_root` | `ContextRoot string` | sanitized for display; `""` ⇒ `null` |
| `context_common_dir` | `ContextCommonDir string` | sanitized for display; `""` ⇒ `null` |
| `context_source` | `ContextSource string` | one of the four enum values; `""` ⇒ `null` |
| `fetch_effect` | `Effect *PlanFetchEffect` | `nil` ⇒ `null`; copied from the pre-fetch enumeration, never re-probed |
| `context_candidates[]` | `ContextCandidates []PlanFetchCandidate` | **never `nil`**; `[]` is encoded as `[]` |
| `attempted` | `Attempted bool` | verbatim |
| `ok` | `OK bool` | encoded as `null` when `Attempted == false`; otherwise the bool. `OK` is meaningless and MUST be ignored when `Attempted` is false |

**`push` (4 members)**

| Field | Type | Nullability | Domain / rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `push.targets[]` | array | never null | the §14.1 row shape `{repo, context_id, repo_root, materialization, git_branch, remote, ref, force, lease, scope}`, whose complete field table is below, sorted `(context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise)` — the array is **totally** ordered even where a row's `context_id` is `null` (§4.8); `[]` whenever `intent.push` is false, and legitimately `[]` with `intent.push: true` when no eligible target exists |
| `push.executable` | bool | nullable | a **conditional** fact: it answers "would the described invocation reach its push?", which is a question the route only asks when `intent.push` is true. `true` when that invocation reaches the push; `false` when a projected gate blocks it or the shipped arm drops it; **`null` in exactly two cells** — `intent.push: false`, where the route performs no push at all and the question was never asked, and `summary.plannability: unavailable`, where nothing about the run was established. `true`/`false` are therefore published **only** when `intent.push` is true **and** plannability is `rows` or `empty` (§14.3, §4.7) |
| `push.blocked_by[]` | array of tokens | never null | sorted, de-duplicated members of the closed compositional domain of §7.5 — every `RefusalKind` that effectively stops the controlled invocation before it reaches the push, plus the warning-only `push-dropped-restoring`, which appears **only** on a `restoring` stage whose persisted `intent.push` is `true` (§13.3); `[]` when push is executable **and** in both `executable: null` cells, where nothing blocks a push the route never performs; never a copy of `blockers[]` |
| `push.scope` | enum | never | `stack-all` \| `selected-rebased` \| `transaction-plan` \| `none`; `none` exactly when `intent.push` is false. It is the projection rule of §14.1, not a per-target label — each `targets[]` row still carries its own `scope` with the same first three values |

**`push.targets[]` row (10 members, closed)** — the normative field table; the §4.1 key-set test
descends into it exactly as it does into `fetch.repos[]`, in **both** directions (§22.33b):

| Field | Type | Nullability | Domain / rule | Go field (`PlanPushTarget`, §14.1a) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | never | the `StackEntry.Repo` token; `""` is a value, not absence; the checkout route emits `""` on every row | `Repo string` |
| `context_id` | 64-lower-hex | **nullable** | the push context's id, produced by `ResolvePushContext` and by nothing else; **the only join key**, and equal to the row's `entries[].base_context.context_id` wherever the two are the same directory (§14.1a rule 2); `null` exactly when that context could not be established, which also raises rank 5.1 on the entry row (§14.1a rule 6) and puts the row's lease in the `expectation: unknown` cell beside its rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker (§14.1a rule 5a). It is **never** REQUIRED, never non-nullable and never the empty string: `null` is the one spelling of "not established", here and in every Go carrier behind it (§14.1a). A `null`-`context_id` row still sorts — first, ahead of every established id (§4.8) — and still binds a `NULL` tuple member (§8.2) | `ContextID *string` |
| `repo_root` | string | nullable | sanitized display path of that context: external `entry.Repo` else the materialized worktree, checkout the workspace repository root; `null` exactly with its `context_id`; never a join, sort or fingerprint input | `RepoRoot *string` |
| `materialization` | enum | never | the §4.2 enum, measured once per entry: `materialized` on every emitted external row (a non-materialized entry is **not** a target — the shipped loops skip it) and on every checkout row; the other three values are reachable here only if a future arm emits a non-materialized target, which v1 does not | `Materialization string` |
| `git_branch` | string | never | `StackEntry.GitBranch()` for external, `tx.Plan[i].Branch` for checkout — the ref the shipped argv really names | `GitBranch string` |
| `remote` | string | never | the literal `origin` (§14.1a rule 4); it is never the §11.4 fetch-side resolved remote | `Remote string` |
| `ref` | string | never | `refs/heads/<git_branch>` | `Ref string` |
| `force` | enum | never | `with-lease` — the only value v1 publishes, mirroring `--force-with-lease` | `Force string` |
| `lease` | object | never | the closed 5-member §14.2 object tabulated below; never `null`, on any route or cell | `Lease PlanLease` |
| `scope` | enum | never | `stack-all` \| `selected-rebased` \| `transaction-plan` — the per-row label of the §14.1 rule that admitted it; the document-level `push.scope` carries the same value plus `none` | `Scope string` |

**`push.targets[].lease` (5 members, closed)** — the §14.2 object, restated as its normative field
table; the key-set test descends into it too, and a sixth member fails §22.33b:

| Field | Type | Nullability | Domain / rule | Go field (`PlanLease`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | enum | never | `implicit-remote-tracking` — the only value; the shipped argv sends no explicit expectation, and an explicit lease is never claimed | `Mode string` |
| `expectation` | enum | never | `sha` \| `absent` \| `unknown`; `absent` is Git's null-OID expectation and is **stricter**, never an unprotected force. `unknown` is reachable in exactly **one** cell — the push context's mapping half could not be read (`MappingReadOK: false`, §14.1a rule 5a) — and it always accompanies that context's rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker. A mapping that **was** read and matched nothing is `absent`, never `unknown` | `Expectation string` |
| `expected_ref` | string | nullable | the mapped remote-tracking ref: non-`null` whenever the first matching **non-negative** refspec maps the branch — including the `absent` cell, where the mapped ref is exactly the ref that must not exist — and `null` exactly where no positive mapping exists **or** where the mapping could not be read (`expectation: unknown`) | `ExpectedRef *string` |
| `expected_sha` | 40/64-lower-hex | nullable | the mapped ref's current value; `null` **iff** `expectation` is not `sha` (i.e. on every `absent` and every `unknown` row) | `ExpectedSHA *string` |
| `expected_sha_freshness` | enum | **never null** | `fresh` \| `possibly-stale`, per §14.2 step 3 — `fresh` **only** on a `sha` row whose facts carry `TrackingPhase: post-fetch`, `MappingReadOK: true`, `TrackingReadOK: true` and `FetchedThisRun: true` (§14.1a rules 7–8), and on an `absent` row whose inventory was read — with the unconditional negative-refspec override of step 4. Every `unknown` row is `possibly-stale`, because nothing was resolved | `ExpectedSHAFreshness string` |

**Restated for readers arriving from §14.2 (the table above is the normative form; this paragraph
adds no field and may not disagree with it):**
`push.targets[].lease` is the closed §14.2 object
`{mode, expectation, expected_ref, expected_sha, expected_sha_freshness}` with
`mode: implicit-remote-tracking`, `expectation` ∈ `sha` \| `absent` \| `unknown`, and
`expected_sha_freshness` ∈ `fresh` \| `possibly-stale`, never `null`. The baseline is the
destination of the **first matching non-negative** configured fetch refspec: a **negative**
refspec (`^…`) is skipped by that mapping and is therefore never a reason to publish
`expectation: absent`. Where the positive mapping exists and the mapped remote-tracking ref
**exists**, the row is `expectation: sha` with that ref and its current value — read **after** this
invocation's fetch decision was carried out (§14.1a rule 7) — labelled `fresh` only where this
invocation's own fetch really refreshed that context's `origin` refs (§14.1a rule 8) and
`possibly-stale` otherwise, including where a negative entry covers the branch, because no fetch of
this configuration can ever refresh it (§14.2). Where the mapping **was read** and no positive
refspec maps the branch, or the mapped tracking ref is absent or unreadable, the row is
`expectation: absent` with `expected_sha: null` — Git's null-OID expectation. Where the mapping
itself could **not** be read, the row is `expectation: unknown` with `expected_ref: null`,
`expected_sha: null` and `possibly-stale`, beside the rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker of §14.1a
rule 5a: an unread mapping is never reported as a null-OID expectation, because that would tell an
operator their push is protected by a check nobody established.

`intent.push` is never derived from `push.targets[]` emptiness, and `push.executable` is never
derived from `blockers[]`; both are computed facts with their own rules (§14.1, §14.3).

### 4.5 `state` — the pre-acquisition snapshot

One top-level object with a fixed key domain:

```text
state = {snapshot, files, external_cell, worktree, git_op, head}
state.files = {checkout_transaction, checkout_lock, external_legacy_state,
               external_payload, external_run_guard}
```

Both maps are fixed-domain objects; neither has `null` members.

**Every row of this section has exactly one typed producer (§12.5a), and the mapping is fixed:**

| JSON path | Go member | Producer |
|---|---|---|
| `state.files.checkout_transaction` | `PlanCheckoutTransactionFile` | `InspectCheckoutPlanState` (checkout); `applicable: false` on external |
| `state.files.checkout_lock` | `PlanCheckoutLockFile` | `InspectCheckoutPlanState` (checkout); `applicable: false` on external |
| `state.files.external_legacy_state` | `PlanLegacySyncStateFile` | `InspectExternalPlanState` (external); `applicable: false` on checkout |
| `state.files.external_payload` | `PlanSyncRunPayloadFile` | `InspectExternalPlanState` (external); `applicable: false` on checkout |
| `state.files.external_run_guard` | `PlanSyncRunGuardFile` | `InspectExternalPlanState` (external); `applicable: false` on checkout |
| `state.snapshot` | `PlanSnapshotFacts` | whichever inspector ran |
| `state.external_cell` | `ExternalPlanState.Cell` (`SyncStateCell`) | `InspectExternalPlanState` |
| `state.worktree`, `state.git_op`, `state.head` | `CheckoutPlanState.Worktree` / `.GitOp` / `.Head` | `InspectCheckoutPlanState` |

`BuildRebasePlan` encodes these rows **from `req.CheckoutState`/`req.ExternalState` only** and
performs no filesystem probe of its own (§13.7a rule 8, §12.5a rule 6). There is no generic
artefact type: the withdrawn `PlanArtefactPresence` is replaced by the five concrete file types of
§12.5a, each carrying its own decoded members, so a member belonging to one artefact cannot be
published on another.

- `state.snapshot = {taken_before_acquisition, self_pid}`. The snapshot is taken at route entry,
  **before** `setupSyncRunState`, `AcquireCheckoutLock`, `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` and
  `ReclaimSyncRunGuard`, and is carried unchanged into the guard seam. Snapshot facts are never
  re-read at a seam.
- Every file row begins `{applicable, presence, unreadable_reason}`. `presence` ∈ `absent` \|
  `readable` \| `unreadable` \| `symlink` \| `not-applicable`, never `null`. `unreadable_reason` ∈
  `not-regular-file` \| `io-error` \| `decode-error` \| `empty-document`, non-null only with
  `presence: unreadable`. Decoded members are `null` unless `presence: readable`.
- Decoded members: `checkout_transaction` → `state_version, route, stage, current_index,
  failed_entry, lock_pid, lock_created, original_branch, plan_len`; `checkout_lock` →
  `pid, created, alive, self`; `external_legacy_state` → `failed_branch, marker_present, marker,
  completed_len, pending_len`; `external_payload` → `state_version, route, stage, failed_branch,
  owner_token_present, selected_len, completed_len, pushed_len`; `external_run_guard` →
  `pid, created, state_version, token_present, alive, self, token_matches_payload`.
- `route` on either decoded artefact is the **effective** route of §13.6 rule 4 — the persisted
  value when present, else the shipped derivation — so it is `new-mode` \| `legacy`, never `null`
  on a `presence: readable` row. `state_version` is published verbatim, including `3`; the run
  guard's own `state_version` stays `2` in every cell (§13.6 rule 2) and is not a route signal.
- `alive` is `null` unless `presence: readable`. `token_matches_payload` is equality (the inverse
  polarity of `GuardForeign()`) and is `null` when either side is unreadable/absent or the payload
  owner token is empty.
- Non-file rows: `state.external_cell = {applies, cell}` (external only);
  `state.worktree = {applies, dirty, probe_ok}` (checkout only);
  `state.git_op = {applies, in_progress, kind, kind_source}` (checkout only);
  `state.head = {applies, detached, branch}` (checkout only).
- `state.git_op.kind` ∈ `none` \| `rebase` \| `merge` \| `cherry-pick` \| `revert` \| `bisect` \|
  `probe-failed`; `kind_source` ∈ `executor-markers` \| `active-op-probe` \| `null`. `in_progress`
  is true **iff** one of the shipped `gitOperationInProgress` markers exists — the four operations
  rebase/merge/cherry-pick/revert over five paths (`rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply`, `MERGE_HEAD`,
  `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD`, §13.7 gate c) — so `bisect` and `probe-failed` are `false`.
  **§19.23 resolved: `kind: bisect` is published as this fact only. It emits no `warnings[]` row**
  — the warning enum stays closed at eight kinds (§4.6) — and it is never a blocker.
- External shape is `{applies: false, in_progress: null, kind: null, kind_source: null}`; a failed
  checkout probe is `{applies: true, in_progress: false, kind: probe-failed, kind_source:
  active-op-probe}`.

### 4.6 `intent`, `guard`, `approval`, `blockers[]`, `warnings[]`, `refusal`

`intent`:

| Field | Domain | Nullability |
|---|---|---|
| `intent.push` | bool | never |
| `intent.push_source` | `flag` \| `persisted-payload` \| `persisted-transaction` \| `flag-legacy-continuation` | never |
| `intent.validation.applies` | bool | never |
| `intent.validation.source` | `none` \| `config-per-entry` \| `persisted-payload` \| `cli-test` \| `persisted-transaction` | never |
| `intent.validation.stability` | `not-applicable` \| `frozen` \| `per-entry-dynamic` | never |
| `intent.validation.guarded_stability` | `not-applicable` \| `frozen-at-plan` \| `per-entry-dynamic` | never |
| `intent.validation.command_digest` | 64-lower-hex SHA-256 | `null` iff validation does not apply |
| `intent.validation.cli_test_ignored` | bool | never |

The raw validation command is **never** published (§15).

`guard.limits` is a single per-key `{value, origin}` encoding:

```text
guard.limits = {max_replay_per_entry: {value, origin},
                max_replay_total:     {value, origin}}
```

`value` is a non-negative integer or `null` (`0` is a real limit). `origin` ∈ `none` \| `flags` \|
`persisted-payload` \| `persisted-transaction` \| `flags-persisted-continuation` \|
`flags-legacy-continuation`. An unarmed key is `{value: null, origin: none}`. No outer or inner
object is ever `null`. There is **no** `guard_enabled` field: "guarded" means at least one
`value != null`.

`guard.limit_conflicts[]` rows are `{key, effective_value, effective_origin, supplied_value}`,
sorted bytewise by `key`, `[]` when there is no conflict. The persisted value stays effective.

`guard.evaluation[]` rows carry all eight members always:

```text
{id, limit, value, basis, entry, verdict, unknown_kind, unknown_entries}
```

- `basis` ∈ `per-entry` \| `total` \| `lower-bound`; `entry` is the logical name on `per-entry`
  rows and `null` on aggregates; `limit` is the effective numeric threshold and is never `null` on
  an emitted row; `verdict` ∈ `within-limit` \| `exceeded` \| `waived` \| `unknown`;
  `unknown_kind` ∈ `deferred-resolvable` \| `not-resolvable`, `null` unless `verdict: unknown`;
  `unknown_entries` is `null` on per-entry and exact-total rows and positive on lower-bound rows.
- `id` is `max_replay_per_entry:<name>` for per-entry rows and `max_replay_total` for the aggregate
  row. Sorted bytewise by `id`.
- Comparison is strict `>`; equality is `within-limit`. `--max-replay-per-entry 0` means any
  replayed candidate exceeds.
- Emission is total **within a plannable document**: one row per published entry per effective
  per-entry limit, and exactly one aggregate row per effective total limit — whether or not
  anything is exceeded. A skip row's `value` is the measured `0`, `verdict: within-limit`. A
  `determinacy: unknown` row has `value: null`, `verdict: unknown`,
  `unknown_kind: deferred-resolvable` for `upstream-deferred` and `not-resolvable` otherwise. Where
  no limit is effective the array is `[]`.
- **The emission rules above apply only when `summary.plannability ∈ {rows, empty}`.** For
  `summary.plannability: unavailable` the array is **`[]`**, even when a per-entry limit, a total
  limit or both are effective, and even when a token was supplied: there is no measured subject to
  compare, so an aggregate row would publish a comparison the planner never performed. The
  `U == 0`, `B == 0` aggregate of the table below is the `empty` cell only; `unavailable` has
  `total_candidates_lower_bound: null` (§4.3) and therefore no `value` to emit. `guard.would_refuse`
  and `guard.would_refuse_without_approval` stay `false` there, and the document's own top-ranked
  `refusal.kind` (rank 1–5) is what refuses.

**Aggregate rule — branch on the unknown count first.** With `L` the effective total limit,
`B = summary.total_candidates_lower_bound` and `U = summary.entries_with_unknown_candidates`:

| Case | `basis` | `value` | `unknown_entries` | `verdict` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `U == 0` | `total` | exactly `B`, which equals `summary.total_candidates` | `null` | `exceeded` iff `B > L`, else `within-limit` |
| `U > 0` and `B > L` | `lower-bound` | `B` | `U` | `exceeded` |
| `U > 0` and `B <= L` | `lower-bound` | `B` | `U` | `unknown` |

When `U == 0` every countable row was counted, so the aggregate **is** the total and MUST NOT be
labelled a lower bound — including when it exceeds. `summary.total_candidates` is non-`null`
exactly in that case **within a `rows` or `empty` document**, and the row's `value` equals it; on an
`unavailable` document there is no aggregate row and `total_candidates` stays `null`, because
`U == 0` there means "no rows were measured", not "every row was counted" (§4.3, §25.43). An `unknown` aggregate carries
`unknown_kind: not-resolvable` if any contributing unknown row is, else `deferred-resolvable`;
an `exceeded` or `within-limit` aggregate carries `unknown_kind: null`. A `plannability: empty`
document is the `U == 0`, `B == 0` cell: `basis: total`, `value: 0`, `unknown_entries: null`,
`within-limit` (no non-negative `L` can be exceeded by `0`). A `plannability: unavailable` document
emits **no** aggregate row and no per-entry row at all, per the scoping rule above.

`guard.indeterminacy_policy` is the constant **`jit-deferred`** (§10.4). It is published, never
`null`, and there is no flag that changes it.

`guard.would_refuse_without_approval` is the raw verdict (true for any `exceeded` row, any
`not-resolvable` unknown row, and — under a `refuse-up-front` policy, which v1 never selects — any
deferred unknown row). `guard.would_refuse` is the post-waiver verdict.

`guard.execute_blocked_by[]` is closed at exactly five sorted, de-duplicated, non-waivable tokens,
and it has **its own Go type** — it is never a `RefusalKind` slice. The type and its five constants
are **declared once, in §19.1** (`internal/rebase_plan.go`), and the schema member is typed
`[]ControlledPathBlocker`:

```text
fetch-context-indeterminate | fetch-local-branch-checked-out |
fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate | live-owner-concurrency |
owner-artefact-undecodable
```

It is deliberately **not** `RefusalKind`: these tokens name controlled-path preconditions the guard
itself owns, they are non-waivable, and three of them (the fetch-effect facts) also exist as
`RefusalKind`s with the same spelling but a different job — the blocker row explains the refusal,
this token admits or declines execution. A schema test asserts `len(ControlledPathBlockers) == 5`
and that the emitted array is a sorted, de-duplicated subset of it (§22.33d).

The array is published even on a rows-less document, and it is `[]` — never `null` — when nothing
blocks. **Membership is decided by ownership, never by consequence.** A token is a member exactly
when it names a precondition of the **controlled path itself**: the two owner-artefact facts the
pre-acquisition snapshot observes (§12.5, §12.5a) and the three fetch-effect facts the controlled
route measures **before its own fetch** (§11.2 causes 4–6). Those are the facts that stop a guarded
execution *even if every limit were within bound and every row were waived*, and they are the facts
a consumer cannot recover from `blockers[]` alone, because they describe the run's own preconditions
rather than a row.

Rank 5.07 `invalid-git-config` and rank 5.08 `identity-not-utf8` are **not** members for reasons of
ownership: 5.07 projects a failure **Git** would raise on the command it is handed, on any route,
guarded or not; 5.08 is a fingerprint-**encoding** fact that decides whether a token can be minted,
not whether execution is admitted. Two earlier justifications are **withdrawn**, and neither is
replaced by another consequence-based one: "both already set `runnable: false`" (which could not
distinguish anything) and its round-13 successor "**every** member of this array sets
`runnable: false` too" (which is simply **false** — see the rule below). Nothing is lost by their
exclusion, because the admission predicate below conjoins `runnable` *and* this array
independently, and both facts are published as ordinary `blockers[]` rows with their §7.1 rank. The
five-token domain itself is unchanged.

**A controlled-path token and `runnable` are independent, and neither implies the other.**
`runnable` is a fact about the **described** route (§7.3); a `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` member is
a precondition of the **controlled** route. Several members do coincide with `runnable: false` —
they do so because the described route's own ladder refuses on the same fact (a live foreign
`.checkout-sync.lock` a fresh checkout run would meet, a rank 5.0/5.05/5.06 fetch-effect fact the
described fetch would hit) — but the coincidence is a consequence of the described route, never of
membership. Where the described route never consults the fact, `runnable` stays `true` beside a
non-empty `execute_blocked_by[]`: that is exactly the `owner-artefact-undecodable` cell of §12.5,
where the shipped ladder reads *through* a symlinked owner artefact and the guard deliberately does
not. A document publishing `runnable: false` merely because a controlled token is present, or
suppressing the token because the described route runs, fails §22.13m.

The single plan→execute admission predicate is:

```text
runnable && !guard.would_refuse && guard.execute_blocked_by == [] && refusal.kind == null
```

It is scoped to **admission** — reaching the first rebase with the identity and declared blockers
of this document. It promises nothing about conflicts, a checkout Git refuses, hooks, validation
failure, or a rejected push. It is also the **only** place the four conjuncts are combined: a
non-empty `execute_blocked_by[]` denies admission on its own, without moving `runnable`, without
inventing a `refusal.kind`, and **without suppressing the token** — `approval.fingerprint` is still
minted whenever the three §8.4 clauses hold, is still printed by the human tail (§6.3 part 4), and
is still bound to these facts. A consumer that reads only the fingerprint line and skips this
predicate will present the token to an invocation that refuses at its guard seam; that is why the
predicate, not the token, is the documented gate (§20).

`approval`:

| Field | Domain | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `approval.fingerprint` | 64-lower-hex or `null` | non-null **iff** all three clauses of §8.4 hold |
| `approval.usable` | bool, never null | exactly `fingerprint != null` |
| `approval.scope` | `full-run` \| `remaining-work` | never null; a `--continue` document is always `remaining-work` |
| `approval.supplied` | bool, never null | `--approve-plan` was given |
| `approval.accepted` | bool or `null` | `null` iff nothing supplied |
| `approval.covers` | closed 8-member object | `{scope, waived_evaluation_ids[], waived_kinds[], hard_blockers_waived, has_work, requires_limits, encoding_safe, note}` |

`hard_blockers_waived` is the constant `false`. `waived_kinds[]` is a sorted subset of
`{limit-per-entry, limit-total}`. `note` is a fixed sanitized sentence.

`blockers[]` and `warnings[]` rows are `{kind, entry, detail}` with `entry: null` for
document-level facts and a sanitized `detail`. Neither array is ever `null`. The
`warnings[].kind` enum is **closed at eight** members and gains none in v1:

```text
collateral-update-refs-config | base-execution-context-split | fetch-context-divergent |
autostash-across-switch | checkout-dirty-present | push-dropped-restoring |
restore-head-collateral-risk | untracked-present
```

**`selection-hazard` is not a member.** The analysis kept it in a nine-kind enum only because
§19.13 was open; §7.1 settles it as **blocking** in v1, so the kind is reachable exclusively as a
`blockers[]` row and a `refusal.kind` (rank 6). A warning of that kind is therefore unreachable,
and an unreachable member of a closed enum is a lie to a consumer switching exhaustively. Every
count, assertion and document that names the warning enum says **eight**.

`refusal` is `{kind, detail}` with `kind: null` when nothing refuses.

### 4.7 `null` semantics

Binding: `unknown ⇒ null`; a known empty set is `[]`; a known negative boolean is `false`; a known
zero count is `0`. An unknown fact MUST NOT be published as `[]`, `false` or `0`.

**Eighteen** arrays are always present and never `null`:

```text
entries[]  entries[].notes[]  blockers[]  warnings[]  encoding_issues[]  config_issues[]
route_triggers[]  repositories[]  fetch.repos[]  fetch.repos[].context_candidates[]
push.targets[]  push.blocked_by[]  restore.blocked_by[]  guard.evaluation[]
guard.limit_conflicts[]  guard.execute_blocked_by[]  approval.covers.waived_evaluation_ids[]
approval.covers.waived_kinds[]
```

**The count is eighteen, not seventeen, and the eighteenth member is the nested
`entries[].notes[]`.** §4.2 declares it `[]` when none — a row with no evaluator identity note
publishes a known-empty array, never `null` — so it satisfies this section's own membership test
exactly as the other nested members (`fetch.repos[].context_candidates[]`,
`approval.covers.waived_*[]`) do, and excluding it would have made the count a claim the schema
test could not verify against the document. Every count in this specification, in §22.33b and in
the §23 schema row says **eighteen**, and the schema test enumerates the eighteen paths above and
asserts each is present, is an array and is non-`null` in every fixture — including a row whose
notes are empty.

Nested arrays that are **not** members, and why: `replay.commits[]`, `collateral_refs[]` and
`summary.collateral_refs` are `null` for an unknown range/inventory (§4.2, §4.3);
`fetch_effect.remotes[]`, `submodule_recursion.submodules[]`,
`local_branch_destinations.branches[]`/`held[]`/`patterns[]` and `remotes[].refspecs[]` live under
objects that are themselves `null` when the effect could not be established (§11.4);
`argv[]`/`argv_alternatives` are `null` on `conditional`/`unknown` rows (§4.2). Each is governed by
its own table, and none may be silently promoted into the eighteen.

Declared exceptions: `branch_checked_out_at` is `null` both for "no holder found after a successful
inventory" and for "inventory failed" — the accompanying probe-failure blocker disambiguates it;
`restore.executable` is `null` in the three cells of §14.4 — `restore.applies: false`,
`summary.plannability: unavailable`, and an `applies: true` document whose target probe failed —
while `restore.blocked_by[]` stays `[]`; and `push.executable` is `null` in the two cells of §14.3 —
`intent.push: false` and `summary.plannability: unavailable` — while `push.blocked_by[]` stays
`[]`. In both `executable` cases the accompanying members disambiguate the `null`: `restore.applies`
and `restore.target_source: null` for the first, `intent.push` and `push.scope: none` for its push
twin, and `summary.plannability` for the shared unavailable cell. Publishing `false`
there would be an unknown dressed as a known negative.

### 4.8 Canonical ordering

Canonicalise the **document**; never make `TopoSort` or `UniqueRepos` deterministic — their map
order is unspecified between processes, and every refusal that would depend on it is decided over
an order-independent **set** instead.

| Array | Order |
|---|---|
| `entries[]` | logical `name` |
| `repositories[]` | `(repo, context_id)` |
| `config_issues[]` | `issue_id` bytewise, de-duplicated |
| `encoding_issues[]` | `(field_id, path_label_ascii, owner_entry [null first], sha256)`, de-duplicated |
| `blockers[]` | `(rank incl. sub-rank, entry [null first], sanitized detail)`, exact-tuple de-duplicated |
| `warnings[]` | `(kind, entry [null first], sanitized detail)`, exact-tuple de-duplicated |
| `guard.evaluation[]` | `id` bytewise |
| `guard.limit_conflicts[]` | `key` bytewise |
| `guard.execute_blocked_by[]`, `push.blocked_by[]`, `restore.blocked_by[]` | token sort, de-duplicated |
| `approval.covers.waived_*` | bytewise |
| `push.targets[]` | `(context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise)` |
| per-entry `collateral_refs` and `summary.collateral_refs` | `(repo, ref)` |
| `fetch.repos[]` | `(repo_token, context_root)` |
| `fetch.repos[].context_candidates[]` | `(context_root, context_source, first_entry)` |
| `fetch_effect.remotes[]` | `name` |
| `submodule_recursion.submodules[]` | bytewise `path` |
| `local_branch_destinations.branches[]` | bytewise |
| `local_branch_destinations.held[]` | `(branch, worktree, hold)` |
| `route_triggers[]` | **bytewise lexical** on the trigger name, de-duplicated |

**`push.targets[]` is totally ordered, `null` included (binding).** The row's `context_id` is
nullable (§4.4a, §14.1a rule 6), so the sort key is the pair `(context_id [null first], git_branch
bytewise)`: every row whose `context_id` is `null` precedes every row carrying an established
64-lower-hex id, `null`-id rows are ordered among themselves by `git_branch` bytewise, and
established ids are compared bytewise as the lower-hex strings they are. No comparison ever
substitutes `""` for an absent id — `""` is not a context id anywhere in this document or in any Go
carrier behind it (§14.1a) — and no arm may drop, coalesce or re-key a `null`-id row to make the
key non-null. The same order is the TLV array order of §8.2 and the order §22.33b/§22.33h assert.

**`route_triggers[]` is sorted bytewise, and the shipped source order is not an ordering rule
(binding).** The six trigger names are the members of `syncTriggerFlags`
(`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:31`), whose slice order — `fetch`, `no-fetch`, `full`, `local-only`,
`only`, `from` — is the **source order of §3.1** and is a *presence-scan* order, not a publication
order. The document publishes the names this invocation really supplied, **bytewise sorted**. At most
**three** can be supplied legally, one per axis, because I1–I3 refuse `--fetch --no-fetch`,
`--full --local-only` and `--only --from` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:58-66`), so the maximal cells
are triples: `--no-fetch --local-only --from x` publishes exactly
`["from", "local-only", "no-fetch"]` — the **reverse** of its slice order — and
`--fetch --full --only x` publishes `["fetch", "full", "only"]`. This is the single
rule; the earlier §4.1 phrase "sorted trigger names" and the earlier §4.8 phrase "trigger key order"
named two different orders for one array, and the second is **withdrawn** — no sentence, test or
skill may order this array by `syncTriggerFlags`'s slice position (§25.94). The shipped code already
prefers this order where it renders trigger names for a human: `syncChangedTriggerList`
(`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:143-152`) walks the slice and then `sort.Strings`es the `--`-prefixed
result, so the I8 sentence is bytewise too — that sentence is **shipped output and is not changed**
by this rule, which governs the JSON array only. The choice moves **no**
fingerprint: `route_triggers[]` is a closed non-member of the approval tuple (§8.3), so the two
orders would have produced the same 64-hex digest, which is exactly why the conflict could survive
this long and why it must be closed in the schema rather than in the fingerprint.

Sequences that MUST NOT be sorted: `replay.commits[]` (Git replay order, oldest-first),
`entries[].notes[]` (evaluator order, verbatim — §4.2), `remotes[].refspecs[]` (configured order),
`local_branch_destinations.patterns[]` (remote-name order, then that remote's configured refspec
order).
