## 5. Candidate semantics (§19.12 resolved)

1. A candidate range is `<replay.upstream_sha>..<git_branch>` with merges excluded. The plan
   publishes **candidates**, never **applied**. No field, message or document may state how many
   commits Git will apply, or which.
2. Merge commits are excluded only because the effective rebase mode drops them. Where the
   **effective merge backend** recreates merges — `rebase_merges.interpretation: true` **and**
   `effective_backend: merge` (§11.7) — the `--no-merges` bound is **withdrawn**: the row is
   `determinacy: unknown`, `reason: merge-recreation`, `candidate_count: null`. Under
   `effective_backend: apply` the apply backend drops merges whatever `rebase.rebaseMerges` says,
   so the bound holds and the row keeps its ordinary determinacy; with an unestablished backend the
   row is rank 2f `probe-failed` (§4.2), never an assumed arm.
3. Both executors pass an explicit upstream; fork-point heuristics MUST NOT widen the modelled
   range.
4. **Count probe** — `git -C <execution_context> rev-list --count --no-merges <upstream>..<branch>`.
5. **First-candidate probe** — for `N > 0`,
   `rev-list --skip=<N-1> --max-count=1 --no-merges --topo-order <upstream>..<branch>`; omitted for
   `N == 0`. `--reverse --max-count=1` MUST NOT be used: it returns the newest commit.
6. **List/digest probe** — exactly one stream,
   `git -C <execution_context> rev-list --reverse --topo-order --no-merges <upstream>..<branch>`,
   read to **EOF**. Retention is capped in process at **50**; the pipe is never closed early, so no
   `EPIPE`/`SIGPIPE` is produced. A second, count-derived `--skip`/`--max-count` window probe MUST
   NOT be issued: it cannot produce the digest and would cost a second full-stream hash.
7. **Rendering cap is exactly 50.** `replay.commits` retains the first 50 full SHAs oldest-first;
   `commits_listed` is that count; `commits_truncated` is derived from `candidate_count > 50` with
   no cap-plus-one probe.
8. **`replay.candidate_digest`** is SHA-256 over **every** candidate SHA of the complete uncapped
   oldest-first sequence, each followed by `\n`, rendered as 64 lowercase hex. A known-empty
   sequence yields the SHA-256 of zero bytes. It is `null` exactly when `replay.commits` is `null`.
   The cap is therefore a pure rendering choice that cannot move a token.
9. The fingerprint binds `replay.candidate_count` **and** the full `replay.candidate_digest`;
   `replay.commits[]` is an explicit non-member. `first_candidate` is bound indirectly by the
   digest, not as a separate member.
10. **Drop signalling.** `replay.may_drop_becomes_empty` is always `true` (Git's default
    `--empty=drop`; neither executor passes `-i`/`--exec`, and there is no `rebase.empty` key to
    probe). `replay.may_drop_patch_equivalent` is derived from the **arm and range**, never from a
    config key, via `git rev-list --count <git_branch>..<upstream>`: empty ⇒ `false`; non-empty ⇒
    `true`; deferred/unresolvable/unset/probe failure ⇒ `null`. It is recomputed at the JIT seam
    when the upstream resolves there. `rebase.reapplyCherryPicks` does not exist and MUST NOT be
    probed; only command-line `--reapply-cherry-picks` or `--keep-base` disables the preliminary
    filter, and neither executor passes either.
11. **Subject sanitation is exactly**: `ancestrySanitize(subject, 120)`
    (`internal/stack_ancestry.go:551-570`, limit `stackStatusSanitizeLimit`), applied to the
    single-line `%s` subject. Non-printable runes — including CR and LF — become `?`, and
    truncation appends `…`, so a subject is structurally one line. Branch, entry and ref names use
    the same limit; rendered repository roots use `ancestryPathLimit` (`200`). A subject MUST NOT
    be interpolated into any suggested command; suggested refs use `ancestryCommandToken`.

---

## 6. Human rendering

Under human `--plan` the document goes to stdout in exactly this block order. Operational prose,
the `Sync mode:` header and verbose child output go to stderr (§3.6).

```text
Plan: route=<legacy|new-mode> mode=<external|checkout> invocation=plan-only
Policy: fetch=<fetch|no-fetch> propagation=<full|local-only> scope=<scope-label>
Freshness: <freshness>
<entries block>
<head-after-run block>
<blockers block>
<warnings block>
<four-part tail>
```

The three framing lines, the head-after-run block, the blockers block and the warnings block are
fixed by this specification; they may never reorder, reword, omit or interleave the entry rows or
the four tail parts.

`<scope-label>` is the shipped `SyncRunPolicy.ScopeLabel()` value, byte for byte: `all`,
`only:<selector>` or `subtree:<selector>` (`internal/sync_selection.go:148-157`). There is **no**
separate ` selector=<name>` token, and the token `from` never appears — a `--from` run renders
`scope=subtree:<name>`, exactly as the shipped `Sync mode:` header already does. The two lines are
therefore consistent even though they land on different streams under `--plan`: the `Sync mode:`
header goes to stderr (§3.6) and this `Policy:` line goes to stdout, and both spell the scope with
the same shipped function. The JSON twin publishes the decomposed
`policy.scope_kind` ∈ `{all, one, subtree}` plus the separate nullable `policy.selector` (§4.1);
the human label is a rendering of that pair, never a second vocabulary.

### 6.1 Entries block — the bound two-line, eleven-field grammar

```text
Entries:
  - <name> [<git_branch>] base <configured> → <resolved>@<destination> cutoff <recorded> upstream <effective> strategy <strategy>
    candidates <count> range <range> first <first>
```

- Exactly one `Entries:` header; exactly two lines per row; canonical row order; exactly **eleven**
  fields. No field may be omitted or reordered. `→` is literal U+2192.
- Every displayed SHA is the first **12** lowercase hex characters of the `--json` twin's full SHA.
  Rendering MUST NOT spawn `rev-parse --short`.
- The header word is `candidates`; `applies` / `will be applied` MUST NOT appear.
- `--verbose` may add lines **below** a row; it may not alter either fixed line.
- An empty entry set renders exactly `Entries: none` with no row lines.

Total field spellings:

| Field | Normal | Fixed absent/unknown |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | sanitized `name` | never absent |
| `<git_branch>` | sanitized `git_branch` | never absent; printed even when equal to `<name>` |
| `<configured>` | sanitized `base.name` | `<none>` for `base.kind: none` |
| `<resolved>` | `base.ref` | `<unresolved>` when `base.ref` is `null` |
| `<destination>` | 12 chars of `destination.sha` | `post-rebase(<depends_on>)` when deferred; `<not-executed>` on every `skipped-*`; `<unresolved>` on a missing/unpeelable ref |
| `<recorded>` | 12 chars of `cutoff.recorded_sha` | `<none>` when absent; append ` (unresolvable)` for `cutoff.state: unresolvable`; append ` (unverified)` when `cutoff.state` is `null` |
| `<effective>` | 12 chars of `replay.upstream_sha` | `<not-executed>` on `skipped-*`; else `<unknown>` |
| `<strategy>` | the ASCII enum token | never absent (includes `unknown` and every `skipped-*`) |
| `<count>` | decimal `replay.candidate_count` | `<unknown>` when `null`; skip rows print `0` |
| `<range>` | `<first 12 chars of replay.upstream_sha>..<sanitized git_branch>`, **composed here** — never a copy of `replay.range`, which carries the full upstream SHA (§4.2) | `<none>` when `replay.range` is `null`, including every `skipped-*` |
| `<first>` | `<12-char sha> "<sanitized subject>"` | `<none>` for a known-empty range; `<unknown>` for an unknown range |

Required customer fixture (§6.4 of the analysis, `master = A-B'-D`, `pr2 = A-B-C`, cutoff `B`):

```text
# checkout — BuildCheckoutPlan resolves the base literally
Entries:
  - pr2 [feat/pr2] base master → master@<D-short> cutoff <B-short> upstream <B-short> strategy onto
    candidates 1 range <B-short>..feat/pr2 first <C-short> "C"

# external — `master` is this repository's default branch, so resolveBase rewrites it
Entries:
  - pr2 [feat/pr2] base master → origin/master@<D-short> cutoff <B-short> upstream <B-short> strategy onto
    candidates 1 range <B-short>..feat/pr2 first <C-short> "C"
```

The customer headline — new base `D`, old cutoff `B`, first candidate `C` — is therefore answered
on the **default** human rendering, not only under `--json`.

In both fixtures `<B-short>` is the first 12 hex characters of `B`, in **both** the `upstream` field
and the left half of `range`, while the JSON twin of the same run publishes
`replay.upstream_sha: "<full B>"` and `replay.range: "<full B>..feat/pr2"`. The customer fixture
tests assert exactly that pairing, so a `<range>` produced by copying `replay.range` fails them.

### 6.2 Head-after-run block (§19.19 resolved)

Exactly one document-level block, printed after the entries block and before the tail. A per-row
`will leave HEAD on …` line MUST NOT appear on the default rendering, because it would add a third
line to the bound row grammar; `--verbose` may add one below a row.

```text
HEAD after run: none
```

or

```text
HEAD after run:
  - <sanitized execution context root>: <git_branch>
```

One line per execution context that at least one row switches HEAD in, carrying the branch the last
switching row of that context leaves HEAD on, sorted bytewise by rendered context root. Checkout
rows contribute no line, because `mutation.head_restored_by_run` is `true` there.

### 6.2a Blockers block and warnings block (fixed, total, complete)

Exactly two document-level blocks, in this order, printed after the head-after-run block and
**before** the four-part tail. Both are total: a document always renders both, either as its
one-line "none" form or as a header followed by **every** row of the corresponding array. Neither
block is ever a count, a sample, a truncation, or an "and N more".

```text
Plan blockers: none
```

or

```text
Plan blockers:
  - <kind> [<entry>]: <sanitized detail>
```

```text
Plan warnings: none
```

or

```text
Plan warnings:
  - <kind> [<entry>]: <sanitized detail>
```

- `<kind>` is the row's ASCII enum token: a `blockers[].kind` (the closed §7.1 domain, including
  every sub-ranked kind) or a `warnings[].kind` (the closed eight-member domain of §4.6).
- `<entry>` is total: the sanitized logical entry name, or the literal `<document>` when
  `entry` is `null`. The square brackets are always present.
- `<sanitized detail>` is the row's `detail`, sanitized by §18.5 and structurally one physical
  line; a raw byte, a raw configuration value and a raw invalid-UTF-8 value never reach it.
- Row order is the canonical array order of §4.8 — `blockers[]` by
  `(rank incl. sub-rank, entry [null first], sanitized detail)` and `warnings[]` by
  `(kind, entry [null first], sanitized detail)` — so the highest-ranked blocker is first and the
  ordering matches the `--json` twin element for element.
- **Every row is printed.** `Refusal kind:` in the tail names only the single highest-precedence
  kind (§7.2); this block is the place where the non-top-ranked blockers are visible, and hiding
  them would leave an operator fixing one refusal at a time with no view of the rest.
- **Warnings are never hidden**, including on a `runnable: false` document, including when a
  refusal is being reported, and including on the default rendering without `--verbose`. A warning
  is a fact the operator is entitled to before authorizing a rebase.
- The two blocks carry no `blocking`/`runnable` claim of their own: `blockers[]` membership already
  means "effective and unwaived" (§7.2), and a waived limit row is not a blocker and does not
  appear here.

Both blocks belong to the human `--plan` document on **stdout**. They add no field to the JSON
twin: they are a rendering of `blockers[]` and `warnings[]`, which the JSON document already
publishes in the same order.

### 6.3 The four-part tail (fixed, byte-exact, always last)

The tail is the **last** thing the human document prints; the blockers and warnings blocks of §6.2a
precede it and never interleave with it.

```text
Plan runnable: yes|no
Guard would refuse: yes|no
Refusal kind: <kind>|none
Configuration issues: none
Guarded execution blockers: none
Approval fingerprint: <64-hex>|none
```

- Part 1 — the three labelled status lines, in that order. `Plan runnable:` maps `runnable`;
  `Guard would refuse:` maps the **post-waiver** `guard.would_refuse`; `Refusal kind:` prints
  `refusal.kind` or the literal `none`. Ordinary refusal prose stays above these lines.
- Part 2 — `Configuration issues:`. Either exactly `Configuration issues: none`, or the header
  alone followed by one line per `config_issues[]` row in `issue_id` order:

  ```text
    - <64-hex issue_id> <key> [<source>, <route_command>]: <value-field>
  ```

  `<value-field>` is total: `<valueless>` when `raw_value_present: false`, `""` for an explicitly
  empty sanitized value, otherwise the sanitized value. Every row is printed; never a count, never
  a sample, never a raw byte.
- Part 3 — `Guarded execution blockers:`. Either exactly `Guarded execution blockers: none`, or the
  header alone followed by every member of `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` in canonical order, one
  token per line and **nothing else**:

  ```text
    - <token>
  ```

  Two spaces, `- `, then the ASCII token. There is **no** ` : <detail>` suffix and no per-token
  prose, because `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` is a token-only array (§4.6): it carries no detail
  for the renderer to print, and composing one here would invent a fact the JSON twin does not
  have. The detailed evidence for every one of the five tokens is published elsewhere and is
  reachable from the same document — `state` (the live-owner and owner-artefact facts, §4.5),
  `fetch` (context candidates, submodule reach, local-branch destinations, §4.4a) and `blockers[]`
  (the ranked rows with their sanitized `detail`, rendered in full by §6.2a). Never a count, never
  a truncation, never "and N more".
- Part 4 — the always-present final stdout line `Approval fingerprint: <64-hex>` or
  `Approval fingerprint: none`. It is a line **containing** the token, never the token itself.
  Documentation MUST NOT teach piping `tail -1` into `--approve-plan`; extraction is explicit,
  e.g. `sed -n 's/^Approval fingerprint: //p'`.

**§19.25 resolved**: `external-rebase-in-progress` is *not* published as a per-row human marker.
It appears in the refusal detail of the blocking row and in `blockers[]`/`entries[].context.
rebase_in_progress` under `--json`; `--verbose` may add a line below the row. The fact never
migrates out of `blockers[]`.

### 6.4 Guarded-execution marker grammar (§19.16 resolved)

A guarded **executing** invocation emits no document and no token. On a guard-owned refusal it
exits `1` and writes exactly one line matching:

```text
^plan-guard: <kind>: <sanitized-detail>$
```

- `<kind>` is a closed `refusal.kind` token; `<sanitized-detail>` is one physical line.
- **The refusal travels as one typed, marker-free value.** Every guard and JIT seam — in both
  workspace modes — returns:

  ```go
  // internal/rebase_plan_guard.go — package internal
  type PlanGuardRefusalError struct {
      Kind           string // a closed refusal.kind token
      Detail         string // sanitized, one physical line, WITHOUT any prefix
      StatePreserved bool   // this invocation already rebased an entry or reclaimed a run guard
  }

  func (e *PlanGuardRefusalError) Error() string // "<kind>: [state-preserved: ]<detail>"
  ```

  `Error()` composes the `state-preserved: ` literal from `StatePreserved`, so the marker line and
  the returned error can never disagree about it. The type carries **no** `plan-guard: ` prefix in
  any field, so an error that escapes marker handling still cannot forge an anchored line.
- The marker is written **exactly once, by exactly one helper, in package `cli`**:

  ```go
  // internal/cli/sync_plan_guard.go
  func writePlanGuardMarker(w io.Writer, e *internal.PlanGuardRefusalError) {
      fmt.Fprintf(w, "plan-guard: %s\n", e.Error())
  }

  // planGuardRefusal writes the marker for a typed refusal and returns the
  // marker-free error to RunE. Any other error is returned unchanged.
  func planGuardRefusal(cmd *cobra.Command, err error) error
  ```

  `planGuardRefusal` uses `errors.As`, writes through `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` — never `os.Stderr` —
  and returns `err` itself, whose `Error()` is the same sentence without the prefix, so the
  production re-print in `internal/cli/root.go:53-56` cannot duplicate the marker. `cmd.SilenceUsage`
  is unchanged.
- **Both modes use that one helper and that one type.** Checkout's guard/JIT seams live in
  `internal` (`internal/checkout_sync.go`, via `internal/rebase_plan_guard.go`) and return
  `*internal.PlanGuardRefusalError` up through `RunCheckoutSync`/`ContinueCheckoutSync`;
  `runCheckoutSync` (`internal/cli/checkout_sync.go`) is the only place that renders it, by
  returning `planGuardRefusal(cmd, err)`. External seams live in package `cli` and construct the
  **same** `*internal.PlanGuardRefusalError`, returned up to `syncCmd`'s `RunE`, which likewise
  returns `planGuardRefusal(cmd, err)`. `internal` therefore imports no Cobra package and writes
  no marker byte.
- The marker may appear at any stderr position; it is not required to be first. Uncontrolled Git
  and Cobra passthrough is explicitly outside the guarantee, so consumers parse only the anchored
  guard-authored line.
- `detail` is sanitized: control characters replaced, CR and LF escaped, and any leading
  `plan-guard: ` ambiguity neutralised so an attacker-controlled subject or branch name cannot open
  a second anchored line.
- Example: `plan-guard: limit-per-entry: pr2 replays 40 candidates (limit 10)`.

**Post-mutation detail prefix.** When this invocation has already rebased at least one entry, **or**
has reclaimed an interrupted run guard, **or** created runtime state it then failed to remove
(§12.2c rule 4), the seam sets `StatePreserved: true`, which makes the rendered detail begin with
the exact **seventeen**-byte literal `state-preserved: ` — fifteen bytes of word, one colon and
**one trailing space** before the sentence proper. The three triggers share one meaning: *something on disk outlives this
refusal and the operator must be told what*. A post-claim refusal whose cleanup **succeeded** is
not one of them: it sets `StatePreserved: false`, because nothing survives.

`Detail` itself never carries the literal — composing it in exactly one place (`Error()`) is what
makes the marker line and the returned error identical modulo the prefix. `Detail` MUST end with
the resume workflow. Example:

```text
plan-guard: revalidation-mismatch: state-preserved: pr2 base moved (approved <sha>, now <sha>); continue with --plan --continue
```

A pre-mutation refusal sets `StatePreserved: false`, MUST NOT suggest `--continue`, and on a
continuation MUST state explicitly that the interrupted recovery state is untouched.

**Marker by origin, never by rank.** The marker is emitted for guard-seam verdicts, guard-owned
ranks 6–12, JIT `revalidation-mismatch`, a JIT-newly-exceeded limit, the legacy external
`plan-unavailable` interception, the `switched`-stage HEAD-identity preflight of §13.3a (a
guard-introduced rank 4 `preflight-refused`, which no shipped code performs), and guard-introduced
`repo-unavailable`, `probe-failed`, `branch-checked-out-elsewhere`, `context-dirty`,
`restore-blocked`, `fetch-context-indeterminate` and live-owner concurrency. It is **never** emitted
for a shipped pre-seam ladder refusal, a shipped continuation gate, I19/I20/dirty/detached/
Git-operation refusals, `BuildCheckoutPlan` head/base failures, **the §12.2d step 2a sort/stack-load
refusal, whose sentence is its own arm's shipped one**, `ReclaimSyncRunGuard`,
`ClaimSyncRunGuard`, `AcquireCheckoutLock`, `forceAcquireCheckoutLock`, or
`staleStackEdgesFiltered`. Those keep their shipped bytes.

**The completion gate is a shipped *post-mutation* refusal, and its guidance says so.**
`staleStackEdgesFiltered` (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:220-226`) runs **after** every selected
rebase of the run, and its failure arm is `syncFailure(...)`, which persists the run's recovery
state (legacy `.sync-state.yaml`, or the payload on a payload-carrying run) and exits `1` with the
shipped `Sync incomplete; stale stack edges remain:` block. Nothing about that changes here: the
gate keeps its position, its predicate, its bytes and its persistence on every route, guarded or
not, and it is marker-free. What is binding is the honesty rule around it — because it fires after
branches have already moved, every sentence, document field, skill and doc line that describes it
MUST use post-mutation guidance (inspect, `--continue`, `--abort`) and MUST NOT imply that nothing
happened. If a guard-owned refusal is ever raised in that same post-mutation position, it carries
`StatePreserved: true` and therefore the `state-preserved: ` prefix, by the rule above.

---

## 7. Refusal precedence and blocker collapse

### 7.1 Ordered precedence table (closed; no kind outside it)

| Rank | `refusal.kind` | Fact | Hard blocker | Waivable | Forces `runnable: false` |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `plan-unavailable` | stack cannot be read | yes | no | yes |
| 1 | `stack-unsortable` | stack cannot be sorted (`cycle detected in stack.yaml`) | yes | no | yes |
| 2 | `selection-refused` | participants cannot be determined | yes | no | yes |
| 3 | `state-refused` | state/transaction/lock/live guard/dirty tree/detached HEAD/Git operation/native acquisition/continuation gate refuses | yes | no | yes |
| 4 | `preflight-refused` | I19 containment, wrong worktree, the external completion gate **on a rows-less push-only continuation only** (rank-4 rule below), checkout `switched`-stage HEAD identity (§13.3a), checkout `rebased`-stage ancestry (§13.7 gate e) | yes | no | yes |
| 4.5 | `restore-blocked` | checkout restore target missing/held, or recorded original HEAD moved | yes | no | yes |
| 5.0 | `fetch-context-indeterminate` | ≥2 candidate contexts differ or cannot be shown equal | yes | no | yes |
| 5.05 | `fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate` | unconditional recursion with unbounded/unknown reach | yes | no | yes |
| 5.06 | `fetch-local-branch-checked-out` | covering positive `refs/heads/**` refspec meets held/unknown destinations | yes | no | yes |
| 5.07 | `invalid-git-config` | route-applicable config value fatal to the command Git will run | yes | no | yes |
| 5.08 | `identity-not-utf8` | bound identity bytes are invalid UTF-8 on a document that would mint or was given a token | yes when emitted | no | yes when emitted |
| 5.1 | `repo-unavailable` | base or execution context cannot be established | yes | no | yes |
| 5.15 | `base-execution-store-divergent` | external base/execution contexts resolve to different common stores | yes | no | yes |
| 5.2 | `head-ref-missing` | row head absent/unpeelable | yes | no | yes |
| 5.3 | `prunable-worktree` | external materialization is `prunable` | yes | no | yes |
| 5.4 | `branch-checked-out-elsewhere` | a planned switch is held by a foreign worktree | yes | no | yes |
| 5.45 | `external-rebase-in-progress` | this row's external execution directory already has a rebase | yes | no | yes |
| 5.5 | `context-dirty` | tracked-dirty context whose arm's next command is a `git rebase` with no applicable autostash — external pass 1/pass 2 and the checkout continuation arms of §13.3b | yes | no | yes |
| 5.6 | `base-unset` | external `base.kind: none` | yes | no | yes |
| 5.7 | `base-ref-missing` | base ref cannot resolve | yes | no | yes |
| 5.8 | `cutoff-unresolvable` | recorded cutoff cannot resolve | yes | no | yes |
| 5.9 | `probe-failed` | replay-critical probe fails without a more specific owner | yes | no | yes |
| 6 | `selection-hazard` | duplicate `GitBranch`, or legacy checkout cross-repo structural hazard | **yes (v1)** | no | **yes (v1)** |
| 7 | `guard-limit-mismatch` | a continuation supplies a limit different from the persisted one | no | no | no |
| 7.5 | `approval-without-limits` | continuation approval with both effective limits absent | no | no | no |
| 8 | `approval-mismatch` | a usable fingerprint exists and the supplied token does not authorize it | no | no | no |
| 9 | `revalidation-mismatch` | matched token, then JIT drift | no | no | no |
| 10 | `indeterminate-entry` | the guard cannot compare a required unknown under the active policy | no | no | no |
| 11 | `limit-per-entry` | effective per-entry limit exceeded and unwaived | no | **yes** | no |
| 12 | `limit-total` | effective aggregate limit exceeded and unwaived | no | **yes** | no |

Rank-specific rules:

- Rank 1: `plan-unavailable` wins if both rank-1 facts were ever recorded.
- Rank 3: live foreign owner and undecodable owner artefact are the controlled-path facts of
  `guard.execute_blocked_by[]`. **A controlled-path fact contributes a rank 3 `blockers[]` row
  exactly where the *described* route's own ladder refuses on it** — a fresh checkout run meeting a
  live foreign `.checkout-sync.lock`, a new-mode external run meeting a live guard — and there it
  sets `runnable: false` like any other rank 3. Where the described route never consults the
  artefact (§12.5's two `owner-artefact-undecodable` cells, whose native ladders read *through* the
  symlink and would not refuse a decodable target), the plan document publishes the fact as
  `state.files.*` evidence plus the `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` token and **no** blocker row, no
  `refusal.kind` and no change to `runnable`; the rank 3 refusal then exists only on the guarded
  route, where the seam is the refusing party (§4.6, §12.5, §22.13m).
- Rank 4: the shipped members (I19 containment, wrong worktree) keep their shipped sentences and
  are marker-free. The **guard-introduced** member is the `switched`-stage HEAD-identity preflight
  of §13.3a — reachable only on the plan and guarded routes, row-scoped to the transaction's
  current entry, and marker-carrying (§6.4). The **shipped** checkout member is the
  `rebased`-stage ancestry gate of §13.7 gate e: its sentence
  (`%s not descended from %s after rebase`) is the shipped one, it is **document-level**
  (`entry: null`) because §13.3's stage table publishes no row for that index, and it is
  **marker-free on the executing route**, where the shipped gate — not the guard — is the refusing
  party and really persists `FailureKind: ancestry` (§13.7 rule 8a (ii), §12.7).
- **Rank 4 carries one postcondition and one precondition, and they are distinct.** The external
  completion gate below is a **postcondition** of the external executor, projected in exactly one
  cell; the checkout `rebased`-stage ancestry gate is a **precondition** of the described checkout
  resume, projected on every `rebased`-stage continuation. They are mode-disjoint and
  cell-disjoint, share no sentence, and neither may be derived from the other; §13.5's
  five-row table is the complete account of the checkout continuation/finalization ancestry facts
  defined here; external continuation and per-entry executor ancestry checks remain specified in
  their owning sections,
  and its fifth row — the checkout whole-plan finalization postcondition
  (`final ancestry check failed: %s not descendant of %s`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:1191-1200`) —
  is deliberately **outside this table**: it is executing-only, carries no rank, no
  `refusal.kind` and no `blockers[]` row, and never moves `runnable` (§13.5 rule F).
- **Rank 4, external completion gate: it is a postcondition, not a precondition, and it is a
  rank-4 blocker in exactly one cell.** `staleStackEdgesFiltered` is evaluated by the shipped
  executor **after** its rebases (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:220-226`), so on a fresh run and on
  any continuation that still has rebase rows, a *currently* stale edge is **the work this run is
  about to do**, not a reason to refuse it. Binding consequences:
  1. A stale current edge on a row this invocation will rebase MUST NOT produce a blocker of any
     rank, MUST NOT set `runnable: false`, and MUST NOT suppress the header or the fetch. It is
     published as **fact** — the row's `ancestry` (`StackEdge.Status`/`Reason`, §4.2) — and
     nothing more.
  2. The **only** cell where the gate is evaluated as a precondition is a continuation whose
     remaining set contains **no rebase row at all** and whose remaining work is the push (and,
     checkout-only, the restore) — the rows-less push-only continuation of §13.3. There, no rebase
     this invocation performs can change the answer, and the shipped executor really does evaluate
     the gate before it reaches the push, so the plan projects it as rank 4 `preflight-refused`
     with the shipped sentences (`Sync incomplete; stale stack edges remain:` plus
     `  [!] %s does not contain parent %s` per edge), `runnable: false`, and
     `push.blocked_by[]` carrying `preflight-refused` by the §14.3 control-flow projection.
  3. On every other route the gate is neither projected nor pre-evaluated, and the executing route
     keeps it exactly where it ships — post-rebase, marker-free, persisting recovery state through
     `syncFailure` and exiting `1` (§6.4, §13.5).
  Any earlier text that listed the completion gate among the external plan route's **pre-fetch**
  gates, or among `blockers[]` on a run with rebase rows, is **withdrawn** (§13.5, §13.7a, §25.24).
- Rank 4.5: checkout-only, document-level (`entry: null`).
- Rank 5.05: never applies to an `on-demand` context — that fetch proceeds with
  `unknown-fetch-effect`.
- Rank 5.06: unknown `held[]`/`branches[]` inventory is fail-closed and included.
- Rank 5.07: applies only where the described route really hands the key to Git; a `--plan` is a
  projection wrapper, never an out-of-scope route.
- Rank 5.08: a limitless plan with invalid bound identity publishes `encoding_issues[]`, mints no
  token, emits **no** rank 5.08 blocker and stays runnable.
- Rank 5.15: external-only; a same-store split is the warning `base-execution-context-split`.
- Rank 5.5: external pass 1/pass 2, **plus** every checkout continuation arm whose next command is
  a `git rebase` (§13.3b) where no autostash applies. The non-blocking `checkout-dirty-present`
  warning covers the *other* checkout continuation hazard — a standalone `git checkout` whose
  success depends on an overlap the plan cannot decide — and the two may legitimately appear on the
  same row. A **fresh** checkout run never reaches either: the shipped whole-repo dirty gate is
  rank 3.
- Rank 5.9: also owns an unparseable or unobtainable `git --version` on a plan/guard path (§16) and
  a push context whose **mapping half** could not be read (`MappingReadOK: false`, §14.1a rule 5a),
  both document-level, `entry: null`. The push cell emits **one** row per affected context, ordered
  and de-duplicated by `context_id`, and its lease publishes `expectation: unknown` rather than the
  null-OID `absent` (§14.2). An unreadable remote-tracking **inventory** is deliberately *not* a
  member: the mapping is known there, and Git evaluates that compare-and-swap itself
  (§14.1a rule 5).
- **Rank 6 (§19.13 resolved): v1 ships the blocking rendering.** `selection-hazard` sits in
  `blockers[]`, forces `runnable: false`, becomes `refusal.kind` absent a higher-ranked blocker,
  and refuses guarded legacy execution. Its membership in `push.blocked_by[]` follows the
  unreachability predicate, not a copy of `blockers[]`. The legacy plan still publishes rows and
  the exact `--only` remedy in its detail; adding a trigger turns the same stack into the shipped
  rank 2 `selection-refused`.
- Ranks 11–12: a matching approval turns a covered `exceeded` verdict into `waived`; no blocker or
  refusal remains for a waived row.

### 7.2 Collapse

1. Keep every detected **effective, unwaived** blocker in `blockers[]`.
2. Ignore `guard.evaluation[].verdict == waived` rows for blocker and rank purposes.
3. `refusal.kind` is the single highest-precedence available kind.
4. Probe, discovery or map order MUST NOT affect the selected kind.
5. A matching approval never touches ranks 1–10.
6. `runnable` is independent of a guard-limit refusal: `refusal.kind: limit-per-entry` may coexist
   with `runnable: true`.
7. A rows-less document that is handed a token keeps its **own** top-ranked `refusal.kind`; it
   never reports `approval-mismatch` (there is no fingerprint to mismatch).
8. **One function implements rules 1–7, and it is named `SelectPrimaryRefusal`:**

   ```go
   // internal/rebase_planner.go — package internal
   func SelectPrimaryRefusal(blockers []PlanBlocker) (kind RefusalKind, ordered []PlanBlocker)
   ```

   It returns the selected `refusal.kind` (the zero `RefusalKind` — encoded `null` — when nothing
   refuses) together with the §4.8-ordered, de-duplicated `blockers[]` slice the document and the
   human renderer publish. The JSON encoder, the human renderer and the guarded stderr refusal all
   call **this** function; none re-implements the precedence. Two naming rules are binding because
   both were violated in an earlier revision: the function is **not** called `RefusalKind`, which
   is the closed enum *type* of §7.5 declared in the same package (`internal/rebase_plan.go`), and
   its parameter and result element type is **`PlanBlocker`** (§19.1) — there is no type named
   `Blocker` in this specification, and introducing one is forbidden.

### 7.3 `runnable`

`runnable` means "a rank 1–5 fact — or rank 6 under its v1 blocking rendering — stops the described
run". It is never moved by a guard verdict, a limit, or an approval. It is likewise never moved by
a fact the described run **exists to fix**: a stale or divergent current ancestry on a row this
invocation will rebase is published as the row's `ancestry` and leaves `runnable: true` (§7.1
rank-4 completion-gate rule).

**The rule is total, and it is the same rule for a document with rows and for one without.**
`runnable` is `true` **iff** the document carries **no** effective, unwaived blocker whose rank is
1, 2, 3, 4, 4.5, or any sub-rank of 5, and **no** rank 6 `selection-hazard`; ranks 7–12 are
excluded by construction (§7.1's last column) and a `verdict: waived` row contributes nothing
(§7.2 rule 2). A **rows-less** document is not a special case of this rule and has no enumeration
of its own: it simply has no row-scoped blockers, so the same predicate is evaluated over its
document-level (`entry: null`) facts plus any fact a projected arm attributes to an entry it
publishes no row for. Any statement that lists "the ranks a rows-less document can reach" is
descriptive, never normative, and where one has been read as a closed list it is **withdrawn**
(§4.3).

### 7.4 Restore hazard loudness (§19.20 resolved)

On a **fresh** checkout run the `OriginalHEAD` consistency rule cannot yet be violated, but the
conditions that would violate it are visible: the restore target lies outside `tx.Plan` and inside
the projected collateral **upper bound** under `rebase.updateRefs`. v1 publishes exactly the
`restore-head-collateral-risk` **warning** with `runnable: true`. Blocking on an upper bound would
refuse runs that succeed. The three probed cells — `restore-target-missing`,
`restore-target-held`, `restore-head-moved` — are rank 4.5 `restore-blocked`, non-waivable, on
**both** arms. This sentence fixes their **rank**, never their scope: they are *evaluated* on every
`applies: true` document **whose route really calls `restoreOriginal`**, fresh and continuation
alike — and on no `completed`-stage document, which calls only `finalizeCleanup` and runs no
`git checkout` (§14.4) — and §14.4's probe-scope table gives the
values each arm can reach — on a fresh run `restore-head-moved` is a known `false`, because no
`OriginalHEAD` is persisted yet, which is exactly why the collateral hazard above is published as a
warning instead of being smuggled into that token.

### 7.5 `push.blocked_by[]` and `restore.blocked_by[]` — one closed compositional domain

Both arrays are token lists, and neither is a free-text channel. Their domains are **composed**
from the closed §7.1 enum plus a small, explicitly enumerated set of surface-specific tokens, and
membership in a given document is decided by **control flow**, never by copying `blockers[]` and
never by inventing a string:

```go
// internal/rebase_plan.go — package internal

// RefusalKind is the closed §7.1 enum, in rank order. RefusalKinds is the
// complete ordered slice; a schema test asserts len(RefusalKinds) == 30 and
// that it equals the §7.1 table row for row.
type RefusalKind string

const (
    RefusalPlanUnavailable             RefusalKind = "plan-unavailable"
    RefusalStackUnsortable             RefusalKind = "stack-unsortable"
    RefusalSelectionRefused            RefusalKind = "selection-refused"
    RefusalStateRefused                RefusalKind = "state-refused"
    RefusalPreflightRefused            RefusalKind = "preflight-refused"
    RefusalRestoreBlocked              RefusalKind = "restore-blocked"
    RefusalFetchContextIndeterminate   RefusalKind = "fetch-context-indeterminate"
    RefusalFetchSubmoduleReach         RefusalKind = "fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate"
    RefusalFetchLocalBranchCheckedOut  RefusalKind = "fetch-local-branch-checked-out"
    RefusalInvalidGitConfig            RefusalKind = "invalid-git-config"
    RefusalIdentityNotUTF8             RefusalKind = "identity-not-utf8"
    RefusalRepoUnavailable             RefusalKind = "repo-unavailable"
    RefusalBaseExecutionStoreDivergent RefusalKind = "base-execution-store-divergent"
    RefusalHeadRefMissing              RefusalKind = "head-ref-missing"
    RefusalPrunableWorktree            RefusalKind = "prunable-worktree"
    RefusalBranchCheckedOutElsewhere   RefusalKind = "branch-checked-out-elsewhere"
    RefusalExternalRebaseInProgress    RefusalKind = "external-rebase-in-progress"
    RefusalContextDirty                RefusalKind = "context-dirty"
    RefusalBaseUnset                   RefusalKind = "base-unset"
    RefusalBaseRefMissing              RefusalKind = "base-ref-missing"
    RefusalCutoffUnresolvable          RefusalKind = "cutoff-unresolvable"
    RefusalProbeFailed                 RefusalKind = "probe-failed"
    RefusalSelectionHazard             RefusalKind = "selection-hazard"
    RefusalGuardLimitMismatch          RefusalKind = "guard-limit-mismatch"
    RefusalApprovalWithoutLimits       RefusalKind = "approval-without-limits"
    RefusalApprovalMismatch            RefusalKind = "approval-mismatch"
    RefusalRevalidationMismatch        RefusalKind = "revalidation-mismatch"
    RefusalIndeterminateEntry          RefusalKind = "indeterminate-entry"
    RefusalLimitPerEntry               RefusalKind = "limit-per-entry"
    RefusalLimitTotal                  RefusalKind = "limit-total"
)

// PushBlockedKind = RefusalKind ∪ {push-dropped-restoring}. The push-only
// member is NOT a RefusalKind: it is the warning kind of §4.6.
type PushBlockedKind string

const PushBlockedDroppedRestoring PushBlockedKind = "push-dropped-restoring"

func PushBlockedFromRefusal(k RefusalKind) PushBlockedKind

// RestoreBlockedKind = RefusalKind ∪ the three probed restore cells of §7.4.
// push-dropped-restoring is NOT a member (§14.4).
type RestoreBlockedKind string

const (
    RestoreBlockedTargetMissing RestoreBlockedKind = "restore-target-missing"
    RestoreBlockedTargetHeld    RestoreBlockedKind = "restore-target-held"
    RestoreBlockedHeadMoved     RestoreBlockedKind = "restore-head-moved"
)

func RestoreBlockedFromRefusal(k RefusalKind) RestoreBlockedKind
```

Binding membership rules:

1. **`push.blocked_by[]`** = every `RefusalKind` that is *effective and unwaived in this document*
   **and** would stop the corresponding controlled invocation **before it reaches the push**, plus
   `push-dropped-restoring` when the shipped `restoring` arm drops a push the run really intended —
   the checkout `restoring` stage **conjoined with** a persisted `intent.push: true` (§13.3).
   "Stops it
   before the push" is answered by the §14.3 projection of the real control flow
   (`pushFeature`/`pushScoped`/the transaction arm), never by rank and never by `blockers[]`
   membership. A waived limit row contributes nothing; an unwaived rank 11/12 refusal that really
   stops the run before the push does contribute.
2. **`restore.blocked_by[]`** = every `RefusalKind` that stops or fails the restore in that same
   control-flow sense, plus exactly `restore-target-missing`, `restore-target-held` and
   `restore-head-moved`. `push-dropped-restoring` is **explicitly excluded**: a dropped push is a
   *consequence* of restoring, never a reason the restore itself cannot run.
3. Both arrays are token-sorted and de-duplicated (§4.8), are `[]` — never `null` — when nothing
   blocks or the answer is unknown, and are fingerprint non-members (§8.3).
4. A token that is neither a §7.1 member nor a declared surface-specific member is a **bug, not an
   extension**: the encoders take the typed values above, so an arbitrary string cannot reach
   either array without a change to this section, to §4.4a/§14 and to the schema tests together.

**Three token domains, four types, one enum.** `RefusalKind` is the closed §7.1 enum;
`PushBlockedKind` and `RestoreBlockedKind` are the two composed surface domains above; and
`ControlledPathBlocker` (§4.6) is a **fourth, independent** type for `guard.execute_blocked_by[]`.
None of the four is an alias of another, no conversion between them is implicit, and
`ControlledPathBlocker` is never produced by `PushBlockedFromRefusal`/`RestoreBlockedFromRefusal`:
its five constants are written literally by the controlled-path code that observes them.

**Schema tests (§23).** The domains are asserted from both directions: every token an emitted
document carries parses back into `PushBlockedKind`/`RestoreBlockedKind`, and the *declared* domain
equals `RefusalKinds` plus exactly one (push) / exactly three (restore) extra members —
`len(pushDomain) == 31`, `len(restoreDomain) == 33` — with `push-dropped-restoring` asserted absent
from the restore domain and each restore-specific token asserted absent from the push domain.
`ControlledPathBlockers` is asserted at exactly **five** members, equal to the §4.6 list in sorted
order, with `invalid-git-config` and `identity-not-utf8` asserted **absent** from it and present in
`RefusalKinds`, and with every emitted `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` token parsing back into the
type (§22.33d).
Fixtures cover at least one `RefusalKind`-derived member on each surface (a rank 3 `state-refused`
blocking both; a rank 4.5 `restore-blocked` continuation cell), the `restoring`-stage document with
a persisted `intent.push: true` that carries `push-dropped-restoring` with
`restore.blocked_by: []`, and its **`intent.push: false` twin**, asserted to carry the token in
neither array, no `push-dropped-restoring` warning, `push.executable: null` and
`restore.push_dropped: false`.

## 8. Fingerprint, TLV tuple, and approval semantics

### 8.1 Domain

`approval.fingerprint` is the SHA-256, rendered as 64 lowercase hex, of a **canonical invariant
tuple projected from the canonical document** — never of the rendered document, never of the JSON
bytes, and never of a hand-rolled string join. `--plan` and `--plan --approve-plan` therefore
publish the same token, and a guarded execution's planner computes the same value.

Pre-image framing (fixed):

```text
"tws-plan-fp\0" || encoding_version 0x0001 || tuple_schema_version 0x0004 || <STRUCT>
```

The document's `schema_version` is **not** the tuple schema version and is not bound.

### 8.2 TLV encoding

Typed, length-prefixed, raw-byte TLV:

| Tag | Type |
|---|---|
| `0x00` | `NULL` |
| `0x01` | `BOOL` |
| `0x02` | `UINT` |
| `0x03` | `BYTES` |
| `0x04` | `STRUCT` |
| `0x05` | `ARRAY` |

- Struct members carry fixed 2-byte ids, are emitted in ascending id order, exactly once each.
  An absent or unknown member is `NULL`, **never** omission.
- Arrays are emitted in the canonical order of §4.8 (entries by name, push targets by
  `(context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise)`, repositories by `(repo, context_id)`,
  collateral by `(repo, ref)`).
- `NULL`, `BOOL false`, `UINT 0`, empty `BYTES` and empty `ARRAY` MUST encode distinctly.
- `BYTES` binds **raw** bytes: no UTF-8 replacement, no Unicode normalisation, no trimming, no
  case folding, no escaping. A ref name Git accepts and UTF-8 does not is bound as the bytes it is.
- Rendered `repo_root` values MUST NOT appear as standalone tuple bytes — **including
  `workspace.repo_root`**; identity travels through `context_id` and through the workspace's own
  `mode`/`stable_id`.
- The per-entry identity binds `execution_context.context_id` at field id **4** and
  `base_context.context_id` at field id **36**; the destination member is the **execution-context**
  SHA, beside a separate `base.decision_sha` at field id **38**; push targets are keyed and bound by
  `context_id`. **That key is nullable, and the nullable case is bound, not skipped**: a target row
  whose `context_id` is `null` binds `NULL` at that member — never empty `BYTES`, which the
  distinctness rule above keeps separate — keeps its place in the array under §4.8's null-first
  order, and binds all of its other tuple members normally. A `null` id is therefore a *bound* fact:
  two runs that differ only in whether a push context resolved produce different pre-images and
  different tokens.

### 8.3 Membership (§19.3: settled, exhaustive, unchanged)

The whitelist rule is binding: **anything not listed is excluded, including future schema
additions.** A future change to membership is a change to §8.2/§8.3, the §23 assertions **and** the
tuple schema version together, in one change — the three move as a unit; the successor version is
`0x0005`.

This specification makes exactly one membership change against the analysis's ratified list: the
rendered **`workspace.repo_root` is removed** (§25.4). It is a correction of an internal
contradiction, not a migration — §8.2 already forbids rendered roots as standalone tuple bytes, so
the analysis's list and its own encoding rule disagreed, and a display path that varies with a
symlink spelling, a `/private` prefix or a moved checkout would have moved a token that describes
the same run. Consequently:

- the tuple schema version **stays `0x0004`**: the corrected membership is what `0x0004` means, no
  binary has ever emitted a `0x0004` pre-image, and there is no consumer to migrate;
- the field id vacated by the removed member is **retired and never reused**, so a decoder that
  ever sees it can only be reading a foreign pre-image;
- workspace identity is bound by `workspace.mode` and `workspace.stable_id`, plus the raw-safe
  `context_id` digests already bound on every `entries[]` row (both contexts), every
  `repositories[]` row and every `push.targets[]` row, each of which is a length-framed raw-byte
  digest of a canonical root and common dir (§4.4). **No new member is added**: a separate
  workspace-identity digest would duplicate identity the action facts already carry. Were one ever
  required, it would be defined as a `context_id`-style raw digest and land together with the
  field-id table and the version bump, never alone.

Included, document level: `approval.scope`; `workspace.mode` and `workspace.stable_id`; `feature`;
the effective `route`; `policy.fetch`/`propagation`/`scope_kind`/`selector`;
`guard.limits.max_replay_per_entry.value` and `guard.limits.max_replay_total.value` (with `0`
distinguishable from absent); `intent.push`; the canonical `push.targets[]` with `repo`,
`context_id`, `git_branch`, `remote`, `ref`, `force`, `scope` and the lease
expectation/ref/SHA; `restore.applies`/`will_switch_head`/`target_branch`/`target_sha`/
`push_dropped`; `intent.validation.applies` and `intent.validation.command_digest`; the canonical
`repositories[]` with `repo`, `context_id` and each config slot's effective `{status, value}` plus
`rebase_merges.interpretation`; and the canonical `entries[]`.

Included, per entry: `name`, `git_branch`, `repo`, role, materialization; both context ids and both
context sources; `head.state` and `head.sha`; `base.name`, `base.ref`, `base.decision_sha`, the
destination SHA or deferred snapshot SHA; `cutoff.recorded_sha` and `cutoff.state`;
`destination.deferred` and `destination.depends_on`; `replay` determinacy, reason, upstream
provenance, upstream SHA, `candidate_count` and the full uncapped `candidate_digest`; `strategy`,
both `argv_alternatives` for a `conditional` row, and `effective_backend`; `mutation.
will_switch_head`/`will_leave_head_on`/`head_restored_by_run`; `context.dirty`,
`context.autostash`, `context.autostash_applies_to_this_arm`, `branch_checked_out_at`; and the
collateral mechanism, exposure, known/unknown state and each `{repo, ref, sha, stack_owned}` tuple.

Excluded (closed non-member table): `invocation`, `requested_route`, `route_triggers[]` — whose
**bytewise** order of §4.8 is therefore a schema rule and not a fingerprint one, and cannot move a
digest in either spelling (§25.94) — and every
policy-source label; `approval.fingerprint`/`supplied`/`accepted`/`usable`/`covers` in all eight of
its members; every guard verdict and evaluation row; `guard.execute_blocked_by[]`,
`guard.limit_conflicts[]`, each limit's `origin` label; `push.executable`, `push.blocked_by[]`,
**`push.scope`** (the projection-rule label; each bound target still carries its own `scope`),
`restore.executable`, `restore.blocked_by[]`; **`push.targets[].materialization`** (the row's
copy of a fact already bound per entry — binding it twice would move a token for one measurement,
and the tuple version stays `0x0004` because no member is added); `blockers[]`, `warnings[]`,
`refusal.*`, `runnable`;
`context.untracked_present`, `context.overwrite_risk`,
`context.autostash_reapply_may_conflict`; `intent.validation.source`/`stability`/
`guarded_stability`, `intent.push_source`, config source labels; the entire `state` object, PIDs and
timestamps; the entire `fetch` block including outcome, freshness and submodule-reach labels;
`config_issues[]`, `encoding_issues[]` and their ids; `summary.*`; `schema_version`;
`replay.commits[]`; **`workspace.repo_root`**, every other rendered `repo_root`, prose, ranges,
subjects, row order and display roots. The whole `fetch` block being excluded is total and
forward-binding: `fetch_effect.head_branch` (§11.4) and every other effect member added under this
schema version are non-members by that clause, so no fetch fact can move an approval token.

### 8.4 The usable-token predicate (three clauses, restated in full wherever it appears)

`approval.fingerprint` is non-`null` **iff all three** hold:

1. **Work**: `entries[]` is non-empty **or** `push.targets[]` is non-empty **or**
   `restore.applies == true`.
2. **Limits**: at least one effective replay limit is in force.
3. **Encoding**: `encoding_issues[] == []`.

Consequences: a rows-less push-stage continuation and a checkout `restoring` resume are approvable,
and so is a `completed`-stage resume, whose `restore.applies` is `true` under §14.4's lifecycle
definition even though it rebases nothing;
a **fresh** checkout run whose built plan is empty is not, because it returns at `len(plan) == 0`
before writing a transaction and publishes `restore.applies: false`; a `stack-unsortable` document
has no work and no token; a limitless plan is a complete, useful document that deliberately mints
nothing and says so through `approval.covers.requires_limits: true` beside `has_work: true` — it
can therefore never produce an `approval-mismatch` in any later invocation. Where no fingerprint
exists, `approval.fingerprint` is `null` whatever the refusal kind, and the human final line is
`Approval fingerprint: none`.

**These three clauses are the *only* inputs to `approval.usable`, and usability is not admission.**
A document may publish a usable token and still describe an invocation the guard will refuse: the
token says "these facts were approvable and are bound", the §4.6 admission predicate says "the
controlled path may run". The two diverge in exactly the cells where a non-`runnable` fact or a
`guard.execute_blocked_by[]` member exists beside real work and an effective limit — including the
`owner-artefact-undecodable` cell of §12.5, whose plan document is `runnable: true`, mints the
token and prints it, while the guarded twin refuses at its guard seam. No clause is added here to
suppress the token in those cells: suppression would hide the bound identity a later, unblocked
invocation legitimately reuses, and the predicate that admits execution already reads the array
(§4.6, §22.13m).

**Binding, stated as a negative because it is the failure mode:** a `guard.execute_blocked_by[]`
member, a `blockers[]` row of any rank, a `refusal.kind`, a `runnable: false` verdict and a
`guard.would_refuse: true` verdict are **not** inputs to `approval.fingerprint` or
`approval.usable`. There are exactly **three** unusable-token causes — no work, no effective limit,
non-UTF-8 bound identity — and no fourth is added by this or any later section. A document that
publishes `approval.fingerprint: null` or `approval.usable: false` *because* a controlled-path
token, a blocker or a refusal is present fails §22.13m (iii), and so does one that omits the human
tail's `Approval fingerprint: <64-hex>` line in that cell (§6.3 part 4).

### 8.5 What a matching approval waives — and what it never waives

Waives: exactly the `guard.evaluation[]` rows that were `verdict: exceeded` in the approved
document and are named by `approval.covers.waived_evaluation_ids[]`. Their verdict becomes
`waived`; the row is **not** deleted, and `limit`, `value` and `entry` are preserved. A legal
executing shape after a valid waiver is
`would_refuse_without_approval: true`, `would_refuse: false`, `refusal.kind: null`.

Never waives, under any token: every rank 1–10 fact. Explicitly including — `plan-unavailable`,
`stack-unsortable`, `selection-refused`, every rank 3 state/lock/guard/continuation gate,
`preflight-refused`, `restore-blocked`, all five `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` members,
`invalid-git-config`, `identity-not-utf8`, `repo-unavailable`, `base-execution-store-divergent`,
`head-ref-missing`, `prunable-worktree`, `branch-checked-out-elsewhere`,
`external-rebase-in-progress`, `context-dirty`, `base-unset`, `base-ref-missing`,
`cutoff-unresolvable`, `probe-failed`, `selection-hazard`, `guard-limit-mismatch`,
`approval-without-limits`, `approval-mismatch`, `revalidation-mismatch`, and rank 10
`indeterminate-entry` (a `merge-recreation` unknown is not a numeric excess, so no token can convert
it to `waived`). It also never waives indeterminacy newly **resolved** at the JIT seam into a real
excess, identity drift, collateral drift, validation drift, or a state/concurrency blocker.

### 8.6 Cross-invocation flag identity

```text
plan     : tws sync <f> --plan [--json] T L P V
execute  : tws sync <f>              T L P V --approve-plan <fp>
```

with `T` = trigger flags, `L` = limits, `P` = `--push` presence, `V` = `--test` (checkout only).
The executing invocation drops only `--plan`/`--json` and adds only `--approve-plan <fp>`. Changing
`T`, an effective `L` value, `P`, or validation identity yields `approval-mismatch`. A token minted
without `--push` never authorizes a push; a token minted for `--only pr2` never authorizes a bare
run. `--no-fetch` MUST NOT be added merely to stabilise a legacy round trip — it selects a different
route.

Required round trips:

```text
# legacy external route — the run a bare `tws sync <f>` performs
tws sync <f> --plan --json --max-replay-per-entry 10
tws sync <f> --approve-plan <fp> --max-replay-per-entry 10

# explicit new-mode no-fetch route — stable and fully local
tws sync <f> --plan --no-fetch --json --max-replay-per-entry 10
tws sync <f> --no-fetch --approve-plan <fp> --max-replay-per-entry 10
```

**Every published workflow carries an effective limit on both lines, and no workflow anywhere in
this specification, in the documentation of §20, or in a skill may show a `--plan` that mints a
token without one.** A limitless `--plan` is a legal, useful document, but it publishes
`approval.fingerprint: null` (§8.4 clause 2), so a workflow that pairs it with `--approve-plan`
would teach a round trip whose second line REFUSEs at §3.3 step 3. The limit repeats on the
executing line because it is part of the bound identity `L` (§8.6) — dropping it changes the plan
and yields `approval-mismatch`, and on the legacy external route it is additionally the only way
that route's guard exists at all before its envelope is written (§13.6).

A fetch-enabled verification is **another fetch**: an `approval-mismatch` at step 2 or 3 normally
means plan drift, and the remedy is a fresh receipt, never `--no-fetch`. No round trip may be
described as atomic.

Token provenance: only a `--plan` document — the human final line or the `--json` field — is a
token source. An executing invocation, successful or refused, never emits a token. No persisted
state ever stores a token.

## 9. Shared planner architecture

### 9.0 The layout boundary — `internal` never learns a `cli` type (§25.10)

`externalSyncLayout` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:174-184`) and `resolveExternalSyncLayout`
(`:186-208`) are **unexported members of package `cli` and stay there**: they are not relocated,
not exported, not duplicated, and package `internal` MUST NOT import package `cli` (the dependency
would also be a cycle). The shared planner therefore takes a **neutral, `internal`-owned request
type**, which package `cli` constructs *after* its own `resolveExternalSyncLayout` call:

```go
// internal/rebase_plan.go — package internal
type RebasePlanLayout struct {
    FeaturePath   string // the feature's metadata directory
    WorktreesRoot string // "" in checkout mode — no linked worktrees exist there
    RepoRoot      string // checkout: the single physical checkout; external: "" unless a pass-2
                         // process-cwd context applies, which the planner measures itself
}

// WorktreePath mirrors externalSyncLayout.WorktreePath exactly and returns ""
// when WorktreesRoot is empty, so a checkout layout can never invent a path.
func (l RebasePlanLayout) WorktreePath(name string) string
```

```go
// internal/cli/sync_plan_guard.go — the single construction site for external runs
func planLayout(layout externalSyncLayout) internal.RebasePlanLayout {
    return internal.RebasePlanLayout{FeaturePath: layout.FeaturePath, WorktreesRoot: layout.WorktreesRoot}
}
```

Binding rules:

1. **Every** shared planner signature that needs a layout takes `RebasePlanLayout` — never
   `externalSyncLayout`, never `interface{}`, never a pair of loose strings. That covers exactly
   `EntryContexts`, `ResolveSyncBase`, `ExecutionOrder`, `RemainingRebaseEntries`,
   `ResolvePushContext`, `PushTargets` (through `PlanPushRequest.Layout`, §14.1a),
   `BuildRebasePlan` and `RevalidatePlanEntry` — the functions an **external** planner call reaches
   with paths it must not invent.
1a. **`BuildCheckoutRebasePlan` is not on that list, and it never takes a layout.** It is exactly
   `BuildCheckoutRebasePlan(insp CheckoutPlanInspection, fetched PlanFetchOutcome,
   push PlanPushFacts) (RebasePlan, error)`, and its continuation twin is
   `BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan(insp CheckoutPlanInspection, push PlanPushFacts)
   (RebasePlan, error)` (§13.7): the
   inspection already carries the invocation's `CheckoutSyncOpts` (`FeaturePath`, `RepoDir`), its
   stack, its selection, its transaction and its projected gates, so the builder constructs the
   layout itself per rule 2 and a caller-supplied `RebasePlanLayout` — or a second, separate
   `CheckoutSyncOpts` argument — would be a contradictable duplicate of what `insp` already holds.
   The **two** value parameters beside it are exactly the facts the inspection cannot hold, because
   both are measured *after* it returns: the outcome of the route's own fetch, and the push facts
   whose baseline half `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` re-read after that fetch (§14.1a rule 7). Passing
   `insp.PushFacts` — the `pre-fetch` value — in that position is a defect the builder's own
   `Phase` assertion catches.
   The same holds for `PlanCheckoutRebase(w PlanWriters, opts CheckoutSyncOpts,
   containment PlanGateResult)`, whose two value parameters are the only inputs `cli` owns. Only
   the external planner entry points above take a `RebasePlanLayout`, because only `cli` owns
   `resolveExternalSyncLayout`'s result.
2. **The checkout arm constructs its own layout inside `internal`, from whatever it already has.**
   A checkout entry point carrying `CheckoutSyncOpts` builds
   `RebasePlanLayout{FeaturePath: opts.FeaturePath, WorktreesRoot: "", RepoRoot: opts.RepoDir}`.
   **`BuildCheckoutPlan` keeps its shipped signature** —
   `BuildCheckoutPlan(repoDir string, stack Stack, sel SyncSelection) ([]CheckoutPlanEntry, error)`
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:464`) — and constructs `RebasePlanLayout{RepoRoot: repoDir}`
   internally, leaving the other two members the zero string. Widening that signature to take a
   layout or a feature path is permitted only as an **explicitly declared** edit in §19.2; v1 does
   not do it, because every shipped caller would have to change and the adapter needs nothing more
   than `repoDir`.
2a. **No shared function may require `FeaturePath` or `WorktreesRoot` on the checkout arm.**
   `ExecutionOrder`, `ResolveSyncBase`, `EntryContexts`, `RebaseStrategy` and `DestinationDeferred`
   MUST read only `layout.RepoRoot` when the mode is checkout, and MUST NOT read, validate or
   dereference the other two members there: a checkout-constructed layout carrying two empty
   strings is a **complete** input, not a partial one. `WorktreePath` returns `""` for it by rule
   1's own definition, and no checkout path ever calls it. A test drives every checkout-arm call
   with `RebasePlanLayout{RepoRoot: dir}` and asserts the results equal those of the fully
   populated `CheckoutSyncOpts`-derived layout, so the two construction sites cannot diverge and
   no "the adapter needs the layout the adapter builds" circularity exists.
3. `WorktreePath` on `RebasePlanLayout` and `WorktreePath` on `externalSyncLayout` MUST agree for
   every name; a table test over the same inputs asserts it, so the planner and the executor can
   never disagree about where a worktree is.
4. Callbacks are used only where a decision genuinely belongs to `cli`: the planner takes no
   function value in v1 beyond the injectable probe seams of §23.1, and MUST NOT be given one to
   smuggle `cli` policy into `internal`.
5. An import assertion (§22.17a) covers both directions: `internal` imports no Cobra package and
   no `internal/cli` package.

### 9.1 One decision function, no third truth

The following are extracted into package `internal` and consumed by **both** executors and by the
planner. Argv equality with the shipped executors is proven by the existing goldens. `layout` is
always the neutral `RebasePlanLayout` of §9.0.

| Symbol | Ownership |
|---|---|
| `EntryContexts(mode, route, layout RebasePlanLayout, entry) (baseCtx, execCtx PlanContext)` | sole producer of both contexts and of `context_id`. External pass 1: base `entry.Repo` else worktree, execution worktree. Pass 2: both `entry.Repo` else **process cwd**, mirroring `RunSilent`/`RunSilentDir`. Checkout: both `layout.RepoRoot`. |
| `ResolveSyncBase(mode, route, stack, entry, sel, baseCtx) (name, kind, ref)` | extracted from `resolveEntryBase`/`resolveBase` (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:335-356`) plus the checkout base rule. Preserves D2 (external maps `DefaultBranch()`/`DefaultBranchIn(repo)` to `origin/<default>`; checkout is literal) and the pass-2 context rule. Never uses the execution context. |
| `RebaseStrategy(mode, materialization, scoped, cutoff, cutoffState, baseState, headState) (strategy, argv, condition)` | sole owner of external pass-1, external pass-2 and checkout argv shapes; **total** over the matrix of §9.3. |
| `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder(stack, order []StackEntry, policy, opts) (SyncSelection, error)` | the selection **body** (§9.2a): every shipped I10–I13 rule, evaluated over a caller-supplied `TopoSort` order. It **MUST NOT** call `TopoSort`, and it emits `sel.Entries` in `order`'s own order, so the selection, the document, the guard seam, `pushScoped` and the executor all traverse one sort result. `ResolveSyncSelection` keeps its shipped signature as the sorting wrapper for the unguarded routes. |
| `ExecutionOrder(mode, route, layout RebasePlanLayout, order []StackEntry, sel, materialization) []string` | the route's real execution order, derived from an **already-sorted** `order` its caller produced: external pass 1 over `order` then pass 2 over the same `order`; checkout the `BuildCheckoutPlan` order over the same `order`. It **MUST NOT** call `TopoSort` (§9.1a rule 3) and it never re-reads `stack.yaml`; `order` is the single sort's `[]StackEntry` result, in `TopoSort` order, and passing an unsorted or re-sorted slice is a test failure. |
| `DestinationDeferred(order, entry, baseRef, providerArm) (deferred, dependsOn)` | deferral from real order and the provider's planned arm, never from topology. |
| `ReplayUpstream(cutoff, cutoffState, baseRef, baseSHA, deferred, materialization) (ref, sha, provenance, determinacy, reason)` | sole source of exact/snapshot/unknown replay analysis. |
| `RemainingRebaseEntries(route, layout RebasePlanLayout, state, order []StackEntry, sel) []string` | sole producer of a continuation's row set (§13.3). It takes the invocation's **already-sorted** order — freshly derived from the current `stack.yaml` by its caller — and MUST NOT call `TopoSort` or `LoadStack` itself (§9.1a rule 3). |
| `ResolvePushContext(mode, layout RebasePlanLayout, entry StackEntry, materialization string, ids PlanContextIdentities) PlanPushContext` | sole producer of a push context and of `push.targets[].context_id`/`.materialization`: external `entry.Repo` when non-empty, else the entry's **materialized** worktree; checkout `layout.RepoRoot` (§14.1a). Pure — it issues no Git process and probes no path; the materialization and the measured identity table are inputs. |
| `ResolvePushLease(gitBranch string, facts PlanPushRemoteFacts) PlanLease` | sole implementation of §14.2 — the `MappingReadOK` short circuit, Git's two-step compare-and-swap mapping, the phase/refresh freshness rule and the negative-refspec override — over facts measured **above** it. Pure; issues no Git process. |
| `MeasurePushRemoteFacts(ctx PlanPushContext, ids PlanContextIdentities) PlanPushRemoteFacts` | sole producer of the **mapping** half of §14.1a rule 7 — canonical common dir, `MappingReadOK`, `origin` existence, `remote.origin.fetch` in configured order — measured above the route's fetch, only for the contexts of an applicable `PlanPushFacts`, reading no remote-tracking ref. |
| `RefreshPushTrackingRefs(facts PlanPushFacts, fetched PlanFetchOutcome) PlanPushFacts` | sole producer of the **baseline** half: the post-fetch (or plan-point) remote-tracking inventory, its `TrackingPhase` provenance and `FetchedThisRun`. Called exactly once per controlled invocation **whose facts apply**, after that route's fetch decision is carried out and before `BuildRebasePlan`, and not at all otherwise (§14.1a rules 7–8). |
| `PushContextRefreshed(fetched PlanFetchOutcome, commonDir string) bool` | the closed four-conjunct predicate behind `FetchedThisRun`: an attempted, successful, contacting row naming a remote `origin` whose **canonical common dir** equals the push context's (§14.1a rule 8). Pure. |
| `GateBlockers(gates []PlanGateResult) []PlanBlocker` | sole conversion of projected gates into blocker rows (§13.5 rule G), called **only** by `BuildRebasePlan`. It is what lets `RebasePlanRequest.Gates` and both inspection structs be typed `[]PlanGateResult` with no site ever assigning a `[]PlanBlocker` into them (§9.1a rule 5). |
| `PushTargets(req PlanPushRequest) []PlanPushTarget` | sole push projection, pure over the facts `req.Facts` carries (§14.1a rule 9): it issues no Git process, pushes nothing, resolves no context of its own beyond `ResolvePushContext` and returns `[]PlanPushTarget` — the spelling `[]PushTarget` is declared nowhere and MUST NOT appear in a signature. |
| `BuildRebasePlan(req RebasePlanRequest) (RebasePlan, error)` | the non-mutating projection layer: cutoff verification, candidates and digest, collateral, config, contexts, deferral, push/restore, fetch/freshness, `StackEdge`. `RebasePlanRequest` carries the `RebasePlanLayout`, the mode, the effective route, the policy, the selection, the guard, the resolved validation command, this invocation's `Fetch PlanFetchOutcome`, its refreshed `PushFacts PlanPushFacts`, its typed `Gates []PlanGateResult`, and the mode-appropriate pre-acquisition snapshot — `ExternalState ExternalPlanState` **and** `CheckoutState CheckoutPlanState`, the inapplicable one carrying `applicable: false` rows (§13.7a rule 8) — all `internal`-owned values. It converts gates through `GateBlockers` and projects the push through `PushTargets(PlanPushRequest{…, Facts: req.PushFacts})`, adding no measurement of its own. Only this function adds planner Git probes, and only when a plan is requested; it never probes the filesystem for `state.files.*`, never fetches and never reads a remote-tracking inventory. |
| `SelectPrimaryRefusal(blockers []PlanBlocker) (kind RefusalKind, ordered []PlanBlocker)` | sole implementation of §7 for JSON, human rendering and the guarded stderr refusal. The name is deliberately **not** `RefusalKind`: that identifier is the closed §7.1 *type* declared in `internal/rebase_plan.go` (§7.5), and a function of the same name in the same package would not compile. The row type is `PlanBlocker` (§19.1) — the spelling `Blocker` is not declared anywhere and MUST NOT appear in a signature. |

### 9.1a `RebasePlanRequest`, `RebasePlan` and the one-sort rule

Two things were previously carried only in prose and were therefore contradictable: the request the
shared builder takes, and the document value it returns. Both are declared here **exactly**, in
Go, with every member; every construction site named anywhere in this specification (§12.2b step
"shared plan computation", §12.2d row 6, §12.3, §13.7 rule 1, §13.7a step 8, §19.2's call-order
table) constructs **this** type and no variant of it, and any field named in this specification but
absent from a block below is a specification defect, not implementer latitude.

```go
// internal/rebase_plan.go — package internal
//
// RebasePlanRequest is the COMPLETE input of BuildRebasePlan. Every member is an
// internal-owned value produced above the builder; the builder derives, it never
// re-measures (§12.5a rule 6, §13.7a rule 8). There is exactly one such struct:
// the checkout builders of §13.7 construct it from a CheckoutPlanInspection and
// runExternalPlan constructs it from its own step 2-7 values (§13.7a).
type RebasePlanRequest struct {
    // 1 — identity and boundary
    Layout     RebasePlanLayout // §9.0; checkout fills RepoRoot only
    Mode       WorkspaceMode    // the shipped ModeExternal | ModeCheckout constants
                                // (internal/workspace.go); never derived from Layout emptiness
    Feature    string           // resolved feature name (document key `feature`)
    Workspace  PlanWorkspace    // {Mode, StableID *string, RepoRoot} — display-only RepoRoot (§8.3)

    // 2 — the effective run, resolved ONCE above the builder (§13.2, §13.6 rule 4, §15)
    Route          string          // RouteLegacy | RouteNewMode — the EFFECTIVE route
    RequestedRoute string          // "" when equal to Route ⇒ requested_route: null
    RouteTriggers  []string        // sorted trigger names; never nil; [] on legacy
    Invocation     string          // "plan-only" in v1 (§4.1)
    Policy         SyncRunPolicy   // effective fetch/propagation/scope/selector
    PolicyFetchDefaultApplied bool // policy.fetch_default_applied (§4.1)
    Push           bool            // intent.push
    PushSource     string          // intent.push_source (§4.6)
    Guard          CheckoutPlanGuard      // the raw control-flag values (§3.2)
    Limits         PlanGuardLimits        // the EFFECTIVE per-key limits (§13.2)
    LimitConflicts []PlanGuardLimitConflict // §4.6; never nil
    Validation     PlanValidationIdentity // §15; Command is never published
    Approve        string                 // the supplied --approve-plan token; "" when absent

    // 3 — the subject, loaded and sorted EXACTLY ONCE by the caller (rule 3)
    Stack     *Stack        // nil iff the route could not read it ⇒ rows-less document
    Order     []StackEntry  // the ONE TopoSort result; nil iff SortErr != nil
    SortErr   error         // the verbatim `cycle detected in stack.yaml`
    StackErr  error         // the verbatim LoadStack error
    Selection SyncSelection // zero value on a legacy route, which selects everything
    SelectionResolved bool  // ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder ran over Order and succeeded (§9.2a)
    SelectionErr      error // the shipped sentence, verbatim
    RowsAvailable     bool  // §13.7 rule 4 / §13.7a rule 4; the sole answer to "publish entries[]?"

    // 4 — continuation inputs (zero on a fresh run)
    Continue         bool
    Remaining        []string             // RemainingRebaseEntries output (§13.3); never re-derived
    StageFacts       []PlanStageFact      // §13.3b; [] outside checkout continuations
    Changed          map[string]bool      // verbatim resolveSyncPolicy output; read-only (§13.7a rule 9)
    ContinuationGate PlanContinuationGate // the projected shipped verdict (§13.7a rule 9)

    // 5 — what this invocation already measured; the builder consumes, never probes
    Fetch         PlanFetchOutcome  // §13.7; the fetch this route really performed or suppressed
    FetchPlan     PlanFetchPlan     // the pre-fetch enumeration (§11.1); source of the rank 5.0x rows
    PushFacts     PlanPushFacts     // §14.1a rule 9: the ONE push-fact carrier — identities,
                                    // materialization, distinct contexts and per-context remote
                                    // facts whose baseline half was refreshed AFTER this route's
                                    // fetch (rule 7). BuildRebasePlan hands it to PushTargets as
                                    // PlanPushRequest.Facts verbatim and measures nothing itself;
                                    // Applies && Phase == "pre-fetch" is a defect, not a document
    BasePreflight PlanBasePreflight // I14, evaluated at most once per invocation (§10.7 rule 1a)
    ExternalState ExternalPlanState // §12.5; Applicable:false on checkout (§12.5a rule 5)
    CheckoutState CheckoutPlanState // §12.5a; Applicable:false on external
    Gates         []PlanGateResult  // every projected shipped gate, in ladder order (§13.5), as
                                    // TYPED gate results — never []PlanBlocker. The gate → blocker
                                    // conversion happens in exactly one place, GateBlockers, called
                                    // by BuildRebasePlan and by nothing else (§13.5 rule G)
    Version       GitVersion        // the one ProbeGitVersion result, COPIED from the inspection
                                    // that issued it (§16 rule 1a); never probed here
    Capabilities  GitCapabilities   // its six gate verdicts (§16). Version.Probed == false is a
                                    // rows-less no-subject document that skipped the probe (rule
                                    // 1b) and publishes NO capability-dependent field; Probed &&
                                    // !OK is the unparseable/failed cell ⇒ rank 5.9 (rule 6)
}
```

**Applicability, member by member (no member is "sometimes absent" — it is zero, and the zero is
meaningful):**

| Member | External | Checkout | Fresh | `--continue` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Layout.WorktreesRoot` | set | `""` | — | — |
| `Layout.RepoRoot` | `""` unless a pass-2 process-cwd context applies | `opts.RepoDir` | — | — |
| `Stack` / `Order` / `SortErr` / `Selection*` | set where step 4 established them | set from `insp` | set | **nil/zero on a checkout continuation** (rule 2 of §13.7 forbids the load) |
| `Remaining` / `StageFacts` | `Remaining` on a continuation | both on a continuation | `nil` | set |
| `Fetch` | the step-7 outcome | the step-4 outcome | set | `PlanFetchOutcome{Applies:false}` |
| `FetchPlan` | `fp` (§13.7a step 4) | `insp.FetchPlan` | set | the zero value |
| `PushFacts` | `insp.PushFacts` refreshed at §13.7a step 7a | `insp.PushFacts` refreshed at §13.7 step 4a/3a | `Phase: post-fetch` on a fetching arm, `plan-point` otherwise | `Phase: plan-point`; `{Applies:false, Phase:"not-applicable"}` where `intent.push` is false |
| `Gates` | step 5's projected ladder, from `insp.Gates` | `insp.Gates` | set | set |
| `ExternalState` / `CheckoutState` | `{Applicable:true}` / `{Applicable:false}` | the mirror | — | — |
| `Changed` / `ContinuationGate` | threaded / projected | threaded / projected | zero | set |
| `Version` / `Capabilities` | `insp.Version` / `insp.Capabilities` from `InspectExternalPlan` | the same members of `CheckoutPlanInspection` | probed once where a subject exists | probed once where the persisted run decoded; `Probed: false` otherwise (§16 rule 1b) |

```go
// RebasePlan is the document value. Its members are the TWENTY-FIVE top-level
// keys of §4.1, in that order and no other, and the JSON encoder emits them in
// declaration order: this struct IS the source model and the projection, so
// there is no second enumeration to disagree with §4.1. Adding, removing or
// reordering a field here without amending §4.1 fails the §22.33b schema test.
type RebasePlan struct {
    SchemaVersion  int                 `json:"schema_version"`   // RebasePlanSchemaVersion == 1
    Route          string              `json:"route"`
    RequestedRoute *string             `json:"requested_route"`  // null when equal to Route
    RouteTriggers  []string            `json:"route_triggers"`   // never nil
    Invocation     string              `json:"invocation"`       // "plan-only"
    Workspace      PlanWorkspace       `json:"workspace"`
    Feature        string              `json:"feature"`
    Policy         PlanPolicy          `json:"policy"`
    Intent         PlanIntent          `json:"intent"`           // §4.6
    Push           PlanPush            `json:"push"`             // §4.4a, 4 members
    Restore        PlanRestore         `json:"restore"`          // §14.4, 10 members
    Fetch          PlanFetch           `json:"fetch"`            // §4.4a, 7 members
    Freshness      string              `json:"freshness"`        // the twelve-value enum (§11.3)
    Repositories   []PlanRepository    `json:"repositories"`     // never nil
    State          PlanState           `json:"state"`            // §4.5
    Runnable       bool                `json:"runnable"`
    Blockers       []PlanBlocker       `json:"blockers"`         // never nil
    Warnings       []PlanWarning       `json:"warnings"`         // never nil
    EncodingIssues []PlanEncodingIssue `json:"encoding_issues"`  // never nil
    ConfigIssues   []PlanConfigIssue   `json:"config_issues"`    // never nil
```
