| 6 | `CapDefaultBackendMerge` is **false** (the host Git predates 2.26, where `rebase.backend` does not exist and the built-in default is the apply backend) | `apply` |
| 7 | `CapDefaultBackendMerge` is **unknown** (unparseable/unobtainable `git --version`, §16) | `null` |

Binding consequences, each one a correction of an earlier revision:

- **Configuration NEVER forces the merge backend.** `rebase.updateRefs` and `rebase.rebaseMerges`
  are **not** inputs to this table, in any cell. Git selects the merge backend from the
  *command line* it is given (`git rebase`'s INCOMPATIBLE OPTIONS list) and from `rebase.backend`;
  a configured `rebase.updateRefs = true` or `rebase.rebaseMerges = true` under
  `rebase.backend = apply` does not silently promote the run to the merge backend, and publishing
  `merge` there would have inverted the two rules this value exists to gate. The previous "any
  configuration input Git itself resolves into the merge backend" clause is **withdrawn**.
- **`--keep-base` is not a merge-forcing option and has been removed from the list.** It does not
  appear in `git rebase`'s merge-backend incompatibility list, and it is additionally incompatible
  with `--onto`, which every tws `onto` argv carries (§9.3) — so listing it was wrong twice.
- **Rows 3–5 are gated on the same 2.26 capability, and the gate is a capability, not a version
  string.** Below the gate `rebase.backend` is a key Git does not read, so no configured value can
  produce `merge` (row 6). On the plan/guard route that cell is additionally **unreachable**,
  because the `config --show-scope` gate — the other 2.26 capability, kept explicitly separate by
  §16 rule 3a — already refused the invocation with rank 5.9 `probe-failed`; row 6 is nevertheless
  specified and tested independently, because the two gates have opposite consequences and a
  future change to either MUST NOT silently move the other.
- **Only argv row 1 is reachable from a tws-issued argv in v1**, and only through `--update-refs`
  on the external `scope=all` arm's **materialized pass-1** rows (§9.3) — never on that same run's
  pass-2 rows, whose argv carries no merge-forcing option. The remaining tokens are listed for
  **totality** — the
  planner publishes `effective_backend` for the argv it publishes, and an argv it never builds must
  still be classified correctly if a later feature builds one — not because v1 emits them.
- **Row 1 is a claim about the row's OWN published argv, and where that argv is `--update-refs` it
  is reachable only above `CapRebaseUpdateRefs` (§16 rule 3b).** The row matches only when the argv
  **this row publishes** carries a merge-forcing option, so a `scope=all` run's **pass-2** row
  (`["rebase", <base.ref>, <git_branch>]`, §9.3) never matches row 1 through `--update-refs`,
  whatever the invocation's scope is. Where a row's argv *does* carry it, a host below Git 2.38
  cannot run that argv at all, so the controlled route refuses with rank 5.9 `probe-failed`
  **above** this inventory; `effective_backend` is then `null` by row 2 (the inventory was not
  read), and no document may publish `merge` — or any other row-1 verdict — from an argv the host
  would reject. The gate is a precondition of row 1 on exactly the rows whose argv triggers it,
  never a competitor to it and never a scope-wide one.
- A **valid** backend value is a default, never a constraint: no backend-based refusal may be
  emitted. The value is consumed by exactly two downstream rules — the `merge-recreation` conjunct
  (§4.2, §5) and the `collateral_mechanism: config` conjunct (§11.8) — and each of those rules is
  asserted against a **real** `git rebase` in the fixture, never against this table's restatement
  (§16 rule 8, §22.27c).

**The push mapping half reads this same inventory, and does not add a second one (§14.1a rule 7).** A push context that is also an execution context reuses the ordered read taken for it; a **push-only** context takes **one** ordered read of its own, whose only consumers are `remote.origin.fetch` and the context identity — the four rebase/fetch slots of `repositories[].config` stay `not-evaluated` there by the scope rule above, because the described route hands Git none of those keys. Either way the per-context budget stays exactly one ordered read (§22.27a), and a failure of it sets `MappingReadOK: false` for that push context — the rank 5.9 `probe-failed` cell of §14.1a rule 5a — rather than a `config_issues[]` row, because nothing was parsed to be invalid.

`rebase.instructionFormat`, `rebase.missingCommitsCheck`, `submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules`
and general `core.*`/`i18n.*`/`commit.gpgsign` are out of the v1 fatal domain. `rebase.empty` and
`rebase.reapplyCherryPicks` do not exist and MUST NOT be probed.

### 11.8 Collateral (§19.4 resolved)

The collateral set is every local branch ref in the row's repository whose tip lies inside the
candidate range, **minus** every ref checked out in any worktree of that repository, computed over
all `refs/heads/*` and never filtered to stack branches. `stack_owned` is a **label**, never a
filter. It is an **upper bound**: the plan MUST NOT claim a listed ref will move, and MUST NOT claim
it will stay, because the two drop filters differ — a candidate removed by the preliminary
clean-cherry-pick filter never enters the todo, so its ref is not updated and may be orphaned,
while a candidate dropped for becoming empty keeps its `update-ref` step and may still move onto the
rewritten parent/base.

`collateral_mechanism` is derived from the real mechanism of **this row's own published argv**:
`argv` when that argv passes `--update-refs`
(which itself forces the merge backend); `config` when effective `rebase.updateRefs` is true
without it **and** `effective_backend == merge`; `none` otherwise. Checkout never passes
`--update-refs`, a `scope=all` run's **pass-2** row never passes it either (§9.3), and
configuration can still enable movement in both cases. The `argv` mechanism — like
§11.7 row 1 — is claimable on such a row **only** above the 2.38 `CapRebaseUpdateRefs` gate: below
it the
controlled route has already refused (§16 rule 3b), so the row publishes the `null` collateral facts
of the paragraph below with `summary.entries_with_unknown_collateral` incremented, never
`mechanism: argv` and never a known-empty set. A run whose rows publish **no** `--update-refs` argv
at all is never gated, and its rows take `config`/`none` on every Git version.

**The merge-backend conjunct is load-bearing on this axis too.** Ref updating is merge-backend
behaviour, so an effective `rebase.updateRefs: true` under `effective_backend: apply` moves
nothing: the row publishes `collateral_mechanism: none`, a **known empty** `collateral_refs: []`,
no `collateral-update-refs-config` warning, and `collateral_exposed: false` unless another
mechanism exposes it. Where `rebase.updateRefs` is true and `effective_backend` is `null` the
mechanism cannot be established, so the collateral facts are `null` per the paragraph below and
`summary.entries_with_unknown_collateral` increments — never `none` and never `[]`.

**Configuration and loudness, both halves closed:**

- When `rebase.updateRefs` re-enables collateral movement on a run whose argv omits `--update-refs`
  — that is, exactly in the `collateral_mechanism: config` cell, which requires
  `effective_backend == merge` — v1 publishes exactly one `collateral-update-refs-config`
  **warning** beside the collateral upper bound. It is never a blocker, never a `refusal.kind`, and
  never moves `runnable`.
- **A guarded run MUST NOT pass any argv override.** No `--no-update-refs` is injected, and (per
  §19.18) no `--no-autostash` is injected. The only argv difference a guarded run may carry is the
  external `--onto` SHA pinning of §10.5. Injecting an override would change the run the operator
  asked for and diverge from the golden-covered argv.

If the config probe, candidate range, branch inventory or worktree inventory fails, the collateral
facts are `null` — never `none`, `[]` or `false` — and
`summary.entries_with_unknown_collateral` increments.

**Collateral is a holder fact, so a guarded run re-measures it at the row's JIT seam (binding).**
The "minus every ref checked out in any worktree of that repository" clause above is answered from
the holder index of §14.4 rule 4, and holders move while a run is executing — an operator can check
a branch out, or an earlier row of this very run can create or release a worktree. Before **any**
guarded row whose own published argv can invoke `--update-refs` — which includes external **pass 1**,
whose unscoped argv is `["rebase", "--update-refs", <base>]`, and excludes, **from this collateral
class only**, every scoped pass-1 row,
every external pass-2 row and every checkout row (those last two are in §14.4 rule 4's **switch**
class and re-probe for their own reason, §25.99) — the seam re-runs `BuildBranchHolderInventory`
for that row's **execution** canonical common dir, recomputes `collateral_refs` and
`collateral_exposed` from the refreshed inventory and the re-probed candidate range, and compares
them through the same `RevalidatePlanGuardEntry` fingerprint every other JIT fact uses.

**Holders are one of four inputs, and the seam re-measures all four (binding, §25.102).** A tuple is
`{repo, ref, sha, stack_owned}`; refreshing only the worktree inventory would compare three stale
members against one fresh one. Immediately before such a row, and before any Git mutation, the seam
therefore also:

- re-reads the **complete local branch ref inventory** of that repository — every `refs/heads/*`,
  never filtered to stack branches — through exactly **one** `BuildBranchRefInventory`
  (`internal/stack_status.go:427-447`) call, i.e. one `git for-each-ref` process per common dir per
  seam, which is what makes a `ref` that appeared or vanished and a `sha` that moved observable at
  all; an unavailable or erroring inventory is rank 5.9 `probe-failed` before Git and is **never**
  read as an empty set;
- **reloads the current `stack.yaml` safely** and rebuilds the stack-owned membership mapping from
  it — a dedicated read-only stack identity probe over `StackEntry.GitBranch()`, adding no process —
  because `stack_owned` is a fact about a file an operator can edit mid-run. It is a **read only**:
  it MUST NOT `TopoSort`, MUST NOT re-select, and MUST NOT change this run's order, universe or
  remaining set (§9.1a rule 3). An unreadable or undecodable `stack.yaml` is rank 5.9
  `probe-failed`; a readable one whose membership differs from the approved mapping flips a
  `stack_owned` member and is therefore rank 9 `revalidation-mismatch`. Membership stays a **label
  and never a filter**, so a ref that left the stack stays in `collateral_refs` with
  `stack_owned: false` rather than disappearing from it;
- re-probes the row's **candidate range and digest**, so "whose tip lies inside the candidate range"
  is answered over the range the executor is about to use.

All four are measured once per seam and never shared across seams, and none of them licenses a
prediction: the upper-bound rule at the top of this section is unchanged at the seam, so no
sentence, field, test name or skill line may say a listed ref **will** move or **will** stay because
a JIT input was refreshed.

**The comparison is over the whole canonical tuple array, and any difference refuses.** The compared
value is this row's `(repo, ref)`-sorted sequence of `{repo, ref, sha, stack_owned}` tuples — the
same shape §8.3 binds into the fingerprint — together with `collateral_exposed`. A tuple **added**, a
tuple **removed**, a tuple whose `sha` **changed** (a listed ref that moved at all, tip-only moves
included), a tuple whose `stack_owned` **changed** in either direction, a nullable member that became
or stopped being `null`, and the array as a whole moving between `null` and known are **each** a
rank 9 `revalidation-mismatch` raised **before** the rebase (§10.3). This is deliberately
**conservative identity drift** and not a prediction: tws does not decide whether a changed tuple
would still have been moved, or moved harmlessly, by the rebase — the approved plan described one
array and the executor is about to run against another, which is enough. The earlier narrow spelling
— "a ref that **entered** the set, or a known-unexposed row that became exposed" — described two
cells of this comparison and is **withdrawn** as a statement of it; no test name, comment or skill
may re-narrow it (§25.100). The refresh is cached once per common dir **within** that seam and is never
shared across seams (§14.4 rule 4). A row in the `config` or `none` mechanism whose argv carries no
`--update-refs` re-probes nothing **on this axis** — it may still re-probe as a switch row — and the
**unguarded** route re-probes nothing at
all — it has no seam (§10.3, §17.1).

## 12. External state, locks, timing and recovery

### 12.1 Global timing invariants

1. The pre-acquisition snapshot is taken at route entry, before **any** create, acquire or reclaim.
2. Guard decisions consume snapshot facts; snapshot facts are never re-read at a seam (one narrow
   carve-out, §12.4). The cell-4 guarded-sentinel decode of §13.6 rule 2c is **not** an exception:
   it is a dispatch-time producer, evaluated once per invocation, above the route and above every
   write, on the one cell whose shipped answer is a refusal — never at a seam, never a second time,
   and never on cells 1 or 7, so no frozen path gains a read.
3. A fresh refusal removes only artefacts **this invocation created**, and every removal it
   performs propagates its own failure (§12.2c rule 4a).
4. A continuation refusal runs no fresh teardown and mutates no interrupted state.
5. The guard seam precedes the first guarded rebase; a JIT seam immediately precedes each rebase.
6. Continuations never fetch.
7. Nothing implies atomicity between the final revalidation and `git rebase`.

### 12.2 External new-mode fresh: two execution orderings (§19.1 resolved)

There are **two** orderings, selected structurally by whether this invocation is guarded. They are
not variants of one pipeline: the unguarded one is frozen byte-, process- and state-order wise, and
the guarded one is a controlled-only pipeline that no shipped invocation can reach without a
control flag.

### 12.2a Unguarded new-mode fresh — frozen, unchanged, not refactored in behaviour

```text
stack load → ResolveSyncSelection → verifySelectedBasesLocally (under --no-fetch)
→ marker + collision check + owner token → LoadConfig().TestCommand
→ setupSyncRunState            (ClaimSyncRunGuard → sentinel → payload at SyncStageInitializing)
→ printSyncModeHeader
→ syncFeatureScoped            (Stage = SyncStageFetching + SaveSyncRunState, then the fetch loop)
→ TopoSort → syncWithStackScoped (Stage = SyncStageRebasing + SaveSyncRunState)
→ first git rebase
```

This is exactly `runScopedSync` (`internal/cli/sync.go:151-208`) as shipped. `SyncStageFetching`
**is still written**, at exactly the shipped point, whenever the effective policy is `fetch` — the
stage constant remains a live, readable value of `SyncRunState.Stage`, not a legacy leftover. Every
byte, every Git process, every state write and their relative order are unchanged. The only edit
this route sees is a pure extraction: the fetch loop's body moves into
`fetchScopedReposTo(os.Stdout, os.Stderr, …)` (§19.2), which `syncFeatureScoped` calls immediately
after its unchanged stage write, discarding the returned outcome.

### 12.2b Guarded new-mode fresh — controlled-only, claim below the guard

```text
pre-acquisition snapshot       (internal.InspectExternalPlanState over classifySyncState's result,
                                §12.5 — the same producer the plan route uses; its value becomes
                                req.ExternalState)
→ insp := InspectExternalPlan(...)
                               (the SAME single subject inspection the plan route makes, §13.7a
                                step 4: stack load → the ONE TopoSort → ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder
                                (§9.2a — never the sorting wrapper) → the ONE ProbeGitVersion
                                (§16 rule 1a) → fetch-context enumeration → push MAPPING facts
                                (§14.1a rule 7; no remote-tracking read here) → the typed gate
                                ladder (§13.5 rule G).
                                Its []StackEntry order feeds the plan AND is threaded to the
                                executor below, so nothing sorts twice)
→ verifySelectedBasesLocally   (only under --no-fetch; shipped sentence, marker-free, §10.7 —
                                consuming insp.BasePreflight, not a second locator run)
→ marker + collision check + owner token   (pure computations; shipped position kept)
→ validation resolution        (internal.LoadConfig().TestCommand once → validationSource →
                                intent.validation.command_digest; §15)
→ printSyncModeHeader          (hoisted above the fetch — controlled route only)
→ fetchScopedReposTo(os.Stdout, os.Stderr, …, insp.FetchPlan)
                               (selected-repo fetch, per policy, writing NO payload/sentinel/guard;
                                returns the PlanFetchOutcome this run's document/plan consumes)
→ RefreshPushTrackingRefs(insp.PushFacts, outcome)
                               (the ONE push baseline read of this invocation, §14.1a rule 7:
                                after the fetch, before the plan, so the lease SHAs the token binds
                                (§8.3) are the ones the projected push would really compare)
→ shared plan computation      (BuildRebasePlan, req.Fetch = that outcome, req.Order = insp.Order,
                                req.PushFacts = the refreshed value, req.Gates = insp.Gates,
                                req.Version/req.Capabilities = insp.Version/insp.Capabilities,
                                consuming the already-resolved validation value)
→ guard seam                   (limits, approval, controlled-path blocks)
→ setupSyncRunState(…, birth)  (ClaimSyncRunGuard → sentinel → payload at SyncStageInitializing,
                                state_version 3 + route + limits — the first shared-state write;
                                §13.6 rules 2, 2a)
→ post-claim revalidation      (RevalidatePlanEntry re-probe + RevalidatePlanGuardEntry verdict,
                                over every row of the claimed plan; on refusal
                                rollbackGuardedRunState removes exactly those three; §12.2c)
→ syncFeatureScopedPlanned     (no fetch block, no second fetch, no SyncStageFetching write, and
                                no second TopoSort: it takes insp.Order as a parameter)
→ syncWithStackScoped          (over that same order; Stage = SyncStageRebasing +
                                SaveSyncRunState)
→ per-entry JIT revalidation
→ first git rebase
```

Consequences, all REQUIRED:

- **A guarded new-mode refusal at or above the guard seam creates nothing to tear down**: no
  payload, no run guard, no sentinel. `clearSyncRunState` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:433-452`)
  is not called on that path because there is nothing to clear. It is nevertheless a **post-fetch
  REFUSE** (Normative vocabulary): this invocation's policy fetch ran above the seam, so the
  refusal means "no tws state and no rebase", never "nothing happened". A refusal **below** the
  claim is §12.2c, which is the one and only cell where this route cleans up after itself.
- **Validation identity is resolved once, above the plan.** `internal.LoadConfig().TestCommand` is
  read exactly once per guarded invocation, before `BuildRebasePlan`, so (i) the digest the
  document binds and the guard seam compares is the digest of the command this run will use,
  (ii) `setupSyncRunState` persists that same value into the payload rather than re-reading config
  under the claim, and (iii) the executor consumes it as an explicit value (§15.3). The read is a
  pure config read: it performs no Git process and no fetch, so hoisting it above the fetch cannot
  move a byte on any route. The unguarded route keeps its shipped read position verbatim.
- **Fetch happens with no payload in existence**, so the shipped `Stage = SyncStageFetching` write
  is unreachable on this route. The guarded fresh payload is born inside `setupSyncRunState` from
  the shipped `NewSyncRunState`, i.e. at `SyncStageInitializing`, **carrying its guarded version,
  route and limits from the one new `syncRunStateBirth` parameter of §13.6 rule 2a**, and **the
  first stage this route
  writes after the claim is `SyncStageRebasing`** — written by the shipped
  `syncWithStackScoped` prologue, an existing constant, with no new stage introduced.
  `SyncStageFetching` therefore never appears in a guarded fresh run's state history, and a
  `--continue` of such a run resumes from `rebasing` exactly as an unguarded run interrupted at the
  same point does. This is a **state-ordering difference**, declared in §17.2 and asserted in §23.
- **The payload-free fetch helper exists for this route, and it is the same helper the plan route
  uses.** `fetchScopedReposTo(out, errw io.Writer, layout, stack, sel, verbose)
  internal.PlanFetchOutcome` is the shipped fetch body — `selectedRealEntries` → `UniqueRepos` →
  `fetchQuietTo` — with no `SyncRunState` argument and no state write, so it *cannot* write a
  stage. The unguarded `syncFeatureScoped` calls it with `os.Stdout, os.Stderr` at its shipped
  point (a pure extraction, §19.4), the guarded route calls it with the same two writers above the
  claim, and the plan route calls it with its prose writer twice over (§13.7a). One body, three
  callers, one set of bytes. Hoisting it is a required part of this feature, not an incidental
  call-site move.
- **The executor runs with no second fetch.** `syncFeatureScopedPlanned` is `syncFeatureScoped`
  with the whole fetch block removed — including its `SyncStageFetching` write — so the guarded
  run fetches **exactly once**, above the claim. A second `git fetch` anywhere on this route is a
  test failure (§22.28), because it would refresh refs the plan and the token already described.
- **stdout stays byte-identical to the unguarded twin on a guarded success, and the header keeps
  its shipped position relative to the fetch.** The shipped unguarded route prints the header
  **after** the claim and **before** the fetch (`setupSyncRunState` → `printSyncModeHeader` →
  `syncFeatureScoped`'s fetch loop); the guarded route prints it **before** its fetch too, which is
  why the hoist is mandatory rather than cosmetic — both orderings emit `header, then fetch prose`.
  What differs is **where the claim sits**, and therefore exactly one output cell: a guarded run
  whose **claim/setup step itself fails** (`setupSyncRunState`, i.e. `ClaimSyncRunGuard`, the
  sentinel write or the first payload save) has already printed the header, while the unguarded
  twin fails at the same step **before** reaching its header and prints none. A refusal **below**
  the claim — the post-claim revalidation seam of §12.2c, a JIT seam, a rebase failure — creates
  **no** header divergence at all: the unguarded twin's claim succeeded there too, so it also
  printed the header. Any earlier text claiming that "a guarded run that refuses inside *or below*
  the claim prints a header the unguarded run would not have printed" is **withdrawn**: only the
  claim/setup-failure position differs, plus the plan-only stream routing of §3.6 (on `--plan` the
  header goes to stderr). Both are declared in §17.2 and asserted in §22.28c/§23; neither can
  reach an unguarded invocation. The **process/state** order difference — fetch before claim, and
  no `SyncStageFetching` write — is a separate declared axis of the same table, not a second output
  divergence.
- **The claim is revalidated.** A claim is a mutation of shared state, so the facts the token
  authorized are re-checked once ownership exists, before the first rebase (§12.2c).
- The pre-acquisition snapshot already excluded this invocation's own artefacts under either
  ordering, so the correctness of the live-owner rule does not depend on this choice; the choice is
  taken for teardown surface.
- Under `--plan` the header goes to stderr (§3.6); the plan route never reaches
  `setupSyncRunState` at all.
- **Checkout keeps its shipped seam positions, and takes the same snapshot the plan route takes**:
  `AcquireCheckoutLock` stays above `BuildCheckoutPlan`, because the lock is what makes the plan
  build meaningful, and the guarded checkout ordering is §12.2d.

### 12.2c Post-claim revalidation and its cleanup (guarded fresh routes, §25.11)

Post-claim revalidation is the seam between "this invocation owns the run" and "this invocation has
changed a branch". It re-probes every row of the claimed plan through `RevalidatePlanEntry` and
re-judges it through `RevalidatePlanGuardEntry`, with the §10.3 JIT outcome table. It exists on
**both** guarded *fresh* routes — new-mode (§12.2b) and legacy (§12.3) — and on neither unguarded
one.

**Binding rules for a refusal at this seam, before any rebase:**

1. **`StatePreserved` is `false` when the cleanup of rule 2 succeeds.** No entry has been rebased
   and no interrupted run guard was reclaimed, so the marker carries no `state-preserved: ` prefix
   and the detail MUST NOT suggest `--continue` (§6.4). On a fetch-policy route it is still a
   **post-fetch REFUSE** — this invocation already fetched above the guard seam — and no text may
   say otherwise; only on an effective `no-fetch` route did nothing happen at all.
2. **Cleanup removes exactly what this invocation created, in the shipped reverse order, through a
   rollback that cannot swallow a removal error.** The shipped teardown helpers cannot be reused
   as-is for this: `internal.DeleteSyncRunState` (`internal/sync_run_state.go:133-135`),
   `internal.DeleteSyncState` (`internal/syncstate.go:43-45`) and `internal.ReleaseSyncRunGuard`
   (`internal/sync_run_state.go:249-251`) each call `os.Remove` and **discard** its error
   (`//nolint:errcheck`), so `clearSyncRunState`'s existing early-return can only observe an
   *injected step-hook* failure, never a real `EACCES`, `EBUSY`, `EIO` or `ENOTEMPTY`. This feature
   therefore adds error-returning removers and one rollback that uses them:

   ```go
   // internal/sync_run_state.go — additive
   func RemoveSyncRunState(featurePath string) error // payload
   func RemoveSyncRunGuard(featurePath string) error // run guard

   // internal/syncstate.go — additive
   func RemoveSyncState(featurePath string) error    // legacy state / sentinel
   ```

   Each is exactly `err := os.Remove(<path>); if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
   return fmt.Errorf("remove <artefact> %s: %w", <path>, err) }; return nil` — **only**
   `fs.ErrNotExist` is ignored, because "already gone" is the outcome the caller asked for; every
   other error, including a permission failure and a directory in the artefact's place, is
   returned. The three shipped `Delete*`/`Release*` functions become one-line wrappers
   (`_ = RemoveX(featurePath)`), which is observationally identical to their shipped bodies — the
   error was already discarded — so every shipped caller keeps its behaviour and its bytes, and a
   test asserts the pair over absent / present / undeletable paths.

   The guarded post-claim rollback is its own function, so `clearSyncRunState` keeps its shipped
   body and its shipped callers:

   ```go
   // internal/cli/sync_modes.go
   type syncStateResidue struct{ Payload, Sentinel, Guard bool }

   func (r syncStateResidue) Empty() bool
   func (r syncStateResidue) String() string // the PRESENT members in the fixed order payload,
                                             // sentinel, guard: "{payload, sentinel, guard}" |
                                             // "{sentinel, guard}" | "{guard}" | "{sentinel}" |
                                             // "{}" — any subset, always that order

   // rollbackGuardedRunState removes exactly the three artefacts a guarded fresh
   // claim created, in the shipped teardown order, propagating the first failure.
   func rollbackGuardedRunState(featurePath string) (syncStateResidue, error)
   ```

   Its body is, in this exact order: `RemoveSyncRunState` → `syncStepHook(SyncStageFinalizing, 0)`
   → `RemoveSyncState` → `syncStepHook(SyncStageFinalizing, 1)` → `RemoveSyncRunGuard`. It **stops
   at the first failing step** — whether that failure came from the remover or from the injected
   hook — and returns the residue **actually left on disk**, which is the failing step's own
   artefact (when the remover failed) plus every artefact of the steps it never attempted. It MUST
   NOT touch a pre-existing artefact (there is none: the claim would have refused), MUST NOT abort
   a rebase, MUST NOT delete `.sync-state.yaml` content it did not write, and MUST NOT run any
   restoration. `clearSyncRunState(featurePath, true)` remains the **success** teardown of both
   guarded and unguarded runs and is unchanged.
3. **The refusal is returned only after the rollback**, so the marker line describes the state the
   operator will actually find.
4. **A cleanup failure propagates and is never swallowed.** When `rollbackGuardedRunState` returns
   a non-empty residue, the invocation:
   - keeps the guard refusal as the **cause** and reports the cleanup failure as the wrapping
     error, in one sentence, exit `1`;
   - writes the marker with `StatePreserved: true` — because state *does* survive — so the
     line reads `plan-guard: <kind>: state-preserved: <detail>`, and the detail names the residue
     **as measured**, in `syncStateResidue.String()` form, plus the exact recovery command
     `tws sync <f> --abort`, which really clears every one of the three residue shapes (§12.8);
   - MUST NOT retry, MUST NOT force-remove a later artefact, and MUST NOT claim the run was cleaned
     up. An honest partial state with a named recovery is required; a silent best-effort sweep is
     forbidden.
4a. **The residue table is total** — five failing steps collapsing onto three reachable shapes:

   | Failing step | Cause | Residue | Recovery cell |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `RemoveSyncRunState` | real removal error | `{payload, sentinel, guard}` | cell 5 `--abort` (shipped arm) |
   | `syncStepHook(Finalizing, 0)` | injected crash after the payload was removed | `{sentinel, guard}` | cell 4 `--abort` (shipped arm; §12.8b's arm where the route was guarded **legacy**, whose sentinel is a backup sentinel) |
   | `RemoveSyncState` | real removal error | `{sentinel, guard}` | cell 4 `--abort` (shipped arm; §12.8b's arm on the guarded legacy route) |
   | `syncStepHook(Finalizing, 1)` | injected crash after the sentinel was removed | `{guard}` | cell 1 `--abort` (**§12.8**) |
   | `RemoveSyncRunGuard` | real removal error | `{guard}` | cell 1 `--abort` (**§12.8**) |

   A real removal error and an injected hook failure at the *same* step therefore differ by exactly
   one artefact, which is why the residue is measured rather than inferred from the step index
   alone. The two `{sentinel, guard}` rows differ by **route**, not by shape: a guarded *new-mode*
   fresh run left a plain sentinel there and gets the shipped cell-4 answers, while a guarded
   *legacy* fresh run left the backup sentinel of §13.6 rule 2c and therefore gets §12.8b's arms —
   an `--abort` that says what it discards and a `--continue` that resumes the interrupted setup.
5. **Crash injection is required, not optional.** The existing `internal.SyncStepHook`
   (`internal/sync_run_state.go:84`) already fires at `SyncStageInitializing` indices 0–2 and at
   `SyncStageFinalizing` indices 0–1, which covers a crash inside the claim and inside each
   teardown step. This feature adds exactly **two** hook sites, both using the existing hook
   variable, indices no shipped site uses and no new hook type: `syncStepHook(SyncStageRebasing, -1)`
   **immediately before** the first post-claim revalidation probe (this rule), and
   `syncStepHook(SyncStageInitializing, 3)` immediately after the guarded legacy setup's byte capture
   and **above** its sentinel write (§13.2a). Tests drive: crash before
   revalidation (state at `initializing` survives, `--continue`/`--abort` both work), refusal with
   successful cleanup (nothing survives), refusal with an injected teardown failure at each of the
   two `SyncStageFinalizing` indices, and refusal with a **real** removal failure at each of the
   three removal steps — forced through the §23.1 injected-failure seam where permissions cannot —
   each asserting the measured residue of rule 4a, the `state-preserved: ` marker, exit `1`, and
   that `tws sync <f> --abort` afterwards clears exactly that residue.
6. **Nothing here is a second guard.** The verdicts, kinds and precedence are §7's; this seam adds
   no kind, no rank and no waiver.

### 12.2d Guarded checkout orderings — the same snapshot, the shipped seams

The checkout executor's seam positions are unchanged (§19.24): the guard seam sits after
the plan is built and before `SaveCheckoutTransaction` on a fresh run, and after
`forceAcquireCheckoutLock` on a continuation. What this feature adds on the **guarded** checkout
routes is the *same inspection the plan route performs* — one `InspectCheckoutPlan` call, which
owns the one `InspectCheckoutPlanState` snapshot, the one stack load, the one `TopoSort`, the one
selection, the one `ProbeGitVersion` and the one I14 evaluation — at the same place in the order,
so that a guarded checkout
run and a `--plan` of the same invocation decide `state.files.*`, the live-owner rule, the
undecodable rule and the row set from **one** producer rather than from two different reads
(§12.1 rules 1–2, §9.1a rule 3, §16 rule 1a).

**Guarded checkout fresh (`opts.PlanGuard.Guarded() && !opts.Continue`):**

```text
insp := InspectCheckoutPlan(CheckoutPlanInspectionRequest{Opts: opts, Containment: containment})
                                                   (§13.7 — pure reads only: the §12.5a snapshot
                                                    (Lstat + decode of the transaction and
                                                    .checkout-sync.lock, the git-op/dirty/HEAD
                                                    probes), LoadStack, TopoSort,
                                                    ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder (§9.2a — never
                                                    the sorting wrapper), the ONE ProbeGitVersion
                                                    (§16 rule 1a), the I14 locator and the
                                                    fetch-context enumeration; no lock, no fetch,
                                                    no write; it excludes nothing this invocation
                                                    created, because it has created nothing yet)
   st, verdict := insp.State, insp.StateVerdict
   fp          := insp.FetchPlan
→ the shipped fresh ladder, unchanged and in its shipped order, reading what insp already measured
   (I19 containment → existing transaction → gitOperationInProgress → dirty tree → detached HEAD
    → HEAD resolution → new-mode LoadStack/selection → I14 under --no-fetch)
→ **the sort verdict, in its own arm's position**: insp.SortErr != nil ⇒ REFUSE here, above the
   lock and above the fetch, with **that arm's shipped sentence** — the bare
   `cycle detected in stack.yaml` on the new-mode arm, where the shipped `ResolveSyncSelection`
   call already returns exactly that from its own internal sort at this same position, and
   `build plan: cycle detected in stack.yaml` on the legacy arm, where the shipped failure happens
   below the lock inside `BuildCheckoutPlan` — exit 1, marker-free, having taken no lock, run no
   fetch and written no transaction. **Only the legacy arm's position moves**; the new-mode arm
   refuses exactly where and as it always did (§13.6 rule 8 row 12, §17.2, §25.35)
→ AcquireCheckoutLock            (the shipped native gate, in its shipped position)
→ outcome := fetchCheckoutRepoTo(os.Stdout, fp.Contexts[0])
                                 (the shipped fetch body, at its shipped point, under the shipped
                                  opts.NewMode / SyncFetchEnabled conditions and only when fp
                                  suppressed nothing; same bytes as the unguarded wrapper, whose
                                  only difference is that it discards the value — §3.6 rule 3)
→ push := RefreshPushTrackingRefs(insp.PushFacts, outcome)
                                 (the ONE push baseline read, §14.1a rule 7 — after the fetch,
                                  before the plan; `plan-point` where no child ran)
→ buildCheckoutPlanFrom(opts.RepoDir, *insp.Stack, insp.Order, insp.Selection)
                                 (the shipped BuildCheckoutPlan body at its shipped position, over
                                  the order insp already produced — no second TopoSort, §9.2)
→ BuildRebasePlan(req)                       (req.CheckoutState = st, req.Order = insp.Order,
                                              req.Gates = insp.Gates, req.PushFacts = push,
                                              req.Fetch = outcome, whose single row carries fp's
                                              pre-measured CommonDir/Source/Effect/Candidates —
                                              rule 1a)
→ guard seam (EvaluatePlanGuard)
→ SaveCheckoutTransaction → executeTransaction → per-entry JIT → first git rebase
```

**Guarded checkout continuation (`opts.PlanGuard.Guarded() && opts.Continue`, which by §13.6
rule 4d is `(opts.PlanGuard.Armed() || checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded(tx)) && !Plan` — so a **flagless**
resume of a `state_version: 3` transaction takes this arm too):** the same single
`InspectCheckoutPlan` call is made **before `forceAcquireCheckoutLock`**, i.e. before the one
reclaim this route performs, and before the shipped continuation ladder; the seam then stays
exactly where §12.4 leaves it, below `forceAcquireCheckoutLock`. Its continuation arm **sorts
nothing and resolves no selection** (§13.7 rule 2) — it reads the stack at most once, only in the
shipped `checkoutSelectedStillPresent` existence-check cell — so the fresh arm's legacy hoist has
no twin here and nothing about this arm's order changes. No enumeration and no fetch happen (§11.2
cause 1), so `req.Fetch` is the zero `PlanFetchOutcome` with `Applies: false` and `req.Order` is
`nil`. Where §13.2a triggers — a transaction whose `state_version` is absent, `1` or `2`, at least
one limit armed by this invocation, and a guard seam that passed — the arm performs **one**
additional write immediately below that seam and above `resumeTransaction`: the upgrade of row 7
below, which is the only write this feature adds to a checkout continuation. **The shipped resume
keeps every write it ships with**: because the seam is below the lock
and the native `resumeTransaction` runs afterwards, a guarded `--continue` that meets either of the
**two** native-write gates of §13.7 rule 8a performs that gate's shipped write before refusing at
exit `1` — the `planned`/`rebasing` active-rebase arm really does reclassify the stage to `conflict`
and persist it, and the `rebased` ancestry arm really does persist `FailureKind: ancestry` and
`FailureMsg` with `Stage` unchanged — and both are the executing twins of that rule, whose
state-preservation is declared honestly rather than described as a no-op (§12.7).

**The exact calls and their order, both arms (normative; nothing else may produce these values):**

| # | Fresh arm | Continuation arm | Value produced |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | `insp := InspectCheckoutPlan(...)` — **before** `AcquireCheckoutLock`; it makes the one `InspectCheckoutPlanState(opts, CheckoutPlanStateOpts{})` call inside | the same call, continuation arm — **before** `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` | `CheckoutPlanInspection`, carrying `State` + the §12.5a verdict (the verbatim loader errors) |
| 2 | the shipped ladder, reading `insp` for the lock/transaction/stack/selection facts it already measured | the shipped continuation ladder, likewise | no new probe |
| 2a | **the sort/load verdict, in its own arm's position**: `insp.SortErr != nil` (and, on the legacy arm only, `insp.StackErr != nil`) REFUSES here with **that arm's** shipped sentence — new-mode `cycle detected in stack.yaml` (already raised at this position by the shipped `ResolveSyncSelection`), legacy `build plan: cycle detected in stack.yaml` / `load stack: %w` (raised below the lock by the shipped route) — above the lock and above the fetch | *not performed*: this arm sorts nothing and loads a stack only for the existence check of §13.7 rule 2 | the declared controlled-path ordering change, **legacy arm only** (§13.6 rule 8 row 12) |
| 3 | `fp := insp.FetchPlan` (§11.1, enumerated inside the inspection, after the one `ProbeGitVersion`) | *not performed* | `PlanFetchPlan` |
| 4 | `AcquireCheckoutLock(opts.FeaturePath)` | `forceAcquireCheckoutLock(opts.FeaturePath)` | shipped native gate, shipped sentence |
| 5 | `outcome := fetchCheckoutRepoTo(os.Stdout, fp.Contexts[0])` under the shipped conditions, and only when `fp.Suppressed == ""` | *not performed* | the shipped fetch, plus the row it observed |
| 5a | `buildCheckoutPlanFrom(opts.RepoDir, *insp.Stack, insp.Order, insp.Selection)` at the shipped `BuildCheckoutPlan` position | *not performed* — the transaction **is** the plan (§13.7 rule 2) | `[]CheckoutPlanEntry`, from the one sort |
| 5b | `push := RefreshPushTrackingRefs(insp.PushFacts, outcome)` — the ONE baseline read, after row 5 and before row 6, and **only** where `insp.PushFacts.Applies` | `push := RefreshPushTrackingRefs(insp.PushFacts, PlanFetchOutcome{Applies: false})`, before row 6, under the same applicability condition | `PlanPushFacts` with `Phase: post-fetch` (fresh, fetched) or `plan-point` (every other applicable cell); `not-applicable`, unrefreshed and unread where the facts do not apply |
| 6 | `BuildRebasePlan(req)` with `req.CheckoutState = insp.State`, `req.Order = insp.Order`, `req.Gates = insp.Gates`, `req.PushFacts = push`, `req.Version`/`req.Capabilities = insp.Version`/`insp.Capabilities`, `req.Fetch = outcome` — or, where `fp.Suppressed != ""`, the un-attempted row projected from `fp.Contexts[0]` with `Attempted: false`, `OK` ignored and `Suppressed` set | `BuildRebasePlan(req)` with `req.CheckoutState = insp.State`, `req.Order = nil`, `req.Gates = insp.Gates`, `req.PushFacts = push`, `req.Version`/`req.Capabilities = insp.Version`/`insp.Capabilities`, `req.Fetch = PlanFetchOutcome{Applies: false}` | the plan |
| 7 | the guard seam, then `SaveCheckoutTransaction` at its shipped position — a **birth** write carrying `state_version: 3` where the run is guarded (§13.6 rule 2) | the guard seam, then — and **only** where §13.2a triggers (a transaction whose `state_version` is absent, `1` or `2`, at least one limit armed by this invocation, the seam having passed) — the **upgrade** write: `StateVersion = CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion`, `Route = TransactionNewMode(tx)` as loaded, the effective limit pointers, the persisted `TestCommand` kept byte-identical, saved through the shipped `SaveCheckoutTransaction` **before** `resumeTransaction`. A write failure returns the shipped `persist transaction: %w`, marker-free, before any Git mutation; a `state_version: 3` transaction is not rewritten | the transaction on disk |

Binding rules:

1. **One producer, both routes, and the value is threaded, not re-derived.**
   `InspectCheckoutPlan` (§13.7) is the single inspection entry point of **every** controlled
   checkout route — the plan route calls it and returns; the guarded executing route calls it at
   step 1 above and then executes — and `InspectCheckoutPlanState` (§12.5a) is called exactly once,
   *inside* it. It is the sole source of
   `state.files.checkout_transaction`, `state.files.checkout_lock`, `state.worktree`,
   `state.git_op` and `state.head`, and `insp` is likewise the sole source of the stack, its one
   `TopoSort` order, the selection, the Git version/capabilities and the I14 verdict. The guarded
   route
   passes the value as `RebasePlanRequest.CheckoutState`/`.Order`/`.Version`/`.Capabilities` and
   reads nothing twice: neither
   route re-reads a snapshot fact at a seam, and neither passes a *different* value to the builder
   than the one its own gates read.
1a. **The fetch plan is threaded the same way.** The pre-fetch enumeration is a
   `PlanFetchPlan` value on both controlled checkout routes — `insp.FetchPlan` on either — and it
   is the **only** source of
   `context_common_dir`, `fetch_effect` and `context_candidates[]` in the resulting
   `fetch.repos[]` row, whether the row was fetched (`Attempted: true`) or suppressed by cause 5/6
   (`Attempted: false`). Neither route measures an effect after its fetch (§13.7 rule 6a), and
   neither reconstructs one in the builder (§12.5a rule 6).
1b. **The inspection is a set of pure reads; it decides nothing the shipped ladder decides.** On
   the guarded executing route the shipped gates still run natively, in their shipped positions,
   with their shipped sentences and their shipped precedence — `insp` supplies the *facts* they
   read, never a substitute verdict. The single exception is step 2a **on the legacy arm**, where
   the stack load and the sort become a **new refusal position** for sentences that
   already exist: same bytes, same exit code, earlier, and therefore with no lock taken, no fetch
   performed and no transaction written. On the **new-mode** arm step 2a is not a new position at
   all — the shipped route already refuses a cyclic stack there, inside `ResolveSyncSelection`,
   and an unreadable one at its own `LoadStack` — so nothing moves and the bytes are the shipped
   ones. It is declared in §13.6 rule 8 row 12, §17.2, §19.4 and
   §25.35, and it is asserted with an unguarded control per arm in §22.13l. On the **legacy** arm
   the
   inspection loads and sorts only after the projected gate j has been evaluated and has not
   refused (§13.7 step 1.3), so the shipped precedence between a live lock and an unreadable stack
   is preserved exactly.
2. **The snapshot excludes this invocation's own lock, by position rather than by filtering.** It
   is taken **before** `AcquireCheckoutLock`/`forceAcquireCheckoutLock`, so a `.checkout-sync.lock`
   it observes is always a *pre-existing* one; `Self` is nevertheless computed (recorded PID ==
   `os.Getpid()`) and published, because a stale lock left by an earlier run of this same process
   is a real cell and must not be mistaken for a live foreign owner. A guarded run therefore never
   blocks on its own not-yet-created lock, and `live-owner-concurrency` is decided exactly as
   §11.2 cause 3 defines it.
3. **The native gates keep their words.** `AcquireCheckoutLock` and `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` run
   unchanged, in their shipped positions, and their refusals stay shipped-byte-identical and
   marker-free (§22.31). The snapshot never pre-empts them, never synthesises their sentences, and
   never turns a cell they would accept into a refusal — except through the two facts the guard
   already owns: a **live foreign** holder (rank 3 + `live-owner-concurrency`) and an
   **undecodable applicable owner artefact** the native ladder would not itself reject (§12.5's
   reduced domain).
4. **The unguarded checkout route inspects nothing at all.** `opts.PlanGuard.Guarded() == false`
   means `InspectCheckoutPlan` and `InspectCheckoutPlanState` are never called, no probe is added
   (no `git --version`, no config inventory), the shipped sorts stay exactly where they are —
   inside `ResolveSyncSelection` above the lock on the new-mode arm **and** inside
   `BuildCheckoutPlan` below the lock and the fetch on both arms (§9.1a rule 3a) — no byte moves,
   and the
   126 goldens plus the checkout no-flag process budget are the enforcement (§17.1, §22.1).
5. **Plan-only and guarded share facts and one inspection function, not one code path.** Both call
   `InspectCheckoutPlan`; the plan route then renders a document and returns, the guarded route
   then executes. Both get the same value for
   the same on-disk state and the same stack, which is what makes `tws sync <f> --plan …` and the
   guarded execution of the same command agree about `state.*`, about the row set and about the
   order (§22.13h, §22.13l).

### 12.3 The other external pipelines

**Legacy fresh (guarded route only; the unguarded route keeps `syncFeature` verbatim).**

```text
pre-acquisition snapshot       (internal.InspectExternalPlanState, §12.5, as in §12.2b)
→ insp := InspectExternalPlan(...)   (stack load → the ONE TopoSort → no selection on this route →
                                the ONE ProbeGitVersion → fetch-context enumeration → push MAPPING
                                facts → the typed gate ladder;
                                the same producer the plan route uses, §13.7a step 4)
→ marker + collision check + owner token   (the shipped pure computations of setupSyncRunState's
                                            inputs — syncMarkerFn, syncMarkerCollision,
                                            newSyncOwnerToken; no write)
→ validation resolution        (internal.LoadConfig().TestCommand once → digest; §15)
→ fetchStackReposTo(os.Stdout, os.Stderr, …, insp.FetchPlan)
                               (the shipped whole-stack fetch loop, extracted; no state write;
                                returns the PlanFetchOutcome the plan consumes)
→ RefreshPushTrackingRefs(insp.PushFacts, outcome)
                               (the ONE push baseline read, after the fetch and before the plan,
                                §14.1a rule 7)
→ shared plan                  (BuildRebasePlan, route = legacy, req.Fetch = that outcome,
                                req.Order = insp.Order, req.Gates = insp.Gates,
                                req.PushFacts = the refreshed value)
→ guard seam                   (limits, approval, controlled-path blocks)
→ setupGuardedLegacyRunState   (the ONE guarded-legacy writer, declared in
                                internal/cli/sync_modes.go, over the four-step order of §13.2a:
                                capture (nothing on this route — a plain run over a real
                                `.sync-state.yaml` is refused above it, so the fresh arm captures
                                no bytes and writes `prior_legacy_present: false`) →
                                ClaimSyncRunGuard → the atomic **backup sentinel** write, here an
                                EXCLUSIVE create because there is no prior document → v3 payload
                                with route=legacy; the guarded legacy envelope of §13.6
                                rules 2b/2c)
→ post-claim revalidation      (§12.2c)
→ syncWithStackScoped(..., insp.Order, run = the legacy run context, guard)   — legacy argv, legacy
                                output, over the SAME single TopoSort result (§9.1a rule 3)
→ per-entry JIT → first git rebase
```

- **No runtime state exists at or above the guard seam**, so a fresh legacy refusal there leaves
  the feature exactly as found; a refusal below the claim is §12.2c.
- **The envelope is what makes a guarded legacy run resumable *and* downgrade-safe.** Instead of
  the shipped `saveIncompleteSync` legacy state, a guarded legacy run persists the **backup
  sentinel** plus a `state_version: 3` payload carrying `route: legacy`, both limits, the frozen
  validation command, and the full-stack `Selected`/`Pending` provenance (§13.6 rules 2b/2c). The
  unguarded legacy route is untouched: it writes `.sync-state.yaml` on failure and nothing else,
  exactly as shipped.
- **Legacy execution semantics are preserved verbatim** — selection (every entry, archived
  included, no `ResolveSyncSelection` and therefore no I11/I13 refusal), the whole-stack fetch
  loop, the `--update-refs` argv shapes, `markUpdatedAncestors`, the unfiltered completion gate,
  and the absence of a `Sync mode:` header. That is carried by a route field on the run context
  rather than by a selection: `syncRunContext` gains `Route` (`legacy` | `new-mode`), and its three
  predicates answer for legacy exactly as `run == nil` does today —
  `scoped() == false`, `selects(name) == true` for every name, `skipsAnchor(name) == false` — so
  the executor's legacy arm is reached with a payload attached. `validate()` is the one deliberate
  difference: a guarded run validates with the frozen command (§15, `guarded_stability:
  frozen-at-plan`).
- **Failure persistence follows the payload, not `.sync-state.yaml`.** `syncFailure` already
  branches on `run != nil && run.Payload != nil` and calls `saveScopedSyncFailure`, so the guarded
  legacy failure writes the payload and keeps the sentinel. Writing a *real* legacy state beside a
  payload would produce cell 8 (`two unfinished syncs are recorded`) for the next invocation, which
  is precisely the state this envelope must not create.
- `TopoSort`, the `git --version` probe, the validation read and the context enumeration are
  hoisted above the fetch **only on
  controlled paths**; the unguarded legacy order (`LoadStack` → fetch → `TopoSort`, inside
  `syncFeature`) is untouched, and the legacy route prints no `Sync mode:` header on either
  ordering. The controlled hoist is also what makes the sort single: `syncFeature`'s and
  `syncFeatureScoped`'s own `TopoSort` calls (`internal/cli/sync.go:548`, `:568`) and the sort
  inside `ResolveSyncSelection` (`internal/sync_selection.go:166`) are reached only
  by the unguarded routes — which therefore keep the shipped counts of §9.1a rule 3a — and their
  planned twins take the order as a parameter.

**Scoped/v2 continuation — `handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue`, the guarded twin of the shipped
`handleScopedSyncContinue`.** The shipped handler is **not** reused, extended or given an optional
guard: it sorts twice (§9.1a rule 3a), it reclaims the run guard **before** it has any plan, and it
has no seam between "the resume is describable" and "the resume owns the guard". A guarded
continuation therefore has its own entry point, reachable only from the §19.2 dispatch, with the
shipped handler left byte-, statement- and sort-count-identical for every unguarded invocation:

```go
// internal/cli/sync.go — package cli
//
// handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue is the CONTROLLED twin of
// handleScopedSyncContinue. Same shipped gates, same shipped sentences, same
// shipped prose, same executor — with the invocation's ONE inspection replacing
// its two sorts, and the guard seam inserted ABOVE the first write.
func handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue(feature string, layout externalSyncLayout,
    ws internal.Workspace, push bool, policy internal.SyncRunPolicy, changed map[string]bool,
    state internal.SyncExternalState, opts planGuardOptions) error
```

```text
 1. payload := state.Payload; nil ⇒ the shipped `nothing to continue — no sync in progress`
 2. pre-acquisition snapshot   (internal.InspectExternalPlanState over `state`, §12.5 — the same
                                producer the plan route and §12.2b use; becomes req.ExternalState)
 3. route and identity         (route = new-mode by construction on this arm — the dispatch already
                                established internal.PayloadNewMode(payload); effective policy =
                                payload.Policy(); limits per §13.2's per-key table, i.e. persisted
                                values inherit and a conflicting supplied value is rank 7;
                                validation per §15)
 4. insp := InspectExternalPlan(...)   — the ONE call, §13.7a step 4, with Continue: true:
                                LoadStack → the ONE TopoSort → ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder over
                                that order, filtered by the persisted Selected through
                                scopedSelectionFromPayloadOrder (§9.2a rule 6) →
                                RemainingRebaseEntries over the same order (§13.3) → the ONE
                                ProbeGitVersion → NO fetch enumeration (a continuation never
                                fetches, §11.2 cause 1, so insp.FetchPlan is the zero value) →
                                push MAPPING facts (only where they apply, §14.1a rule 7) → the
                                typed gate ladder of §13.7a step 5, which evaluates EVERY
                                continuation gate of this arm EXACTLY ONCE — external-d
                                (syncContinueMismatches over all four axes), external-e1 (the
                                failed-branch rebase-in-progress check, applicable on the bare
                                shipped `payload.FailedBranch != ""` condition), external-e2 (the
                                failed-branch existence check) and external-e3 (the
                                configured-parent ancestry check), both applicable ONLY under the
                                shipped conjunct
                                `payload.FailedBranch != "" && !payloadCompleted(payload,
                                payload.FailedBranch)` (§13.7a step 5), and external-e4
                                (state.GuardForeign()) — and
                                returns them as insp.Gates plus insp.ContinuationGate
 5. the projected ladder is CONSUMED, not re-evaluated: the handler walks insp.Gates in ladder
    order and, on the first row with Applies && Failed, returns that row's Detail — the shipped
    sentence, verbatim, at exit 1, marker-free — at the position the shipped handler raises it.
    It MUST NOT call syncContinueMismatches, isRebaseInProgress, internal.GetBranch for the
    failed-branch existence test or branchContainsConfiguredParent again; a second evaluation of
    any of them is a specification violation and is asserted against by call counters (§22.14b).
    The shipped `[~] resolved` line is printed **during** that walk, at its shipped position —
    after external-e3 has been consulted and passed, and therefore BEFORE external-e4
    (`GuardForeign()`) is consulted, exactly as the shipped handler prints it above its own
    `GuardForeign()` refusal — and it is emitted exactly when gates external-e2 and external-e3
    both APPLIED and neither failed, derived from those gate rows and never from a re-check.
    On a **push-failure resume** — the payload records the entry in both `Completed` and
    `FailedBranch` — those two gates are `Applies: false`, so this arm performs no parent check
    and prints no `[~] resolved` line, byte-identically to the shipped handler.
    THE SOLE EXCEPTION to "evaluate once" is step 6, and it is an exception because it is a
    liveness claim about *now*, not a projection (§12.4)
 6. fresh native reclaim precheck   (checkSyncRunGuardReclaimable, §12.4 — a pure re-read of the
                                     guard bytes, required because ReclaimSyncRunGuard's
                                     compare-and-swap must be anchored to the bytes it judged and
                                     because a live foreign holder may have appeared since the
                                     snapshot; no write, not fingerprint input, and its own
                                     refusals are the §12.4 native sentences)

                                (the ONE baseline read, at this arm's plan point: TrackingPhase
                                 `plan-point`, FetchedThisRun false everywhere, §14.1a rule 7)
 8. BuildRebasePlan(req)        (req.Continue = true, req.Remaining = insp.Remaining,

                                 req.Gates = insp.Gates,
                                 req.ContinuationGate = insp.ContinuationGate,
                                 req.Changed = the threaded map, req.PushFacts = step 7's value,
                                 req.Fetch = PlanFetchOutcome{Applies: false},
                                 req.ExternalState = step 2's snapshot,
                                 req.CheckoutState = the applicable:false value)

10. internal.ReclaimSyncRunGuard(layout.FeaturePath, payload.OwnerToken)   — the FIRST write
10a. the §13.2a upgrade, where it triggers   (a state_version: 2 payload plus at least one limit
                                 armed by THIS invocation, the seam having passed): set
```

Binding consequences: (i) **a refusal at or above step 9 leaves the payload, the sentinel and the
run guard byte-identical** — nothing has been written, and no fetch happened either, so this is the
one guarded cell where the "nothing happened" claim is *absolute* (Normative vocabulary), and the
§13.2a upgrade of step 10a is below that line, so it never weakens it;
(ii) the sort count is **one** (§9.1a rule 3a's second row keeps its shipped **two** for the
unguarded handler, which no guarded invocation reaches); (iii) every gate keeps its shipped
sentence, position and exit code, and the guard seam adds only the anchored marker of §6.4 when it
is the refusing party; (iv) no `Sync mode:` header moves — this arm never fetches, so there is
nothing to hoist above (§12.2b's hoist is fresh-route-only); and (v) `handleScopedSyncContinue`
itself is untouched, including its `scopedSelectionFromPayload` call, its `internal/cli/sync.go:411`
`TopoSort` and every byte it prints.

**Legacy continuation, `.sync-state.yaml` cell (cell 7) — `handleGuardedLegacySyncContinue`, the
guarded twin of the shipped `handleSyncContinue`.** An unguarded legacy run failed and left
`.sync-state.yaml`; this invocation may arm limits. When it does — `opts.Armed()` — the cell-7
`--continue` dispatches to `handleGuardedLegacySyncContinue` (§19.2), the **same** entry point the
`state_version: 3` `route: legacy` envelope and the cell-4 backup-sentinel residue use, taking its
legacy-state arm. When it does not, the shipped `handleSyncContinue` runs verbatim: same bytes,
same statements, same single `TopoSort` at `internal/cli/sync.go:343`, same output (§17.1).

**The entry point is declared exactly, and it is the structural twin of the scoped one.** Nothing
about its signature, its arm selection or its return domain is left to the implementer:

```go
// internal/cli/sync.go — package cli
//
// handleGuardedLegacySyncContinue is the CONTROLLED legacy continuation and the
// ONLY entry point of all three legacy resume arms: the cell-5 state_version: 3
// route: legacy envelope, the cell-7 real .sync-state.yaml, and the cell-4
// backup-sentinel setup residue of §13.2a's second crash window (and of its
// `{sentinel, guard}` rollback residue). Its parameter
// list is IDENTICAL in shape, types and order to handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue
// above — the two functions differ only in which persisted subject they resume —
// with exactly ONE addition, the `sentinel` view its cell-4 recovery arm resumes
// from, which the scoped twin has no cell for. The §19.2 dispatch passes the same
// values to whichever handler it selects, and it is the ONLY producer of that
// view. The shipped handleSyncContinue is neither called from it nor modified by
// it.
func handleGuardedLegacySyncContinue(feature string, layout externalSyncLayout,
    ws internal.Workspace, push bool, policy internal.SyncRunPolicy, changed map[string]bool,
    state internal.SyncExternalState, sentinel internal.GuardedLegacySentinelView,
    opts planGuardOptions) error
```

**Inputs (exact; each has one source and no other):**

| Parameter | Source at the call site | What it is — and what it is not |
|---|---|---|
| `feature` | `args[0]`, after `internal.GuardFeatureName` | the logical feature name; the handler validates no name of its own |
| `layout` | `resolveExternalSyncLayout(ws, twsRoot, feature)` | the one resolved layout; `layout.FeaturePath`/`WorktreePath`/`WorktreesRoot` are its only path sources, and it resolves no layout of its own (§9.0) |
| `ws` | `internal.RequireWorkspace()` | the workspace the document's `workspace` block and `planLayout(...)` are built from; never re-required, never re-probed |
| `push` | the `--push` flag of **this** invocation | legacy honours the **flag** on both arms, published as `intent.push_source: flag-legacy-continuation` (§13.6 rule 4). A persisted `payload.Push` on the envelope arm is **provenance only** and MUST NOT override it |
| `policy` | the one `resolveSyncPolicy(cmd, ws.Mode)` result | published as `policy.*`. On this route it is provably the legacy default triple, because the I20 refusal above the dispatch rejects every trigger flag on cells 1/7 and on a `route: legacy` cell 5 (§13.6 rule 4a); it never narrows the resumed universe, which is §13.3's full-stack legacy rule |
| `changed` | the same `resolveSyncPolicy` call's map, threaded | the single owned `changed` map (§13.7a rule 9); the handler never calls `cmd.Flags().Changed`. It feeds `route_triggers` and the continuation-mismatch projection, which is `Applies: false` on **both** legacy arms — a legacy resume applies no frozen-axis check beyond I20 (§13.6 rule 4) |
| `state` | `classifySyncState(layout.FeaturePath, newMode)` | the decoded classifier view, threaded. It selects the arm (below) and is the **input** to `internal.InspectExternalPlanState`, never the snapshot itself (§12.5); the handler never re-classifies, and it never reads `.sync-state.yaml`/`.sync-state.v2.yaml` itself. On the cell-7 arm `state.Legacy` **is** the resumed subject — the classifier already decoded it — so a second `internal.LoadSyncState` is a specification violation (§22.14c (ii)) |
| `sentinel` | `internal.InspectGuardedLegacySentinel(layout.FeaturePath, feature)`, evaluated by the §19.2 dispatch **only on cell 4** and threaded in | the one guarded-legacy sentinel view of §13.6 rule 2c: its verdict, its intent block and its verified prior state. It is the zero value (`verdict: not-applicable`) on the cell-5 and cell-7 arms, which never consult it, and the handler never decodes the sentinel itself |
| `opts` | `resolvePlanGuardOptions(cmd)` at §3.3 step 3 | this invocation's limits, approval token and `--plan` bit. `opts.Armed()` already decided the cell-7 dispatch; inside the handler `opts` is the flag-origin limit source of §13.2 and the approval input of the step-8 guard seam. `opts.Plan` is `false` by construction — `--plan --continue` never reaches an executing handler (§3.3 step 6) |

**Arm selection (exact; the classifier's own answer plus the one sentinel verdict, no third
predicate):**

```go
switch state.Cell {
case 5:
    // ENVELOPE arm — a state_version: 3, route: legacy payload. The §19.2
    // dispatch already established internal.PayloadNewMode(state.Payload) ==
    // false, so this arm re-derives no route. Limits: §13.2's per-key table
    // over the persisted values (origin: persisted-payload).
case 7:
    // LEGACY-STATE arm — a real .sync-state.yaml, no payload, no sentinel. The
    // dispatch already established opts.Armed(). The resumed subject is
    // state.Legacy — the value the classifier ALREADY decoded — and this arm
    // MUST NOT call internal.LoadSyncState again (§12.3 step 1, §22.14c (ii)).
    // Limits: this invocation's flags (origin: flags-legacy-continuation).
    //
    // NOTHING PRE-HANDLES A GUARD ON THIS CELL. syncCellLiveGuardRefusal is a
    // pure extraction of the shipped switch, which guards cells 2, 4 and 5 ONLY
    // (internal/cli/sync_modes.go:303-311), and syncCellRefusal returns nil for
    // cell 7; the classifier does not even read the guard here, because
    // AlwaysReadGuard is newMode and a continuation carries no trigger (§12.5).
    // A `.sync-run.lock` beside this subject therefore reaches step 9, where
    // setupGuardedLegacyRunState's ClaimSyncRunGuard is the AUTHORITATIVE
    // live/foreign/invalid ladder — O_EXCL first, then the shipped sentences
    // (§13.2a step 2, §25.103).
case 4:
    // RECOVERY arm — a VALID guarded legacy backup sentinel with no payload:
    // §13.2a crash window 2, or its `{sentinel, guard}` rollback residue — the
    // guard is present in both, and absent only where an operator removed
    // `.sync-run.lock` by hand. The §19.2 dispatch
    // already established internal.GuardedLegacySentinelResumable(state, view)
    // over the ONE sentinel view of §13.6 rule 2c, and already let
    // syncCellLiveGuardRefusal raise the shipped live-guard sentence where the
    // guard is live — FOREIGN OR SELF-RECORDED, because the shipped GuardLive
    // has no self conjunct (§12.8b) — so this arm only ever meets a dead,
    // absent or undecodable guard and never reclaims a live one. The resumed subject is the sentinel's verified prior state; the
    // limits, the frozen validation command and the universe are the sentinel's
    // intent block (origin: persisted-payload, §13.2).
default:
    // Unreachable by construction: §19.2 routes no other cell here. It fails
    // closed with the SHIPPED sentence and adds none of its own.
    return fmt.Errorf("nothing to continue — no sync in progress")
}
```

**Outputs (exact; the return domain is closed):**

| Return | Meaning and rendering |
|---|---|
| `nil` | the resume completed: the shipped legacy tail ran (`Sync complete.`, then the shipped `--push` tail when `push` is true), and the arm cleared exactly the state that arm owns — **all three** arms end at the same guarded teardown, `finalizeScopedSyncRun` → `clearSyncRunState(featurePath, true)`, which removes payload, sentinel and run guard in that order. On the envelope arm that state was inherited; on the legacy-state arm it is the envelope step 9 created in place of the `.sync-state.yaml` it replaced; on the recovery arm it is the sentinel the interrupted setup had already installed plus the payload this invocation completed. A completed resume therefore leaves neither a payload nor a legacy state behind (§13.2a) |
| `*internal.PlanGuardRefusalError` | the step-8 guard seam (or a JIT seam below it) refused. `sync.go`'s `RunE` wraps the return in `planGuardRefusal(cmd, err)`, which writes the **one** anchored `plan-guard: ` line to stderr and returns the marker-free error; exit `1` (§6.4) |
| any other non-`nil` error | a **shipped** sentence, verbatim and marker-free, at exit `1`: a consumed gate row's `Detail` (step 5), a native reclaim refusal on the envelope arm (§12.4), the shipped executor's own failure, or the state-write failure of §13.2a. The handler introduces no sentence of its own in any cell |

It prints nothing of its own: every byte it emits is a shipped sentence or prose line at its
shipped position, and neither arm prints a `Sync mode:` header. It calls neither
`handleSyncContinue` nor `handleScopedSyncContinue` nor `ResolveSyncSelection` nor
`scopedSelectionFromPayload`, and it performs exactly **one** `TopoSort`, inside its one
`InspectExternalPlan` call (§9.1a rule 3, §22.14c).

**The order the operator sees is the SHIPPED order, and the inspection may not hoist a byte of it
(binding, cell-7 arm).** `InspectExternalPlan` measures everything up front, which is what makes
the sort single and the gates single-evaluated — but measuring early MUST NOT publish early. On
this arm the handler emits refusals and prose in exactly the positions
`handleSyncContinue` (`internal/cli/sync.go:311-350`) emits them, from the rows step 4 already
computed:

| # | Shipped statement | Guarded cell-7 equivalent |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | the failed-branch **rebase-in-progress** gate (`rebase still in progress in %s; …`) | row `external-e1`, raised FIRST — **above** any stack-load or sort failure the inspection observed, because the shipped handler tests it before it loads the stack |
| 2 | `LoadStack` failure (`load stack: %w`) | `insp.StackErr`, raised second, verbatim |
| 3 | the failed-branch **existence** gate (`failed branch %q no longer exists in stack`) | row `external-e2` |
| 4 | the configured-**parent** gate (`resolved branch %s still does not contain its configured parent %s`) | row `external-e3` |
| 5 | `fmt.Println(formatSyncStatus(state.FailedBranch, "active", "resolved"))` — the `[~] resolved` line | printed exactly where the shipped handler prints it: after e3 has been consulted and passed, and only when e2 and e3 both **applied** and neither failed — derived from those two rows, never from a re-check |
| 6 | `TopoSort` failure (`cycle detected in stack.yaml`, returned bare) | `insp.SortErr`, raised here — **after** the `[~] resolved` line, exactly as the shipped handler sorts after printing it |
| 7 | `fmt.Printf("Resuming sync with %d pending branch(es)\n", len(state.Pending))` | printed with **`len(state.Legacy.Pending)`** — the count persisted in the legacy state this arm resumes, NOT `len(insp.Remaining)` and NOT the envelope's `Pending`. The two differ whenever the stack changed under the interrupted run, and the shipped number is the one the operator has already seen |
| 8 | `syncWithStackFiltered(…)` | steps 8–10: the guard seam, then the setup of step 9, then `syncWithStackScoped` with the legacy run context |

Binding consequences: (i) **the guard seam sits between the shipped prose and the shipped
executor call**, so a proceeding guarded resume's stdout is byte-equal to the unguarded control's
and a *refusing* one has already printed the shipped `[~] resolved` and `Resuming sync with %d
pending branch(es)` lines on **stdout** before its single anchored `plan-guard: ` line reaches
**stderr** — deliberate, since the prose describes the resume the operator asked for and the two
streams are separate (§3.6, §6.4); (ii) an inspection failure MUST NOT be raised earlier than the
row above gives it — in particular a stack-load or sort failure never precedes the
rebase-in-progress gate, and neither ever precedes it merely because the inspection measured it
first; (iii) nothing in the table is re-evaluated: every row is consumed once, from
`insp.Gates`/`insp.StackErr`/`insp.SortErr` (§22.14c (ii), (iv)); and (iv) the **plan-only** twin of
the same cell keeps §13.7a's declared subject-before-gates order and prints **no** prose at all —
it publishes the same facts as document rows at exit `0` (§3.6 row 2), which is why the reordering
is scoped to `--plan` and this table is scoped to guarded execution.

**The cell-4 recovery arm is the same order with a different first write (binding).** Where §19.2
selects the recovery arm, steps 1–8 are performed over the sentinel's **verified prior state**
instead of `state.Legacy` — that value is the resumed subject, `state.Legacy` on this cell being the
sentinel itself — with the limits, the frozen validation command, `push` provenance and the
universe read from the sentinel's intent block (§13.6 rule 2c). Step 9 does **not** re-write the
sentinel: it is already on disk and already carries this run's intent, so the arm performs only the
guard claim/reclaim of §13.2a's step 2 and the v3 payload write of its step 4, in that order,
skipping the replacement of step 3, with the same
rollback — which, because this invocation did **not** install the sentinel, removes only the
payload it wrote and releases only the guard it claimed
(`guardedLegacySetupProgress{Sentinel: false}`), leaving the sentinel and its backup exactly as
found. The guard step is a **reclaim** on every residue this feature can produce — the crash window
and the failed rollback both leave the guard beside the sentinel — and a **claim** only where an
operator removed `.sync-run.lock` by hand; the arm decides between them from the measured snapshot,
never from provenance. Steps 10–11 are unchanged.

Its prose follows the sentinel's own provenance, and the two cells are total:

| Sentinel | Resumed subject | Rows 5 and 7 of the ordering table |
|---|---|---|
| `prior_legacy_present: true` (an interrupted **cell-7** setup) | the verified prior state | exactly as above: the `[~] resolved` line under the shipped legacy conjunct, then `Resuming sync with %d pending branch(es)` over `len(prior.Pending)` — the same number the interrupted invocation printed |
| `prior_legacy_present: false` (an interrupted **fresh** guarded legacy setup) | none — `Completed` is empty, `FailedBranch` is `""`, and gates e1–e3 are `Applies: false` | **no** resume prose at all: no `[~] resolved`, no `Resuming sync with …` line, exactly as the guarded legacy **fresh** route prints none. The executed universe is §13.3's full-stack legacy set over the current stack, as it would have been |

A recovery arm that re-plans the run, re-selects it, re-freezes its validation command, writes a
second sentinel, or prints a resume line for a fresh-setup sentinel fails §22.24j.

**Steps 10–11 are payload-aware, and that is what makes the envelope true.** Before step 9 there is
no payload, so there is nothing to attach; after it there is one, and every executor decision that
consumes a payload MUST consume *that* one. Six consequences are binding and separately asserted
(§22.14c (vi)–(vii), §22.24i):

- **The executor is `syncWithStackScoped`, entered with the run context, on every one of the three
  arms.** The cell-5 envelope arm, the cell-7 arm and the cell-4 recovery arm all call
  `syncWithStackScoped(feature, layout, stack, insp.Order, done, run, guard)` with a non-`nil`
  `run` whose `Route` is `legacy` and whose `Payload` is the envelope this invocation holds — the
  one it inherited, created at step 9, or completed on the recovery arm. There is no second
  executor, no `syncWithStackFiltered` call and no `run == nil` call site on any of them.
- **Git argv, selection and output stay legacy and full-stack.** The route field, not a selection,
  carries legacy semantics: `run.Route == legacy` makes the three predicates answer exactly as
  `run == nil` does, so the executor takes its legacy arm — `--update-refs`, archived entries,
  `markUpdatedAncestors`, the unfiltered completion gate, no anchor skip, no `Sync mode:` header —
  and the rebase argv sequence matches the flagless control's for the same remaining set **element
  for element, with exactly one intended exception: the `--onto` operand is the pinned full SHA
  the plan resolved and the JIT seam revalidated, where the unguarded control passes the ref name**
  (§10.5). Shape, flag set, cutoff operand, branch operand, order, cwd, environment and stdout are
  identical; the plain-rebase arm is not converted to `--onto` (§12.3's fresh legacy rule,
  §22.14c (vi)).
- **A failure updates the v3 payload rather than writing a real legacy state.** `syncFailure`
  branches on `run != nil && run.Payload != nil` and calls `saveScopedSyncFailure`
  (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:256-263`), so the interrupted run is persisted as
  `stage: failed` + `FailedBranch` + recomputed `Completed`/`Pending` **in the envelope**, and
  `saveIncompleteSync` is never reached. A real `.sync-state.yaml` written beside the payload would
  be cell 8 (`two unfinished syncs are recorded`), which is precisely the state this arm must not
  create — the same rule the guarded legacy fresh route already carries.
- **Validation is the frozen command, not a per-entry re-read.** `run.validate()` uses the payload's
  persisted `TestCommand` — which step 9 wrote from this invocation's frozen value, and which the
  recovery arm reads from the sentinel's intent block rather than re-freezing — so the
