| the row's `ancestry` (`StackEdge.Status`/`Reason`, §4.2) | both modes, every row | continuously, as evidence | **fact only** — never a blocker, never `runnable: false` (§7.1 rank-4 rule 1) |
| the external completion gate (`Sync incomplete; stale stack edges remain:`) | external only | **after** the executor's rebases (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:220-226`) — a **postcondition** | rank 4 `preflight-refused` in **exactly one** cell, the rows-less push-only continuation, where no rebase of this invocation can change the answer (§7.1 rank-4 rule 2, §22.12b (iii)) |
| the checkout `conflict`-stage gate (`after conflict resolution, %s is not descended from base %s`) | checkout `--continue` only, stage `conflict` only | after the rebase-in-progress short-circuit and before this resume records the post-SHA, on a row the operator resolved by hand (`internal/checkout_sync.go:875-881`) | rank 3 `state-refused`, document-level, by the general rule of this subsection — the recovery-state class, because the fact it judges is the operator's own recorded resolution — through **exactly one** probe (§13.7 gate e) |
| the checkout `rebased`-stage ancestry gate (`%s not descended from %s after rebase`) | checkout `--continue` only, stage `rebased` only | **before** anything this resume runs for the current row (`resumeFromRebased`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:941-953`) — a **precondition** of the described invocation | rank 4 `preflight-refused`, document-level, projected on every `rebased`-stage continuation through **exactly one** probe (§13.7 gate e) |
| the checkout **whole-plan finalization** postcondition (`final ancestry check failed: %s not descendant of %s`) | checkout only, **executing** routes only (fresh and continuation), guarded and unguarded alike | **after** `SaveStack` has written every entry's `LastBaseSHA` and **before** `tx.Stage = StageRestoring`, over **every** `tx.Plan` entry (`finalizeTransaction`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:1191-1200`) — a postcondition of the whole run | **not a blocker of any rank, in any cell** — no `blockers[]` row, no `refusal.kind`, no `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` token, no change to `runnable`; disclosed only as the postcondition it is (rule F below) |

They cannot collide: the second is external-only and needs an **empty** remaining rebase set, the
third needs `tx.Stage == conflict`, the fourth needs `tx.Stage == rebased`, the fifth is reachable
only *below* every seam this feature adds, and the first is never a blocker at all — one `tx.Stage`
value selects at most one checkout row, and the two modes select at most one of the remaining two.
Two evaluations of `gitIsAncestor` are deliberately projected by **nobody**: the one `processBranch`
and `resumeFromSwitched` reach *after* a rebase this invocation performed, which is a postcondition
of work in progress and falls under rank-4 rule 1 exactly as a stale edge on a row about to be
rebased does; and the `conflict` arm's fall-through into `resumeFromRebased`, which re-evaluates the
predicate its own rank 3 gate just satisfied and can therefore only differ through a race, which is
a JIT question and not a plan one.

**Rule E — the continuation-gate ancestry probe budget is exactly two cells, one probe each
(binding).** A controlled checkout continuation **inspection** — plan-only and guarded executing
alike — issues:

| `tx.Stage` | `git merge-base --is-ancestor` processes the inspection issues for a continuation gate |
|---|---|
| `conflict`, where the rebase-in-progress short-circuit did **not** fire | **exactly one**, over `(entry.NewBaseSHA, entry.Branch)` for `entry := tx.Plan[tx.CurrentIndex]` |
| `conflict`, where that short-circuit **did** fire | **zero** — the shipped arm returns its sentence above the gate, so the projection stops there too |
| `rebased` | **exactly one**, over the same persisted pair, independently of the row above |
| `planned`, `switched`, `rebasing`, `validating`, `restoring`, `completed` | **zero** |

Neither cell borrows the other's probe or its verdict: a `conflict`-stage inspection issues **one**
probe and never a second for the fall-through into `resumeFromRebased`, and a `rebased`-stage
inspection issues its own **one** probe rather than reusing a `conflict`-stage answer. Both are
controlled-path processes: the **unguarded** resume issues only the shipped ones, unchanged, and the
guarded executing route's native arm then evaluates the shipped gate again where it ships (§13.7
gate e, rule 8a). The finalization postcondition of the table's fifth row adds **no** plan-time
probe at all.

**Rule F — the finalization postcondition is disclosed, never projected (binding).**
`finalizeTransaction` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1191-1200`) re-checks **every** `tx.Plan` entry
with `gitIsAncestor(opts.RepoDir, pe.NewBaseSHA, pe.Branch)` and may return
`fmt.Sprintf("final ancestry check failed: %s not descendant of %s", pe.Branch, pe.Base)`. It is an
**executing-only** fact, and this feature neither moves it, re-ranks it nor pre-empts it:

1. **It is not a plan preflight and not a JIT input.** No `--plan` document publishes a blocker,
   warning, refusal kind or controlled-path token for it, no `runnable` value moves because of it,
   and no guard or JIT seam evaluates it: the drift it detects is a **future concurrent ref move**
   that no plan-time or seam-time read can prove, so refusing on it before the run would refuse
   runs that will succeed. A plan **may** disclose it as a postcondition in prose (§20) exactly as
   the external completion gate is disclosed; that disclosure adds no document field, no schema key
   and no enum member (§4.1, §4.6, §7.1).
2. **Its position and residue are shipped and stay shipped.** It runs *after* the `SaveStack`
   `LastBaseSHA` mutation and *before* `tx.Stage = StageRestoring`, so on failure `stack.yaml` may
   **already** record the new bases while no restore, no push, no transaction delete and no lock
   release has happened. The shipped arm writes no `FailureKind`, no `FailureMsg` and no
   transaction, so `.checkout-sync.tx.yaml` and `.checkout-sync.lock` **both survive** exactly as
   they were left; nothing in this feature may delete, rewrite, roll back or "tidy" either
   (§12.7).
3. **The sentence is native and marker-free.** It is returned as an ordinary error, never wrapped in
   `*PlanGuardRefusalError`, never given a `plan-guard:` marker and never given the
   `state-preserved: ` prefix of §6.4 — the refusing party is the shipped finalizer, not the guard
   — and it is byte-identical on the guarded and unguarded routes, which are asserted as a matched
   pair (§22.13n).
4. **A probe failure keeps its shipped shape too**: `gitIsAncestor` returning an error is returned
   verbatim by the shipped loop, and no rank 5.9 row, marker or re-wording is added to it.

**Two of those sentences are conditional, and the condition is the shipped one.** The external
`failed branch %q no longer exists in stack` and
`resolved branch %s still does not contain its configured parent %s` gates are projected **only**
where the shipped resume evaluates them: on a payload arm, where
`payload.FailedBranch != "" && !payloadCompleted(payload, payload.FailedBranch)`
(`internal/cli/sync.go:386`), and on the real legacy `.sync-state.yaml` arm, where
`state.FailedBranch != ""` (`:326`). A **push-failure** resume — the entry is recorded in both
`Completed` and `FailedBranch` — makes both gates `Applies: false`, so neither sentence can be
published as a blocker, no parent edge is re-checked and no `[~] resolved` line is printed on
either route (§12.3, §13.7a step 5, §22.14b). The failed-branch **rebase-in-progress** gate keeps
the bare `FailedBranch != ""` condition of the shipped code on every arm.

**The external completion gate is not in that set, and is not a continuation gate at all.**
`staleStackEdgesFiltered` (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:220-226`) is evaluated by the executor
**after** its rebases, so on any continuation that still has rebase rows it describes work this
invocation is about to perform. Projecting it as a pre-run blocker would refuse — or mark
`runnable: false` on — exactly the resume that fixes it. Binding:

- On a continuation **with** remaining rebase rows, and on every fresh run, the plan publishes the
  current edge state as the row's `ancestry` fact (§4.2) and nothing else: no blocker, no rank, no
  `runnable: false`, no suppression (§7.1 rank-4 rule, §11.2).
- On a **rows-less push-only continuation** — `RemainingRebaseEntries` yields no rebase row and the
  remaining work is the push (checkout: the push and/or the restore) — the executor really does
  evaluate the gate before the push, and no rebase can change its answer, so the plan projects it
  as rank 4 `preflight-refused` with the shipped sentences byte-identical
  (`Sync incomplete; stale stack edges remain:` and `  [!] %s does not contain parent %s` per
  edge), `runnable: false`, and `preflight-refused` in `push.blocked_by[]` (§14.3). Its
  `push.targets[]` is **non-empty** wherever entries were rebased and never pushed: the membership
  rule for that cell is `payload.Completed ∪ {FailedBranch}` minus `payload.Pushed` (§14.1a
  rule 10d), and those targets are exactly the work the refusal is about.
- On the executing route the gate keeps its shipped position, bytes, `syncFailure` persistence and
  exit `1` on every route, guarded or not; it is marker-free, and its guidance is post-mutation
  (§6.4).

**Rule G — a projected gate is a `PlanGateResult`, and exactly one function turns it into a
blocker.** Every gate above — the checkout ladders of §13.7, the external ladder of §13.7a step 5
and the I19 containment value of §13.7 step 0 — is carried as the typed `PlanGateResult` of §13.7,
in the ladder's own order, on `CheckoutPlanInspection.Gates`, `ExternalPlanInspection.Gates` and
`RebasePlanRequest.Gates`. Nothing on those paths is a `[]PlanBlocker`, and no site converts one
into the other except:

```go
// internal/rebase_planner.go — package internal
//
// GateBlockers is the ONLY gate → blocker conversion in the tree. It is called
// by BuildRebasePlan and by nothing else, and it is total over the rows it is
// given:
//   - a gate with Applies == false or Failed == false contributes NO row;
//   - a failing gate contributes exactly one PlanBlocker{Kind: g.Kind,
//     Entry: g.Entry (""  ⇒ entry: null), Detail: g.Detail}, with the shipped
//     sentence copied verbatim and never re-worded, re-wrapped or re-formatted;
//   - input order is the ladder order, and the output preserves it; §7.1's rank
//     ordering and §7.2's collapse are applied afterwards, by SelectPrimaryRefusal,
//     over the combined blocker set.
// It performs no probe, issues no Git process and invents no sentence.
func GateBlockers(gates []PlanGateResult) []PlanBlocker

// GateControlledTokens collects the controlled-path tokens the same rows carry
// (§4.6): the sorted, de-duplicated union of every failing gate's Controlled
// slice — in v1 exactly the live-FOREIGN owner arms' `live-owner-concurrency`,
// which the pre-acquisition snapshot observed (§11.2 cause 3) and the projected
// gate re-publishes rather than re-deriving. It is the gate half of
// guard.execute_blocked_by[]; the three fetch-effect tokens come from
// PlanFetchPlan.Controlled and `owner-artefact-undecodable` from §12.5, and the
// builder unions the three sources into the one sorted, de-duplicated array. The
// domain is unchanged at five tokens.
func GateControlledTokens(gates []PlanGateResult) []ControlledPathBlocker
```

Three consequences are binding: (i) a `PlanGateResult` may be **read** by the route that projected
it — that is how a guarded route knows whether its own ladder refused — but only `BuildRebasePlan`
turns it into a document row; (ii) an inspection that wanted to publish a blocker with no shipped
gate behind it — the rank 5.0/5.05/5.06 enumeration rows — carries it on `PlanFetchPlan.Blockers`
as a `PlanBlocker`, which is a different member with a different producer, so the two can never be
confused; and (iii) assigning a `[]PlanBlocker` into a `Gates` member does not compile, which is
the mechanical form of this rule (§9.1a rule 5, §22.33g).

### 13.6 Persisted guard state: versions, routes and downgrade safety (§25.9)

A guarded run's limits are *load-bearing*: if an older binary resumes that run without them, the
guard the operator asked for silently disappears exactly where it matters — mid-run, with branches
already rewritten. **Guarded state therefore fails closed to older binaries.** An "unsupported
downgrade" statement is explicitly *not* sufficient; the preservation is carried by the state
itself.

**1. Version constants.** `internal/sync_run_state.go` keeps its two shipped constants at their
shipped values and gains two guarded ones:

```go
const SyncRunStateVersion         = 2 // unguarded new-mode payload — unchanged
const SyncRunStateGuardedVersion  = 3 // guarded envelope, either route
const CheckoutTransactionVersion        = 2 // unguarded new-mode transaction — unchanged
const CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion = 3 // guarded transaction, either route
```

**2. Birth rule (where a version is chosen for a NEW run).** The version is decided **once, at the
run's birth**, and the only thing that may ever change it afterwards is the declared upgrade of
rule 2b — no save, failure write, stage update or teardown does:

| Fresh run | `state_version` written | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| No-flag / unguarded legacy checkout | **omitted** (as shipped) | shipped legacy transaction |
| Unguarded new-mode checkout | `2` (as shipped) | shipped v2 transaction |
| Unguarded new-mode external | `2` (as shipped) | shipped v2 payload + sentinel + guard |
| Unguarded legacy external | none — `.sync-state.yaml` on failure only (as shipped) | shipped legacy state |
| **Guarded** checkout, either route | `3` | v2-shaped transaction plus `route` and the two limits |
| **Guarded** new-mode external | `3` | v2-shaped payload plus `route: new-mode` and the two limits |
| **Guarded** legacy external | `3` | the **backup sentinel** of rule 2c (marker + intent + the replaced document, or `prior_legacy_present: false` on a fresh run) plus a payload with `route: legacy`, the two limits, the frozen validation command, and full-stack `Selected`/`Pending` |
| Plan-only, any route | **nothing at all** | `--plan` writes no state, no lock, no sentinel (§18.1) |

The run guard document (`.sync-run.lock`) keeps `state_version: 2` in every cell: it carries only
`pid`/`created`/`token`, it authorizes no resume, and `writeSyncGuardExclusive` is therefore
**unchanged**. Downgrade safety lives entirely in the document that *does* authorize a resume.

**2a. Birth implementation (exact signatures; `setupSyncRunState` is *not* unchanged).** The birth
rule needs a writer, and the shipped one cannot express it: `setupSyncRunState`
(`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:385-422`) builds its payload with
`internal.NewSyncRunState(feature, marker, token, sel.Policy)`, which hard-codes
`StateVersion: SyncRunStateVersion`, and `SaveSyncRunState` then re-forces that constant
(`internal/sync_run_state.go:122-124`). Any earlier statement that `setupSyncRunState` is unchanged
is withdrawn; the exact changes are:

| Symbol | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `NewSyncRunState(feature, marker, token string, policy SyncRunPolicy) *SyncRunState` | `internal/sync_run_state.go:144-169` | **signature and body unchanged.** It keeps writing `StateVersion: SyncRunStateVersion` (`2`), so every `internal` caller and every unguarded run is untouched |
| `SaveSyncRunState` | `internal/sync_run_state.go:122-131` | rule 3: preserve a non-zero `s.StateVersion`, default a zero one to `SyncRunStateVersion`, refuse any other value. Without this the guarded `3` would be silently rewritten to `2` on the first save |
| `setupSyncRunState` | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go:385` | **gains exactly one trailing parameter**, `birth syncRunStateBirth`, and applies it to the payload **before** the first `SaveSyncRunState`. Nothing else in the body moves: the claim → sentinel → payload order, the three step hooks, the two failure teardowns and the error sentences are byte-identical |
| `setupGuardedLegacyRunState` | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go` | new; the guarded **legacy** envelope of §12.3, used by the guarded legacy **fresh** route and by the §13.2a setup of the cell-7 continuation. **One owner file, chosen to be the one that already owns `setupSyncRunState`, `clearSyncRunState` and the failure writers** — no second declaration exists in `internal/cli/sync.go` or anywhere else, and `sync.go` only *calls* it (§19.2). Its two writes are the conditional **backup sentinel** and the v3 payload, in the four-step order of §13.2a, with the shipped sentences, `birth.Route = "legacy"` and the full-stack `Selected`/`Pending` provenance. Its guard claim keeps the shipped **first** position; its continuation-only parameter and its own capture/rollback are declared below |
| `upgradeGuardedSyncRunState` | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go` | new; the external **upgrade** writer of rule 2b — the one-line re-versioning of an existing `state_version: 2` payload (`StateVersion`, `Route`, the two limit pointers, the payload's own frozen command written back byte-identically, then one `SaveSyncRunState`). **Same owner file as `setupSyncRunState` and `setupGuardedLegacyRunState`, and declared nowhere else**: `internal/cli/sync.go` only *calls* it, from `handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue`'s step 10a (§12.3, §19.2, §22.24i (x)) |

```go
// internal/cli/sync_modes.go — the one new parameter; its zero value is the shipped behaviour
type syncRunStateBirth struct {
    StateVersion int    // 0 ⇒ leave NewSyncRunState's 2; 3 ⇒ guarded envelope
    Route        string // "" ⇒ omitted (shipped); "new-mode" | "legacy" on a guarded run
    MaxPerEntry  *int   // nil ⇒ key omitted; non-nil ⇒ persisted, including 0
    MaxTotal     *int
}

func setupSyncRunState(layout externalSyncLayout, feature, marker, token string,
    sel internal.SyncSelection, push bool, testCommand, validationSource string,
    birth syncRunStateBirth) (*internal.SyncRunState, error)

// setupGuardedLegacyRunState writes the guarded LEGACY envelope over the exact
// four-step, crash-safe order of §13.2a: capture the CURRENT .sync-state.yaml
// bytes (absent ⇒ nil, which is every fresh run, since a plain run over a real
// legacy state is refused above this point) → ClaimSyncRunGuard (the shipped
// O_EXCL claim, FIRST, exactly as setupSyncRunState orders it, so two new
// binaries racing over one feature cannot both reach the replacement) → the
// CONDITIONAL atomic write of
// the BACKUP SENTINEL over that same path (an exclusive create where nothing
// was captured, a compare-and-swap over the captured bytes where something was)
// → atomic v3 payload write → return the payload. The
// sentinel carries the marker, this run's whole intent block and the captured
// document with its SHA-256 (§13.6 rule 2c), which is what makes every crash
// window recoverable. The steps keep the shipped sentences and the shipped
// SyncStageInitializing hook indices, which name ARTEFACTS (0 = guard,
// 1 = sentinel, 2 = payload) and are therefore fired here in the order
// 3 → 0 → 1 → 2; the capture adds index 3.
//
// `universe` is the full-stack legacy Selected list in the invocation's one
// TopoSort order and `pending` is the remaining set (§13.3); both are the fresh
// route's own values on a fresh run. The continuation-only `carry` parameter
// holds what a cell-7 setup (§13.2a) must not lose:
//
//   carry — the legacy state's Completed (verbatim, in its persisted order),
//           its FailedBranch and its persisted pending COUNT, written into the
//           payload and the sentinel's intent block so the resumed `done` set
//           and the shipped `Resuming sync with %d pending branch(es)` number
//           survive the transition; the zero value on a fresh run.
//
// The captured bytes are owned by this function, not by its caller: on any
// failure at or below the claim — a writer error, a claim refusal or a
// boundary hook that RETURNS an error — it rolls back through
// rollbackGuardedLegacyRunState in reverse creation order (payload →
// the CONDITIONAL undo of the sentinel replacement: RestoreSyncStateBytes over
// the captured bytes, or RemoveSyncStateIfUnchanged where there were none —
// never an unconditional RemoveSyncState — → guard, released LAST so the undo
// itself is protected), so a failed setup leaves a
// byte-identical legacy state and no payload, sentinel or guard, and a failed
// ROLLBACK returns the measured residue instead of pretending (§13.2a). Residue
// is reachable only from a process that died, never from a returned error.
type guardedLegacyCarry struct {
    Completed         []string
    FailedBranch      string
    PriorPendingCount int
}

func setupGuardedLegacyRunState(layout externalSyncLayout, feature, marker, token string,
    universe, pending []string, push bool, testCommand, validationSource string,
    birth syncRunStateBirth, carry guardedLegacyCarry) (*internal.SyncRunState, error)
```

Binding:

1. The birth values are applied to the payload struct **before** the first `SaveSyncRunState`, so
   the guarded envelope is complete on its very first byte on disk. A *birth* is never written at
   version `2` and then patched into an envelope; the only later transition is rule 2b's
   armed-continuation upgrade, which is a different event, with its own trigger, its own position
   and its own writer (§13.2a).
2. `syncRunStateBirth{}` — the value every unguarded call site passes — leaves the payload exactly
   as shipped: `StateVersion` stays `2`, `route` is omitted, neither limit key is written. This is
   a §19.4 *signature-only* change, and the unguarded on-disk bytes are asserted byte-identical
   (§22.24a).
3. The **frozen validation command** does not need a new parameter: it travels through the shipped
   `testCommand`/`validationSource` arguments, which the guarded routes now source from
   `planGuardRun.Validation` (resolved once above the plan, §12.2b, §15.5a) instead of from a
   second `internal.LoadConfig()` read under the claim. The unguarded call sites pass exactly what
   they pass today.
4. `clearSyncRunState` keeps its shipped body and its shipped signature; guarded post-claim
   rollback is the separate `rollbackGuardedRunState` of §12.2c rule 2.
5. Checkout's twin needs no new signature: `RunCheckoutSync` already builds its
   `CheckoutTransaction` literal, so a guarded run sets `StateVersion =
   CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion`, `Route`, `MaxReplayPerEntry` and `MaxReplayTotal` on that
   literal before the first `SaveCheckoutTransaction` (§19.2).
6. **The complete, closed set of sites that may write a `state_version` other than the loaded one
   is five, and each is classified as a *birth* or an *upgrade*.** The distinction is not
   cosmetic: a birth creates a document that did not exist, an upgrade re-versions one that did,
   and only the two upgrades are bounded by §13.2a's four trigger conjuncts.

   | Site | File | Class | Writes |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `setupSyncRunState(…, birth)` | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go` | **birth** | `2` with a zero `birth` (every unguarded run), `3` with a guarded one |
   | `setupGuardedLegacyRunState` | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go` | **birth** | always `3`, `route: legacy` — on the guarded legacy **fresh** route *and* on the cell-7 continuation, where §13.2a's trigger selects it |
   | the `CheckoutTransaction` literal in `RunCheckoutSync` | `internal/checkout_sync.go` | **birth** | absent/`2` unguarded, `3` guarded |
   | `upgradeGuardedSyncRunState` | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go` | **upgrade** | `2` → `3` on an existing external payload |
   | `upgradeGuardedCheckoutTransaction` | `internal/checkout_sync.go` | **upgrade** | absent/`1`/`2` → `3` on an existing transaction |

   `setupGuardedLegacyRunState` is a **birth** site even when §13.2a invokes it, because its
   semantics are creation, not re-versioning: it captures, claims, replaces a *different* file with
   a sentinel and writes a payload that did not exist, and it can leave residues no upgrade can
   (§13.2a's crash windows). Calling it "the third upgrade writer" would put a four-step,
   rollback-bearing creator under an exclusivity assertion written for two one-line re-versioners,
   so the assertion of §22.24i (x) enumerates **three birth sites and two upgrade writers**
   separately and asserts each class's own properties. `SaveSyncRunState`/`SaveCheckoutTransaction`
   preserve whatever version they are handed (rule 3) and are therefore not sites at all.

**Tests (§23, §22.24a).** The eight birth cells are asserted on disk after the *first* save, not
only at the end of the run; `setupSyncRunState(..., syncRunStateBirth{})` is asserted to produce a
file byte-identical to the shipped one; a guarded call is asserted to produce `state_version: 3`
with `route` and both limit keys, including a persisted `0`; and a save/load/save round trip is
asserted not to rewrite the version in either direction — the **only** version transition in the
tree being rule 2b's upgrade.

**2b. The one declared version transition: the armed-continuation upgrade (§13.2a).** A run whose
birth was unguarded becomes guarded — and its state becomes a `state_version: 3` envelope — exactly
when a `--continue` arms a limit over it and that invocation's guard seam passes, at the position
§13.2a fixes per route, below the seam and above the next Git mutation. It is the **only** rule in
this specification that writes a version other than the birth one, and it is bounded by five
properties, each of which is separately asserted (§22.24i):

1. **It is a promotion, never a demotion or a re-decision.** `2 → 3` and *version-absent* → `3` are
   the only transitions; `3 → 2`, `3 → absent` and any rewrite of an already-guarded subject are
   forbidden, and the `route` it writes is the value `PayloadNewMode`/`TransactionNewMode` already
   derived from the subject as loaded — so no run's route, gates, verbs or executor change. On the
   `.sync-state.yaml` arm there is no version to promote — a legacy state carries none — so the
   transition is expressed as a **birth**: `setupGuardedLegacyRunState` creates the v3 envelope in
   place of that file (rule 2a binding 6), with `route: legacy` fixed by construction rather than
   inherited from a version. The run's *effective* transition is still exactly one step, and the
   exclusivity assertion classes the site as a birth (§22.24i (x)).
2. **It carries the guard, and only the guard.** `state_version`, `route`, the two limit pointers
   and the frozen validation command; every other field byte-identical; no approval token, no
   `guard_enabled`, no digest key (§13.1 rule 2).
3. **It is unreachable without a control flag on that very invocation** (§13.2a trigger
   conjunct 3), so no unguarded run and no unguarded resume can produce it — §17.1's state-shape
   freeze is untouched.
4. **It fails closed to old binaries**, exactly as a guarded birth does (rule 5), and that is the
   declared cost of keeping the operator's limit alive across a re-interruption.
5. **A failed write leaves the pre-upgrade state intact and moves no ref** (§13.2a's save-failure
   rule), so the run remains resumable by both binaries.

**2c. The guarded legacy sentinel — a v3 extension of `.sync-state.yaml` that carries the prior
document, the run's intent, and a marker an old binary fails closed on.** A guarded legacy setup
must replace the operator's `.sync-state.yaml`, and a replacement that only *marks* the file
destroys recovery information at the instant it lands. The replacement is therefore one document
that is simultaneously (i) a shipped-shaped sentinel, (ii) this run's complete intent, and (iii) a
byte-exact, checksummed backup of the document it replaced. It is written to the **same path**
(`.sync-state.yaml`) — no new runtime file is introduced anywhere in this feature — and it is
installed by exactly one conditional atomic write (§13.2a step 2).

```go
// internal/syncstate.go — additive; the shipped SyncState, SaveSyncState,
// LoadSyncState, DeleteSyncState and HasSyncState keep their exact bodies.

// GuardedLegacySentinelVersion is the guarded legacy sentinel's own version. It
// is deliberately a SEPARATE constant from SyncRunStateGuardedVersion: the
// payload and the sentinel are different documents with different readers.
const GuardedLegacySentinelVersion = 3

// GuardedLegacySentinel is .sync-state.yaml as a guarded legacy run writes it.
// The shipped SyncState is embedded INLINE and written exactly as the shipped
// sentinel writes it, so a v1.2.15 binary — whose decoder ignores unknown keys
// — sees a sentinel and nothing else, and fails closed on the marker in every
// cell (rule 5, §13.2a's old-binary table).
type GuardedLegacySentinel struct {
    SyncState `yaml:",inline"`   // started_at, failed_branch = the marker, pending/completed/
                                 // skipped = [], byte-for-byte the shipped sentinel shape

    GuardedStateVersion int    `yaml:"guarded_state_version"` // always 3
    Route               string `yaml:"route"`                 // always "legacy"
    Feature             string `yaml:"feature"`
    Marker              string `yaml:"marker"`                // MUST equal FailedBranch
    OwnerToken          string `yaml:"owner_token"`           // the token step 2 claimed with
    CreatedAt           string `yaml:"created_at"`            // RFC3339 UTC
    WriterPID           int    `yaml:"writer_pid"`            // diagnostic only; never a verdict

    MaxReplayPerEntry *int  `yaml:"max_replay_per_entry,omitempty"` // the EFFECTIVE limits, so a
    MaxReplayTotal    *int  `yaml:"max_replay_total,omitempty"`     // persisted 0 survives
    Push              bool   `yaml:"push"`                          // provenance; the flag still wins
    TestCommand       string `yaml:"test_command,omitempty"`        // the FROZEN validation command
    ValidationSource  string `yaml:"validation_source,omitempty"`   // its provenance. There is NO
                                                                    // digest member and no
                                                                    // validation_digest key: §15's
                                                                    // identity is DERIVED from
                                                                    // TestCommand by whoever needs
                                                                    // it (§13.1 rule 2, §25.3)

    Universe          []string `yaml:"universe"`             // the full-stack Selected list in the
                                                             // invocation's ONE TopoSort order
    PendingIntent     []string `yaml:"pending_intent"`       // the remaining set of §13.3
    CarriedCompleted  []string `yaml:"carried_completed"`    // the prior state's Completed, verbatim
    CarriedFailed     string   `yaml:"carried_failed_branch"`// the prior state's FailedBranch
    PriorPendingCount int      `yaml:"prior_pending_count"`  // len(prior.Pending) — the number the
                                                             // shipped resume prints (§12.3 row 7)

    PriorLegacyPresent bool   `yaml:"prior_legacy_present"`            // false on a FRESH run only
    PriorLegacySHA256  string `yaml:"prior_legacy_sha256,omitempty"`   // 64-lower-hex over the bytes
    PriorLegacyBase64  string `yaml:"prior_legacy_base64,omitempty"`   // std base64 of the CAPTURED
                                                                       // bytes, verbatim
}

// SaveGuardedLegacySentinel installs the sentinel at .sync-state.yaml through
// ONE conditional atomic write at the shipped 0644 mode. `expect` is the
// captured prior bytes; nil means "expect the path to be absent" (the fresh
// route). The write refuses — writing nothing — when the current file is not
// what `expect` says it is, so the path is either the old bytes/absent or the
// complete sentinel, never anything between.
func SaveGuardedLegacySentinel(featurePath string, s *GuardedLegacySentinel, expect []byte) error

// RemoveSyncStateIfUnchanged is the fresh route's rollback counterpart of
// RestoreSyncStateBytes: it removes .sync-state.yaml only while its bytes are
// still `expect` AND no payload exists beside it, returning ErrSyncStateChanged
// or ErrSyncStateHasPayload otherwise and removing nothing.
func RemoveSyncStateIfUnchanged(featurePath string, expect []byte) error
```

**The safe inspector, and the closed verdict domain.** The classifier decodes `.sync-state.yaml`
into the shipped `SyncState` and therefore cannot see the extension, and it is **not** changed
(§12.5 rule 2). One additive, read-only `internal` producer decodes and *validates* the extension,
and it is the only place that does:

```go
// internal/syncstate.go — additive, read-only, no write, no lock, no process
type GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict string

const (
    SentinelNotApplicable GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "not-applicable" // the zero value
    SentinelAbsent        GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "absent"
    SentinelNotGuarded    GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "not-guarded"    // real legacy state, or
                                                                          // a PLAIN shipped sentinel
    SentinelValid         GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "valid"
    SentinelSymlink       GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "symlink"
    SentinelUnreadable    GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "unreadable"
    SentinelUnsupported   GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "unsupported-version"
    SentinelCorrupt       GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "corrupt"
    SentinelForeign       GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "foreign"
    SentinelHashMismatch  GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict = "hash-mismatch"
)

// GuardedLegacySentinelView is the decided view. Sentinel and Prior are
// non-nil ONLY under SentinelValid, so no caller can resume from a document
// this ladder did not accept.
type GuardedLegacySentinelView struct {
    Verdict  GuardedLegacySentinelVerdict
    Path     string
    Sentinel *GuardedLegacySentinel // the decoded extension
    Prior    *SyncState             // the VERIFIED backed-up legacy state; nil when
                                    // PriorLegacyPresent is false
    Version  int                    // the raw guarded_state_version, for the unsupported sentence
    Err      error                  // the underlying I/O or decode error; sanitized by cli
}

// InspectGuardedLegacySentinel performs ONE Lstat and at most ONE read of a
// regular file, follows no symlink, and applies the ordered ladder below. It
// refuses nothing and prints nothing: internal decides, cli speaks.
func InspectGuardedLegacySentinel(featurePath, feature string) GuardedLegacySentinelView

// GuardedLegacySentinelResumable is the ONE dispatch predicate (§19.2): a
// classifier cell 4 — sentinel present, payload absent — whose sentinel this
// ladder accepted. It is evaluated on NO other cell.
func GuardedLegacySentinelResumable(st SyncExternalState, v GuardedLegacySentinelView) bool
```

**The ladder is ordered and total; the first failing clause decides, and only `valid` resumes.**

| # | Clause | Verdict when it fails |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `Lstat`: the path exists, is not a symlink and is a regular file | `absent` / `symlink` / `unreadable` |
| 2 | the bytes read and decode as YAML into `GuardedLegacySentinel`, and the document is non-empty | `unreadable` |
| 3 | `isSyncMarker(FailedBranch)` — i.e. the classifier would call this a sentinel | `not-guarded` (a **real** legacy state: cell 7 semantics, untouched) |
| 4 | `guarded_state_version` is present and non-zero | `not-guarded` (a **plain** shipped sentinel: every shipped cell-4 answer stands verbatim) |
| 5 | `guarded_state_version == GuardedLegacySentinelVersion` | `unsupported-version` (a newer writer: fail closed, never guess) |
| 6 | `route == "legacy"`, `marker == failed_branch`, `isSyncMarker(marker)`, `owner_token != ""`, `feature != ""`, `universe`/`pending_intent`/`carried_completed` decoded as arrays | `corrupt` |
| 7 | `feature` equals the feature this invocation is operating on | `foreign` |
| 8 | `prior_legacy_present == false` ⇒ `prior_legacy_base64`, `prior_legacy_sha256` absent, `prior_pending_count == 0`, `carried_completed` empty, `carried_failed_branch` empty | `corrupt` |
| 9 | `prior_legacy_present == true` ⇒ `prior_legacy_base64` decodes, `prior_legacy_sha256` is 64-lower-hex **and** equals SHA-256 of the decoded bytes | `hash-mismatch` |
| 10 | those decoded bytes decode as a `SyncState` whose `failed_branch` is **not** a marker (a sentinel can never back up a sentinel), and `prior_pending_count == len(prior.Pending)` | `corrupt` |
| 11 | everything above held | **`valid`** — `Sentinel` and (where present) `Prior` are populated |

**Outcomes per verdict (composed in `cli`, where `feature` is in scope; `internal` decides).** Only
`valid` enables the recovery arm; every other guarded verdict fails closed, removes nothing and
leaves `.sync-state.yaml` byte-identical:

| Verdict | Verb | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `not-guarded` | any | **every shipped cell-4 (or cell-7) answer, verbatim.** No new sentence, no new arm, no behaviour change |
| `absent` | any | **not a verdict about a document — the path vanished between the classifier and this read.** `cli` re-classifies once and dispatches that cell's ordinary answer (§12.8b's vanished-state row): a plain run continues as a fresh run with no state, `--continue` gets the shipped `nothing to continue — no sync in progress` at exit `1`, `--abort` the shipped `Nothing to abort — no sync in progress.` at exit `0`. No sentence of this section is emitted and no backup is claimed to exist |
| `valid` | `--continue` | the **recovery arm** of §12.3 (claim/reclaim, payload, guarded legacy continuation) |
| `valid` | `--abort` | §12.8b's clearing arm and its own success line — the backup is deliberately discarded |
| `valid` | plain | §12.8b's fail-closed sentence naming both recovery verbs, exit `1` |
| `symlink` | any | the **shipped** `refusing to use %s: runtime state path is a symlink`, exit `1` |
| `unreadable` | any | the **shipped** `sync state at %s is unreadable: %v; inspect and remove it manually`, exit `1` |
| `unsupported-version` | any | `guarded sync setup state at %s uses version %d, which this tws does not support; upgrade tws or remove it manually`, exit `1` |
| `corrupt` | any | `guarded sync setup state at %s is incomplete or invalid; inspect it and remove it manually — tws will not guess`, exit `1` |
| `foreign` | any | `guarded sync setup state at %s belongs to %q, not %q; inspect it and remove it manually`, exit `1` |
| `hash-mismatch` | any | `guarded sync setup state at %s no longer matches the sync state it backed up; inspect it and remove it manually — tws will not guess`, exit `1` |
| a **live** guard beside any of the above — foreign **or** self-recorded, because the shipped `GuardLive` has no self conjunct | any | the **shipped** live-guard sentence `syncCellRefusal` already emits for cells 2/4/5, unchanged and evaluated first, in its verb-specific spelling (§12.3, §12.8b, §25.95) |

Binding:

1. **No schema member is added.** The view drives dispatch and refusals; it is **not** published in
   the plan document, `state.files.*` keeps its shipped five rows and its shipped vocabulary
   (§4.5), no §4.1 key moves, and no fingerprint member changes (§8.3). Publishing the sentinel's
   intent block is a §24 follow-up, not a v1 schema change.
2. **One producer, two consumers, one cell.** `InspectGuardedLegacySentinel` is called by the §19.2
   `--continue` dispatch and by the `--abort`/plain arms of §12.8b, **only** when the classifier
   reported cell 4, and its result is threaded (never recomputed) into whichever arm runs. Cells 1
   and 7 — the flagless legacy resume and every fresh no-flag run — never call it, so the frozen
   path performs **zero** extra reads (§17.1); cell 4's shipped answer is a refusal for every verb,
   and no golden covers it. The **one** permitted second read of the whole interception is the
   single re-classification of the vanished-state row (rule 3a), which re-reads the *classifier's*
   inputs and not this view.
3. **It never follows a symlink and never writes.** One `Lstat`, at most one `ReadFile`, no
   `os.Stat`, no repair, no removal, no lock, no process.
3a. **The read is *fresh*, and `absent` is a real answer it may return on cell 4.** The classifier
   ran earlier; this inspector `Lstat`s and reads the path itself, so a document the classifier saw
   may already be gone. `SentinelAbsent` is therefore reachable from a cell-4 dispatch — it is
   **not** an impossible state, **not** an error and **not** a guarded verdict — and it is answered
   by §12.8b's vanished-state row: one re-classification, then the ordinary behaviour of the cell
   that second classification reports, for that verb. That cell is decided by the **whole** second
   snapshot, guard included: removing the sentinel leaves `{guard}`, which is cell 1 **with** a
   guard and therefore §12.8's arm on `--abort` and `ClaimSyncRunGuard`'s shipped ladder under a
   claiming plain run — only a cell with no state **and** no guard yields the ordinary absent-state
   answers. Fabricating a `valid`, `corrupt` or `not-guarded` answer for a path that
   is not there, retrying the read, looping until the two reads agree, hardcoding the absent-state
   answers regardless of what the second classification found, or emitting a sentence that
   claims a backup exists are each forbidden (§12.8, §12.8b, §25.97). `SentinelNotApplicable` remains the
   **zero value** and is returned by no call.
4. **The extension is invisible to every shipped reader.** `LoadSyncState`, `tws status`,
   `tws doctor` and `tws import` decode or filter this file exactly as they do a plain sentinel,
   because YAML decoding into `SyncState` ignores unknown keys and the path is unchanged (rule 6).
5. **No digest is persisted — here or anywhere.** The sentinel carries the frozen validation
   **command** and its provenance and **no** `validation_digest` key of any spelling. §15's
   64-lower-hex identity stays **derived** from `TestCommand` by whoever needs it — the plan that
   publishes `intent.validation.command_digest`, the guard seam that compares it, the JIT seam that
   re-derives it — exactly as it is for a payload and for a transaction (§13.1 rule 2, §13.2a's
   upgrade table, §25.3). The recovery arm therefore resumes from the sentinel's **command**, and
   digests it itself; it can never resume from a digest whose command it did not read. A writer
   that adds the key, a reader that requires one, and a ladder clause that validates one each fail
   §22.24j (i).
6. **Every non-`valid` guarded verdict names a manual remedy and never names `--abort`.** `corrupt`
   and `hash-mismatch` are documents this ladder could not verify, and §12.8b's `--abort` arm
   refuses over exactly those verdicts — so a sentence telling the operator to run
   `tws sync <f> --abort` would name a verb that fails closed with the same sentence. Each of
   `symlink`, `unreadable`, `unsupported-version`, `corrupt`, `foreign` and `hash-mismatch`
   therefore carries the **same** sentence for **all three** verbs (plain, `--continue`, `--abort`)
   at exit `1`, removing nothing and writing nothing, and each names inspection plus manual removal
   as the remedy. The three-verb byte-identity is asserted in §22.28e (v).

**3. Loader rule (new binary).** `LoadSyncRunState` accepts `2` **and** `3` and rejects anything
else with its shipped sentence shape (`unsupported scoped sync state version %d`).
`SaveSyncRunState` MUST stop forcing the constant: it preserves a non-zero `s.StateVersion`,
defaults a zero one to `SyncRunStateVersion`, and refuses to write any other value. Checkout's
`ContinueCheckoutSync` upper bound becomes `tx.StateVersion > CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion`.
Old v2 payloads and v2/legacy transactions therefore stay fully readable, resumable and
byte-preserving under the new binary.

**4. Route derivation (new binary), replacing three shipped version comparisons.** A single
predicate owns "is this persisted run a new-mode run?", and every shipped
`tx.StateVersion >= CheckoutTransactionVersion` test is rewritten to call it:

```go
// internal/checkout_sync.go
func txNewMode(tx *CheckoutTransaction) bool {
    if tx == nil {
        return false // nil is never a new-mode run; see rule 4b
    }
    switch tx.Route {
    case RouteNewMode: // "new-mode"
        return true
    case RouteLegacy: // "legacy"
        return false
    default: // absent — every v1/v2 document ever written — AND any route string
        // this binary does not know. Both are decided by the version, and by
        // nothing else: an unknown token is never treated as a route.
        return tx.StateVersion >= CheckoutTransactionVersion // i.e. >= 2
    }
}

// TransactionNewMode is the exported wrapper package cli calls. Both are
// nil-safe by construction, so no caller needs a nil check of its own.
func TransactionNewMode(tx *CheckoutTransaction) bool { return txNewMode(tx) }
```

The external twin is `PayloadNewMode(payload *SyncRunState) bool` in `internal/sync_run_state.go`,
built from the same three-way switch on `payload.Route`, with `nil` meaning `false` and the
`default` arm — **absent or unknown alike** — decided by `payload.StateVersion >=
SyncRunStateVersion` (i.e. `>= 2`). Because `LoadSyncRunState` accepts only `2` and `3`, that
default is `true` for every payload a caller can hold, which reproduces the shipped rule "every
persisted v2 payload is a new-mode run" exactly. For **every** state a
shipped binary can have written, `Route` is absent and both derivations reproduce the shipped
comparison exactly, so this is a derivation-preserving rewrite, not a behaviour change (§19.4).

**The `default` arm is total, and it is the only place an unknown token is decided (binding).** The
three-way switch has exactly three outcomes and no fourth:

| `route` | `state_version` | `txNewMode` / `PayloadNewMode` |
|---|---|---|
| `"legacy"` | any | **`false`** — the version is not consulted |
| `"new-mode"` | any | **`true`** — the version is not consulted |
| absent | `>= 2` | `true` |
| absent | absent, `0`, `1` | `false` |
| **any other string** (`"bogus"`, `"Legacy"`, `" new-mode"`, an empty-but-present value) | `>= 2` | **`true`** |
| **any other string** | absent, `0`, `1` | **`false`** |
| — | `nil` receiver | `false` |

An unknown token is therefore neither an error, nor `legacy`, nor "not new-mode": it is *ignored*,
and the document's version decides, exactly as an absent token does. Any statement that an unknown
route "is never treated as new-mode" is **withdrawn** — it is false for a bogus `route` on a v2 or
v3 document, which is precisely the cell the table above pins.

Consequences that MUST hold:

- **I20 is route-derived, not version-derived.** Trigger flags on `--continue` require an effective
  **new-mode** persisted route. A `route: legacy` envelope — external cell 5 or a v3 checkout
  transaction — refuses with the shipped I20 sentence
  (`cannot use sync mode flags on --continue without v2 state; continue without them or abort and
  start a new run`), exactly as a legacy state does today. Without that rule a v3 legacy envelope
  would silently accept `--only`, which legacy semantics never permit.
- **Continuation dispatch is route-derived.** External cell 5 with `route: legacy` dispatches to
  the guarded legacy continuation of §12.3, never to `handleScopedSyncContinue`; checkout
  `ContinueCheckoutSync` applies `checkoutContinueMismatches`/`checkoutSelectedStillPresent`/the
  header **only** when `txNewMode(tx)` is true.
- **Legacy semantics survive the envelope.** The legacy continuation honours the `--push` **flag**
  (shipped legacy behaviour, published as `intent.push_source: flag-legacy-continuation`), applies
  no frozen-axis mismatch check beyond I20, resumes every entry of the current stack minus `done`
  (§13.3), and prints no `Sync mode:` header. The persisted `Selected` is provenance for the
  document and MUST NOT narrow the resumed universe.
- **Limits are re-validated on every continuation** through §13.2's per-key table; a supplied value
  that disagrees with the persisted one is rank 7 `guard-limit-mismatch` and the persisted value
  stays effective, on the legacy envelope exactly as on a v2 payload.
- **A guarded legacy envelope makes the *next* invocation's cell sentences the cell-5 ones.** A
  plain `tws sync <f>` over that state prints the shipped
  `a scoped sync is incomplete (failed on: %s); use --continue or --abort` rather than the legacy
  `previous sync incomplete (failed on: %s); use --continue or --abort`, and `--abort` takes the
  shipped cell-5 arm (abort the failed branch's rebase, delete payload + sentinel, release the
  guard, print `Sync state cleared.`). Both are **shipped sentences and shipped arms, unchanged in
  bytes**, reached because this run really did record scoped-shaped state; they name the same
  recovery verbs, and no unguarded run can reach them. This is declared in §17.2 and asserted in
  §22.24d.

**4a. The exact I20 predicates, in both modes, nil-safe and load-error-safe.**

External, in `internal/cli/sync.go`'s `--continue` arm, replacing the shipped
`newMode && (state.Cell == 1 || state.Cell == 7)`:

```go
// internal/cli/sync.go
// syncTriggersNeedV2 answers I20 rule 0 for the external route. Cells 1 and 7
// are the shipped members; cell 5 joins them only when the persisted payload
// says the run was a legacy one. It takes NO sentinel view and has NO cell-4
// arm: cell 4 keeps the shipped `false`, because this predicate sits BELOW
// syncCellRefusal in the shipped ladder and a cell-4 document has therefore
// already been decided above it — a plain sentinel by syncCellRefusal's own
// shipped refusal, and a VALID backup sentinel by the §12.8b interception,
// which owns that document's trigger-flag answer and raises the I20 sentence
// itself. An earlier revision gave this predicate a cell-4 arm AND placed the
// interception above it, so the arm was unreachable while the text claimed I20
// ran first; that pair is withdrawn (§25.82).
func syncTriggersNeedV2(st internal.SyncExternalState) bool {
    switch st.Cell {
    case 1, 7:
        return true
    case 5:
        return !internal.PayloadNewMode(st.Payload)
    default:
        return false
    }
}
```

used as `if newMode && syncTriggersNeedV2(state) { return fmt.Errorf("%s",
errSyncModeFlagsNeedV2) }`, at its **shipped position** — below `syncCellRefusal` (§19.2). Every
other
cell keeps its shipped outcome, including the unreadable-payload cells, which `syncCellRefusal` has
already refused before this point, and including cell 4, which is decided above it in both of its
reachable shapes. The sentence a valid backup sentinel gets for a trigger flag is **the same
sentence**, byte for byte — it is raised by the interception rather than by this predicate, and
§22.28e (vii) asserts the two are byte-identical.

Checkout, in `internal/cli/checkout_sync.go`, replacing the shipped
`loadErr != nil || tx == nil || tx.StateVersion < internal.CheckoutTransactionVersion`:

```go
// internal/cli/checkout_sync.go
// checkoutTriggersNeedV2 keeps all three shipped arms: an unreadable or absent
// transaction refuses exactly as it does today, and the version comparison is
// replaced by — and only by — the route derivation. It takes the transaction
// the --continue arm already loaded (rule 4d), so the arm performs exactly one
// LoadCheckoutTransaction rather than one per predicate.
func checkoutTriggersNeedV2(tx *internal.CheckoutTransaction, loadErr error) bool {
    return loadErr != nil || tx == nil || !internal.TransactionNewMode(tx)
}
```

used as `if opts.NewMode && checkoutTriggersNeedV2(tx, loadErr) { return fmt.Errorf("%s",
errSyncModeFlagsNeedV2) }`. The `loadErr != nil` and `tx == nil` disjuncts are **preserved
verbatim**: dropping them would turn a missing or corrupt transaction from an I20 refusal into a
fall-through, which is a behaviour change the shipped code does not have. `TransactionNewMode` is
additionally nil-safe (rule 4), so the three arms are independent rather than order-critical.

Equivalence obligation: for a transaction whose `route` is absent,
`!TransactionNewMode(tx) ≡ tx.StateVersion < CheckoutTransactionVersion`, and a table test
enumerates `(route ∈ {absent, "legacy", "new-mode", "bogus"}) × (state_version ∈ {absent, 1, 2, 3})`
plus the `nil` and load-error rows, asserting the shipped answer in every cell a shipped binary can
have produced **and the exact declared answer in every cell it cannot**: `"legacy"` is `false` at
every version, `"new-mode"` is `true` at every version, and `"bogus"` follows the version —
`true` at `2` and `3`, `false` at absent and `1`. An unknown `route` string falls to the `default`
arm and is therefore decided by the version, exactly as an absent one is; it is neither an error nor
an implicit `legacy`.

**4b. The deferred half of I7 is route-derived too.** The shipped predicate
(`internal/cli/sync.go:81-85`) is
`cont && abort && (state.Marker != "" || state.Payload != nil)`, and it fires **before** the abort
arm, so on legacy state — where neither disjunct holds — `--abort` wins over `--continue`, exactly
as `sync-modes` shipped it. A `state_version: 3`, `route: legacy` envelope satisfies **both**
disjuncts (it writes a sentinel *and* a payload), so the naive predicate would refuse
`--continue --abort` on a run whose semantics are legacy — a silent semantic change introduced by
the envelope, not by the operator. The new binary therefore asks the same route question I20 asks:

```go
// internal/cli/sync.go
// syncStateRefusesContinueAbort implements the deferred half of I7. It refuses
// only against state whose EFFECTIVE route is new-mode; a decoded payload
// decides, and an undecodable one fails closed through the marker disjunct.
func syncStateRefusesContinueAbort(st internal.SyncExternalState) bool {
    if st.Payload != nil {
        return internal.PayloadNewMode(st.Payload)
    }
    return st.Marker != ""
}
```

used as `if cont && abort && syncStateRefusesContinueAbort(state) { return errSyncContinueAbort() }`.

| Persisted state | Shipped binary | New binary | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| none (cell 1) | no refusal ⇒ `--abort` wins | identical | no payload, no marker |
| legacy `.sync-state.yaml` (cell 7) | no refusal ⇒ `--abort` wins | identical | legacy semantics preserved |
| v2 payload, sentinel (cell 5) | refuse `--continue and --abort are mutually exclusive` | identical | `PayloadNewMode` ⇒ `true` (route absent) |
| v3 payload `route: new-mode`, sentinel (cell 5) | n/a — cannot be written | refuse, same sentence | guarded new-mode keeps I7 |
| **v3 payload `route: legacy`, sentinel (cell 5)** | n/a | **no refusal ⇒ `--abort` wins**, taking the shipped cell-5 abort arm and printing `Sync state cleared.` | the declared refinement: legacy semantics survive the envelope |
| sentinel only (cell 4), payload absent | refuse | identical | route unknown ⇒ fail closed on the marker |
| **valid backup sentinel (cell 4), payload absent** | n/a | **refuse, same shipped sentence** | the route *is* knowable here (`legacy`), but `--continue --abort` is a contradictory pair and is refused rather than silently resolved; each verb alone has its own declared arm (§12.3's recovery arm, §12.8b) |
| payload undecodable (cells 3, 6, 9, 12) | refuse | identical | `Payload == nil` ⇒ marker disjunct decides; `syncCellRefusal` refuses the verb anyway |

The I7 sentence itself is unchanged and is never a `plan-guard:` marker. An **old** v1.2.15 binary
meeting the same v3 legacy envelope decodes no payload (version 3 is rejected) but *does* see the
sentinel, so it refuses `--continue --abort` with the same shipped I7 sentence and refuses every
single verb with the cell-6 unsupported-version sentence of rule 5 — fail-closed in both, and
unchanged by this feature.

**4c. Checkout recovery asks the same route question, through one nil-safe helper.** Two shipped
checkout comparisons decide *recovery* semantics rather than continuation dispatch, and both are
route questions wearing a version's clothes:

- `AbortCheckoutSync` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:820-824`) —
  `if opts.Continue && tx.StateVersion >= CheckoutTransactionVersion { return "--continue and
  --abort are mutually exclusive" }`, the checkout half of the deferred I7, where a legacy
  transaction lets `--abort` win;
- `ContinueCheckoutSync` (`:727-737`) — `tx.StateVersion >= CheckoutTransactionVersion` selects the
  v2 gates (`checkoutContinueMismatches`, `checkoutSelectedStillPresent`, the `Sync mode:` header)
  instead of the legacy `cannot add --push to an existing transaction …` check.

Both are rewritten to call one nil-safe predicate, and no other `StateVersion` read decides a
route:

```go
// internal/checkout_sync.go
// checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode answers "is this persisted transaction a new-mode
// run?" for BOTH recovery verbs. It is exactly txNewMode (rule 4) under a name
// that says why it is being asked, and it is nil-safe by construction, so
// neither caller needs a nil check of its own.
func checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode(tx *CheckoutTransaction) bool { return txNewMode(tx) }
```

| Persisted transaction | `checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode` | `--continue --abort` (new binary) | Continuation gates |
|---|---|---|---|
| version absent / `1` (legacy) | `false` | `--abort` wins — **shipped** | legacy push-mismatch check — **shipped** |
| `state_version: 2`, `route` absent | `true` | refuse `--continue and --abort are mutually exclusive` — **shipped** | v2 gates + header — **shipped** |
| `state_version: 3`, `route: new-mode` | `true` | refuse, same sentence | v2 gates + header |
| `state_version: 3`, `route: legacy` | `false` | **`--abort` wins**, taking the shipped abort arm | legacy push-mismatch check, no header |
| `nil` / load error | `false` (nil-safe) | unreachable: the shipped `no transaction to abort: %w` / `no transaction to continue: %w` already refused | unreachable |

Binding: for every transaction a shipped binary can have written, `route` is absent and
`checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode(tx) ≡ tx.StateVersion >= CheckoutTransactionVersion`, so this is a
derivation-preserving rewrite (§19.4). Only the `state_version: 3`, `route: legacy` cell differs,
and there **not** refusing is what preserves legacy semantics — the exact mirror of the external
rule 4b. `ContinueCheckoutSync`'s upper bound is separately raised to
`tx.StateVersion > CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion` by rule 3; the upper bound is a *readability*
question and is never routed through this predicate.

**The old-binary asymmetry is declared.** A `v1.2.15` binary meeting a `state_version: 3`,
`route: legacy` transaction cannot decode `route`, sees `3 >= 2`, and therefore refuses
`--continue --abort` with the shipped I7 sentence where the new binary lets `--abort` win — while
its plain `--abort` still aborts (rule 5's declared exception) and its `--continue` still refuses
with `checkout sync transaction state version 3 is newer than 2; upgrade tws or remove <path>`.
Every one of those is a shipped sentence and a shipped arm; none is added or changed here, and no
ref moves in any of those cells.

**Tests (§22.24g).** The five rows above under the new binary, driven through production
`Execute()`; the same v3 `route: legacy` transaction under a real `v1.2.15` binary asserting the
shipped I7 sentence, the shipped unsupported-version sentence and the aborting `--abort`; and an
equivalence table asserting `checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode` equals the shipped comparison for every
`(route ∈ {absent, legacy, new-mode, bogus}) × (state_version ∈ {absent, 1, 2, 3})` cell a shipped
binary can have produced, plus the `nil` row.

**4d. A persisted guarded checkout run stays guarded on a flagless `--continue`.** External cell 5
already has this disjunct (§19.2): a `state_version: 3` payload dispatches to
`handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue` **whether or not** this invocation supplies a flag, because a
guarded run's limits and its frozen validation command are persisted and load-bearing (§13.2,
rule 2). The checkout half needs the same disjunct, and it is a **version** question, not a route
one — rule 2 makes `state_version: 3` the guarded birth marker on *both* checkout routes:

```go
// internal/checkout_sync.go
// checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded answers "was this persisted transaction born
// guarded?". It is nil-safe and load-error-safe by construction: an absent or
// unreadable transaction is never guarded, so the caller needs no nil check of
// its own. It is deliberately NOT routed through txNewMode: route decides
// legacy-vs-new-mode semantics (rule 4), version decides whether a guard was
// armed at birth (rule 2), and a `route: legacy` v3 transaction is guarded.
func checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded(tx *CheckoutTransaction) bool {
    return tx != nil && tx.StateVersion >= CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion
}

// TransactionGuarded is the exported wrapper package cli's dispatch calls.
func TransactionGuarded(tx *CheckoutTransaction) bool { return checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded(tx) }
```

`CheckoutPlanGuard` carries the answer in **one** additional field, and only the executing-route
selector changes (§3.2):

```go
// internal/rebase_plan_guard.go
PersistedGuarded bool // set ONLY by the checkout --continue dispatch below, from
                      // TransactionGuarded(tx). False on every fresh run, on every external
                      // route, and in every value resolvePlanGuardOptions/checkoutGuard()
                      // produce from flags.

func (g CheckoutPlanGuard) Armed() bool   // UNCHANGED: a limit present, or a token supplied —
                                          // it still means "this invocation armed something",
                                          // which is what §13.2's origin labels read
func (g CheckoutPlanGuard) Guarded() bool // (Armed() || PersistedGuarded) && !Plan
```

**The dispatch, in `internal/cli/checkout_sync.go`'s `--continue` arm, in this exact order:**

```go
if opts.Continue {
    tx, loadErr := internal.LoadCheckoutTransaction(featurePath)   // ONE load, this arm only
    if opts.NewMode && checkoutTriggersNeedV2(tx, loadErr) {       // I20 rule 0 — rule 4a, verbatim
        return fmt.Errorf("%s", errSyncModeFlagsNeedV2)
    }
    opts.PlanGuard.PersistedGuarded = internal.TransactionGuarded(tx)   // rule 4d
    if err := internal.ContinueCheckoutSync(opts); err != nil {         // the SAME entry point
        return planGuardRefusal(cmd, err)                               // §6.4, unchanged
    }
    fmt.Println("Checkout sync completed.")                             // the shipped line
    return nil
}
```

Binding:

1. **Position.** The dispatch decision is taken **after** the transaction load, the `nil`/load-error
   arms and the I20 refusal, and **before** the call into `internal.ContinueCheckoutSync` — the
   same position at which the external arm chooses its continuation handler (§19.2). Every gate
   above it keeps its shipped sentence and its shipped position.
2. **One entry point, not two.** There is no second checkout continuation executor: the guarded
   arm is `ContinueCheckoutSync`'s own, selected by `opts.PlanGuard.Guarded() && opts.Continue`
   exactly as §12.2d already specifies, and the seam still sits **below**
   `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` (§12.4, §19.24). What rule 4d changes is *which invocations reach
   that arm*: `checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded(tx) || opts.PlanGuard.Armed()`, which is what
   `Guarded()`'s new disjunct spells.
3. **Limits and validation are inherited, never repeated.** A flagless `--continue` over a v3
   transaction resolves both limits through §13.2's per-key table with
   `origin: persisted-transaction`, and validates with the transaction's persisted `TestCommand`
   (§15). The operator does not restate `--max-replay-per-entry`/`--max-replay-total` on the
   resume, and a **supplied** value that disagrees is rank 7 `guard-limit-mismatch` with the
   persisted value still effective — the same table the external envelope uses.
4. **The unguarded path is untouched.** A transaction with `state_version` absent, `1` or `2` and
   an invocation with no control flag yields `PersistedGuarded == false` and `Armed() == false`,
   so `Guarded()` is false, `ContinueCheckoutSync` takes its shipped arms, no inspection runs
   (§12.2d rule 4), no probe is added and the goldens are the enforcement (§17.1).
5. **The one declared cost is a pure read.** The shipped arm loaded the transaction only under
   `opts.NewMode`; the arm above loads it **once, unconditionally**, on every `--continue`, and
   passes the pair into `checkoutTriggersNeedV2`, whose three arms
   (`loadErr != nil || tx == nil || !TransactionNewMode(tx)`) are otherwise unchanged — the helper
   simply takes the already-loaded pair instead of loading it itself, so the arm still performs
   exactly one load. That is a pure file read: no process, no write, no lock, no stream byte, and
   `ContinueCheckoutSync` still performs its own shipped load with its shipped
   `no transaction to continue: %w` sentence. A `--continue` over a **missing** transaction
   therefore still fails with that shipped sentence, from the shipped site.
6. **`--plan --continue` is not this route, twice over.** The plan dispatch sits above this arm
   (§3.3 step 6), so a plan-only invocation never reaches the assignment at all; and `Guarded()`
   conjoins `!Plan`, so even a value carrying `PersistedGuarded` could not select the guarded
   executing arm. A `--plan --continue` over a v3 transaction publishes the persisted limits with
   `origin: persisted-transaction` in its document and executes nothing (§13.2, §13.7, §3.6).

**Tests (§22.24h).** The dispatch table of rule 4d in all six rows, driven through production
`Execute()`, with a call counter on the guarded arm; the flagless v3 resume asserted to refuse on
the **persisted** limit with the §6.4 marker and `origin: persisted-transaction`; the v2/no-flag
control asserted byte-, exit- and process-identical to the pre-feature run; and a source assertion
that `checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded` is the only `CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion` comparison that
decides a route.

**5. What an old (v1.2.15) binary does — exact, asserted messages.** These are shipped sentences;
this feature adds none of them and changes none of them:

| Old-binary invocation | Encounters | Exact outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `tws sync <f> --continue` (external, v3 payload + sentinel) | `LoadSyncRunState` rejects version 3 ⇒ classifier cell 6 | `scoped sync state at <path> is unreadable or uses an unsupported version (unsupported scoped sync state version 3); inspect it and remove it manually — tws will not guess`, exit `1`, **no rebase** |
| `tws sync <f>` / `tws sync <f> --abort` (same state) | same cell | the same sentence, for every verb — the old binary can neither resume nor abort, and says so |
| `tws sync <f> --continue --abort` (same state) | sentinel present ⇒ the shipped deferred-I7 disjunct | `--continue and --abort are mutually exclusive`, exit `1`, **no rebase** — the old binary cannot decode the payload's `route: legacy`, so it fails closed exactly as it does for a v2 payload (§13.6 rule 4b) |
| `tws status` / `tws doctor` (same state) | `PayloadErr` set | the shipped `IssueSyncStateInvalid` warning `scoped sync state at <path> is unreadable or uses an unsupported version`, with the shipped `inspect …` guidance |
| `tws sync <f> --continue` (checkout, v3 transaction) | `tx.StateVersion > CheckoutTransactionVersion` | `checkout sync transaction state version 3 is newer than 2; upgrade tws or remove <path>`, exit `1`, **no rebase** |
| `tws sync <f>` fresh (checkout, v3 transaction present) | `HasCheckoutTransaction` | `previous checkout-sync incomplete; use --continue or --abort`, exit `1` |
| `tws sync <f> --abort` (checkout, v3 transaction) | `AbortCheckoutSync` reads v1 keys it understands | **it aborts**: restores `original_branch`/`original_head`, deletes the transaction, releases the lock. This is declared, not accidental — abort is an explicit destructive-recovery request that rebases nothing, so the guard has nothing left to protect. The asymmetry with external (which refuses even `--abort`) is a property of the shipped ladders, and neither is changed by this feature |
| `tws sync <f>` / `--continue` (external, a **backup sentinel** with no payload — §13.2a crash window **2**, or the `{sentinel, guard}` rollback residue of §22.24i (ix-a); window 1 is **not** this row, because it leaves the real legacy state, not a sentinel) | its decoder ignores every extension key and sees the marker ⇒ classifier cell 4 | the shipped cell-4 sentence `a scoped sync left partial state for %q: …; Inspect the worktrees, then run: tws sync %s --abort`, exit `1`, **no ref moved** — fail closed on the marker, exactly as for a plain sentinel |
| `tws sync <f> --abort` (same state) | same cell | the shipped cell-4 arm: it deletes the sentinel, releases the guard and prints `Sync state cleared.` at exit `0`, **discarding the embedded backup**. That is the same choice the new binary's `--abort` makes deliberately (§12.8b), it moves no ref, and it is the one cell where an old binary can still clear this residue |

The one thing no old binary can do in any cell is **continue rebasing a guarded run without its
guard**, which is the property this version bump exists to buy.

**6. Import, export and status filtering.** No new runtime file is introduced: the envelope reuses
`.sync-state.v2.yaml`, `.sync-state.yaml` and `.sync-run.lock` — the **backup sentinel of rule 2c
is that same `.sync-state.yaml`**, not a fourth artefact — so `isRuntimeState`
(`internal/cli/importcmd.go:177-184`) keeps its exact three-name list and needs no edit: both the
version and the backup are *document fields*, never paths. `tws import` therefore filters a v3
envelope and a backup sentinel exactly as it filters a v2 one and a plain sentinel, and
`tws status`/`tws doctor` decode them through the shipped `LoadSyncState`/extended payload loader
instead of reporting them unreadable — the sentinel's extension keys are simply ignored by
`SyncState`'s decoder, so `buildExternalSyncCell`'s cell-4 and cell-5 arms behave exactly as they
do for a plain sentinel and **no** status key, enum value or issue kind is added. Their **wording
is unchanged in v1**: the external projection keeps its "scoped sync" vocabulary even for a
`route: legacy` envelope, and its cell-4 guidance keeps naming `tws sync <f> --abort` even where a
valid backup sentinel would also resume, because inventing route-aware status prose — and teaching
`tws status` to decode a guarded sentinel's intent — is a separate, user-visible surface (§24.9).
The plan document is where the route is published truthfully.

**7. Required tests (§23).** A version/state matrix over every cell of rule 2 (written version,
written keys, byte-diff against the shipped shape for every unguarded cell) plus the rule 2a
first-save assertions; a real-binary
downgrade suite built from the `v1.2.15` tag — reusing the shipped downgrade harness pattern of
`internal/cli/sync_downgrade_test.go` (`downgradeTag`) — asserting each exact sentence of rule 5
and that **no ref moved**; a new-binary compatibility suite proving v2 payloads and v2/legacy
transactions still load, resume and round-trip byte-identically; route-derivation tests over the
full `(route, state_version)` × `{nil, load-error}` table of rule 4a for `txNewMode`,
`TransactionNewMode` and `PayloadNewMode`, including the unknown-`route` cell; the two I20 helpers
asserted equal to the shipped predicate in every shipped cell and refusing on a `route: legacy`
envelope; the deferred-I7 matrix of rule 4b in all seven rows, in both binaries; and an
import/status test over a v3 envelope.
