### 13.7 Checkout plan-only ordering (state, gates, one fetch, writers, typed refusal)

The checkout plan route never enters `RunCheckoutSync`/`ContinueCheckoutSync` (§3.3 step 6), so it
owes three things, not one: it must **inspect its subject exactly once**, it must **project every
gate those executors raise above their own fetch**, and it must then perform the described route's
header and fetch itself — in the executor's
order, exactly once, through explicit writers. A plan that fetched before projecting those gates
would perform network I/O for a run that could never have reached its fetch; a plan that inspected
twice could publish a gate verdict and a row set computed from two different reads of the same
`stack.yaml`. §13.7a is the external
twin of this subsection, with the same obligations.

**Entry points (package `internal`, one fresh order and one continuation order):**

```go
// internal/rebase_plan_guard.go — package internal, no Cobra import

// PlanWriters is the ONE writer package cli hands to the checkout plan route.
// It carries prose only — the `Sync mode:` header, the fetch line and (if a
// verbose arm is ever added) child output. There is deliberately NO document
// writer here: the document travels back to cli as a RebasePlan value and is
// written by renderPlanDocumentTo, the sole document writer in the tree (§3.6
// rules 2 and 5). A previous revision's unused `Doc` field is withdrawn — a
// second, never-written writer invited exactly the internal-writes-to-stdout
// mistake this boundary exists to prevent.
type PlanWriters struct {
    Prose io.Writer // header, fetch prose, verbose child output
}

// PlanFetchRepoResult is one fetch context's observed outcome. The writer-taking
// fetch helpers of §3.6 rule 3 RETURN it — they are never void and never a bare
// bool — so `fetch.repos[]` is a record of what happened, not a re-derivation.
// It has EXACTLY these eight fields, one per §4.4a row member, and both modes'
// helpers fill all eight (§13.7 rule 6a, §13.7a rule 1).
type PlanFetchRepoResult struct {
    RepoToken        string               // StackEntry.Repo token; "" is a value (§4.4a)
    ContextRoot      string               // the directory the child ran in, or would have
    ContextCommonDir string               // the PRE-MEASURED --git-common-dir; "" ⇒ null
    ContextSource    string               // worktree | entry-repo | process-cwd |
                                          // workspace-repo-root
    ContextCandidates []PlanFetchCandidate // NEVER nil; [] when the enumeration produced none.
                                          // Copied from the context, never rebuilt after the fetch
    Effect           *PlanFetchEffect     // enumerated BEFORE the fetch (§11.1) and COPIED from the
                                          // PlanFetchContext, never re-probed after it; nil exactly
                                          // when the effect could not be established
    Attempted        bool                 // a git fetch child really ran
    OK               bool                 // the child's exit status; meaningful ONLY when
                                          // Attempted, and encoded as `ok: null` otherwise
}

// PlanFetchOutcome is what this invocation's plan-path fetch observed, handed to
// the builder so the document's fetch/freshness facts describe its own fetch.
// One shape serves both modes: checkout produces exactly one row with
// RepoToken "" and ContextSource workspace-repo-root.
type PlanFetchOutcome struct {
    Applies    bool   // the described route's effective policy fetches at all
    Attempted  bool   // at least one Repos row has Attempted true
    Suppressed string // "" or EXACTLY ONE §11.2 cause token
    Repos      []PlanFetchRepoResult // never nil; see the domain table below
}

// PlanFetchContext is ONE enumerated fetch context with its measured effect,
// produced BEFORE any network call (§11.1). It is the only carrier of an effect
// into a fetch and out of it.
type PlanFetchContext struct {
    RepoToken  string              // "" on the checkout route
    Root       string              // the directory the fetch child will run in
    CommonDir  string              // measured --git-common-dir; "" when unmeasurable
    Source     string              // worktree | entry-repo | process-cwd | workspace-repo-root
    Effect     *PlanFetchEffect    // §11.4-§11.6; nil exactly when it could not be established
    Candidates []PlanFetchCandidate // the §4.4a disclosure rows for this context
}

// PlanFetchPlan is the whole pre-fetch enumeration for this invocation: which
// contexts the described route would fetch in, what each would do, and whether
// any §11.2 cause 4-6 fact forbids the fetch outright.
type PlanFetchPlan struct {
    Applies    bool               // the effective policy says fetch
    Contexts   []PlanFetchContext // exactly one row on the checkout route
    Blockers   []PlanBlocker      // ranks 5.0 / 5.05 / 5.06, on their §7.1 ranks
    Controlled []ControlledPathBlocker // the matching §4.6 tokens, sorted and de-duplicated
    Suppressed string             // the single satisfied §11.2 cause token; "" when none
}

// PlanGateResult is one projected shipped gate: which ladder row it is, whether
// the described route really evaluates it, whether it refuses, which §7.1 rank
// it projects onto, and the shipped sentence verbatim. The plan never composes a
// gate sentence of its own (§13.5). It is the ONLY carrier of a gate on every
// controlled route — CheckoutPlanInspection.Gates, ExternalPlanInspection.Gates
// and RebasePlanRequest.Gates are all []PlanGateResult — and it becomes a
// PlanBlocker exactly once, inside BuildRebasePlan, through GateBlockers
// (§13.5 rule G).
type PlanGateResult struct {
    ID      string      // the ladder label, closed by construction: "checkout-fresh-a" …
                        // "checkout-fresh-l" (§13.7 fresh ladder), "checkout-continue-a" …
                        // "checkout-continue-e" (§13.7 continuation ladder) and "external-a",
                        // "external-b", "external-c", "external-d", "external-e1", "external-e2",
                        // "external-e3", "external-e4", "external-f" (§13.7a step 5). It is not
                        // published in the document; it
                        // exists so a test can assert ladder order and totality per arm
    Applies bool
    Failed  bool
    Kind    RefusalKind // rank of the projected blocker
    Entry   string      // logical entry name; "" for a document-level gate
    Detail  string      // the shipped sentence, verbatim. Where the shipped
                        // sentence wraps a loader error — `no transaction to
                        // continue: %w`, every `%w` arm of the lock ladder — the
                        // wrapped value is the VERBATIM error the snapshot
                        // already carries (CheckoutPlanStateVerdict /
                        // PlanFilePresence.Err, §12.5a rule 8). Producing it
                        // requires no second read, and re-wording it is forbidden
    Controlled []ControlledPathBlocker // never nil; [] on every gate but the live-FOREIGN owner
                        // arms, which carry `live-owner-concurrency` (§4.6, §11.2 cause 3). The
                        // self-PID arm carries [] — the holder is not foreign (§13.7 gate j
                        // row 5a)
}

// PlanGuardLimits is the effective per-key limit pair of §4.6/§13.2, resolved
// once for this invocation (flags on a fresh run, the persisted values plus the
// §13.2 conflict rule on a continuation).
type PlanGuardLimits struct {
    PerEntry PlanGuardLimit // {Value *int, Origin string}
    Total    PlanGuardLimit
}

// PlanValidationIdentity is the frozen validation value of §15, resolved once
// above the plan and never re-read.
type PlanValidationIdentity struct {
    Applies bool
    Command string // never published (§15); only its digest is
    Source  string // none | config-per-entry | persisted-payload | cli-test | persisted-transaction
    Digest  string // 64-lower-hex SHA-256 of Command; "" iff !Applies
}

// PlanStageFact is one remaining-work row's per-stage execution facts (§13.3b):
// which command the resume runs next for that row, whether that command is a
// rebase, and whether rebase.autoStash can reach it.
type PlanStageFact struct {
    Entry              string
    Stage              string // the stage this row is judged under; later indices are "planned"
    NextCommand        string // "checkout+rebase" | "rebase" | "checkout" | "validation" | "none"
    RebaseIsNext       bool
    StandaloneCheckout bool
    AutostashApplies   *bool // nil exactly when the rebase.autoStash probe failed
}

// CheckoutPlanInspectionRequest is everything a controlled checkout route knows
// before it touches the repository — the plan route and the guarded executing
// route alike (§12.2d). It is exactly two members, both produced by
// package cli above the I19 containment refusal (§13.7 step 0), so the
// inspection has one construction site and no hidden input.
type CheckoutPlanInspectionRequest struct {
    Opts        CheckoutSyncOpts
    Containment PlanGateResult // the I19 predicate evaluated as a value, never returned
}

// CheckoutPlanInspection is the SINGLE composite result of inspecting a
// checkout plan subject. It replaces the disconnected CheckoutPlanState +
// CheckoutPlanGates(opts, st, nil, SyncSelection{}) pair of an earlier
// revision, which asked a gate projector to judge a stack and a selection it
// was handed as nil and then forced its caller to load both a second time. Every
// member is measured or derived EXACTLY ONCE, at inspection time; nothing below
// re-reads, re-loads, re-resolves or re-probes any of them, and no member is a
// nil placeholder to be filled in later.
type CheckoutPlanInspection struct {
    // 1 — inputs, echoed so no consumer re-derives them
    Opts        CheckoutSyncOpts
    Containment PlanGateResult

    // 2 — the §12.1 pre-acquisition snapshot, produced by ONE
    // InspectCheckoutPlanState call (§12.5a): the transaction, the
    // Lstat-first lock inspection and the git-op/dirty/HEAD facts. Pure reads:
    // no lock, no fetch, no write, no symlink followed. The guarded executing
    // route reads this same value from this same inspection (§12.2d), and it
    // travels to the builder as RebasePlanRequest.CheckoutState.
    State        CheckoutPlanState
    StateVerdict CheckoutPlanStateVerdict // the shipped loaders' errors, verbatim (§12.5a rule 8);
                                          // the ONLY source of a projected gate's wrapped %w

    // 3 — the run's subject, loaded and resolved exactly once
    Stack             *Stack   // nil iff StackErr != nil or the described route never loads it.
                               // On the CONTINUATION arm it is nil unless the shipped
                               // checkoutSelectedStillPresent gate really loads it (rule 2)
    StackErr          error    // the shipped LoadStack error, verbatim
    Order             []StackEntry // the ONE TopoSort result of this invocation (§9.1a rule 3);
                                   // nil when SortErr != nil or the arm loads no stack, and ALWAYS
                                   // nil on the continuation arm, which sorts zero times. It is
                                   // []StackEntry, never []string: every consumer needs
                                   // GitBranch()/Base/Archived/LastBaseSHA, and re-looking them up
                                   // by name would be a second derivation of the same fact
    SortErr           error        // the shipped `cycle detected in stack.yaml`, verbatim
    Selection         SyncSelection
    SelectionResolved bool  // ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder ran over Order and succeeded (§9.2a);
                            // the sorting wrapper ResolveSyncSelection is NOT called here
    SelectionErr      error // the shipped sentence, verbatim

    // 3a — the one Git version probe of this invocation (§16 rule 1a), issued
    // AFTER the subject above exists and BEFORE the enumeration in member 6.
    // Version.Probed is false exactly on a rows-less no-subject arm, which skips
    // it (§16 rule 1b); Probed && !OK is the rank 5.9 cell (§16 rule 6). Both
    // members are copied into RebasePlanRequest and are never re-probed below.
    Version      GitVersion
    Capabilities GitCapabilities

    // 4 — the effective run identity (§13.2, §13.6 rule 4c, §15)
    Route      string // RouteLegacy | RouteNewMode: trigger-derived fresh,
                      // checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode(State.Files.CheckoutTransaction.Transaction)-
                      // derived on --continue
    Policy     SyncRunPolicy
    Limits     PlanGuardLimits
    Validation PlanValidationIdentity

    // 5 — projected preflights and gates
    BasePreflight PlanBasePreflight // I14; this struct's producer is its ONLY caller (§10.7, rule 3 below)
    Gates         []PlanGateResult  // every projected gate of this arm's ladder, in ladder order,
                                    // TYPED (§13.5 rule G) and never []PlanBlocker: each row
                                    // carries its ladder ID, its Applies/Failed verdict, its §7.1
                                    // rank, its entry and the shipped sentence verbatim. It travels
                                    // to the builder as RebasePlanRequest.Gates and becomes
                                    // blockers[] rows only there, through GateBlockers. The
                                    // enumeration's own rank 5.0/5.05/5.06 rows are NOT gates and
                                    // stay on FetchPlan.Blockers

    // 6 — the pre-fetch enumeration of §11.1: the single workspace-root context,
    // its measured effect (head_branch, remotes, refspecs, prune/tag mappings,
    // the local-branch destinations WITH their held[] inventory and the
    // submodule recursion WITH its reach verdict), its measured --git-common-dir
    // and its one candidate row. Produced BEFORE the Fetches decision below,
    // consumed by the fetch itself (rule 6a), and — when a cause 5/6 fact
    // suppresses the fetch — projected into the un-attempted fetch.repos[] row
    // (§4.4a, §11.2). It is the value the guarded executing route consumes too,
    // from this same inspection (§12.2d rule 1a).
    FetchPlan PlanFetchPlan

    // 6a — the MAPPING half of this invocation's push facts (§14.1a rule 7),
    // measured only where intent.push is true: the distinct push contexts (here
    // exactly one, opts.RepoDir), the measured identity table, the per-entry
    // materialization, and per context the `origin` existence and the ordered
    // `remote.origin.fetch` decomposition. Phase is `pre-fetch`; NO
    // remote-tracking ref is read here, because a fetch of this same route may
    // be about to move them. PlanCheckoutRebase refreshes it into the baseline
    // half exactly once, after its fetch decision (steps 3a/4a), and the guarded
    // executing route does the same at §12.2d step 5b.
    PushFacts PlanPushFacts

    // 7 — remaining work on a --continue (§13.3, §13.3a, §13.3b)
    RemainingApplies bool
    Remaining        []string // RemainingRebaseEntries over the transaction's Plan and Stage
    StageFacts       []PlanStageFact

    // 8 — derived decisions the caller MUST NOT recompute
    Refusing      bool   // at least one member of Gates refuses, or FetchPlan.Blockers is
                         // non-empty, before the fetch
    Fetches       bool   // the described route reaches its own fetch. It is derived LAST, after
                         // ALL SIX §11.2 causes have been decided, as exactly:
                         //   FetchPlan.Applies && !Opts.Continue && !Refusing && Suppression == ""
                         // — cause 1 is !Opts.Continue, cause 2 and cause 3 are !Refusing, causes
                         // 4-6 are Suppression == "" (cause 4 being unreachable in checkout mode).
                         // A route that decided Fetches before evaluating causes 5/6 would fetch
                         // exactly where the guard declines to (§11.1, §11.2)
    Suppression   string // the single satisfied §11.2 cause token; "" when nothing was suppressed
    RowsAvailable bool   // rule 4 below: the inputs a row needs were established
}

// InspectCheckoutPlan is the single inspection entry point for BOTH checkout
// plan arms AND for the guarded executing checkout routes (§12.2d), selected by
// req.Opts.Continue. It runs no fetch, acquires no lock,
// writes nothing and prints nothing; it calls the shipped predicates rather
// than re-deriving them (§10.7, §13.5); and it is the ONLY site on a controlled
// checkout route that loads the stack, SORTS it, resolves the selection (through
// the order-taking ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder, §9.2a), probes the Git version
// (§16 rule 1a), runs the I14 locator, takes the state snapshot or enumerates
// the fetch context.
func InspectCheckoutPlan(req CheckoutPlanInspectionRequest) CheckoutPlanInspection

// PlanCheckoutRebase is the single checkout plan entry point. It dispatches on
// opts.Continue, inspects once, performs the described route's header and
// policy fetch, and builds the plan. It writes no document byte to any stream,
// takes no lock and writes no state; w carries prose only.
func PlanCheckoutRebase(w PlanWriters, opts CheckoutSyncOpts,
    containment PlanGateResult) (RebasePlan, error)

// BuildCheckoutRebasePlan projects a FRESH checkout run from the inspection,
// this invocation's own fetch outcome and its refreshed push facts. It is pure
// with respect to the network and the filesystem: it never fetches, never
// prints, never loads the stack, never resolves a selection, never re-runs the
// I14 preflight (rule 3) and never reads a remote-tracking inventory (§14.1a
// rule 7). Its signature is fixed by §9.0 rule 1a — the inspection, the fetch
// outcome and the post-fetch push facts, never a RebasePlanLayout and never a
// second copy of CheckoutSyncOpts, which it reads from insp.Opts.
func BuildCheckoutRebasePlan(insp CheckoutPlanInspection, fetched PlanFetchOutcome,
    push PlanPushFacts) (RebasePlan, error)

// BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan projects a --continue from the same inspection
// plus its plan-point push facts. It NEVER fetches (§11.2 cause 1), takes the
// decoded transaction insp.State.Files.CheckoutTransaction.Transaction as the
// run, consumes insp.Remaining/insp.StageFacts, and MUST NOT call
// BuildCheckoutPlan, buildCheckoutPlanFrom, TopoSort, ResolveSyncSelection or
// ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder as a substitute for it.
func BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan(insp CheckoutPlanInspection,
    push PlanPushFacts) (RebasePlan, error)
```

**`PlanFetchOutcome` — exact members and domains (the builder consumes this and re-derives
nothing):**

| Member | Domain | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `Applies` | bool | the described route's **effective policy** is `fetch`. It is a policy fact, not an outcome: a suppressed fetch still has `Applies: true`, and only `local-only`/a continuation/a legacy checkout route has `Applies: false` |
| `Attempted` | bool | `true` **iff** at least one `Repos` row has `Attempted: true`. It is an invariant, not an independent value; a value disagreeing with the rows is a test failure |
| `Suppressed` | `""` \| one §11.2 token | at most **one** token, in §11.2's precedence order: `not-refreshed-continuation`, `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject`, `not-refreshed-live-run`, `not-refreshed-context-indeterminate`, `not-refreshed-submodule-reach-indeterminate`, `not-refreshed-local-branch-checked-out`. It is `""` for `local-only` and for `not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets`, which are **not** suppressions (§4.4a). `Suppressed != ""` ⇒ `Attempted == false` |
| `Repos` | `[]PlanFetchRepoResult`, never `nil` | `[]` **exactly** for causes 1–3, `local-only` and `not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets`; one row per resolved context otherwise — **including** causes 4–6, whose rows carry `Attempted: false` and the members §4.4a requires for that cause |

`fetch.outcome` (`ok` \| `failed` \| `partial` \| `skipped`) and `freshness` are derived by
`BuildRebasePlan` from these rows through the total tables of §4.4a and §11.3, in **one** place;
neither is a member of this struct, so there is no second truth to keep in step.

**Exact ordering inside `PlanCheckoutRebase` — fresh arm (`opts.Continue == false`)**, the same

**Gate j is the WHOLE native ladder, not just the live-holder arm.** The plan projects every
pre-fetch refusal `AcquireCheckoutLock` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:185-220`) and
`forceAcquireCheckoutLock` (`:262-288`) can raise from the state the snapshot already measured,
each with the shipped sentence **verbatim** and each suppressing both the header and the fetch
(rule 5). The mapping is total and is decided from `insp.State.Files.CheckoutLock` +
`insp.StateVerdict`, never from a second read (§12.5a rule 8):

| # | Snapshot cell | Fresh arm (`AcquireCheckoutLock`) | Continuation arm (`forceAcquireCheckoutLock`) |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | `presence: absent` | no refusal (the exclusive create succeeds) | no refusal (the shipped `os.IsNotExist` arm writes the lock) |
| 2 | `presence: unreadable`, `io-error` **or** `not-regular-file` | `read existing checkout-sync lock: %w` | `read checkout-sync lock: %w` |
| 3 | `presence: unreadable`, `decode-error` **or** `empty-document` | `invalid checkout-sync lock; inspect %s and use --abort to recover: %w` | `invalid checkout-sync lock %s: %w` |
| 4 | `readable`, `pid <= 0` | `checkout-sync lock is being initialized or is invalid; retry or inspect %s` | the identical sentence (the shipped arms share it byte for byte) |
| 5 | `readable`, **live foreign**: `alive: true`, i.e. `pid > 0 && pid != self && alive(pid)` | `checkout-sync lock held by live process %d (created %s); cannot steal live lock` | `lock held by live process %d; cannot reclaim` |
| 5a | `readable`, **self**: `self: true` (recorded PID == `os.Getpid()`); the *process* is running by construction, while the published `alive` is `false`, because that field is foreign-only by §12.5a's definition | the **same** fresh sentence, `checkout-sync lock held by live process %d (created %s); cannot steal live lock` — the shipped fresh ladder tests `isProcessAlive(info.PID)` with **no** self conjunct (`internal/checkout_sync.go:207`) — but **no** `live-owner-concurrency` token and **no** cause 3, because the holder is not foreign (§11.2 cause 3) | **no refusal**: `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` skips its live check for `info.PID == os.Getpid()` (`:281`) and reclaims, so the continuation projects nothing here |
| 6 | `readable`, `pid > 0`, **dead and foreign** (`alive: false`, `self: false`), **and** a transaction path exists | **not projected.** The native arm is `stale lock from PID %d detected with existing transaction; use --continue or --abort to recover` (`:210-212`), but it is **unreachable below gate b**: gate b's predicate is `HasCheckoutTransaction`, a bare `os.Stat` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:173-176`) evaluated at `internal/cli/checkout_sync.go:60` **above** the lock, so any fresh run that has a transaction path at all — decodable or not — refuses earlier with `previous checkout-sync incomplete; use --continue or --abort`. The plan therefore publishes **gate b's** sentence for this cell and never the lock's, exactly as the shipped route does | *not an arm of this ladder*: `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` has no transaction relation, so the continuation projects nothing here |
| 7 | `readable`, `pid > 0`, **dead and foreign** (`alive: false`, `self: false`), no transaction path | the reclaim is projected as **succeeding**; a `removeLockIfUnchanged` failure (`reclaim stale checkout-sync lock: %w`, including `lock changed while checking staleness`) is a **race**, not a snapshot fact, and is projected only through the JIT/execution seam, never as a plan blocker | same, with `reclaim checkout-sync lock: %w` |
| 8 | `presence: symlink` | **no synthesized native sentence.** The ladder reads *through* the link and the inspector never does (§12.5a rule 9), so the plan publishes the row as `presence: symlink`, refuses nothing of its own on the plan route, and the guarded route refuses under §12.5's `owner-artefact-undecodable` rule | identical |

Five rules bind the table: (0) the rows are evaluated **top-down, first match wins**, in the
shipped ladder's own order, and each row's predicate is read **after** the negation of every row
above it — which is what makes `pid <= 0` land on row 4 rather than on rows 6/7. Within that
reading the rows are disjoint: `alive` means `pid > 0 && pid != self && alive(pid)` (§12.5a), so
rows 6 and 7 name `pid > 0` and **dead and foreign** explicitly and a self-PID lock can only reach
row 5a; (0a) the two arms are projected from **their
own** predicates and never
from a shared one — the fresh ladder has no self-PID conjunct and the continuation ladder has one,
which is exactly why rows 5 and 5a differ per column; (i) the plan never invents a sentence — every
projected string is the
shipped `fmt.Errorf` format of the arm it names, with the same operands in the same order;
(ii) cells 7's write-race arms and the `create lock directory: %w` mkdir arm are **not** projected,
because they describe a future write this invocation has not attempted and a snapshot cannot
predict — a plan that guessed them would refuse runs that would have succeeded; (iii) every
projected arm is a rank 3 `state-refused` blocker, publishes **no** header and **no** fetch, and
leaves the executing twin's own refusal byte-identical and marker-free (§22.31).

Binding rules (numbered; the orderings above reference them by number):

1. **One inspection, one load, one sort, one resolution, one snapshot, one probe, one enumeration.**
   `InspectCheckoutPlan` is called **exactly once**
   per controlled checkout invocation — plan-only *and* guarded executing (§12.2d) — and it is the
   only site on those routes that calls `LoadStack`, `TopoSort`,
   `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder`, `ProbeGitVersion`,
   `InspectCheckoutPlanState` (and therefore `LoadCheckoutTransaction` and
   the §12.1 artefact probes), `firstUnresolvedCheckoutBase` or the fetch-context enumeration.
   The sorting wrapper `ResolveSyncSelection` (§9.2a) is **not** called on a controlled route at
   all: calling it would sort a second time (§9.1a rule 3).
   There is **no second stack load**, **no second sort** and **no selection resolved around the
   fetch**: an earlier revision's `CheckoutPlanGates(opts, st, nil, SyncSelection{})` — a gate
   projector handed a `nil` stack and a zero selection, followed by a caller that loaded both again
   after the fetch — is **withdrawn**, because it forced two loads of the same file, allowed the
   pre-fetch gate verdict and the post-fetch rows to disagree, and left the gates that *depend* on
   the stack (g, g1, h, i) unable to see it. **The inspection is total**: every input the two
   builders need is a measured member of it, no member is a nil placeholder a later step fills in,
   and no consumer below may re-measure any of them. Everything the builders need travels on the
   single `CheckoutPlanInspection` value. Both builders construct the shared `RebasePlanRequest`
   of §9.1a — that exact struct, with every member set — from that value and nothing else:
   `Layout` per §9.0 rule 2,
   `CheckoutState: insp.State`, `ExternalState` as the `applicable: false` value (§12.5a rule 5),
   `Order: insp.Order`, `Stack: insp.Stack`, `SortErr: insp.SortErr`, `Selection: insp.Selection`,
   `FetchPlan: insp.FetchPlan`, `Version: insp.Version`, `Capabilities: insp.Capabilities`,
   `Gates: insp.Gates` — the typed `[]PlanGateResult` ladder, assigned as itself and converted only
   inside the builder (§13.5 rule G); an earlier revision's `insp.Blockers`' gate results is
   **withdrawn**, because a `[]PlanBlocker` cannot be a `[]PlanGateResult` and the sentence
   described an assignment that does not compile —
   `PushFacts` as the value `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` returned at step 4a/3a (§14.1a rule 7),
   never `insp.PushFacts` itself,
   `Fetch` as the `PlanFetchOutcome` they were handed (`BuildCheckoutRebasePlan`) or the zero
   outcome with `Applies: false` (`BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan`), and `Route`/`Policy`/`Limits`/
   `Validation`/`BasePreflight`/`Remaining`/`RowsAvailable` echoed from the inspection.
2. **A continuation plan MUST NOT rebuild the plan, and the one stack read it may perform proves
   existence only.** `BuildCheckoutPlan`, `buildCheckoutPlanFrom`, `TopoSort`,
   `ResolveSyncSelection`, `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder`
   and fresh base resolution are **forbidden** as a substitute for `tx.Plan` on that arm: the
   transaction *is* the run. Rebuilding it would describe a different run — a different entry set
   if `stack.yaml` changed, different `LastBaseSHA`/`NewBaseSHA` pins, and on `Stage: switched` a
   different destination (§13.3a) — and the document, the guard seam and the executor would then
   disagree about the very thing this feature exists to make agree.
   `InspectCheckoutPlan` therefore **sorts nothing and selects nothing** on the continuation arm
   (`insp.Order == nil`, `insp.SelectionResolved == false`), and §22.13d asserts zero calls of all
   five functions. It **may** call `LoadStack` exactly once there, and only in the cell the shipped
   executor already does: `checkoutSelectedStillPresent` with `len(tx.Selected) > 0`
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:795-812`). That read answers two questions and no third — *does each
   persisted logical name still exist in the stack* (`HasBranch`) and, where §13.3a needs it, *does
   a row's logical identity still match the persisted branch* — and its failure is projected with
   the shipped `load stack: %w` sentence. It never becomes a row source, a base source, an order
   source or a selection source. A continuation whose `tx.Selected` is empty performs no stack read
   at all, exactly as the shipped gate does not. The
   **fresh** arm is the mirror image: it derives its rows from exactly the inputs the
   `buildCheckoutPlanFrom` adapter body consumes — `insp.Opts.RepoDir`, `insp.Stack`, `insp.Order`
   and `insp.Selection` —
   through the shared planner of §9.2 (`ExecutionOrder` → `ResolveSyncBase` → `RebaseStrategy`), so
   the document and the executing plan build agree on order, bases, pins and argv by
   construction rather than by comparison, and over **one** `TopoSort` result rather than two
   (§9.1a rule 3).
2a. **The containment gate has exactly one evaluation, and the CLI owns it.** Gate a of **both**
   arms is `req.Containment` — the `PlanGateResult` `runCheckoutSync` built at step 0 by evaluating
   the shipped I19 predicate (`os.Getwd` → `internal.GitRepoRootIn(cwd)` →
   `filepath.Clean(top) != filepath.Clean(ws.RepoRoot)`, `internal/cli/checkout_sync.go:22-31`)
   **once**, above the plan dispatch and above its own refusal. `InspectCheckoutPlan` copies that
   value into `insp.Gates[0]` unchanged — same `Applies`, `Failed`, `Kind`, `Entry` and `Detail`,
   with the shipped sentence verbatim — and evaluates **no** containment predicate of its own:
   `CheckoutPlanInspectionRequest` has exactly two members precisely so the inspection cannot
   acquire a second source for this fact. A second probe is forbidden even where it would agree,
   because the cwd is the one input to this gate that a concurrent process can change under the
   invocation, and the plan and the executing twin must refuse — or not refuse — on the same
   reading. §22.13d asserts **one** `GitRepoRootIn` call per controlled checkout invocation and
   value identity between `req.Containment` and the projected row.
3. **`InspectCheckoutPlan` is the single I14 owner on the checkout plan route (§10.7).** It calls
   `firstUnresolvedCheckoutBase` at most once, over `insp.Stack`/`insp.Selection`, and publishes
   the result as `insp.BasePreflight`. `BuildCheckoutRebasePlan` **consumes** that value and
   **MUST NOT** call the locator, `verifyCheckoutBasesLocally` or any equivalent probe again;
   `BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan` never runs I14 at all (§10.7 rule 7). A second evaluation is
   forbidden even when it would agree: it would double the probe budget, and a mid-invocation
   change would let the gate verdict and the row's blocker disagree inside one document. The
   external route has the same single-owner rule (§13.7a rule 3), and the guarded **executing**
   routes keep the shipped wrapper as their one owner (§10.7 rule 5).
4. **Rows exist exactly where their inputs were established.** `insp.RowsAvailable` is the sole
   answer to "may this document publish `entries[]`?": on the new-mode fresh arm it is
   `insp.Stack != nil && insp.SortErr == nil && insp.SelectionResolved`, on the legacy fresh arm
   `insp.Stack != nil && insp.SortErr == nil` (that route resolves no selection), and on the
   continuation arm `insp.State.Files.CheckoutTransaction.Transaction != nil`. A document with
   `RowsAvailable == false` is the
   rows-less
   `summary.plannability: unavailable` profile of §4.3 — never a partially populated one — and a
   document with `RowsAvailable == true` publishes its rows even when a gate refuses, with the
   blocker attached to the offending row or to the document. This is the checkout half of the
   symmetric rule §13.7a states for external. **The rule is symmetric; the gate *order* is not, and
   the difference is now declared rather than assumed, per arm.** Checkout keeps the shipped ladder
   order for every gate the shipped executor already evaluates above its own fetch — its stack
   load, its selection and I14 really do sit in the shipped pre-lock preflight
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:588-607`: LoadStack → ResolveSyncSelection →
   verifyCheckoutBasesLocally), and because the shipped `ResolveSyncSelection` **sorts inside
   itself** (`internal/sync_selection.go:166`), the **new-mode** arm already sorts there too, above
   the lock and above the fetch. That preflight contains no *visible* `TopoSort` call, and the
   **legacy** arm has no preflight at all: its load happens below the lock and its sort inside
   `BuildCheckoutPlan` (`:465`). Any earlier claim that checkout has "nothing to hoist" is
   **withdrawn**, and so is the round-8 claim that the hoist changes the **new-mode** arm's
   ordering: on that arm the controlled route sorts in the same place the shipped route already
   did, and only the second, below-lock sort disappears. The observable hoist is the **legacy**
   arm's, where the load (gate k) and the sort (gate g1) both move above the lock; only controlled
   routes see it. The external executor loads its stack *after* its state
   gates, so §13.7a hoists the subject reads on the plan route only, to buy rows the checkout route
   already has. Neither reordering touches an **unguarded** route.
5. **The header and the fetch are both gated on `!insp.Refusing`, at every rank.** A refusing
   pre-fetch blocker — I19 containment, an existing transaction, a Git operation, a dirty tree, a
   detached HEAD, a HEAD-resolution failure, an unreadable stack, a refused selection, I14, a live
   foreign lock, a gate-l fetch-effect fact, I20 or any continuation gate — suppresses **both** the
   `Sync mode:` header and the fetch. There is no rank whose refusal prints a header, and none that
   fetches. A *stale current ancestry* is **not** such a blocker: it is the work the run performs
   (§7.1 rank-4 completion-gate rule).
6. **Exactly one fetch per invocation, and the plan build follows it.** The fetch happens in the
   context step 1.5 enumerated (`insp.FetchPlan.Contexts[0].Root`, which is `opts.RepoDir`),
   through `fetchCheckoutRepoTo` — not a re-implementation but *the* body of the
   shipped block, whose executing call site is the one-line wrapper `fetchCheckoutRepo(opts.RepoDir)`
   (rule 7, §3.6 rule 3). Same label, same words, same non-verbose silence; only the writer differs.
   It uses `RunSilentDir`, so no writer-taking exec helper is needed here; a future verbose arm MUST
   use `RunDirTo` (§3.6 rule 4). A plan built **before** its own fetch would describe stale refs and
   then publish `freshness: fetched`, which is a lie about the document's own inputs; a fetch
   performed **before** the inspection would perform network I/O for a run that stops above its
   fetch. There is **no fetch at all** on the default checkout route (`no-fetch`), under
   `--no-fetch`, on any `--continue`, or when rule 5 suppresses it — matching §11.2 causes 1 and 2
   and the shipped executor, which fetches only inside its `opts.NewMode` block *after* the whole
   ladder and the lock.
6a. **The fetch effect is enumerated before the fetch and carried through it — never re-probed
   after it.** `insp.FetchPlan` is produced at step 1.5, before any network call, and
   `fetchCheckoutRepoTo` takes that `PlanFetchContext` and **copies** its `Effect`,
   `CommonDir`, `Source`, `RepoToken` and `Candidates` into the single `PlanFetchRepoResult` row of
   the `PlanFetchOutcome` it returns, adding only what it observed itself: `Attempted` and `OK`.
   The row therefore always carries `context_common_dir` and a one-member, never-`nil`
   `context_candidates[]` (§4.4a, §13.7a rule 8), whether the fetch ran or a cause 5/6 fact
   suppressed it. It performs **no** config
   read, **no** remote resolution, **no** submodule walk and **no** local-branch inventory of its
   own, because measuring the effect after the fetch would describe a repository the fetch had
   already changed. Two consequences are binding: the checkout route reaches
   `freshness: fetched` whenever its known effect is contacting and its child succeeded — it is
   **not** condemned to `unknown-fetch-effect` merely for being checkout (§11.1, §11.3) — and a
   checkout plan whose effect could not be established publishes `fetch_effect: null` with
   `freshness: unknown-fetch-effect`, exactly as external does. The executing wrapper
   `fetchCheckoutRepo` passes a context carrying only `Root`/`Source` and discards the result,
   which cannot move a byte; the **guarded** executing route calls the writer-taking twin with
   `os.Stdout` and the enumerated context, and consumes the outcome (§12.2d).
   **The push baseline is the deliberate opposite, and the two rules are not in tension.** A fetch
   *effect* describes what a fetch **would do**, so it is a pre-fetch fact by definition and
   re-measuring it afterwards would describe a repository the fetch already changed. A lease
   *baseline* describes the ref a projected `git push --force-with-lease` **will compare against**,
   which this very fetch may have just moved, so it is a post-fetch fact by the same reasoning
   (§14.1a rule 7). `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` is therefore the one read this route performs after
   its fetch, it reads **refs only** — no config, no remote resolution, no submodule walk, no
   local-branch inventory — and it touches no member of `fetch.repos[]`.
7. **Checkout prose has exactly one body per printer, in package `internal`, and the shipped
   symbols are wrappers (§3.6 rule 3).** The exact signatures and their ownership:

   ```go
   // internal/checkout_sync.go — package internal, one body each
   func printSyncModeHeaderTo(w io.Writer, p SyncRunPolicy)
   func printSyncModeHeader(p SyncRunPolicy) { printSyncModeHeaderTo(os.Stdout, p) }

   func fetchCheckoutRepoTo(w io.Writer, ctx PlanFetchContext) PlanFetchOutcome
   func fetchCheckoutRepo(repoDir string) {
       _ = fetchCheckoutRepoTo(os.Stdout, PlanFetchContext{Root: repoDir, Source: "workspace-repo-root"})
   }
   ```

   `printSyncModeHeaderTo`'s body **is** the shipped `printSyncModeHeader` body
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:519-521`) with `fmt.Printf` → `fmt.Fprintf(w, …)`;
   `fetchCheckoutRepoTo`'s body **is** the shipped inline fetch block (`:618-625` — the
   `if opts.Policy.Fetch == SyncFetchEnabled { … }` block **only**; the `printSyncModeHeader` call
   at `:617` belongs to the header twin and is not part of it) with the same
   substitution, the child running in `ctx.Root`, and its status recorded in the single-row
   `PlanFetchOutcome` it returns (rule 6a). Neither
   format string may exist twice in the package, `RunCheckoutSync` calls the two **wrappers** at
   its shipped call sites inside the shipped `opts.NewMode` / `SyncFetchEnabled` conditions, and
   the plan route calls the two **writer-taking** twins with `w.Prose`. Because the body exists
   once, the executing route and its plan twin cannot drift; the 126 `sync_noflag` goldens are
   byte-identical and are the enforcement (§17.1, §22.1).
8. **No lock, no transaction, no restoration — and no transaction *mutation* — on the plan route**:
   `AcquireCheckoutLock`,
   `forceAcquireCheckoutLock`,
   `SaveCheckoutTransaction`, `printLocalOnlyNoOp`, `executeTransaction` and `resumeTransaction`
   are not reached. `AcquireCheckoutLock` staying above the plan build on the *executing*
   route is unaffected, and the guarded executing route makes the **same** `InspectCheckoutPlan`
   call above that lock (§12.2d), so plan-only and guarded decide `state.*`, the row set and the
   order from one producer — with the single declared consequence of the legacy arm's hoisted
   load/sort (gate g1/k, §25.35).
8a. **Two shipped continuation gates evaluate by WRITING, and for each the difference between
   projecting it and executing it is declared, not glossed.** The mutation exception of rule 8 has
   exactly these two members — the `planned`/`rebasing` active-rebase gate and the `rebased`
   ancestry gate — and no third; any other gate that acquired a write would be a change to this
   rule. The `conflict`-stage ancestry gate of gate e is deliberately **not** a member: its
   refusing arms return above every write, and the `PostSHA`/`Stage: rebased`/
   `SaveCheckoutTransaction` writes that follow it in the shipped code belong to the resume the
   gate **admits**, not to the gate — so on both routes a refusal there leaves
   `.checkout-sync.tx.yaml` byte-identical, and rule 8 alone keeps the plan route from performing
   the admitted writes (§13.5 rule E, §12.7).

   **(i) The `planned`/`rebasing` active-rebase gate.** The shipped arm
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:912-921`) does **three** things *before it returns its sentence*
   when it finds
   `gitRebaseInProgress(opts.RepoDir)` on stage `planned` or `rebasing`: it sets
   `tx.Stage = StageConflict`, it sets `tx.FailureKind = FailConflict`, and it **persists** the
   transaction through `SaveCheckoutTransaction`; the returned error is then
   `rebase in progress; resolve conflicts then --continue`. The two routes therefore differ, and
   each is binding:
   - **plan-only** projects the gate as a rank 3 `state-refused` blocker with that sentence
     verbatim, at exit `0`, and performs **none** of the three writes: it takes no lock, does not
     reclassify the stage and does not call `SaveCheckoutTransaction`. `.checkout-sync.tx.yaml` is
     byte-identical after a `--plan --continue` of that state — this is the "no mutating tx"
     property §18.1 already requires of the plan route, restated here because this shipped arm is
     one of the two gates whose native evaluation *is* a write;
   - **guarded executing** preserves shipped behaviour exactly: the guard seam sits **below**
     `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` (§12.4), so a guarded `--continue` that reaches native
     `resumeTransaction` performs the shipped reclassification and the shipped save before
     returning the shipped sentence at exit `1`, marker-free. Its refusal is therefore **not** a
     "nothing happened" refusal, and no text, marker or `detail` may present it as one: the run's
     recorded stage changed from `planned`/`rebasing` to `conflict` and its `FailureKind` became
     `conflict`, which is exactly what the next `--continue` will read. Where a **guard-owned**
     refusal (a limit, an approval, the JIT) fires after that point, its detail carries the
     `state-preserved: ` prefix of §6.4 naming that persisted stage; where the shipped gate itself
     refuses, the sentence is the shipped one and carries no marker at all (§22.31).

   **(ii) The `rebased` ancestry gate (§13.7 gate e, §13.5).** The shipped `resumeFromRebased`
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:941-953`) likewise evaluates by writing: on
   `!gitIsAncestor(opts.RepoDir, entry.NewBaseSHA, entry.Branch)` it sets
   `tx.FailureKind = FailAncestry`, sets
   `tx.FailureMsg = fmt.Sprintf("%s not descended from %s after rebase", entry.Branch, entry.Base)`,
   calls `SaveCheckoutTransaction` (whose error the shipped arm deliberately discards, `_ =`), and
   returns `errors.New(tx.FailureMsg)`. Note what it does **not** touch: `tx.Stage` stays `rebased`,
   so the next `--continue` re-enters the same arm. The two routes are:
   - **plan-only / inspection** evaluates the same predicate and performs **none** of those writes:
     no `FailureKind`, no `FailureMsg`, no `SaveCheckoutTransaction`, no lock. It publishes the
     rank 4 `preflight-refused` blocker of §13.7 gate e with the sentence byte-identical, sets
     `runnable: false` and exits `0`, and `.checkout-sync.tx.yaml` is **byte-identical** before and
     after — the transaction's `FailureKind` is still whatever the interrupted run left (`none` on a
     crash-parked fixture, `interruption` on one parked through the shipped `StepHook`), never
     `ancestry`. The one Git process it adds is the single `merge-base --is-ancestor` read;
   - **guarded executing** preserves shipped behaviour exactly, because the guard seam sits below
     `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` and this gate lives inside native `resumeTransaction`: a guarded
     `--continue` that reaches it performs the shipped `FailureKind`/`FailureMsg` assignment and the
     shipped `SaveCheckoutTransaction`, then fails with the shipped sentence at exit `1`,
     **marker-free** — the refusing party is the shipped gate, not the guard (§6.4, §22.31). Its
     refusal is therefore **not** a "nothing happened" refusal either: the transaction bytes really
     changed, `FailureKind` is `ancestry` and `FailureMsg` carries the sentence, exactly as the
     unguarded control leaves them, and no text may present it otherwise. **No JIT seam and no
     `plan-guard:` marker is added to this arm**: the refusal the operator sees is the shipped
     gate's, raised in its shipped position, and the guard adds no refusal, no sentence and no
     second verdict of its own for it (§12.2d rule 1b). The guarded route's own inspection does
     issue the one projected `merge-base --is-ancestor` read described in gate e — a controlled-path
     probe, exactly like §13.3a rule 6's `rev-parse --verify` — and the native arm then evaluates
     the gate again where it ships; the **unguarded** resume issues only its shipped one and is
     unchanged.

   A plan that mutated the transaction, and a guarded executing twin that *avoided* either shipped
   write in order to look cleaner, both fail §22.13d.
9. **Streams.** The header and fetch prose go to `w.Prose`, which `runCheckoutSync` binds to
   `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`. **The plan route hands `internal` no document writer at all**: the
   document travels back to `cli` as the returned `RebasePlan` and is written by
   `renderPlanDocumentTo` to `cmd.OutOrStdout()` (§3.6 rules 2 and 5). Under `--plan --json` stdout
   carries exactly one JSON value followed by one `\n` and no other byte (§22.9).
10. **The CLI arm is four statements and no logic**: `runCheckoutSync` resolves the feature path,
   sets `opts.FeaturePath`/`opts.RepoDir` (hoisted, step 0), evaluates the shipped I19 predicate
   into a `PlanGateResult`, then — above the I19 *refusal* — calls
   `internal.PlanCheckoutRebase(writers, opts, containment)`, then
   `renderPlanDocument(cmd, plan, opts.PlanGuard.JSON)`, then returns. It contains no limit
   arithmetic, no approval comparison, no fetch, no stack load and no ordering decision of its own.
   On the **executing** route the I19 check keeps its shipped position and its shipped sentence
   exactly.
11. **Typed refusal is for the executing route only; the plan route encodes refusals in its
   document.** `PlanCheckoutRebase`, `BuildCheckoutRebasePlan` and `BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan`
   MUST NOT return a `*PlanGuardRefusalError` for any **document-level** refusal — an I19
   containment projection, any projected fresh or continuation gate, an I14 base failure, a rank
   5.x fact, a limit that would be exceeded, an approval mismatch or any other `refusal.kind`.
   Those are encoded **inside** the returned `RebasePlan` as `blockers[]` + `refusal.kind` +
   `runnable`/`guard.*`, and `runCheckoutSync` renders the document and returns `nil`, so the
   process exits `0` (§3.6). A plan route that returned a typed refusal would (i) print no
   document, (ii) exit `1` on a route whose whole contract is "exit `0` and read the fields", and
   (iii) write a `plan-guard:` marker for a non-executing invocation.
12. **Hard, no-document errors stay ordinary errors, and each function is only accountable for its
   own layer.** A non-`nil` return from these functions means exactly one thing: *this layer could
   not produce a document at all*. The class is §3.6 rows 4–7 — a subject or security failure
   (§3.3 steps 1–5, including the shipped symlink refusal), a control-flag error (already refused
   at step 3, above this route), a document that could not be **encoded**, and an `io.Writer`
   failure while emitting the document or the prose — and none of them is typed. Because the
   control-flag and subject/security causes are decided **above** `PlanCheckoutRebase`, by
   `runCheckoutSync`/`resolvePlanGuardOptions`, they cannot occur inside it: they are members of
   the plan route's error class, not of this function's. Per layer, therefore:
   - `PlanCheckoutRebase` returns non-`nil` **only** for a prose-writer failure and for an error
     its builder returned;
   - `BuildCheckoutRebasePlan` and `BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan` return non-`nil` **only** where
     the document itself could not be constructed — the encoding-class failures of §3.6 row 6 —
     and never for a gate, a limit, an approval, a fetch failure or a rank 5.x fact;
   - the **document** writer failure (§3.6 row 7) is raised by `renderPlanDocumentTo` in `cli`,
     because that is the only function holding a document writer (rule 9, §3.6 rule 5).
   An unreadable or unsortable `stack.yaml`, a refused selection and every projected gate are
   **not** members: they are rows 2–3 of §3.6 and publish the rows-less document at exit `0`
   (rule 4, §22.16). Any earlier statement that a "`stack.yaml`-class failure leaves no document to
   publish" is withdrawn. Errors are returned unwrapped, `planGuardRefusal` passes them through
   unchanged (§6.4), and the process exits `1` with no partial document and no marker. The
   **route-level** count stays exactly four cause classes over five cells (§3.6, §22.12a); this
   rule attributes them to layers, it does not add or remove one.
13. **The typed refusal remains the executing guard/JIT contract.** Every checkout guard seam
   (`RunCheckoutSync` after `BuildCheckoutPlan`, `ContinueCheckoutSync` after
   `forceAcquireCheckoutLock`) and every checkout JIT seam (`processBranch`, `resumeFromSwitched`)
   returns `*internal.PlanGuardRefusalError`; `internal` writes no marker byte; `runCheckoutSync`
  renders it exactly once by returning `planGuardRefusal(cmd, err)`.

**Symbols and files touched by this subsection:** `internal/rebase_plan_guard.go`
(`PlanWriters`, `PlanGateResult`, `PlanGuardLimits`, `PlanValidationIdentity`, `PlanStageFact`,
`CheckoutPlanInspectionRequest`, `CheckoutPlanInspection`, `InspectCheckoutPlan`,
`PlanCheckoutRebase`, `BuildCheckoutRebasePlan`, `BuildCheckoutContinuationPlan`,
`PlanFetchOutcome`, `PlanFetchRepoResult`, `PlanFetchContext`, `PlanFetchPlan`),
`internal/rebase_plan_state.go` (`InspectCheckoutPlanState`, `CheckoutPlanState`,
`CheckoutPlanStateVerdict` and the five concrete artefact types of §12.5a),
`internal/checkout_sync.go` (`fetchCheckoutRepoTo` + its `fetchCheckoutRepo` wrapper and the
shipped call site that now calls it, `printSyncModeHeaderTo` + the `printSyncModeHeader` wrapper,
`buildCheckoutPlanFrom` + the `BuildCheckoutPlan` wrapper that owns the unguarded sort (§9.2),
`firstUnresolvedCheckoutBase`, `checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode`),
`internal/sync_selection.go` (`ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder` + the `ResolveSyncSelection` wrapper,
§9.2a), `internal/git_capability.go` (`ProbeGitVersion`, §16 rule 1a),
`internal/rebase_plan_probe.go` (the §14.1a push-context facts),
`internal/cli/checkout_sync.go` (the
hoisted `opts.FeaturePath`/`opts.RepoDir` assignment, the containment predicate evaluated as a
`PlanGateResult` value, the plan dispatch and `planGuardRefusal` wrapping),
`internal/cli/sync_plan_guard.go` (`renderPlanDocumentTo`).
**Tests (§22.13b, §22.13d, §22.13g, §22.13h, §22.13l):** the plan-path argv sidecar shows exactly one
`git fetch` under
`--plan --fetch` and **zero** under `--plan`, `--plan --no-fetch`, `--plan --continue`, and under a
`--plan --fetch` run failing **each** pre-fetch gate in turn — I19 containment, an existing
transaction, an in-progress Git operation, a dirty tree, a detached HEAD, an unreadable stack, **a
cyclic stack (gate g1)**, a
refused selection, an I14 base failure, a live foreign lock and each of the two gate-l
fetch-effect facts — each of which instead publishes its projected blocker with the shipped
sentence (or, for gate l, its §7.1 rank and `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` token),
`freshness: not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` (or `not-refreshed-live-run` for the lock, or the
matching cause-5/6 token for gate l), exit `0`,
**and no `Sync mode:` header**, while its executing twin keeps the shipped refusal at exit `1`; the
header/fetch prose land on stderr while stdout holds only the document; the fetch is recorded
**before** the first plan probe; no `.checkout-sync.lock` and no transaction file exists afterwards;
`--plan --continue` at every stage of §13.3's table publishes the persisted plan's rows with
`approval.scope: remaining-work` and is asserted to issue **no** `BuildCheckoutPlan`/
`buildCheckoutPlanFrom` call, **no** `TopoSort` call, no
`ResolveSyncSelection` and no `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder` call (probe/seam counter) — and
**at most one** `LoadStack`, exactly in the `checkoutSelectedStillPresent` cell with a non-empty
`tx.Selected`, and zero where that list is empty (rule 2) — and to print the header exactly when
`checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode(tx)` is true; a **document-level** refusal (projected I19, projected
continuation gate, exceeded limit) returns `err == nil` with the refusal inside the document at
exit `0`, while a hard no-subject failure returns an ordinary error at exit `1` with no document;
and a guarded checkout refusal produces the typed error in `internal` with
the single anchored line written in `cli` (§22.17a).
Eight single-owner assertions accompany them (rules 1–3, 6a, §9.1a rule 3, §16 rule 1a): a call
counter shows
`InspectCheckoutPlan` invoked **exactly once** per controlled checkout invocation — plan-only and
guarded executing alike — `InspectCheckoutPlanState`
invoked **exactly once** per controlled checkout invocation on both the plan and the guarded
executing route, `TopoSort` invoked **exactly once** per controlled **fresh** invocation and
**zero** times on a controlled continuation, while the unguarded controls keep their shipped counts
of §9.1a rule 3a — **two** on an unguarded new-mode fresh run (inside `ResolveSyncSelection` above
the lock, then inside `BuildCheckoutPlan` below it) and **one** on an unguarded legacy fresh run —
and `LoadStack`,
`ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder` and `firstUnresolvedCheckoutBase` invoked **at most once** each —
zero for the two latter on a continuation, where `LoadStack` is also zero unless the
`checkoutSelectedStillPresent` cell applies — with the argv sidecar showing a single `stack.yaml`
read; `ProbeGitVersion` invoked **exactly once** per controlled invocation that establishes a
subject, **zero** times on every rows-less no-subject document, and always **after** the subject
read and **before** the first fetch-effect or ordered-config read in the recorded process order
(§16 rules 1a–1b);
the fetch-effect probe set (config inventory, remote resolution, submodule walk, local-branch
inventory) is asserted to run **once, before** the `git fetch` in the recorded process order and
**never after** it, while the push **baseline** read of `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` is asserted to
run exactly once and **after** it (§14.1a rule 7); `BuildCheckoutRebasePlan` is asserted to take
exactly
`(CheckoutPlanInspection, PlanFetchOutcome, PlanPushFacts)` — never a `RebasePlanLayout`, never a
bare
`CheckoutSyncOpts`, never a stack or selection argument — and to issue **no** Git process at all
when called directly with a pre-built inspection; `PlanWriters` is asserted to have exactly one
field (`Prose`) and `PlanCheckoutRebase` to write **nothing** to a buffer bound as stdout; and an
**unreadable** and a **cyclic**
`stack.yaml` each produce the rows-less document at exit `0` with `refusal.kind` set, proving they
are not members of rule 12's error class.

### 13.7a External plan-only ordering — the normative twin

The external plan route is the *other* half of the same contract and is specified here, not left to
inference from §12.2b. Like the checkout route it never enters its executor
(`runScopedSync`/`syncFeature`/`handleSyncContinue`/`handleScopedSyncContinue`), so it performs the
described route's header and policy fetch itself — in the executor's order, exactly once, through
explicit writers — and it publishes every refusal it can compute inside the document.

**Entry points (package `cli`, one inspection producer and one route function):**

```go
// internal/cli/sync_plan_guard.go — package cli
//
// `changed` is the flag-presence map produced by resolveSyncPolicy
// (internal/cli/sync_modes.go:42-45) and is threaded in unchanged; this function
// MUST NOT call cmd.Flags().Changed itself (§13.7a rule 9).
func runExternalPlan(cmd *cobra.Command, feature string, layout externalSyncLayout,
    ws internal.Workspace, policy internal.SyncRunPolicy, newMode, push, verbose bool,
    changed map[string]bool, opts planGuardOptions, state internal.SyncExternalState) error

// ExternalPlanInspectionRequest is everything a controlled EXTERNAL route knows
// before it reads its subject. It is constructed in exactly two places — the
// plan route at step 4 and the guarded routes of §12.2b/§12.3 at their
// subject-read step — and nowhere else.
type ExternalPlanInspectionRequest struct {
    Feature   string
    Layout    externalSyncLayout        // cli-owned; the planner-facing twin is planLayout(layout)
    Mode      internal.WorkspaceMode
    Route     string                    // the EFFECTIVE route of §13.6 rule 4, decided at step 3
    Policy    internal.SyncRunPolicy    // the EFFECTIVE policy (payload-derived on a --continue)
    Continue  bool
    Push      bool
    Changed   map[string]bool           // the resolveSyncPolicy-owned flag-presence map, threaded
                                        // in so gate d can be projected from the SHIPPED
                                        // syncContinueMismatches predicate; this struct is the
                                        // only way it crosses into the inspection, which MUST NOT
                                        // call cmd.Flags().Changed (rule 9)
    Snapshot  internal.ExternalPlanState // step 2's five-artefact snapshot (§12.5)
    Payload   *internal.SyncRunState     // the persisted run on a --continue; nil on a fresh run
}

// ExternalPlanInspection is the external twin of CheckoutPlanInspection: the
// single composite result of reading an external plan subject. Every member is
// measured EXACTLY ONCE, and nothing below re-loads, re-sorts, re-resolves or
// re-probes any of them. It lives in package cli because the reads it composes
// need cli-owned values (externalSyncLayout, firstUnresolvedSelectedBase); it
// carries only internal-owned RESULTS across the boundary, so §9.0's rule that
// `internal` never learns a `cli` type is untouched.
type ExternalPlanInspection struct {
    Stack             *internal.Stack
    StackErr          error                    // the shipped sentence, verbatim
    Order             []internal.StackEntry    // the ONE TopoSort result (§9.1a rule 3)
    SortErr           error                    // `cycle detected in stack.yaml`, verbatim
    Selection         internal.SyncSelection   // from ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder (§9.2a)
    SelectionResolved bool
    SelectionErr      error
    Remaining         []string                 // RemainingRebaseEntries on a --continue (§13.3)
    BasePreflight     internal.PlanBasePreflight // I14; this producer is its ONLY caller (rule 3)
    Version           internal.GitVersion      // the ONE ProbeGitVersion of this invocation
    Capabilities      internal.GitCapabilities // §16 rule 1a; skipped ⇒ Version.Probed == false
    FetchPlan         internal.PlanFetchPlan   // the pre-fetch enumeration of §11.1
    PushFacts         internal.PlanPushFacts   // §14.1a rule 7, MAPPING half only, Phase pre-fetch:
                                               // the distinct push contexts, the identity table,
                                               // the materialization map and each context's
                                               // origin/refspec decomposition. NO remote-tracking
                                               // ref is read here; step 7a refreshes it
    Gates             []internal.PlanGateResult // step 5's ladder, TYPED and in shipped order
                                               // (§13.5 rule G); never []internal.PlanBlocker
    ContinuationGate  internal.PlanContinuationGate // gate d decomposed, from the SAME single
                                               // syncContinueMismatches call that produced its
                                               // PlanGateResult row (rule 9)
    RowsAvailable     bool                     // rule 4
}

// InspectExternalPlan performs steps 4 and 5 below — and nothing else. It runs
// no fetch, claims no guard, writes no state and prints nothing; it is called
// EXACTLY ONCE per controlled external invocation, by the plan route and by the
// guarded routes alike, and it is the ONLY site on those routes that calls
// LoadStack, TopoSort, ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder,
// scopedSelectionFromPayloadOrder, RemainingRebaseEntries,
// firstUnresolvedSelectedBase, ProbeGitVersion, the fetch-context enumeration
// or the push mapping-fact enumeration, and the only site that projects the
// external gate ladder into []internal.PlanGateResult.
//
// The name is deliberately the exported twin of internal.InspectCheckoutPlan,
// so the two controlled routes are found by one search; package cli lives under
// internal/, so the capital adds no external API surface, and no other spelling
// (inspectExternalPlan, ExternalSubjectReads, …) may be used for it.
func InspectExternalPlan(req ExternalPlanInspectionRequest) ExternalPlanInspection
```

**Exact ordering inside `runExternalPlan`.** The plan-only order is **deliberately not** the
executor's order, and the difference is a decision, not an accident: the executor raises its state
gates first because it is about to *mutate*, while the plan's job is to publish as much of the run
as it can measure. Loading and resolving the subject **before** projecting the state gates is what
lets a refused document still carry `entries[]` wherever the stack and the selection were readable
(rule 4). Nothing observable moves because of it — the reads below are pure, they are performed on
a route the executor never enters, and every gate keeps its shipped predicate, its shipped sentence
and its shipped rank. **Native guarded execution keeps the shipped gate order verbatim** (§12.2b,
§12.3): this reordering is scoped to `--plan`.

```text
1. dispatch position: below classifySyncState, above abort/continue routing, syncCellRefusal, I20,
   the previous-incomplete refusal, runScopedSync and syncFeature (§3.3 step 6).
2. safe snapshot: snap := internal.InspectExternalPlanState(layout.FeaturePath,
   internal.ExternalPlanStateOpts{Classified: state}) — the five-artefact presence/decode snapshot
   of §12.5, composed around the classifier `state` this route was handed. It is the ONLY source of
   `state.files.*`, of guard liveness and of the §11.2 cause-3 observation on this route; `state`
   alone is not that snapshot (rule 6).
3. route and identity: derive the EFFECTIVE route from `state` (§13.6 rule 4) — trigger-derived on
   a fresh run, payload-derived through internal.PayloadNewMode on a --continue — and the effective
   policy, limits and validation identity from the persisted payload on a continuation, from this
   invocation's flags on a fresh run (§13.2, §15).
4. insp := InspectExternalPlan(ExternalPlanInspectionRequest{…}) — ONE call, performing the pure
   subject reads BEFORE any gate and BEFORE any network call, each EXACTLY ONCE and in this order:
     4.1 stack load → **TopoSort** (the ONE sort of this invocation, §9.1a rule 3; its
         []StackEntry result is kept as insp.Order and is what every consumer below receives)
     4.2 `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder(stack, insp.Order, policy, …)` — the order-taking body of

     4.3 on a --continue, RemainingRebaseEntries (§13.3) over that same order
     4.4 firstUnresolvedSelectedBase under an effective no-fetch policy (§10.7, and this is its ONE
         call site on this route, rule 3)
     4.5 the ONE `ProbeGitVersion()` of this invocation (§16 rule 1a), issued **after** 4.1–4.2
         established a subject and **before** 4.6; **skipped** — insp.Version.Probed false, zero
         `git --version` processes — where 4.1/4.2 failed and the document is rows-less (§16

     4.6 fetch-context candidate enumeration (§11.1), kept as insp.FetchPlan (the value step 7
         calls `fp`) and consumed by step 7 and by nothing else, with every capability-dependent
         claim decided from insp.Capabilities
     4.7 the **mapping half** of the push facts of §14.1a rule 7 where `intent.push` is true **and**
```
