```text
         `PlanPushRemoteFacts` per **distinct push context** the projection will name — `entry.Repo`
         else the entry's materialized worktree, enumerated through `ResolvePushContext` (§14.1a) —
         carrying that context's measured identity and canonical `--git-common-dir`, its ordered
         config inventory, whether a remote literally named `origin` exists and
         `remote.origin.fetch` decomposed in configured order, plus the per-entry materialization,
         kept as `insp.PushFacts` with `Phase: pre-fetch`. Each context's `MappingReadOK` records
         whether that identity/config pair really was read; a failure there is rule 5a's rank 5.9
         `probe-failed` row, never an `absent` lease. **No remote-tracking ref is read here**:
         step 7 may fetch and move exactly those refs, and the lease's expectation/ref/SHA are
         approval-tuple members (§8.3). Pure local reads: no network call, and no push
     4.8 the gate ladder of step 5, projected into `insp.Gates` as typed `[]internal.PlanGateResult`
         rows in the shipped order, each with its ladder ID, its `Applies`/`Failed` verdict, its
         §7.1 rank, its entry and the shipped sentence verbatim (§13.5 rule G). Gate d is projected
         by calling the **shipped** `syncContinueMismatches(payload, policy, req.Changed, push)`
         exactly once and decomposing its error into **both** that row and
         `insp.ContinuationGate` (rule 9); gate f reads the snapshot's live-foreign observation and
         carries `Controlled: [live-owner-concurrency]`. The projection is pure: it evaluates
         shipped predicates over values already in hand, writes nothing and prints nothing
   A failure here is itself a document-level fact, not an error: an unreadable stack is rank 1
   `plan-unavailable`, an unsortable stack rank 1 `stack-unsortable`, a refused selection rank 2
   `selection-refused`, each yielding the rows-less document of §4.3 at exit `0` (§3.6 row 2).
   The **guarded** external routes (§12.2b, §12.3) make this same one call at their own
   subject-read step and execute from its results, so plan-only and guarded external runs decide
   the order, the selection, the preflight, the capabilities, the fetch plan, the push mapping
   facts and the projected gate ladder from one producer.
5. gate projection, still BEFORE any network call, in the shipped ladder's order, each onto its
   §7.1 rank with the shipped sentence verbatim (§13.5). **It happened at step 4.8, inside the
   inspection**; this step is where the route *reads* `insp.Gates`, decides whether any row
   refuses, and — on the **guarded** routes — lets the native ladder raise its own refusal in its
   shipped position (§12.2b, §12.3). No predicate is evaluated twice, and `runExternalPlan`
   calls none of them itself:
     a. syncCellRefusal for this verb — preceded, on classifier cell 4 and on no other cell, by the
        §12.8b interception, whose sentence (the valid-backup-sentinel plain/verdict sentence, or
        the shipped I20 sentence where this invocation supplies a mode-trigger flag) is what this
        gate publishes there                              → rank 3 state-refused
     b. I20 (syncTriggersNeedV2)                          → rank 3
        — Applies: false on cell 4, whose answer gate (a) already owns (§13.6 rule 4a, §25.82)
     c. the legacy previous-incomplete refusal            → rank 3
     d. --continue only, and only where a payload persists a policy: syncContinueMismatches(payload,
        policy, changed, push) — the SHIPPED
        predicate, called with the SHIPPED `changed` map (§13.7a rule 9)   → rank 3
     e1. --continue only: the failed-branch rebase-in-progress check
        (`rebase still in progress in %s; …`)             → rank 3
     e2. --continue only, and only where the **resolved-failure conjunct** below holds: the
        failed-branch existence check
        (`failed branch %q no longer exists in stack`)    → rank 3
     e3. --continue only, under the same conjunct: the configured-parent ancestry check
        (`resolved branch %s still does not contain its configured parent %s`); its
        `Applies && !Failed` verdict, together with e2's, is also what tells a guarded resume to
        print the shipped `[~] resolved` line at its shipped position (§12.3) → rank 3
     e4. --continue only, envelope arms only: state.GuardForeign()          → rank 3
     f. a pre-existing live foreign .sync-run.lock in `snap` → rank 3 + §11.2 cause 3
   **The resolved-failure conjunct is the shipped one, per arm, and it is not a simplification of
   it.** Gates e2 and e3 — and therefore the `[~] resolved` line — are `Applies: true` **iff**:

   | Arm | Predicate | Shipped site |
   |---|---|---|
   | scoped v2/v3 payload (`handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue`, and every `--plan --continue` over a payload) | `payload.FailedBranch != "" && !payloadCompleted(payload, payload.FailedBranch)` | `internal/cli/sync.go:386` |
   | v3 `route: legacy` envelope (`handleGuardedLegacySyncContinue`, envelope arm) | the same payload predicate — the envelope persists `Completed`/`FailedBranch` with the same meaning | `internal/cli/sync.go:386`, by construction of §13.6 |
   | real legacy `.sync-state.yaml` (cell 7) | `state.FailedBranch != ""` — the legacy state has no push stage and therefore no push-failure encoding | `internal/cli/sync.go:326` |

   `payloadCompleted` (`internal/cli/sync.go:462-476`) is called, never re-implemented, and gate e1
   keeps the **bare** `FailedBranch != ""` condition on every arm, exactly as shipped
   (`:369-372`, `:315-319`): a push failure records the entry in **both** `completed` and
   `failed_branch`, and the shipped resume then re-checks nothing about its parent edge, re-runs no
   validation and prints no `[~] resolved` for it. A **push-failure resume** therefore performs
   **zero** `internal.GetBranch` existence lookups, **zero** `branchContainsConfiguredParent`
   calls and emits **zero** `[~] resolved` lines, and the inspection records gates `external-e2`
   and `external-e3` as `Applies: false, Failed: false` — not-applicable rows, which
   `GateBlockers` drops and which no document may publish as a blocker (§13.5 rule G, §22.14b).
   A projection that dropped the `payloadCompleted` conjunct would re-check a parent edge the
   shipped resume never re-checks, and could refuse a push retry the shipped binary completes.
   Each of a–f is evaluated **exactly once per invocation**, here, and the row it produces is the
   only verdict any consumer reads: the plan route renders it, and a guarded route returns its
   `Detail` natively at the shipped position (§12.3). The one predicate a guarded route re-reads
   below this ladder is `checkSyncRunGuardReclaimable` (§12.4), because it is a compare-and-swap
   precondition about *now* rather than a projection.
   **The external completion gate is NOT a member of this list** (rule 15): `staleStackEdgesFiltered`
   is a POSTCONDITION the executor evaluates after its rebases, so on a fresh run and on any
   continuation with rebase rows a currently stale edge is the work this run performs, not a reason
   to refuse or to suppress the fetch. It is projected as a rank 4 blocker in exactly one cell — a
   rows-less push-only continuation (rule 15, §7.1, §13.5) — and published as the row's `ancestry`
   fact everywhere else.
   **The deferred half of I7 is NOT a member either** (rule 7): `--plan` with `--abort` is an
   early REFUSE at §3.3 step 3 (§3.4), so no `--plan` invocation can ever carry both verbs, and
   projecting `syncStateRefusesContinueAbort` here would be dead code plus a blocker no document
   can publish. The predicate itself is unchanged and stays on the executing route (§13.6 rule 4b).
6. prose := cmd.ErrOrStderr()
   if newMode && NO refusing pre-fetch blocker of ANY rank was recorded in steps 4–5:
       printSyncModeHeaderTo(prose, policy)
   — header first, as shipped; the legacy route prints NO header on any ordering (§12.3), and a
   live-owner, state, I20, continuation-mismatch, unreadable-stack or
   selection refusal suppresses the header exactly as it suppresses the fetch (rule 5). A stale
   current ancestry never suppresses either (rule 15)
7. the route's own policy fetch, EXACTLY ONCE and only when no §11.2 cause suppressed it:
       legacy, fresh              → fetchStackReposTo(prose, prose, layout, stack, verbose, fp)
       new-mode, fresh, fetch     → fetchScopedReposTo(prose, prose, layout, stack, sel, verbose,
                                                       fp)
       new-mode, fresh, no-fetch  → no fetch at all       (freshness: local-only)
       any --continue             → no fetch at all       (§11.2 cause 1)
       any refusing gate or step-4 failure → no fetch at all
                                            (freshness: not-refreshed-no-plan-subject, or
                                             not-refreshed-live-run for gate f)
   where `fp` is step 4's enumerated PlanFetchPlan. Where a cause **4, 5 or 6** fact suppressed the
   fetch, the outcome is built from `fp` instead of from a child: one un-attempted row per resolved
   context, carrying exactly what §4.4a requires of that cause (cause 4: known tokens and
   candidates only; causes 5–6: the whole measured row), with `Attempted: false` and `Suppressed`
   set. Causes 1–3, `local-only` and `not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets` produce `Repos: []`
7a. push := internal.RefreshPushTrackingRefs(insp.PushFacts, <step 7's PlanFetchOutcome>)
   — the ONE baseline measurement of this invocation (§14.1a rule 7), performed **iff**
   `insp.PushFacts.Applies` is true and then placed **after** step 7 in every cell, including the
   cells where step 7 fetched nothing. Where the facts are not applicable — `intent.push` false, or
   a rows-less document — this step is **skipped entirely**: zero calls, zero ref reads, and the
   `{Applies: false, Phase: "not-applicable"}` value travels to the builder unchanged. Otherwise it
   re-reads each push context's
   remote-tracking inventory, stamps `TrackingPhase: post-fetch` where a child really ran and
   `plan-point` where none did (`--no-fetch`, any `--continue`, a suppression, a refusing gate),
   and sets `FetchedThisRun` through `PushContextRefreshed` conjoined with the two read flags —
   true only for a context whose mapping and inventory were both read and whose
   canonical common dir was fetched successfully **by a fetch that contacted the remote named
   `origin`** (§14.1a rule 8). Two external consequences follow directly and are asserted in
   §22.33f: two linked worktrees sharing one common dir are **both** `fresh` after the single fetch
   §11.4's collapse rule performs, and a context whose `branch.<name>.remote` is `upstream`
   publishes `possibly-stale` even though its own fetch succeeded, because `origin`'s baseline was
   not refreshed
8. internal.BuildRebasePlan(req)  — `req` is the §9.1a `RebasePlanRequest`, constructed here and
   nowhere else on this route: req.Fetch is the PlanFetchOutcome returned by step 7,
   req.FetchPlan is `fp` (insp.FetchPlan), req.Order is insp.Order — step 4's single TopoSort
   result, never re-sorted —
   req.Stack/req.Selection/req.SelectionResolved/req.RowsAvailable are step 4's values,
   req.Version/req.Capabilities are insp.Version/insp.Capabilities (§16 rule 1a; never re-probed),
   req.Layout is planLayout(layout), req.ExternalState is step 2's snapshot,
   req.CheckoutState is the not-applicable value (§12.5a rule 5),
   req.BasePreflight is insp.BasePreflight, req.Changed is the threaded `changed` map,
   req.ContinuationGate is insp.ContinuationGate, req.Gates is insp.Gates — the typed ladder,
   assigned as itself and converted to blockers only inside the builder (§13.5 rule G) —
   req.PushFacts is step 7a's refreshed value, **never** insp.PushFacts,
   req.Route/req.Policy/req.Limits/
   req.Validation are step 3's EFFECTIVE values, and req.Remaining is insp.Remaining on a
   continuation. The push projection consumes req.PushFacts through `PushTargets` (§14.1a rule 9),
   inside the builder and nowhere else
9. renderPlanDocument(cmd, plan, opts.JSON)   — document to stdout, prose already on stderr
10. return nil  — exit 0, whatever refusal.kind the document carries
```

**Rows, plannability and freshness per gate (total; the external twin of §13.7 rule 4).**
`entries[]` exists exactly where step 4 established the inputs a row is made of — the stack, its
sort and (new-mode) the selection on a fresh run; the persisted remaining set on a continuation:

| Refusing fact | Rows? | `summary.plannability` | `freshness` |
|---|---|---|---|
| unreadable `stack.yaml` (rank 1 `plan-unavailable`) | no | `unavailable` | `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` (or `local-only` under a no-fetch policy) |
| cyclic stack (rank 1 `stack-unsortable`) | no | `unavailable` | same |
| `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder` failure (rank 2) | no | `unavailable` | same |
| `--continue` whose payload/remaining set could not be established | no | `unavailable` | `not-refreshed-continuation` |
| cell refusal (5a), I20 (5b), previous-incomplete (5c) | **yes** where step 4 succeeded | `rows` (or `empty` for a zero-row selection) | `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` / `not-refreshed-continuation` on a `--continue` |
| continuation mismatch (5d), failed-branch checks (5e1–5e3), `GuardForeign()` (5e4) | **yes** — the persisted run's remaining rows are already in hand | `rows` | `not-refreshed-continuation` |
| live foreign guard (5f) | **yes** | `rows` | `not-refreshed-live-run` |
| I14 (step 4, rank 5.7) | **yes**, blocker on the offending row | `rows` | `local-only` — the route is `no-fetch`, so nothing was suppressed |
| completion gate, rows-less push-only continuation only (rule 15) | no rebase rows by definition; `push.targets[]` and the blocker are published | `empty` | `not-refreshed-continuation` |

Because the gates are projected **after** step 4, a refusing state gate no longer costs the
operator the rows: a `--plan` that meets a live foreign guard or a cell refusal
still shows what the run *would* replay, which is the whole point of asking for a plan. That is the
declared behavioural difference between this order and the executor's, and it is asserted in
§22.13c.

**Writer-aware fetch helpers (the shipped bodies, returning what they observed):**

```go
// internal/cli/sync.go — one body each; the shipped symbols are wrappers (§3.6 rule 3)
func fetchQuietTo(out, errw io.Writer, repo, wtPath string, verbose bool,
    ctx internal.PlanFetchContext) internal.PlanFetchRepoResult
func fetchScopedReposTo(out, errw io.Writer, layout externalSyncLayout, stack internal.Stack,
    sel internal.SyncSelection, verbose bool, plan internal.PlanFetchPlan) internal.PlanFetchOutcome
func fetchStackReposTo(out, errw io.Writer, layout externalSyncLayout, stack internal.Stack,
    verbose bool, plan internal.PlanFetchPlan) internal.PlanFetchOutcome
```

```go
// internal/rebase_plan_guard.go — the join the aggregating helpers use
//
// ContextFor returns the enumerated context for one (repoToken, worktree path)
// pair of the shipped loops. On the ZERO PlanFetchPlan — the value the unguarded
// executing wrapper passes — it returns the minimal context
// {RepoToken, Root, Source} with Effect nil and Candidates [], and it probes
// nothing: the unguarded route enumerates nothing and reads no result.
func (p PlanFetchPlan) ContextFor(repoToken, wtPath string) PlanFetchContext
```

Binding rules (numbered; the ordering above references them by number):

1. **`fetchQuietTo` returns a complete row; it is never `void` and never partially filled.** Its
  body **is** the shipped `fetchQuiet`
  body (`internal/cli/sync.go:604-635`) with `fmt.Printf` → `fmt.Fprintf(out, …)` and the child's
  error captured instead of discarded: the quiet arm already computes `err` for its `done`/`failed`
  line, and the **verbose** arm — which today discards `RunDir`'s error — captures the return of
  `internal.RunDirTo(out, errw, …)` / `internal.RunTo(out, errw, …)` (§3.6 rule 4). It fills all
  **eight** fields of `PlanFetchRepoResult` (§13.7), from two sources and no third:
  - observed by itself — `RepoToken` (the `repo` argument, `""` included), `ContextRoot` and
    `ContextSource` from the **shipped** cwd ladder it already runs (`wtPath` ⇒ `worktree`, else
    `repo` ⇒ `entry-repo`, else the process cwd ⇒ `process-cwd`), `Attempted`, and `OK`;
  - **copied** from `ctx`, the pre-fetch enumeration for that same context — `ContextCommonDir`,
    `Effect` and `ContextCandidates`. `ContextCandidates` is normalised to `[]` when `ctx` carries
    none, so the field is **never `nil`** (§4.4a).

  It measures **no** effect, resolves **no** remote and reads **no** config of its own, so the plan
  never re-derives a fetch fact after the fact (the checkout twin's rule 6a, applied here).
  **The shipped `fetchQuiet` becomes a one-line wrapper** — `_ = fetchQuietTo(os.Stdout, os.Stderr,
  repo, wtPath, verbose, internal.PlanFetchContext{})` — so the quiet prose still lands on stdout
  and the verbose child's stderr
  still lands on stderr, exactly as `RunDir` wires it today. Its output bytes, its ordering and its
  interleaving are unchanged, which the 126 `sync_noflag` goldens enforce; **no executing route
  observes the return value.**
2. **The outcome-returning writer variants are the only fetch implementations, and exactly one of
  them runs per invocation.** `fetchScopedReposTo` / `fetchStackReposTo` return `PlanFetchOutcome`,
  aggregating one `PlanFetchRepoResult` per fetched context in the order the shipped loops visit
  them and setting `Applies`, `Attempted` and `Suppressed` per the §13.7 domain table. Each row is
  produced by `fetchQuietTo(out, errw, repo, wtPath, verbose, plan.ContextFor(repo, wtPath))`, so
  the join to the pre-fetch enumeration happens **inside** the helper and every returned row is
  complete. `fetchScopedReposTo` is the extracted
  shipped scoped loop (`selectedRealEntries` → `UniqueRepos` → per-repo fetch) and
  `fetchStackReposTo` the extracted shipped legacy loop (`UniqueRepos` over the whole stack) —
  **including their shipped iteration order**, which the added `plan` parameter never reorders;
  neither takes a `*SyncRunState`, so neither can write a stage (§12.2b). All three callers share
  them: the unguarded executor with `os.Stdout, os.Stderr` and the **zero** `PlanFetchPlan` at its
  shipped point (a pure extraction, §19.4), the **guarded** routes of §12.2b/§12.3 with the same
  two writers, their enumerated plan, above their claim **and
  consuming the returned outcome**, and the plan route with its prose writer twice over.
  **No result-less fetch helper may feed `BuildRebasePlan` on any route.** The three result-less
  spellings that still exist — `fetchQuiet`, and any shipped inline loop they wrap — are wrappers
  for the *executing unguarded* path only; no planned or guarded route calls them, and the builder
  never receives a fetch fact that was not returned by a writer variant. Step 7 is the only fetch
  site on this route: the builder never fetches, `syncFeature`/`syncFeatureScoped` are never
  entered, and a second `git fetch` in the argv sidecar for one plan invocation is a test failure
  (§22.13c). The returned `PlanFetchOutcome` **fully determines** the document's `fetch.*` schema
  and `freshness` (rule 10).
3. **`InspectExternalPlan` is the single I14 owner and the single subject reader on every
  controlled external route (§10.7, §9.1a rule 3, §16 rule 1a).** Step 4 calls
  `firstUnresolvedSelectedBase` **at most once**, under an effective `no-fetch` policy, and the
  route passes the result as `req.BasePreflight`. It likewise calls `LoadStack`, `TopoSort`,
  `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder`, `RemainingRebaseEntries` and `ProbeGitVersion` at most once
  each, and the sorting wrapper `ResolveSyncSelection` **never**.
  `BuildRebasePlan` **consumes** those values and MUST NOT call the
  locator, `verifySelectedBasesLocally`, `TopoSort`, `ProbeGitVersion` or any equivalent probe; no
  other site on this route calls
  either. The guarded **executing** external routes make the **same one** `InspectExternalPlan`
  call at their subject-read step and keep the shipped
  `verifySelectedBasesLocally` wrapper as the executing preflight owner at its shipped position
  (§12.2b) — the wrapper's locator half is the value the inspection already produced, so the probe
  budget stays one per invocation — and the checkout twin is
  §13.7 rule 3. One evaluation per invocation, in every mode, on every route.
4. **Rows exist exactly where step 4 established them**, per the table above: `entries[]` is
  published whenever the stack loaded, sorted and (new-mode) resolved a selection on a fresh run, or
  whenever the persisted remaining set was established on a continuation — refusing gate or not —
  and the document is the rows-less `summary.plannability: unavailable` profile of §4.3 otherwise.
  This is the exact twin of §13.7 rule 4. The sort that decides it is the **same single**
  `TopoSort` whose result reaches `ExecutionOrder` as `req.Order`; this route never sorts twice and
  never re-loads `stack.yaml` after step 4 (§9.1a rule 3).
5. **The header and the fetch are both gated on "no refusing pre-fetch blocker of any rank".** A
  refusing cell refusal, I20, previous-incomplete refusal, continuation mismatch, failed-branch
  check, `GuardForeign()`, live foreign guard, unreadable/unsortable stack, refused
  selection or I14 suppresses **both**. There is no rank whose refusal prints a `Sync mode:` header,
  and none that fetches. The legacy route prints no header in any cell (§12.3). The completion gate
  is **not** on that list (rule 15).
6. **The five-artefact snapshot has exactly one producer, and `SyncExternalState` alone is not
  it.** `internal.InspectExternalPlanState` (§12.5) is the sole source of `state.files.*`, of guard
  liveness and of the §11.2 cause-3 observation on every controlled external route — the plan route
  at step 2, and the guarded routes at their §12.1 snapshot step — and its value travels to the
  builder as `req.ExternalState`. **No text in this specification, in a comment or in a test may
  claim that the classifier's `SyncExternalState` carries that snapshot**: it decodes at most three
  paths, it skips `.sync-run.lock` entirely on a legacy route (`AlwaysReadGuard: newMode`), and it
  has no `presence`/`unreadable_reason` vocabulary at all. It is an **input** to the snapshot, not
  the snapshot.
7. **The deferred half of I7 is not projected on this route, and no dead gate is kept for
  symmetry.** `--plan` with `--abort` is refused at §3.3 step 3 by §3.4, so a `--plan` invocation
  can never carry `--continue --abort`; `syncStateRefusesContinueAbort` therefore has no reachable
  cell here, and projecting it would publish a blocker no document can contain. The predicate keeps
  its shipped, route-derived definition and its executing call site (§13.6 rule 4b), and the
  checkout twin `checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode` likewise stays on `AbortCheckoutSync`'s executing path
  (§13.6 rule 4c). Any earlier list that included deferred I7 among this route's projected gates is
  **withdrawn**, in this subsection, in §11.2 cause 2's membership prose, in §17.2 and in §22.13c.
8. **`RebasePlanRequest` is the §9.1a struct, and it carries the outcome, the order, the gates,
  the push facts, the
  capabilities and both snapshots.** Its complete declaration is §9.1a; the members this subsection
  adds to the earlier revisions' picture are
  `Fetch PlanFetchOutcome`, `FetchPlan PlanFetchPlan`, `PushFacts PlanPushFacts`,
  `Gates []PlanGateResult`, `Order []StackEntry`,
  `Version GitVersion`, `Capabilities GitCapabilities`,
  `ExternalState ExternalPlanState` and
  `CheckoutState CheckoutPlanState`, and `BuildRebasePlan` derives
  `fetch.attempted`, `fetch.outcome`,
  `fetch.suppression_cause`, **every one of the eight members of each `fetch.repos[]` row**
  (`repo_token`, `context_root`, `context_common_dir`, `context_source`, `fetch_effect`,
  `context_candidates[]`, `attempted`, `ok`), `freshness` (§11.3) and every `state.files.*` row
  **from
  them** — never by re-probing and never by assuming. Exactly one of the two state members is
  applicable per invocation: the other carries the `applicable: false` rows of §12.5a rule 5, and
  the builder publishes them as `presence: not-applicable` rather than omitting the keys. The row
  members that were **measured before** the fetch —
  `context_common_dir`, `fetch_effect` and
  `context_candidates[]` — reach the outcome through the fetch helpers themselves, which copy them
  from the pre-fetch enumeration (rule 1 on this route, §13.7 rule 6a on the checkout route); the
  builder therefore performs **no** join of its own and has no second source to disagree with. So
  every published fetch fact is either what was measured before the fetch or
  what the fetch itself reported. **No result-discarding fetch wrapper may feed `BuildRebasePlan`
  on any route**: `fetchQuiet`, `fetchCheckoutRepo` and any shipped inline loop they wrap exist for
  the *executing unguarded* path only, and a source assertion shows no planned or guarded route
  calls one (rule 2, §22.13c).
9. **The `changed` map has exactly one owner, and the continuation mismatch is projected, not
  re-derived.** `resolveSyncPolicy` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:41-45`) is the **sole** producer of
  the flag-presence map over `syncPresenceFlags`; `runExternalPlan` receives it as a parameter and
  threads it into `InspectExternalPlan` through `ExternalPlanInspectionRequest.Changed`. Neither
  function may call `cmd.Flags().Changed` for any purpose, and neither `internal` nor the builder
  may reconstruct it. `RebasePlanRequest` gains exactly two members for this axis:

  ```go
  // internal/rebase_plan.go
  Changed          map[string]bool      // verbatim resolveSyncPolicy output; read-only
  ContinuationGate PlanContinuationGate // the projected shipped verdict
  ```

  ```go
  type PlanContinuationGate struct {
      Applies bool   // the described route really runs the frozen-axis comparison
      Failed  bool   // the shipped predicate refused
      Axis    string // "fetch" | "propagation" | "scope" | "push" — the axis it named
      Detail  string // the shipped sentence, verbatim
  }
  ```

  `Failed`/`Axis`/`Detail` are produced by calling the **shipped**
  `syncContinueMismatches(payload, policy, changed, push)` (`internal/cli/sync.go:435-456`) and
  decomposing its error; the planner MUST NOT re-implement its four comparisons, its
  "only if changed" conditions or its sentence. Because the same map and the same predicate decide
  the executing route's refusal, the projection is exact by construction: a `--plan --continue` that
  publishes `ContinuationGate.Failed: false` is a run whose executing twin passes that gate, and one
  that publishes `true` carries the byte-identical sentence in its rank 3 blocker (§13.5). The map
  is a fingerprint non-member (§8.3: `route_triggers[]` and every policy-source label are excluded),
  so threading it changes no token.
10. **Suppression short-circuits step 7 entirely**, in the §11.2 precedence order: a `--continue`, a
  route with no plannable subject (including `plan-unavailable`, `stack-unsortable`,
  `selection-refused` and every refusing pre-fetch gate of step 5), a pre-existing live foreign
  owner in the snapshot, an indeterminate context, unbounded submodule reach, or a held covered
  local-branch destination. `PlanFetchOutcome.Suppressed` carries the single satisfied cause token,
  which is exactly the `fetch.suppression_cause` the document publishes (§4.4a).
11. **Freshness on a refusing cell.** `fetch.attempted: false` and `fetch.outcome: skipped` in
  every suppressed cell, spelled
  `not-refreshed-continuation` on any `--continue` (§11.2 cause 1, which outranks everything else
  here), `not-refreshed-live-run` for the live-guard gate (cause 3), `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject`
  for every other refusing gate or step-4 failure on a route whose effective policy would have
  fetched (cause 2), and `local-only` where the effective policy is `no-fetch`, because nothing was
  suppressed. `fetch.repos[]` follows §4.4a, not the refusal: `[]` for causes 1–3, `local-only` and
  `not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets`, and the enumeration's **un-attempted rows** for causes 4–6 —
  tokens and candidates for cause 4, the whole measured row for causes 5–6. `entries[]` rows are
  decided by rule 4 and the table above, never by which gate refused.
12. **Streams.** The `Sync mode:` header and all fetch prose go to `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`; the document
  goes to `cmd.OutOrStdout()` through `renderPlanDocument` (§3.6). Under `--plan --json` stdout
  carries exactly one JSON value followed by one `\n` and no other byte (§22.9); under
  `--plan --verbose` the child
  fetch output lands on stderr through `RunDirTo`/`RunTo`.
13. **No state, no lock, no claim.** `setupSyncRunState`, `ClaimSyncRunGuard`,
  `ReclaimSyncRunGuard`,
  `saveIncompleteSync`, `saveScopedSyncFailure` and `syncFallback` are unreachable from this route
  (§18.1). The `plan-unavailable` interception of §19.2 replaces the `syncFallback` arm before it
  can run.
14. **Refusal semantics mirror §13.7 exactly, layer by layer.** Every document-level refusal — a
  projected continuation gate, a projected cell refusal, an unreadable or cyclic stack, a refused
  selection, I14, any rank 1–12 fact — is encoded in the returned
  document and exits `0`. `runExternalPlan` returns a non-`nil` error only for the §3.6 rows 4–7
  class, and only for the members its **own layer** can raise: an encoding failure and a writer
  failure (its own prose writer, and the document writer it hands `renderPlanDocument`). The
  subject/security row is raised **above** it, at §3.3 steps 1–5, and the control-flag row at step
  3, so neither can originate inside this function — they are members of the route's class, not of
  this function's. `internal.BuildRebasePlan` likewise returns non-`nil` only where the document
  could not be constructed, never for a gate, a fetch failure or a rank 5.x fact. It
  never constructs a `*internal.PlanGuardRefusalError`, which stays the guarded **executing**
  contract. The route-level count is unchanged: four cause classes over five cells (§3.6,
  §22.12a).
15. **The completion gate is a postcondition, and this route projects it in exactly one cell.**
  `staleStackEdgesFiltered` runs **after** the executor's rebases (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:
  220-226`) and its failure arm persists recovery state through `syncFailure`. Therefore:
  a. On a fresh run and on any continuation whose remaining set contains at least one rebase row,
     `runExternalPlan` MUST NOT evaluate it as a gate. The current edge state is published as each
     row's `ancestry` fact (§4.2) — a `stale` or `divergent` edge on a row this run rebases is the
     *reason to run*, not a blocker — and `runnable` stays `true` on account of it. No blocker, no
     rank, no header suppression, no fetch suppression.
  b. On a **rows-less push-only continuation** — `RemainingRebaseEntries` yields no rebase row and
     the remaining work is the push — the executor really evaluates the gate before the push and no
     rebase of this invocation can change its answer, so the route evaluates the *current* gate,
     projects it as rank 4 `preflight-refused` with the shipped sentences verbatim, sets
     `runnable: false`, `push.executable: false` and `preflight-refused` in `push.blocked_by[]`,
     beside the **non-empty** `push.targets[]` that cell's membership rule produces (§14.1a
     rule 10d). It is still a `--continue`, so §11.2 cause 1 already suppressed the fetch; the gate
     suppresses nothing of its own.
  c. The executing route is untouched in every cell: shipped position, shipped bytes, shipped
     `syncFailure` persistence, exit `1`, marker-free, post-mutation guidance (§6.4, §13.5).
  Any earlier text projecting the completion gate as a pre-fetch gate of this route — in step 5, in
  the rows table, in §11.2 cause 2, in §17.2 or in §22.13c — is **withdrawn** (§25.24).

## 14. Push, leases and restore

### 14.1 Projected targets

`push.targets[]` rows are `{repo, context_id, repo_root, materialization, git_branch, remote, ref,
force, lease, scope}` — **ten** members, closed and field-tabulated in §4.4a — sorted
`(context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise)`, with `remote: origin`,
`ref: refs/heads/<git_branch>` and
`force: with-lease`. `context_id` is the only join key **and it is nullable**: it is `null` exactly
where the push context could not be established, the row is still emitted there (§14.1a rule 6),
and that row sorts ahead of every established id under §4.8's total order. No sentence in this
specification may call it REQUIRED, non-`null` or empty-string-valued — the earlier "`context_id` is
REQUIRED" phrasing is **withdrawn** (§25.104) — and `repo` and `repo_root` remain descriptive.

| Route | Target rule | `scope` |
|---|---|---|
| External `scope=all` and every legacy run | every materialized stack entry in stack-file order, including local-only anchors and entries this invocation does not rebase (mirrors `pushFeature` → `pushEntries`, `internal/cli/push.go:57-155`) | `stack-all` |
| External `only`/`from`, **fresh** run | selected, materialized, expected-to-rebase-and-validate entries, excluding anchors, blocked rows and already-pushed persisted rows (`pushScoped`), **in `sel.Entries` order**, which is the one supplied `TopoSort` order (§9.2a rule 2; the shipped loop is `for _, selected := range sel.Entries` at `internal/cli/push.go:83`) | `selected-rebased` |
| External `only`/`from`, **continuation** (a v2/v3 payload, both guarded handlers and the `--plan --continue` twin) | the same `pushScoped` filter over a rebased set that is **not** this invocation's work alone: `payload.Completed` ∪ `{payload.FailedBranch}` ∪ the entries this resume expects to rebase and validate, minus `payload.Pushed` — so an entry that was rebased before the interruption and never pushed **is** a target even though this invocation will not rebase it. The exact set, its order and its measured facts are §14.1a rule 10 | `selected-rebased` |
| Checkout | every `tx.Plan` entry, stage-aware (`completed` can push; `restoring` projects none) | `transaction-plan` |

`push.targets[]` is `[]` whenever `intent.push` is false, and MAY be `[]` with `intent.push: true`
when no eligible target exists. `intent.push` is **not** derived from target emptiness. Targets are
never derived from a `completed` list — a fresh plan would then hide every target.

### 14.1a The push context, the projection input, and where each fact is measured

Two things were previously left to inference and are therefore declared here: **which directory a
projected push would run in**, and **what the lease projection is allowed to read**. Both are
shipped facts, not new policy.

**The shipped context rule, in the two lines it really has.** `pushEntries`
(`internal/cli/push.go:123-150`, the context lines at `:139-141`) and `pushScoped` (`:70-118`, the
context lines at `:99-101`) both compute
`path := layout.WorktreePath(entry.Name)`, **skip** the entry when that path does not exist (the
archived/non-materialized skip), and then run the child in `repoDir := path`, overridden by
`entry.Repo` when it is non-empty. Checkout pushes through `gitPush(opts.RepoDir, pe.Branch)`
(`internal/checkout_sync.go:1224` and `:1241`, over the shipped helper at `:438-445`), i.e. the
single workspace repository root. The projection
mirrors exactly that, and nothing else:

| Mode / arm | Eligibility | `push.targets[].repo_root` | context source used (**not published** on the row; it selects the root and the id) | `materialization` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| External, `entry.Repo != ""` | the entry's **worktree path exists** (the shipped `os.Stat` skip is on the worktree, not on `Repo`) | `entry.Repo` | `entry-repo` | `materialized` |
| External, `entry.Repo == ""` | same | the materialized worktree path | `worktree` | `materialized` |
| External, worktree absent/prunable | **not a target** — the shipped loop skips it and prints `(archived, skipped)` | — | — | the row is absent; the entry's `entries[]` row still publishes `archived-metadata`/`worktree-missing`/`prunable` |
| Checkout, any `tx.Plan` row | the stage rule of §14.1 | `layout.RepoRoot` (`opts.RepoDir`) | `workspace-repo-root` | `materialized` |

```go
// internal/rebase_plan.go — package internal

// PlanPushContext is the ONE context of a projected push target: the directory
// the shipped `git push` child would really run in, plus its measured identity.
// It is produced only by ResolvePushContext.
type PlanPushContext struct {
    ContextID       *string // 64-lower-hex when the identity was established; nil ⇒ the identity
                            // was NOT established, which is published as `context_id: null` (rank
                            // 5.1, §4.2) and yields rule 5a's `expectation: unknown` lease. nil is
                            // the ONE spelling: "" is never a context id here, in
                            // PlanContextIdentities (rule 2a), in PlanPushRemoteFacts or on the
                            // emitted row, so no consumer may test `== ""` or key anything by it
    RepoRoot        string  // sanitized, display-only, never a join or sort input
    Source          string  // entry-repo | worktree | workspace-repo-root
    Materialization string  // the closed §4.2 enum, measured once per entry
}

// PlanContextIdentities is this invocation's measured context-identity table:
// canonical top level plus canonical --git-common-dir per directory, hashed into
// the context_id of §4.2. It is measured ONCE, by the probe layer, and is the
// only source of a context_id anywhere in the document — EntryContexts and
// ResolvePushContext read the same table, so a row's base context and its push
// context carry the same id whenever they are the same directory.
//
// THE MAP KEY IS EXACTLY THE 64-lower-hex context_id — never a repo root, never
// a common dir, never a display path. Every consumer therefore looks a context
// up DIRECTLY, `ids[contextID]`, in one map read and with no scan, no path
// canonicalisation and no second identity derivation; a helper that iterates the
// table looking for a matching field is a defect (§22.33h (ii-a)).
//
// A context whose identity could NOT be established has no id to key by and is
// therefore ABSENT from the table — it is never stored under the empty string,
// so two unestablished contexts can never collide into one row. Absence is the
// single, total spelling of "identity not established", and every consumer maps
// it onto its own already-declared unknown cell: `context_id: null` plus rank
// 5.1 on a published context (§4.2), an `Available: false` holder entry with Err
// set (BuildPlanHolderIndex below), and §14.4's probe-failure cell for the
// restore question. `PlanContextIdentity.ContextID` is consequently always equal
// to the key it is stored under and is never "".
//
// THE TABLE ANSWERS ONE DIRECTION ONLY: context_id → measured facts. The other
// direction — directory → context_id — is answered by the MEASUREMENT, not by
// the table: the probe layer canonicalises and hashes each distinct directory of
// the closed set the invocation will use (every row's base and execution
// context, every fetch context, every push context and, in checkout, the restore
// context) exactly once through §4.4's one generic context-identity function,
// and stamps the resulting id onto the PlanContext / PlanPushContext value for
// that directory at the same moment; where the measurement FAILED it stamps nil
// (PlanPushContext.ContextID) instead, which is the same absence the table
// records by having no row. EntryContexts and ResolvePushContext
// therefore CARRY their context's id — which is why ResolvePushContext stays
// pure, issues no Git process, canonicalises no path and hashes nothing (rule 1),
// and why rule 2's `ResolvePushContext(...).ContextID ==
// EntryContexts(...).baseCtx.ContextID` identity holds by construction rather
// than by a second derivation — and they read `ids[*ctx.ContextID]`, guarded by
// `ctx.ContextID != nil` and never by a `== ""` test, only for the
// row's measured facts (RepoRoot for display, CommonDir for the holder and lease
// joins). A nil id performs no lookup at all: there is nothing to look up, and
// the consumer takes its own declared unknown cell instead.
type PlanContextIdentities map[string]PlanContextIdentity // key: context_id

type PlanContextIdentity struct {
    ContextID string // == the map key; 64-lower-hex, never ""
    RepoRoot  string // sanitized display path
    CommonDir string // measured canonical --git-common-dir; "" when the common
                     // dir itself could not be measured, which is a MEASURED
                     // row with an unmeasured store — not an absent row
}

// PlanRefspec is one configured fetch refspec of the pushed remote, in
// configured order, decomposed once.
type PlanRefspec struct {
    Raw      string
    Negative bool   // spelled `^…`
    Forced   bool   // spelled `+…`
    Src      string // "" for a negative entry that carries only a pattern
    Dst      string // "" when the entry has no destination (negative entries)
}

// PlanPushRemoteFacts is everything §14.2 needs about ONE push context. It is
// measured in TWO declared phases (rule 7), because its halves are facts of
// different kinds: the MAPPING half — RemoteExists, FetchRefspecs, CommonDir,
// MappingReadOK — is configuration and MAY be read before the route's fetch; the
// BASELINE half — TrackingRefs, TrackingReadOK, TrackingPhase, FetchedThisRun —
// describes refs the route's own fetch may have just moved, and MUST be read (or
// re-read) AFTER that fetch and BEFORE BuildRebasePlan. ResolvePushLease is pure
// over this value and issues no Git process of its own. It has EXACTLY these ten
// fields (§22.33h (iv)).
type PlanPushRemoteFacts struct {
    ContextID      *string           // the context these facts were measured for; nil ⇒ that
                                     // context's identity was never established, which is
                                     // MappingReadOK false by construction (rule 5a). "" is never
                                     // a value here, exactly as on the emitted row (§4.4a)
    CommonDir      string            // the push context's canonical --git-common-dir, copied from
                                     // the measured PlanContextIdentity; "" when unmeasurable. It
                                     // — never ContextID — is the join key between a fetch row and
                                     // this context (rule 8): two linked worktrees of one common
                                     // dir carry two different context ids and ONE shared
                                     // remote-tracking store
    RemoteName     string            // always "origin": the shipped argv names it literally,
                                     // and the §11.4 remote-resolution ladder is a FETCH fact
                                     // that MUST NOT be substituted here
    MappingReadOK  bool              // the MAPPING half was really established: the context's
                                     // identity read and its ordered config inventory both
                                     // succeeded, so RemoteExists and FetchRefspecs describe the
                                     // configuration rather than the absence of a read. FALSE is
                                     // the probe-failure cell of rule 5a — never an "origin is not
                                     // configured" claim — and it is the ONLY source of
                                     // `expectation: unknown` (§14.2, §4.4a)
    RemoteExists   bool              // a remote literally named origin is configured. Meaningful
                                     // ONLY when MappingReadOK; false with MappingReadOK false is
                                     // "not established", not "absent"
    FetchRefspecs  []PlanRefspec     // remote.origin.fetch in configured order; never nil, and
                                     // empty-with-MappingReadOK-false is likewise "not
                                     // established"
    TrackingRefs   map[string]string // fully-qualified remote-tracking ref → current 40/64-hex
                                     // value, read in the phase TrackingPhase names; a MISSING
                                     // KEY means the ref does not exist
    TrackingReadOK bool              // false when the ref inventory itself could not be read
    TrackingPhase  string            // post-fetch | plan-point | unread — the provenance of the
                                     // three members above, and the first conjunct of a `fresh`
                                     // lease (rule 7, §14.2 step 3)
    FetchedThisRun bool              // THIS invocation's own fetch really refreshed THIS context's
                                     // `origin` remote-tracking refs, per the closed predicate of
                                     // rule 8 — which additionally requires TrackingPhase
                                     // `post-fetch`, MappingReadOK and TrackingReadOK. It is NEVER
                                     // "the fetch outcome carried a row whose context_id equals
                                     // this one"
}

// PlanPushFacts is the ONE push-fact carrier of an invocation, and the single
// member RebasePlanRequest and both inspection structs carry (§9.1a, §13.7,
// §13.7a). It travels from the inspection that measured its mapping half,
// through the post-fetch refresh that measures its baseline half, into
// BuildRebasePlan, which hands it to PushTargets UNCHANGED. There is exactly one
// producer per half and no second carrier anywhere: a route that rebuilt a
// map[string]PlanPushRemoteFacts of its own beside this value is a specification
// violation (rule 9).
type PlanPushFacts struct {
    Applies         bool                           // intent.push AND a subject to project targets
                                                   // from (rule 7). false ⇒ every member below is
                                                   // the zero value, Phase is `not-applicable`,
                                                   // NEITHER half is measured, RefreshPushTrackingRefs
                                                   // is never called, and PushTargets emits []
    Phase           string                         // not-applicable | pre-fetch | post-fetch |
                                                   // plan-point — the phase of the whole value.
                                                   // `not-applicable` iff !Applies; on an
                                                   // applicable value the inspection stamps
                                                   // `pre-fetch` and the one refresh replaces it
                                                   // with `post-fetch` or `plan-point`. Publishing
                                                   // a lease from a `pre-fetch` value is a defect
                                                   // (rule 7)
    Identities      PlanContextIdentities          // the ONE measured identity table (§4.2);
                                                   // keyed by context_id, the sole source of every
                                                   // context_id, read only as the direct ids[id]
    Contexts        []PlanPushContext              // the DISTINCT push contexts this invocation
                                                   // measured facts for, sorted by ContextID with
                                                   // nil first — the same total order the emitted
                                                   // rows take (§4.8) —
                                                   // never nil; enumerated through the same sole
                                                   // producer ResolvePushContext (rule 7). External
                                                   // enumerates one per eligible entry and
                                                   // de-duplicates by ContextID, treating every nil
                                                   // id as its OWN distinct context (two
                                                   // unestablished contexts never collapse into
                                                   // one); checkout has
                                                   // exactly one row and needs no entry at all —
                                                   // the context is layout.RepoRoot by the table
                                                   // above, so the call passes the zero StackEntry
                                                   // and the `transaction-plan` arm reuses that
                                                   // single row for every tx.Plan branch
    Materialization map[string]string              // per logical name, the closed §4.2 enum,
                                                   // measured once
    Remotes         map[string]PlanPushRemoteFacts // keyed by context_id; one entry per Contexts
                                                   // row WHOSE ID WAS ESTABLISHED and no other. A
                                                   // nil-id context has no key and therefore NO
                                                   // entry — "" is never a key (rule 2a) — and its
                                                   // facts are rule 5a's not-established value by
                                                   // construction, so a missing entry is read as
                                                   // MappingReadOK false and never as "origin is
                                                   // absent"
}

// PlanPushRequest is the COMPLETE input of PushTargets. Every member is measured
// or decided above it; the function derives, it never probes.
type PlanPushRequest struct {
    Mode        WorkspaceMode
    Route       string                // RouteLegacy | RouteNewMode
    Layout      RebasePlanLayout      // §9.0
    Intent      bool                  // intent.push
    Scope       string                // stack-all | selected-rebased | transaction-plan | none
    Stack       *Stack                // nil ⇒ no targets
    Order       []StackEntry          // the ONE sort's order (§9.1a rule 3); never re-sorted
    Selection   SyncSelection         // sel.Entries order IS the traversal order of the scoped arm
    Remaining   []string              // the continuation's rows (§13.3)
    Transaction *CheckoutTransaction  // the checkout arm's tx.Plan and Stage
    Expected    map[string]bool       // per logical name: this run expects to rebase AND validate
                                      // it — plus, on a continuation, the entries an EARLIER
                                      // invocation of the same run already rebased. Derived per
                                      // arm by rule 10 and by nothing else
    AlreadyPushed map[string]bool     // the payload's Pushed set (the shipped pushScoped skip)
    Facts       PlanPushFacts         // req.PushFacts, verbatim: identities, materialization,
                                      // contexts and per-context remote facts in ONE member.
                                      // The former loose Materialization/Identities/Facts trio is
                                      // withdrawn — three carriers of one measurement could
                                      // disagree, and only one of them was ever produced above
                                      // the fetch (rule 9)
}

// PlanPushTarget is the row. Its members are the TEN §4.4a keys, in that order.
type PlanPushTarget struct {
    Repo            string    `json:"repo"`
    ContextID       *string   `json:"context_id"`
    RepoRoot        *string   `json:"repo_root"`
    Materialization string    `json:"materialization"`
    GitBranch       string    `json:"git_branch"`
    Remote          string    `json:"remote"`
    Ref             string    `json:"ref"`
    Force           string    `json:"force"`
    Lease           PlanLease `json:"lease"`
    Scope           string    `json:"scope"`
}
```

**The six producers below live in `internal/rebase_planner.go`, and in no other file.**
`internal/rebase_plan.go` declares the *types and constants* above — the values these functions
take and return — and declares **no function of this subsection**; it is the document-model file,
exactly as §19.1 states for `SelectPrimaryRefusal`, which is likewise declared in
`internal/rebase_planner.go` and never beside its `RefusalKind` type. The probe-layer helpers that
`MeasurePushRemoteFacts` and `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` call to read configuration and refs live in
`internal/rebase_plan_probe.go` (§19.1), which declares **none** of the six names below: one owner
per symbol, and the owner is named here and in §19.1 identically.

```go
// internal/rebase_planner.go — package internal
//
// The SIX push producers of §14.1a, declared here and nowhere else. None of them
// is declared in internal/rebase_plan.go, which holds their parameter and result
// types only, and none is re-declared in internal/rebase_plan_probe.go, which
// holds the read helpers the two measuring producers call.

// ResolvePushContext is the sole producer of a push context (§9.1). It is called
// twice per invocation and never by a third site: once by the inspection, to
// enumerate the DISTINCT contexts it must measure facts for, and once per
// emitted row by PushTargets. Both calls are pure and equal by construction.
func ResolvePushContext(mode WorkspaceMode, layout RebasePlanLayout, entry StackEntry,
    materialization string, ids PlanContextIdentities) PlanPushContext

// MeasurePushRemoteFacts is the sole producer of the MAPPING half of one push
// context: its canonical common dir (from the measured identity table), whether
// a remote literally named origin exists, and remote.origin.fetch decomposed
// into []PlanRefspec in configured order. It sets MappingReadOK true only where
// the identity read AND the ordered config inventory both succeeded; where
// either failed it returns MappingReadOK false with RemoteExists false and an
// EMPTY (never nil) FetchRefspecs, which the caller MUST read as "not
// established" rather than "no origin" (rule 5a). A ctx.ContextID of nil IS the
// failed-identity cell: it performs ZERO reads — no identity lookup, no config
// inventory, no process — and returns that same not-established value with
// ContextID nil, so an unresolvable context costs nothing and still lands in
// rule 5a. It reads NO remote-tracking
// ref, makes no network call and pushes nothing; the value it returns carries
// TrackingPhase "" and no TrackingRefs, and is never publishable on its own. It
// is called only for the contexts of an APPLICABLE PlanPushFacts (rule 7).
func MeasurePushRemoteFacts(ctx PlanPushContext, ids PlanContextIdentities) PlanPushRemoteFacts

// RefreshPushTrackingRefs is the sole producer of the BASELINE half, and the
// ONLY site in the tree that reads a remote-tracking ref inventory for a lease.
// It is called EXACTLY ONCE per controlled invocation whose PlanPushFacts is
// APPLICABLE, and NOT AT ALL otherwise: a value with Applies false is neither
// measured nor refreshed, keeps Phase `not-applicable`, and reaches the builder
// as it left the inspection (rule 7). On an applicable value the call is placed
// immediately after that route's fetch decision has been carried out — after the
// fetch child on a fetching arm, and at the plan point on a no-fetch,
// suppressed, refusing or continuation arm — and always BEFORE BuildRebasePlan,
// because the lease's expectation/ref/SHA are approval-tuple members (§8.3) and
// a pre-fetch baseline would bind a token to refs the same invocation then
// moved. For every context of that applicable value — exactly one baseline read
// each, and zero for a context of a non-applicable value — it re-reads
// TrackingRefs/TrackingReadOK and stamps TrackingPhase from a three-value
// ladder, first match wins: `unread` when TrackingReadOK is false, else
// `post-fetch` when `fetched` really attempted a child in this invocation, else
// `plan-point`. It then sets FetchedThisRun from PushContextRefreshed conjoined
// with MappingReadOK && TrackingReadOK && TrackingPhase == post-fetch — so it is
// false whenever either half was unread — and stamps PlanPushFacts.Phase with
// the same value the contexts agree on (`post-fetch` when the route fetched,
// `plan-point` otherwise). A context whose ContextID is nil has no mapping and
// therefore no destination to baseline: it is visited like any other, reads
// NOTHING (zero ref reads), and keeps TrackingReadOK false with TrackingPhase
// `unread`, which is exactly rule 5a's already-declared unknown cell rather than
// a second one. It never re-reads the mapping half, never issues a
// network call and never pushes.
func RefreshPushTrackingRefs(facts PlanPushFacts, fetched PlanFetchOutcome) PlanPushFacts

// PushContextRefreshed is the closed predicate behind FetchedThisRun (rule 8).
// It joins on the canonical common dir, not on context_id.
func PushContextRefreshed(fetched PlanFetchOutcome, commonDir string) bool

// ResolvePushLease is the sole producer of a lease (§14.2).
func ResolvePushLease(gitBranch string, facts PlanPushRemoteFacts) PlanLease

// PushTargets is pure over the request: no Git process, no filesystem probe, no
// context resolution of its own beyond ResolvePushContext, no sort beyond the
// final (context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise) ordering of the emitted
// rows — the ONE total order of §4.8, which a nil id takes part in rather than
// being dropped from.
func PushTargets(req PlanPushRequest) []PlanPushTarget
```

Binding rules:

1. **One producer per fact, the producer is named, and so is the file it lives in.**
   `ResolvePushContext` produces every
   `context_id`/`repo_root`/`materialization` a target carries; `MeasurePushRemoteFacts` produces
   every mapping fact and `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` every baseline fact; `ResolvePushLease`
   produces every `lease` object; `PushTargets` decides membership, `scope` and order. All six —
   those five plus `PushContextRefreshed` — are declared in **`internal/rebase_planner.go`**, one
   declaration each; `internal/rebase_plan.go` declares their types and constants and **no**
   function of this subsection; `internal/rebase_plan_probe.go` declares the config/ref read
   helpers the two measuring producers call and **none** of the six names (§19.1). No other
   function may compute any of them, and neither `PushTargets`, `ResolvePushContext` nor
   `ResolvePushLease` may issue a Git process — the argv sidecar asserts **zero** child processes
   across a direct call of all three with a pre-built request.
2. **The push context is the base context wherever they are the same directory.** On external
   pass 1 `EntryContexts` resolves the base context as `entry.Repo` else the worktree (§9.1) — the
   identical ladder — and on checkout both are `layout.RepoRoot`. A test asserts
   `ResolvePushContext(...).ContextID == EntryContexts(...).baseCtx.ContextID` for every
   materialized row in both modes — **pointer-insensitively, over the pointed-to values, with
   `nil == nil` an admitted match** — so `push.targets[].context_id` really joins to
   `entries[].base_context.context_id` (§4.2's join-key rule), including in the cell where both are
   `null` because one directory failed one identity measurement. External **pass 2** is not a push
   context: the push loop has no pass-2 arm.
2a. **`PlanContextIdentities` is keyed by `context_id`, and every read of it is a direct map
   index.** The table's key is exactly the 64-lower-hex `context_id` — never a repo root, never a
   common dir, never a display path — so `ResolvePushContext`, `MeasurePushRemoteFacts`,
   `EntryContexts`, `BuildPlanHolderIndex` and the §10.3 JIT seam all read it as `ids[id]`, in one
   map read, with no scan and no re-derivation. The `directory → context_id` direction is owned by
   the **measurement** (§4.4's one generic context-identity function), which runs once per distinct
   directory of the closed set the invocation will use and stamps the id onto the context value it
   produced; that is what keeps `ResolvePushContext` pure under rule 1. A context whose identity was
   never established is **absent** from the table rather than stored under `""`, so unestablished
   contexts never collide, and each consumer takes its own declared unknown cell instead
   (§4.2's `context_id: null` + rank 5.1, `Available: false` in the holder index, §14.4's
   probe-failure cell). The carriers agree with the table on that spelling: a nil
   `PlanPushContext.ContextID`/`PlanPushRemoteFacts.ContextID` and a missing `PlanPushFacts.Remotes`
   entry are the same absence, `""` is a value of none of them, and no consumer may test `== ""`,
   key by `""` or synthesize a placeholder id. Asserted by §22.33h (ii-a), declared in §25.91 and
   §25.104.
3. **The lease facts are measured for the push context, not for the fetch context.** The two
   coincide on the ordinary stack, but a plan MUST NOT assume it: `PlanPushRemoteFacts` is keyed by
   `context_id`, the probe layer measures one entry per **distinct push context** (§11.7's ordered
   inventory for that root, `remote.origin.fetch` in configured order, and — in the baseline phase
   of rule 7 — the remote-tracking ref inventory for the destinations those refspecs produce), and
   `FetchedThisRun` is decided by rule 8's predicate, never by "this invocation fetched something".
4. **`RemoteName` is the literal `origin`.** The shipped push argv is
   `git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>`; the §11.4 fetch-side remote ladder
   (`branch.<name>.remote` → sole remote → `origin`) belongs to the *fetch* effect and MUST NOT be
   substituted here. A context whose mapping was **read** and carries no configured `origin`
   publishes `RemoteExists: false`, which yields the unmapped cell of §14.2 (`expectation: absent`,
   `expected_ref: null`). A context whose mapping could not be read publishes neither — it is
   rule 5a's cell.
5. **An unreadable tracking inventory is `absent`, never a guess.** `TrackingReadOK: false` —
   published as `TrackingPhase: unread` — yields the
   §14.2 "mapping exists but the mapped ref is absent or unreadable" cell — `expectation: absent`
   with `expected_ref` naming the mapped ref, and `expected_sha_freshness: possibly-stale`, because
   nothing was read — and never a SHA.
   It adds no blocker of its own: the mapping is known, the lease is disclosure, and a
   compare-and-swap that Git will evaluate itself is not a replay-critical probe.
5a. **An unreadable MAPPING is a probe failure, not a lease.** The two halves fail differently and
   MUST NOT be collapsed. Where `MappingReadOK` is false — the identity read or the ordered config
   inventory of §11.7 failed for that push context — nothing about the destination was
   established, so the row publishes the third cell of §14.2:
   `{expectation: unknown, expected_ref: null, expected_sha: null,
   expected_sha_freshness: possibly-stale}`, and the document additionally carries **one**
   rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker per affected context — document-level with `entry: null`,
   de-duplicated and ordered by `context_id`, its sanitized `detail` naming the context id and the
   verbatim probe error (§6.4, §18.5). It is a hard, non-waivable blocker (§7.1), so it forces
   `runnable: false`, contributes `probe-failed` to `push.blocked_by[]` through the §14.3
   control-flow projection, and refuses the guarded twin. Two spellings are **forbidden** and no
   text may restore either: publishing `expectation: absent` from an unread mapping — which would
   claim Git will send a null-OID check nobody established — and publishing
   `expected_sha_freshness: fresh` on any row of an unread mapping or an unread inventory.
   The target row itself is still emitted (rule 6): the blast radius is what the operator asked to
   see.
   **The unestablished-identity cell is inside this rule, not beside it, and its ordering is
   total.** A push context whose identity was never established (`ContextID` nil, rule 2a) has
   `MappingReadOK: false` by construction, so it takes exactly this cell — `expectation: unknown`
   plus the rank 5.9 row — with **no** second vocabulary and no new kind. Because it has no id to
   name or to order by, its blocker `detail` says so in place of the id (the sanitized context root
   plus the verbatim identity-probe error), and the row is ordered and de-duplicated as `blockers[]`
   already orders every document-level row: exact-tuple, `entry: null` first, sanitized `detail`
   bytewise (§4.8). Several unestablished contexts therefore collapse to one row only where their
   sanitized details are byte-identical, never because their ids compared equal — they have none.
6. **Emptiness is decided by the rules above, never by a probe failure.** `intent.push: true` with
   an unresolvable context still emits the row with `context_id: null` and the rank 5.1
   `repo-unavailable` blocker on the corresponding `entries[]` row; it does not drop the target,
   because the blast radius is what the operator asked to see (§14.3). That emitted row is total in
   every other member: `repo`, `materialization`, `git_branch`, `remote`, `ref`, `force` and `scope`
   are published as usual, `repo_root` is `null` exactly with the id (§4.4a), the `lease` object is
   present and carries rule 5a's `expectation: unknown` cell, and the row takes its place in the
   `(context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise)` order rather than being appended, sorted last or
   emitted out of band. **Two blockers legitimately co-occur** and neither is a duplicate of the
   other: rank 5.1 `repo-unavailable` is the *entry row's* context fact, and rank 5.9 `probe-failed`
   is the *push destination's* fact; §7.2's collapse selects `repo-unavailable` as `refusal.kind`
   because it outranks, and both rows stay in `blockers[]`.
7. **The measurement has two phases, it happens only where it applies, and the phase is published
   as provenance.** Applicability is decided first, once, by the inspection: `PlanPushFacts.Applies`
   is true **iff** `intent.push` is true **and** the invocation established a subject to project
   targets from — `RowsAvailable` on a fresh arm, a decoded transaction/payload on a continuation.
   The two phases and their quantifiers are total over that decision:

   | Cell | Mapping half | Baseline half (`RefreshPushTrackingRefs`) | `Phase` |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `intent.push` false, **or** a rows-less document (`summary.plannability: unavailable`), **or** any arm with no push-target subject | **not measured** — zero identity reads, zero config reads | **not called** — zero calls, zero ref reads | `not-applicable`, with `push.targets: []` |
   | applicable, target contexts enumerated, before the route's fetch decision | measured **once per distinct push context**, through `MeasurePushRemoteFacts` — a context whose identity was never established (`ContextID` nil) is visited once and records **zero** reads, taking rule 5a's cell | not yet called | `pre-fetch` — an inspection result is always `pre-fetch` on an applicable value, and never publishable |
   | applicable, the route really attempted its fetch child | already measured | called **exactly once**, after that child; **one** baseline read per applicable context, and **zero** for a nil-id context, which has no mapping to baseline | `post-fetch`, `TrackingPhase: post-fetch`, `TrackingReadOK` set per context |
   | applicable, no child ran — `--no-fetch`, any `--continue`, a §11.2 suppression, or a refusing-but-rows-available gate (a live lock, a cell refusal, I14) | already measured | called **exactly once**, at the plan point; **one** baseline read per applicable context, and **zero** for a nil-id context | `plan-point`, `TrackingPhase: plan-point`, `FetchedThisRun` false everywhere |

   The **mapping** half (`CommonDir`, `MappingReadOK`, `RemoteExists`, `FetchRefspecs`, and the
   `Contexts`/`Identities`/`Materialization` members of `PlanPushFacts`) is configuration and is
   measured by the invocation's inspection — `InspectCheckoutPlan` step 1.5a/2.6,
   `InspectExternalPlan` step 4.7 — which runs **above** the route's fetch and stamps
   `Phase: pre-fetch`. The **baseline** half (`TrackingRefs`, `TrackingReadOK`, `TrackingPhase`,
   `FetchedThisRun`) is measured by exactly one `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` call, placed immediately
   after the route's fetch decision has been carried out and before `BuildRebasePlan`:

   | Arm | Where the refresh runs | Resulting `Phase` / `TrackingPhase` |
   |---|---|---|
   | checkout fresh, fetch performed (child ran, ok **or** failed) | `PlanCheckoutRebase` step 4a; guarded twin §12.2d step 5b | `post-fetch` |
   | checkout fresh, no fetch (policy `no-fetch`, a §11.2 suppression, or a refusing gate) | the same step, with the outcome it was handed | `plan-point` |
   | checkout `--continue` | `PlanCheckoutRebase` step 3a; guarded twin §12.2d continuation row 5b | `plan-point` |
   | external fresh (legacy or new-mode), fetch performed | §13.7a step 7a; guarded twins §12.2b/§12.3 | `post-fetch` |
   | external fresh, `--no-fetch`/suppressed/refusing | §13.7a step 7a | `plan-point` |
   | external `--continue` (v2/v3 scoped, legacy envelope, `.sync-state.yaml`) | the same step of its route (§12.3, §13.7a) | `plan-point` |

   **When the halves are measured at all.** Both halves are measured **iff** `PlanPushFacts.Applies`
   is true, per the totality table above. A rows-less document
   (`summary.plannability: unavailable`) measures neither half, publishes `push.targets: []` and
   carries `PlanPushFacts{Applies: false, Phase: "not-applicable"}`; so does any document whose
   `intent.push` is false. In those cells `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` is **not called at all** — the
   call count is **zero**, and so is the ref-read count (§22.33h (vii)). Any earlier statement that
   it is "still called, unconditionally, once per controlled invocation" is **withdrawn**: a
   no-op call was assertable only by counting a call that does nothing, while what the document
   actually promises is that no unapplicable invocation reads a ref. A
   refusing-but-rows-available document (a live lock, a cell refusal, I14) **is** applicable and
   does measure both halves: its targets are the blast radius the operator asked to see (§14.3).

   A value whose `Phase` is `pre-fetch` MUST NOT reach a published document: `BuildRebasePlan`
   asserts `req.PushFacts.Phase != "pre-fetch"` whenever `req.PushFacts.Applies` is true, and a
   route that skipped the refresh fails that assertion rather than publishing a baseline measured
   before its own fetch. On a non-applicable value the same assertion is vacuous, because `Phase`
   is `not-applicable` and no lease is published. A `plan-point` read is a real read of the current
   refs — it is simply not a *refreshed* one, which is what §14.2 step 3 turns into
   `possibly-stale`.
8. **`FetchedThisRun` requires a read of both halves, and joins on the canonical common dir and on
   the remote named `origin`.** It is `true` **iff** all three of `TrackingPhase == "post-fetch"`,
   `MappingReadOK` and `TrackingReadOK` hold **and** `PushContextRefreshed(fetched, commonDir)` is
   `true`; the first three conjuncts are what stop a fetch from labelling an unread mapping or an
   unread inventory `fresh`. `PushContextRefreshed(fetched, commonDir)` is itself `true` **iff**
   `commonDir != ""` and **some** row `r` of `fetched.Repos` satisfies **all four** conjuncts:

   | # | Conjunct | Why it is required |
   |---:|---|---|
   | i | `r.Attempted && r.OK` | a `git fetch` child really ran in that context and exited `0`; a suppressed, un-attempted or failed row refreshed nothing |
   | ii | `r.Effect != nil && r.Effect.Contacted` | the fetch resolved a remote and contacted it; an unresolved-remote fetch writes no remote-tracking ref (§11.3) |
   | iii | some member of `r.Effect.Remotes` is named **`origin`** | the lease baseline is `origin`'s tracking ref (rule 4). A context whose `branch.<name>.remote` is `upstream` fetches `upstream`, refreshes `refs/remotes/upstream/**` and leaves the `origin` baseline exactly as stale as it was — so that row's lease stays `possibly-stale` even though this invocation fetched, successfully, in that very directory |
   | iv | `canonical(r.ContextCommonDir) == canonical(commonDir)`, both non-empty | remote-tracking refs live in the **common dir** (§11.4), so the fetch and the push context share a baseline exactly when they share that directory |

   Conjunct iv is why the join is **not** `r.ContextID == facts.ContextID`: a `context_id` hashes
   the canonical top level **and** the canonical common dir (§4.2), so two linked worktrees of one
   repository carry two different ids and one shared remote-tracking store. A fetch performed in
   worktree A therefore makes worktree B's lease `fresh` — the ordinary multi-worktree stack, where
   §11.4's collapse rule already means one fetch serves every sibling — while an
   equal-`context_id` test would have marked every sibling `possibly-stale` and an
   equal-`context_root` test would have done the same. Where `commonDir` is `""` the predicate is
   `false`: an unmeasurable common dir cannot be shown to be the fetched one.
9. **One carrier, one owner, no duplicate producer.** `PlanPushFacts` is the only push-fact
   value in the tree. It is produced by the invocation's inspection, refreshed once by
   `RefreshPushTrackingRefs`, carried as `RebasePlanRequest.PushFacts`, and handed to
   `PushTargets` as `PlanPushRequest.Facts` **verbatim** by `BuildRebasePlan` — which adds the
   run-shape members (`Mode`, `Route`, `Layout`, `Intent`, `Scope`, `Stack`, `Order`, `Selection`,
   `Remaining`, `Transaction`, `Expected`, `AlreadyPushed`) and nothing else. The builder MUST NOT
   measure, re-key, filter or reconstruct any member of it, and no route may build a second
   `map[string]PlanPushRemoteFacts`, a second identity table or a second materialization map beside
   it. A source assertion shows exactly one construction site per producer and exactly one
   `PushTargets` call in the tree (§22.33h).
10. **`Expected` and `AlreadyPushed` are declared per arm, and the continuation arm's rebased set
   is not this invocation's work alone.** The two membership members of `PlanPushRequest` are what
   turn the §14.1 route rule into a set, and the scoped continuation is the arm where the naive
   reading ("the entries this run rebases") is wrong: the shipped `pushScoped` is handed
   `result.Completed`, which `syncWithStackScoped` seeds from the resume's `done` map
   (`completed := completedNames(alreadyDone)`, `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:78-81`) before it
   appends anything of its own. A projection that omitted the already-completed entries would
   publish an empty `push.targets[]` for the exact cell the operator resumes for — a push retry.
   Per arm, therefore, with no other source:

   | Arm | `req.Expected` (per logical name) | `req.AlreadyPushed` |
   |---|---|---|
   | external `scope=all`, every legacy run | **not consulted** — the `stack-all` rule admits every materialized stack entry, mirroring `pushEntries`, which has neither a rebased set nor a payload skip | empty; `pushEntries` skips nothing persisted |
   | external `only`/`from`, **fresh** | `E_run` = the selected entries this run expects to **rebase and validate**: selected by `sel.Names`, materialized, **not** an anchor the run skips (`skipsAnchor` — a skipped anchor is marked done but never appended to `completed`, `sync_helpers.go:99-104`), and carrying no hard unwaived blocker that stops the row | `set(payload.Pushed)`, which is empty at birth |
   | external `only`/`from`, **continuation** (v2/v3 payload; both guarded handlers and the `--plan --continue` twin) | `set(payload.Completed)` ∪ `{payload.FailedBranch}` (when non-empty) ∪ `E_resume`, where `E_resume` is `E_run` computed over `insp.Remaining` (§13.3) — the rows this resume expects to rebase and validate | `set(payload.Pushed)` |
   | checkout | the `transaction-plan` stage rule of §14.1 over `tx.Plan`; `Expected` carries the entries that stage table admits | the transaction's recorded pushed entries where the stage records them, else empty |

   Binding consequences, all of them shipped facts:

   a. **The emitted membership is exactly `(Expected \ AlreadyPushed)`, filtered as `pushScoped`
      filters.** `PushTargets` walks `req.Selection.Entries` in order and emits a row **iff**
      `Expected[name] && !AlreadyPushed[name]`, the name still resolves in the stack
      (`internal.GetBranch(...).Name != ""`, the shipped `internal/cli/push.go:87-90` skip) and its
      worktree is materialized (the shipped `os.Stat` skip, `:91-97`). Those are the shipped
      `rebased` and `alreadyPushed` maps of `:74-84` under their declared names, so the
      projection's membership test is the shipped skip statement for statement. Writing the
      subtraction into `Expected` instead — publishing
      `Expected = (Completed ∪ {FailedBranch} ∪ E_resume) \ Pushed` with an empty `AlreadyPushed`
      — yields the identical set and is the same rule stated in one member instead of two; what is
      **not** permitted is applying it twice, or letting the two members disagree.
   b. **`{payload.FailedBranch}` is admitted on the bare non-empty condition**, exactly as the
      shipped `done` map admits it (`internal/cli/sync.go:399-407`), with **no** `payloadCompleted`
      conjunct: on a rebase-failure resume the entry was resolved by the operator and is pushable,
      and on a push-failure resume it is already in `payload.Completed`, so the union is
      idempotent. The `payloadCompleted` conjunct of §13.5/§13.7a step 5 governs gates e2/e3 and
      the `[~] resolved` line, and it governs nothing here.
   c. **Order is the selection's, never the completed list's.** The traversal is `sel.Entries` —
      on a continuation, the persisted-`Selected` filtering of `scopedSelectionFromPayloadOrder`
      applied over the invocation's one `TopoSort` order (§9.2a rules 2 and 6) — and the emitted
      rows are then sorted canonically by `(context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise)` (§4.8).
      `payload.Completed`
      and `result.Completed` are **sets**: the shipped `completedNames` iterates a map, so their
      order is unspecified between processes and MUST NOT reach any published order or any
      traversal (§4.8's map-order rule).
   d. **A rows-less push-only continuation therefore publishes a non-empty `push.targets[]`.**
      Where `RemainingRebaseEntries` yields no rebase row, `E_resume` is empty but
      `set(payload.Completed) ∪ {payload.FailedBranch}` is not, so `(Expected \ AlreadyPushed)` is
      non-empty exactly when entries were rebased and never pushed — which is the whole content of
      that cell (§13.3, §13.5, §13.7a rule 15b). `summary.plannability` is `empty` there, **not**
