## 22. Acceptance criteria

Each criterion is independently verifiable. Commands are runnable from the repository root.

**Frozen path**

1. `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestSyncNoFlag_' -count=1` passes with **zero** changes under
   `internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag/`; `git status --porcelain internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag`
   is empty; `find internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag -type f | wc -l` still reports `126`.
2. A no-flag `tws sync <f>` in both modes issues exactly the shipped Git argv sequence, in the
   shipped order, with the shipped process count — asserted through the argv sidecar with no
   `--version`, no `config --list`, and no `rev-list` added.

**CLI contract**

3. `tws sync <f> --json` exits `1` with `--json requires --plan` and emits no JSON. It is asserted
    as a **§3.6 row 4 early control error** — decided at §3.3 step 3, before subject resolution,
    with no fetch, no probe and no document — and explicitly **not** as a plan-only route that
    failed to publish one; the test asserts zero `git` processes for the invocation.
4. Each of `--plan`, `--max-replay-per-entry 1`, `--max-replay-total 1`,
   `--approve-plan <64-hex>` combined with `--abort` exits `1` with its §3.4 sentence and writes no
   state.
5. `tws sync <f> --max-replay-per-entry -1` and `--max-replay-total -1` exit `1` before any probe.
6. `tws sync <f> --approve-plan <64-hex>` without `--continue` and without a limit exits `1` with
   `--approve-plan requires --max-replay-per-entry or --max-replay-total`, **with and without
   `--plan`**, before any subject resolution, probe or state read; adding either limit makes both
   forms legal.
7. `tws sync <f> --approve-plan deadbeef` exits `1` with the 64-hex message; a value with
   surrounding whitespace and a valid digest is accepted.
8. `--plan` alone does not set new mode: the emitted document has `route: legacy` and
   `route_triggers: []`, and no v2 state file is created.
8a. `tws sync --help` prints the §3.1a `Long` verbatim and the five flag help strings of §3.1
    verbatim; the captured help snapshot contains no unqualified "without mutating anything"
    claim, and states all six disclosures of §3.1 rule 4 — the non-mutation scope, the external
    fetch default beside checkout's `--fetch`-only fetch, the per-invocation limit scope, the
    distinct `--plan --no-fetch` route, the guarded `state_version 3` recovery state that older
    releases refuse to resume, and the `plan-guard:` refusal line with its `state-preserved:`
    distinction. The snapshot is asserted through production `Execute()`, and no pre-existing
    golden or snapshot is modified by this criterion.
8b. **`route_triggers[]` is bytewise sorted, and one rule decides it (§4.1, §4.8).** Because I1–I3
    refuse the three contradictory pairs, at most **three** trigger flags can be supplied, so the
    maximal cells are triples. A `--plan --json` run supplying
    `--no-fetch --local-only --from <name>` publishes `route_triggers` exactly
    `["from", "local-only", "no-fetch"]` — asserted **element by element**, not as a set — which is
    the exact **reverse** of those flags' `syncTriggerFlags` slice order
    (`no-fetch, local-only, from`), so an
    implementation that publishes the shipped source order fails this criterion. Four companion
    cells complete it: `--fetch --full --only <name>` publishes `["fetch", "full", "only"]`; the
    mixed triple `--fetch --local-only --from <name>` publishes
    `["fetch", "from", "local-only"]` against a slice order of `fetch, local-only, from`; a two-flag
    run (`--no-fetch --from <name>`) publishes `["from", "no-fetch"]`
    — reversed relative to the slice — and a legacy run publishes `[]`; and two documents that differ
    **only** in the order a shell supplied the flags publish byte-identical arrays. A sixth cell
    asserts the array is a fingerprint **non-member**: the triple document's
    `approval.fingerprint` is asserted equal to the digest computed over a pre-image in which the
    array is spelled in the other order (through the §23.1 fingerprint debug accessor), proving the
    ordering rule is a schema contract and cannot be enforced by the digest. A seventh asserts the
    **shipped** I8 sentence is untouched: `--abort --no-fetch --from <name>` still prints
    `syncChangedTriggerList`'s own `--`-prefixed, sorted list byte-for-byte, because this criterion
    governs the JSON array and not that sentence (§8.3, §25.94).

**Plan surface**

9. `tws sync <f> --plan --json | jq -e '.schema_version == 1'` succeeds, and **stdout is exactly
   one JSON value followed by exactly one `\n`, and no other byte** — `len(stdout) ==
   len(document) + 1`, the last byte is `0x0A`, and there is no second newline, no leading byte, no
   trailing whitespace and no second value. This is the `encoding/json` convention the renderer
   already follows (§3.6 rules 1–2: `MarshalRebasePlan` returns a complete buffer whose last byte
   is the newline `json.Encoder.Encode` appends, and `renderPlanDocumentTo` writes that buffer in
   exactly one `Write`), so "one JSON object and no other
   byte" — which would forbid that newline — is **withdrawn** wherever it appears. Every other
   statement of this contract in the specification, the tests and the skills reads the same way.
10. On the §6.4 reparent topology, `tws sync <f> --plan` prints — on the **default** rendering —
    a row whose destination is `D`, whose cutoff and upstream are `B`, and whose first candidate is
    `C`, in the exact two-line eleven-field grammar, in both modes, with the external
    `origin/master` rewrite.
10a. On the same topology the human row's `range` field is `<12-char B>..feat/pr2` while the
    `--json` twin publishes `replay.range == "<full B>..feat/pr2"` and
    `replay.upstream_sha == "<full B>"`; a renderer that copies `replay.range` fails this
    criterion.
10b. A human `--plan` prints `Policy: fetch=… propagation=… scope=all` for a bare run,
    `scope=only:<name>` under `--only <name>` and `scope=subtree:<name>` under `--from <name>`,
    byte-equal to `SyncRunPolicy.ScopeLabel()`; the `--json` twin of the `--from` run publishes
    `policy.scope_kind == "subtree"` with `policy.selector == "<name>"`; the token `from` appears
    nowhere in either document except inside `route_triggers`.
10c. A human `--plan` always prints both `Plan blockers:` and `Plan warnings:` — the `none` forms on
    a clean plan — and on a document carrying three blockers of different ranks and two warnings it
    prints **every** one of the five rows, in the canonical order of §4.8, above the four-part tail,
    with `<document>` rendered for `entry: null`; the tail's `Refusal kind:` still names only the
    top-ranked kind.
10d. **The `Guarded execution blockers:` block is token-only (§6.3 part 3).** On a document whose
    `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` carries two members, the human tail prints the header followed by
    exactly `  - <token>` per member, in canonical order — no colon, no detail, no count, no "and N
    more" — and each rendered line is asserted byte-equal to `"  - " + token`. The corresponding
    detail is asserted to be reachable from the same document through `blockers[]` (rendered in
    full by the `Plan blockers:` block), `state` and `fetch`, and the `--json` twin's
    `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` is asserted to be an array of bare tokens with no object member.
    A renderer that appends a detail fails this criterion.
11. `tws sync <f> --plan` and `tws sync <f> --plan --json` publish the **same**
    `Approval fingerprint:` / `approval.fingerprint` value for the same facts, across repeated
    processes.
12. A document with `runnable: false`, one with `guard.would_refuse: true`, and one with
    `approval.accepted: false` each exit `0`.
12a. **The plan-only exit contract is total (§3.6).** Exit `0` with a document is asserted for each
    of: a clean plan, a `runnable: false` plan, an unreadable `stack.yaml`, a cyclic stack, a
    refused selection, every projected state/continuation gate and an exceeded limit — the last six
    in **both** modes. Exit `1` with **no** stdout byte and **no** `plan-guard:` marker is asserted
    for exactly **four cause classes** covering **five** labelled cells, and no others:

    | # | Cell label | §3.6 row | Cause class | Trigger |
    |---:|---|---:|---|---|
    | 1 | `control-flag` | 4 | control-flag error | any §3.4 row, e.g. `--json` without `--plan` (§22.3) |
    | 2 | `subject-unresolvable` | 5 | subject/security failure | an unresolvable feature or workspace subject |
    | 3 | `security-symlink` | 5 | subject/security failure | the shipped runtime-state symlink refusal |
    | 4 | `encode-failure` | 6 | encoding failure | an injected `MarshalRebasePlan` failure |
    | 5 | `writer-failure` | 7 | writer failure | an injected stdout `io.Writer` failure, in **both** of its shapes (§23.1 seam 4) |

    Cells 4 and 5 run through the failing-writer seam, which asserts the **one-write** contract of
    §3.6 rules 1–2 directly: `renderPlanDocumentTo` is counted at **exactly one** `Write` call on
    every successful document, at **zero** `Write` calls in cell 4 (the renderer returned no
    buffer, so nothing was offered), and at **one** in cell 5. Cell 5 is asserted in both writer
    shapes — a writer whose sole `Write` returns `(0, error)`, after which the harness's stdout
    buffer holds **zero** bytes, and a writer that returns a short write `(n < len(p), error)`,
    after which it holds exactly the `n` bytes it itself reported accepting and **no** further byte
    is ever offered to it or to any other stream. Both cells also assert that no partial JSON value
    reached stdout — in the `(0, error)` cell because nothing was accepted, in the short-write cell
    because the truncation is the writer's own reported prefix of a buffer that was complete when
    it was handed over — and that the returned error is an ordinary untyped error, never
    `*PlanGuardRefusalError`. A test that injects a failure on an *Nth* document write fails this
    criterion: the document is emitted in one write, so no Nth document write exists.
    Cells 2 and 3 are two cells of **one** class, which is why the class
    count is four and the cell count is five; no text may call the five cells "four causes". A
    **sixth** cell, or a **fifth** cause class, anywhere on the plan route fails this criterion, and
    so does any assertion expecting exit `1` for an unreadable stack, a cyclic stack, a refused
    selection, a projected gate, an exceeded limit or a controlled-path blocker (§22.15, §22.16).
    **The count is per route, and each layer is asserted only for the causes it can raise**
    (§13.7 rule 12, §13.7a rule 14): `PlanCheckoutRebase`/`runExternalPlan` are asserted to return
    non-`nil` only for a writer failure and for an error their builder returned; the two checkout
    builders and `BuildRebasePlan` only for an encoding-class construction failure; and cells 1–3
    are asserted to be raised **above** those functions, by `resolvePlanGuardOptions` and by §3.3
    steps 1–5, with a call counter showing the plan function was never entered. A test that
    attributes a control-flag or subject error to a builder, or that counts more than four classes
    on the route, fails this criterion.
12b. **The external completion gate is a postcondition, and the plan says so (§7.1 rank 4, §13.5,
    §13.7a rule 15).** Over a feature whose child branch does **not** contain its configured parent
    — exactly the fixture `staleStackEdgesFiltered` reports — the following are asserted:
    (i) `tws sync <f> --plan` and `tws sync <f> --plan --fetch` publish that edge as the row's
    `ancestry` (`stale` or `divergent`, with the shipped `StackEdge` reason), publish **no**
    blocker of any rank for it, keep `runnable: true`, print the `Sync mode:` header where the
    route prints one, and perform their route's normal fetch — a document whose only stale edge is
    a row it will rebase is never suppressed, never `runnable: false`, and never
    `freshness: not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` on that account;
    (ii) the same holds for a `--plan --continue` whose remaining set still contains a rebase row;
    (iii) a **rows-less push-only** continuation over the same stale edge publishes rank 4
    `preflight-refused` whose `detail` carries the shipped sentences byte-for-byte
    (`Sync incomplete; stale stack edges remain:` and `  [!] %s does not contain parent %s`),
    `runnable: false`, `push.executable: false`, `preflight-refused` in `push.blocked_by[]`, a
    **non-empty** `push.targets[]` — the entries an earlier invocation rebased and never pushed are
    the blast radius this refusal is about (§14.1a rule 10d) — `summary.plannability: empty`,
    `freshness: not-refreshed-continuation` and exit `0`;
    (iv) the **executing** twin of (i) really rebases, and where the edge survives the run the
    shipped gate fires **after** the rebases with its shipped bytes, exit `1`, **no**
    `plan-guard:` marker, and recovery state persisted by `syncFailure` — asserted by loading the
    state file afterwards and by a following `tws sync <f> --continue`/`--abort` both working;
    (v) a source assertion shows `runExternalPlan` evaluates `staleStackEdgesFiltered` in no cell
    other than the rows-less push-only continuation of (iii). An implementation that blocks,
    suppresses a fetch, or sets `runnable: false` for a stale edge on a rebase row fails this
    criterion.
12c. **Rows-less runnability is the general rule, not an enumeration (§4.3, §7.3).** A
    `plannability: empty` document is asserted `runnable: true` **iff** it carries no effective,
    unwaived blocker of ranks 1–5 (any sub-rank) and no rank 6 `selection-hazard`. Both directions
    are fixtured, in the modes each cell is reachable in:
    (i) **`true` cells** — a rows-less continuation whose remaining set is empty and whose only
    facts are informational (warnings, `ancestry`, an `intent.push: false` restore/push projection)
    keeps `runnable: true`, and so does a **limitless** rows-less plan whose bound identity is
    invalid UTF-8, which publishes `encoding_issues[]`, mints no token and emits **no** rank 5.08
    blocker (§7.1 rank 5.08);
    (ii) **`false` cells, each asserted individually on a rows-less document** — document-level
    rank 5.05 `fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate`; document-level rank 5.06
    `fetch-local-branch-checked-out`; **route-applicable** rank 5.07 `invalid-git-config` on a
    rows-less run that still fetches, pushes or restores; **conditional** rank 5.08
    `identity-not-utf8` on a rows-less document that would mint or was given a token; rank 5.9
    `probe-failed` from an unreadable push mapping on a rows-less push-only continuation
    (§14.1a rule 5a); rank 5.0/5.1/5.15 context facts measured for a fetch, push or restore
    context; rank 4 `preflight-refused` from the completion gate of §22.12b (iii); rank 4.5
    `restore-blocked`; rank 3 `state-refused`; and rank 6 `selection-hazard`;
    (iii) **rank independence** — a rows-less document carrying only a rank 7, 7.5, 8, 9, 10, 11 or
    12 refusal keeps `runnable: true`, with `refusal.kind` still published;
    (iv) **`unavailable`** — every `plannability: unavailable` fixture in the suite is asserted
    `runnable: false`, and the assertion is written as the general predicate evaluated over
    `blockers[]`, not as a hard-coded value;
    (v) a **source assertion** shows exactly one implementation of the predicate, consuming the
    same `[]PlanBlocker` slice `SelectPrimaryRefusal` returns, with **no** rows-less branch and no
    rank list of its own. An implementation or test that enumerates "the ranks a rows-less document
    can reach" fails this criterion.
13. `tws sync <f> --plan --no-fetch` performs no network I/O and leaves every ref byte-identical,
    with `route: new-mode`, `fetch.attempted: false`, `freshness: local-only`.
13a. **I14 is projected, not guessed (§10.7).** With a selected entry whose base does not resolve
    locally, `tws sync <f> --plan --no-fetch` publishes `runnable: false` and a rank 5.7

    (`tws sync <f> --no-fetch --max-replay-per-entry 10`) exits `1` with that same shipped

    checkout archived entry and a checkout empty-`Base` entry with the same unresolvable base leave
    the document `runnable: true`, matching the executor's own skips. The unguarded control's
    sentence, exit code and process count are unchanged.
13b. **A checkout plan projects every pre-fetch gate, and fetches only under `--fetch` when the

    `--plan --fetch` invocation records **zero** `git fetch`, prints **no** `Sync mode:` header,
    publishes that gate's blocker with the shipped sentence byte-for-byte, `runnable: false` and
    exits `0`, while its executing twin keeps the shipped refusal, sentence and exit `1`.

    (§13.7 step 2, §11.2): gates a–h publish `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` (cause 2) on a

    `summary.plannability: unavailable` with `entries: []`, while the new-mode live-lock cell and
    the I14 cell — which refuse with the stack loaded and the selection resolved — publish their

    `BuildCheckoutRebasePlan(insp, outcome, push)` is asserted to issue no Git process of its own.

    **after** the `git fetch` (step 4a) — or at the plan point, with `TrackingPhase: plan-point`,
    in every non-fetching cell above and on the continuation arm (step 3a) — **zero** calls and
    zero reads where `intent.push` is false or the document is rows-less, and

    **The Git-operation gate is asserted per artefact (§13.7 gate c):** with the repository put, in

13c. **An external plan performs exactly one policy fetch, through the writer-aware route

13d. **The checkout plan's continuation arm and the hoisted opts assignment (§13.7).**

    `tws sync <f> --plan --continue` publishes the rank 3 `state-refused` blocker whose `detail` is

    from the `conflict` stage's `rebase still in progress; finish resolving conflicts then run

    equal to `fmt.Sprintf("%s not descended from %s after rebase", entry.Branch, entry.Base)` for

    which is asserted to remain evidence-only in every other cell — exits `0`, takes no lock, and

    **satisfied** twin — the same fixture with the branch really descended — publishes **no**

    checkout run is the shipped rank 3 `working tree is dirty; commit or stash changes before
    checkout sync`, never an autostash row.

13g. **The checkout route enumerates its fetch context and effect before fetching, and can reach

    reachable in checkout mode: a superproject with
    unconditional recursion and unbounded reach (rank 5.05), and a covering positive

    `context_source`, the full `fetch_effect` (with the unbounded `submodule_recursion.reach` /

    this criterion (§4.4a, §11.2). The corresponding cause 1–3 and `local-only` cells are asserted
    `[]` in the same table, so the two shapes cannot be conflated. Cause 4 is asserted **unreachable** here: a checkout fixture with a
    broken remote or an unmeasurable common dir publishes **no** rank 5.0 blocker, no

13i. **The runtime snapshot types are concrete and Lstat-first (§12.5a).** For each applicable

13j. **The projected `.checkout-sync.lock` ladder is the whole native ladder, in both arms
    (§13.7 gate j).** For **every** row of the gate-j table, a checkout `--plan --fetch` (fresh)
    and a checkout `--plan --continue` (continuation) are asserted against their executing twins:
    an **absent** lock refuses nothing; an **I/O-unreadable** and a **directory** lock publish
    `read existing checkout-sync lock: %w` (fresh) / `read checkout-sync lock: %w` (continuation);
    a **corrupt** and an **empty** lock publish `invalid checkout-sync lock; inspect %s and use
    --abort to recover: %w` / `invalid checkout-sync lock %s: %w`; a **`pid: 0`** and a **`pid:
    -1`** lock publish `checkout-sync lock is being initialized or is invalid; retry or inspect
    %s` in both arms; a **live foreign** lock publishes `checkout-sync lock held by live process %d
    (created %s); cannot steal live lock` / `lock held by live process %d; cannot reclaim`; a
    **self-PID** lock (row 5a) publishes the fresh sentence with an **empty**
    `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` and **no** `not-refreshed-live-run` on the fresh arm, and **no
    blocker at all** on the continuation arm, whose executing twin really reclaims and proceeds —
    a self-PID cell publishing `live-owner-concurrency`, or refusing a continuation, fails this
    criterion; and a
    **dead, foreign lock beside an undecodable transaction** publishes **gate b's** sentence,
    `previous checkout-sync incomplete; use --continue or --abort`, and **not** the lock ladder's
    `stale lock from PID %d detected with existing transaction; use --continue or --abort to
    recover` — because `HasCheckoutTransaction` is a bare `os.Stat` evaluated above the lock, so
    the native arm is unreachable below gate b (row 6), and the executing twin is asserted to print
    the same gate-b sentence. Each cell asserts: the blocker is rank 3 `state-refused`, its `detail` is
    **byte-equal** to the shipped sentence with the shipped operands, `runnable: false`, exit `0`,
    **zero** `git fetch`, **no** `Sync mode:` header, and the executing twin's stderr is
    byte-identical to the shipped refusal and **marker-free** (§22.31). Only the live-holder cell
    carries `guard.execute_blocked_by: ["live-owner-concurrency"]` and
    `freshness: not-refreshed-live-run`; every other cell carries an empty
    `execute_blocked_by[]` and cause 2 (or `local-only` on a no-fetch route). Three negative
    assertions complete it: a **dead, foreign** PID lock with no transaction relation publishes
    **no** blocker at all (the reclaim is projected as succeeding), no cell projects
    `reclaim stale checkout-sync lock: %w`, `reclaim checkout-sync lock: %w`,
    `acquire checkout-sync lock after stale recovery: %w` or `create lock directory: %w` — they
    are write races and future writes, not snapshot facts — and a **symlinked** lock publishes
    `presence: symlink`, no synthesized native sentence, zero reads of that path, while its
    **guarded** twin refuses with `owner-artefact-undecodable` (§12.5). A projected sentence that

13k. **The fetch effect resolves the remote against the fetch context's own HEAD (§11.4).** Four

    linked worktree whose HEAD is `feat/y` with `branch.feat/y.remote = alt` publishes
    `context_source: worktree`, `head_branch: "feat/y"` and remote `alt`, **even though** the
    workspace repository's own HEAD names a different branch whose `branch.<name>.remote` is
    `origin` — a document publishing `origin` there fails this criterion; (iii) **`entry.Repo` and
    process-cwd contexts** — the same assertion with `context_source: entry-repo` and
    `process-cwd`, each reading the HEAD of *that* directory; (iv) **detached HEAD** — a fetch
    context on a detached HEAD publishes `head_branch: null`, consults **no**
    `branch.<name>.remote` at all (asserted through the config-read argv), and resolves by the
    sole-remote-then-`origin` ladder, matching what a real `git fetch` in that directory contacts.
    The equivalence half is asserted with them: two linked worktrees of one common dir on
    **different** branches whose resolved effects agree still collapse to **one** `git fetch` and

    **different** remotes are rank 5.0 `fetch-context-indeterminate` with the sorted candidate
    disclosure and zero fetches. Finally, `approval.fingerprint` is asserted **unchanged** across

    fingerprint non-member (§8.3).

    that prints `[~] resolved` for it, fails this criterion;
    (v) **no fetch, plan-point leases** — the argv sidecar records zero `git fetch`, the document
    the seam evaluated carries `freshness: not-refreshed-continuation` and every
    `expectation: sha` lease is `possibly-stale` with `TrackingPhase: plan-point` (§14.1a rule 7);
    (vi) **executor identity, and the one intended argv divergence** — the resume reaches
    `syncWithStackScoped` with `insp.Order` and finishes through the shipped
    `runNewModePush`/`finalizeScopedSyncRun` tail. Its rebase argv is asserted against the
    unguarded control's for the same remaining set as a **matched pair, element by element**: every

    (vii) **an armed v2 payload is upgraded at step 10a** — the same resume over a
    `state_version: 2` payload **with** a limit flag is asserted to write the §13.2a upgrade after

    `route: new-mode` with the effective limits and unchanged `test_command`; the persisted-v3 and

14c. **A guarded legacy continuation runs one entry point with three arms, and the flagless legacy
    resume is frozen (§12.3, §13.6 rule 8 rows 9 and 14, §19.2).** Over a real interrupted

    (i) **dispatch** — `tws sync <f> --continue --max-replay-per-entry N` over a real

    (ii) **one sort, one inspection, one subject read** — the guarded cell-7 arm records **exactly

    (ii-b) **the resumed count is the persisted one** — the `Resuming sync with %d pending

    (ii-c) **the prose precedes the seam** — a guarded cell-7 invocation whose limit refuses is

    (iii) **the legacy universe is full-stack** — with a stack whose entries were **not** all

    (iv) **gates once, sentences verbatim** — `isRebaseInProgress`, the failed-branch

    branch(es)` lines appear at their shipped positions, and **no** `Sync mode:` header is printed

    (v) **limits, no fetch, nothing written above the seam** — the effective limits carry
    `origin: flags-legacy-continuation` in **this** document; the argv
    sidecar records **zero** `git fetch` with `freshness: not-refreshed-continuation` and

    `route: legacy` payload carrying those limits, the frozen command and the carried

    `prior_legacy_sha256` equal to the SHA-256 of the pre-run `.sync-state.yaml` bytes, a

    to the persisted `len(pending)` (§22.24j);
    (vi) **executor identity is payload-aware and legacy-shaped** — a passing run is asserted to
    enter `syncWithStackScoped` with a non-`nil` `run` whose `Route` is `legacy` and whose
    `Payload` is **pointer-identical** to the envelope `setupGuardedLegacyRunState` just returned
    (`syncWithStackFiltered`/`run == nil` at this call site fails this criterion), and, in the same
    test, that this changes nothing observable beyond the one declared pin: its rebase argv
    sequence — `rebase --update-refs` shapes, the amend-aware `--onto` form, `markUpdatedAncestors`,
    archived-entry handling and the unfiltered completion gate — is asserted against the flagless
    control's for the same remaining set as a **matched pair, element by element**, equal
    everywhere except the `--onto` operand, which is the pinned full SHA here and the ref name
    there (§10.5, §22.14b (vi)); its stdout matches the control's; and its per-entry JIT seams fire
    between the shipped rebases without changing any of them. Three state consequences are asserted with it: an
    interrupted run persists `stage: failed`, `FailedBranch` and the recomputed
    `Completed`/`Pending` **in the v3 payload** with **no** real `.sync-state.yaml` written beside
    it (classifier cell **5**, never cell 8); a completed run ends through
    `finalizeScopedSyncRun` → `clearSyncRunState(featurePath, true)` leaving no payload, no
    sentinel, no run guard and no `.sync-state.yaml`; and the shipped `saveIncompleteSync` is
    asserted **never** called on this arm;
    (vii) **validation is the frozen command** — with a `test_command` configured, the executor is
    asserted to run the command the envelope persisted (the value this invocation froze and
    digested), to perform **zero** `internal.LoadConfig()` reads for validation below the seam, and
    to be unaffected by a configuration edit injected after step 9 — no `revalidation-mismatch`,

15. A cyclic stack yields `refusal.kind: stack-unsortable`, `entries: []`, `fetch.attempted: false`,
    `fetch.repos: []`, `approval.fingerprint: null`, exit `0` in **both** modes —
    `freshness: not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` where the described route's effective policy is
    `fetch`, and `local-only` where it is `no-fetch`, which is every default and legacy checkout
    plan (§10.2, §13.7 step 2). The unguarded controls keep their shipped, **arm-specific**
    behaviour: the external legacy control still fetches and then fails; the **legacy** checkout
    control still takes its lock and then fails inside `BuildCheckoutPlan` with
    `build plan: cycle detected in stack.yaml`; and the **new-mode** checkout control still fails
    *above* its lock and its fetch, inside `ResolveSyncSelection`, with the bare
    `cycle detected in stack.yaml` (§9.1a rule 3a, §22.13l).
16. An unreadable `stack.yaml` yields `refusal.kind: plan-unavailable` and **no** `git rebase`
    process at all — `syncFallback` is never reached on a planned or guarded route. On the
    plan-only route it is a **document**, not an error: `entries: []`,
    `summary.plannability: unavailable`, `guard.evaluation: []`, exit `0`, with the returned error
    asserted `nil` in both modes (§3.6 rows 2–3, §13.7 rule 12). A test that expects exit `1` for
    an unreadable or cyclic stack on `--plan` fails this criterion.

**Guard and approval**

17. With a plan whose entry replays 40 candidates, `tws sync <f> --max-replay-per-entry 10` exits
    `1`, moves no ref, and writes exactly one stderr line matching `^plan-guard: limit-per-entry: `;
    the returned error contains no marker.
17a. Criterion 17 is asserted **through production `cli.Execute()`** in **both** workspace modes.
    The post-mutation prefix is asserted **byte-exactly**: `PlanGuardRefusalError.Error()` with
    `StatePreserved: true` is asserted to begin with the literal `state-preserved: ` whose length
    is **exactly 17** (`len("state-preserved: ") == 17`, asserted as a number, not as a prose
    claim), to carry exactly one trailing space, and to be absent — length `0` — with
    `StatePreserved: false`; a test asserting 18 bytes, or a second space, fails this criterion.
    The checkout half proves the ownership split: the refusal originates as an
    `*internal.PlanGuardRefusalError` returned by `internal.RunCheckoutSync`, `internal` writes no
    marker byte, `runCheckoutSync` writes the single anchored line through `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`, and
    a `go list -deps`-style import assertion shows package `internal` importing **no** Cobra
    package **and no `internal/cli` package** (§9.0 rule 5). A companion source assertion shows no
    shared planner signature naming `externalSyncLayout`, and a table test shows
    `internal.RebasePlanLayout.WorktreePath` and `externalSyncLayout.WorktreePath` agreeing on
    every fixture name (§9.0 rule 3).
18. The §8.6 legacy round trip succeeds end-to-end on a stable repository, and the executing
    invocation performs the rebase; changing any of `T`, `L`, `P`, `V` yields
    `approval-mismatch` and no rebase.
19. A token cannot waive any rank 1–10 fact: for each of `state-refused`, `preflight-refused`,
    `restore-blocked`, `repo-unavailable`, `head-ref-missing`, `prunable-worktree`,
    `branch-checked-out-elsewhere`, `context-dirty`, `base-ref-missing`, `cutoff-unresolvable`,
    `probe-failed`, `invalid-git-config`, `identity-not-utf8`, `selection-hazard`,
    `guard-limit-mismatch`, `approval-without-limits` and `indeterminate-entry`, the guarded run
    still refuses with a matching token.
20. `guard.evaluation[]` uses strict `>`: a plan with exactly 10 candidates and
    `--max-replay-per-entry 10` is `within-limit` and executes.
20a. The aggregate row branches on the unknown count first: with **no** unknown rows and
    `--max-replay-total`, it is `basis: total`, `unknown_entries: null`, `value` equal to
    `summary.total_candidates`, and `exceeded` exactly when that value `> L` — including when it
    exceeds, where `basis: lower-bound` is a failure; with at least one unknown row it is
    `basis: lower-bound` with `unknown_entries == summary.entries_with_unknown_candidates`,
    `exceeded` when `B > L` and `unknown` otherwise.
20b. **`guard.evaluation[]` is scoped to plannable documents (§4.6).** A `plannability: rows`
    document with an effective limit emits one row per entry plus the aggregate; a
    `plannability: empty` document with a total limit emits exactly the `basis: total`, `value: 0`,
    `within-limit` aggregate and no per-entry row; and a `plannability: unavailable` document —
    driven by a cyclic stack and by an unreadable `stack.yaml` — emits **`[]`** even with
    `--max-replay-per-entry 0 --max-replay-total 0` supplied, with `guard.would_refuse: false` and
    the document's own rank 1 `refusal.kind`. An aggregate row on an `unavailable` document fails
    this criterion.
21. `--max-replay-per-entry 0` refuses any entry with ≥1 candidate and executes a plan whose rows
    all replay `0`.
22. A limitless `--plan` publishes `approval.fingerprint: null`,
    `approval.covers.requires_limits: true`, `has_work: true`, and `guard.evaluation: []`; adding a
    limit produces a usable token over the same facts.
23. A guarded continuation inherits persisted limits; a conflicting supplied limit yields rank 7
    `guard-limit-mismatch` naming the key, keeps the persisted value effective, and still mints a
    token over those values.
24. Persisted `0` survives a save/load round trip on disk in both `SyncRunState` and
    `CheckoutTransaction`, and neither file gains `guard_enabled` or an approval token — including
    after the §13.2a upgrade, whose written key set is asserted to be exactly `state_version`,
    `route` and the effective limit keys over an otherwise byte-identical document (§22.24i (i)).
24a. **Version/state matrix (§13.6 rule 2).** Each of the eight birth cells writes exactly the
    declared version and key set: every unguarded cell's file is byte-identical to the shipped
    shape (no `route`, no limit key, `state_version` `2`/absent/none as shipped), every guarded
    cell writes `state_version: 3` plus `route` and the persisted limits — the guarded **legacy
    external** cell additionally writing the backup sentinel of §13.6 rule 2c, asserted to decode
    as the shipped sentinel shape under `internal.SyncState` (§22.24j (i)) — and the plan-only cell
    writes nothing at all. The version is birth-decided: a continuation, a failure write, a push
    write and a teardown of an existing run never change it, asserted by re-reading the file after
    each.
24b. **Downgrade is fail-closed.** With a real `v1.2.15` binary (the shipped downgrade-harness
    pattern of `internal/cli/sync_downgrade_test.go`): a guarded external run's state makes
    `tws sync <f>`, `--continue` **and** `--abort` all exit `1` with
    `scoped sync state at <path> is unreadable or uses an unsupported version (unsupported scoped
    sync state version 3); inspect it and remove it manually — tws will not guess`; a guarded
    checkout run's transaction makes `--continue` exit `1` with `checkout sync transaction state
    version 3 is newer than 2; upgrade tws or remove <path>`, and a fresh run exit `1` with
    `previous checkout-sync incomplete; use --continue or --abort`. In every one of those cells
    **no ref moved**. The declared exception is asserted too: the old binary's checkout `--abort`
    still restores and clears, and performs no rebase.
24c. **The new binary is backward compatible, and the three route-derived predicates are
    equivalent on every shipped state.** A `state_version: 2` payload, a `state_version: 2`
    transaction and a legacy version-less transaction each load, resume to completion and
    round-trip byte-identically under the new binary **when the resume supplies no control flag** —
    the §13.2a upgrade is asserted **not** to fire on any of those runs, so the round-trip claim is
    a claim about the unguarded path and is asserted as such (§22.24i (v)). `txNewMode`/`TransactionNewMode` and
    `PayloadNewMode` return the shipped answer for every `(route ∈ {absent, legacy, new-mode,
    bogus}) × (state_version ∈ {absent, 1, 2, 3})` cell a shipped binary can have produced, **plus
    the exact declared answer for every cell it cannot**: `legacy` ⇒ `false` and `new-mode` ⇒
    `true` at every version, and `bogus` ⇒ the version's answer (`true` at `2`/`3`, `false` at
    absent/`1`), per §13.6 rule 4's `default`-arm table. The `nil` row returns `false` and neither
    function panics
    on `nil`. `checkoutTriggersNeedV2` is asserted equal to the shipped
    `loadErr != nil || tx == nil || tx.StateVersion < CheckoutTransactionVersion` for an absent
    transaction, an unreadable transaction, a v1 transaction and a v2 transaction, and to refuse on
    a v3 `route: legacy` transaction; `syncTriggersNeedV2` is asserted equal to the shipped
    `Cell == 1 || Cell == 7` on every shipped cell, to refuse on cell 5 with `route: legacy`, and to
    return **`false`** on cell 4 — including over a valid backup sentinel, whose trigger-flag answer
    is owned by the §12.8b interception above it — with a source assertion that the function takes
    no sentinel-view parameter (§13.6 rule 4a, §25.82).
24d. **Guarded legacy external envelope.** A guarded `tws sync <f> --max-replay-per-entry N` on the
    legacy route produces stdout and selection identical to its unguarded twin (no `Sync mode:`
    header, `--update-refs` argv, archived entries still handled) and Git argv equal element by
    element except the SHA-pinned `--onto` operand of §10.5, writes the **backup sentinel** of
    §13.6 rule 2c (here `prior_legacy_present: false`, since a fresh run replaced nothing) +
    a `state_version: 3` payload with `route: legacy`, both limits and the frozen validation
    command, in §13.2a's canonical four-step order — **capture (step 1) → guard claim (step 2) →
    conditional backup sentinel (step 3) → payload (step 4)** — with a source assertion and a
    filesystem-observer assertion together showing `ClaimSyncRunGuard` is this arm's **first**
    write and the sentinel is written under it (a run whose sentinel precedes its claim fails this
    criterion), and clears all three on success. After an induced conflict, `--continue` resumes through the
    legacy path with `origin: persisted-payload` limits, honours the `--push` **flag** as legacy
    does, and `--continue --only x` is refused with the shipped I20 sentence. A plain re-run over
    that state prints the shipped cell-5 sentence and `--abort` takes the shipped cell-5 arm, both
    byte-identical to their shipped forms. The unguarded legacy twin still writes only
    `.sync-state.yaml`, and a plain re-run over *that* state still prints the legacy
    `previous sync incomplete (failed on: %s); use --continue or --abort`.
24e. **The deferred half of I7 is route-derived (§13.6 rule 4b).** Over the seven-row matrix of
    that rule, `tws sync <f> --continue --abort` refuses with the shipped
    `--continue and --abort are mutually exclusive` for a v2 payload, a v3 `route: new-mode`
    payload, a sentinel-only cell 4 and every undecodable-payload cell; and it
    does **not** refuse for no state at all, for a legacy `.sync-state.yaml`, or for a v3
    `route: legacy` envelope, where `--abort` wins and takes the shipped cell-5 arm printing
    `Sync state cleared.` with the payload, sentinel and guard all gone afterwards. The same v3
    legacy envelope presented to a real `v1.2.15` binary refuses `--continue --abort` with the
    identical shipped I7 sentence and refuses every single verb with the cell-6
    unsupported-version sentence, moving no ref.
24f. **The validation freeze is authoritative (§15.9).** Editing the configured validation command
    **after** the run's state exists changes nothing: the guarded `--continue` of an interrupted
    guarded run — legacy envelope, v3 new-mode payload and checkout transaction alike — resumes
    with the **persisted** command, runs exactly that command, emits **no** `revalidation-mismatch`
    and **no** `approval-mismatch`, and the edited configuration is never read (asserted by a
    config value that would fail if used). Editing it between a `--plan` and its guarded executing
    twin **does** refuse: rank 8 `approval-mismatch` at the guard seam, before
    `setupSyncRunState`, with no payload, sentinel or run guard created. No criterion anywhere
    requires a configuration change to produce a rank 9 refusal.

24g. **Checkout recovery is route-derived (§13.6 rule 4c).** Under the new binary, driven through
    production `Execute()`: a version-less and a `state_version: 2` transaction reproduce the
    shipped `--continue --abort` answers exactly (abort wins / refuse
    `--continue and --abort are mutually exclusive`) and the shipped choice of continuation gates; a
    `state_version: 3`, `route: new-mode` transaction refuses `--continue --abort` with the same
    sentence and takes the v2 gates plus the header; and a `state_version: 3`, `route: legacy`
    transaction does **not** refuse — `--abort` wins and takes the shipped abort arm — while
    `--continue` applies the legacy push-mismatch check, prints **no** `Sync mode:` header, and
    refuses `--continue --only x` with the shipped I20 sentence. A table test asserts
    `checkoutRecoveryIsNewMode` equals the shipped
    `tx.StateVersion >= CheckoutTransactionVersion` for every
    `(route ∈ {absent, legacy, new-mode, bogus}) × (state_version ∈ {absent, 1, 2, 3})` cell a
    shipped binary can have produced, and equals §13.6 rule 4's `default`-arm table in the cells it
    cannot (a `bogus` route at `state_version` `2` or `3` is **new-mode**, at absent or `1` it is
    not), and returns `false` without panicking for `nil`. The declared
    asymmetry is asserted with a real `v1.2.15` binary over the same v3 `route: legacy`
    transaction: it refuses `--continue --abort` with the shipped I7 sentence, refuses `--continue`
    with `checkout sync transaction state version 3 is newer than 2; upgrade tws or remove <path>`,
    and its plain `--abort` still restores and clears — with **no ref moved** in any of those cells.
24h. **A persisted guarded checkout run stays guarded on a flagless `--continue` (§13.6 rule 4d,
    §12.2d).** Over a real interrupted **guarded** checkout run — started with
    `tws sync <f> --max-replay-per-entry 2`, interrupted mid-transaction, so
    `.checkout-sync.tx.yaml` carries `state_version: 3`, `route`, both limit keys and the frozen
    `test_command` — driven through production `Execute()`:
    (i) **dispatch** — the six-row table is asserted with a counter on `ContinueCheckoutSync`'s
    guarded arm: `state_version: 3` + no control flag ⇒ **guarded**; `state_version: 3` + a limit
    flag ⇒ guarded; `state_version: 3` + `--plan` ⇒ **neither** (the plan route, which executes
    nothing); `state_version: 2` + no flag ⇒ **unguarded**, taking the shipped arms; version-less
    + no flag ⇒ unguarded; and an **absent** transaction ⇒ the shipped
    `no transaction to continue: %w` sentence from its shipped site, guarded or not;
    (ii) **inheritance, with no flag repeated** — the flagless v3 resume is asserted to refuse on
    the **persisted** `max_replay_per_entry` with exactly one `^plan-guard: limit-per-entry: `
    line, `guard.limits.max_replay_per_entry.origin == "persisted-transaction"` on the matching
    `--plan --continue` document, and the transaction's persisted `test_command` used for
    validation while an edited configuration is never read (§15.9, §22.24f). A resume that
    completed without the guard — no marker, no refusal, the over-limit entry rebased — fails this
    criterion, because that is exactly the silent-drop defect the version bump exists to prevent;
    (iii) **conflict is still rank 7** — the same resume with a *different* supplied limit publishes
    `guard-limit-mismatch` with the persisted value still effective (§13.2);
    (iv) **the frozen path is untouched** — the `state_version: 2`/version-less flagless controls
    are asserted byte-, exit- and process-identical to the pre-feature run over the same fixture,
    with `InspectCheckoutPlan` and `InspectCheckoutPlanState` counted at **zero** calls and no
    `git --version` or config-inventory process added (§12.2d rule 4, §17.1);
    (v) **the added read is pure and singular** — the `--continue` arm is asserted to perform
    exactly **one** `LoadCheckoutTransaction` of its own on every cell (the I20 predicate takes the
    loaded pair, §13.6 rule 4a) and to write nothing before `ContinueCheckoutSync`, with an
    unchanged file hash and an unchanged process count on the unguarded control;
    (vi) **predicate table** — `checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded`/`TransactionGuarded` are asserted `true`
    exactly for `state_version >= 3` over
    `(route ∈ {absent, legacy, new-mode, bogus}) × (state_version ∈ {absent, 1, 2, 3})`, `false`
    for `nil` and for a load error without panicking, and a source assertion shows it is the only
    `CheckoutTransactionGuardedVersion` comparison that decides a route (the loader's upper bound
    of §13.6 rule 3 is a readability check and is asserted separately).
24i. **An armed continuation persists its guard before it mutates, and the run stays guarded

    `GuardedLegacySentinel`, to carry `guarded_state_version: 3`, `route: legacy`, this feature's

    `validation_source` — with **no** `validation_digest` key of any spelling, asserted by decoding

    lists in the
    invocation's one `TopoSort` order, the carried `Completed`/`FailedBranch`, `prior_pending_count`
    and — on a continuation — `prior_legacy_present: true` with a `prior_legacy_base64` whose

    them. A **fresh** guarded legacy run's sentinel is asserted to carry

    (ii) **the ladder is total and fail-closed** — `InspectGuardedLegacySentinel` is driven through

**Planner unification**

25. For every `(mode × scope × cutoff state × materialization)` cell, `RebaseStrategy`'s argv equals
    the argv the executor really passes, asserted through the argv sidecar.
25a. Every `strategy: unknown` row publishes `argv: null` and `argv_alternatives: null` — never
    `[]`, which is reserved for `skipped-*` — together with `replay.determinacy: unknown`, a
    `replay.reason` that is not `not-executed`, `candidate_count: null`, `blocking: true`, and a
    `guard.evaluation[]` row with `unknown_kind: not-resolvable`. The complementary assertions hold
    for `conditional` (`argv: null`, two `argv_alternatives`) and for all four `skipped-*`
    strategies (`argv: []`).
25a-i. **`replay.reason` is total over one precedence list (§4.2).** A `strategy: unknown` row in a
    context with `rebase.rebaseMerges = true` and `effective_backend: merge` publishes
    `replay.reason: merge-recreation` — **not** the row's own missing-input reason — while the same
    fixture with `effective_backend: apply` publishes that missing-input reason
    (`base-ref-missing`, `head-ref-missing`, `cutoff-unresolvable`, `repo-unavailable` or
    `probe-failed`); a deferred-upstream unknown row publishes `upstream-deferred`. A table test
    asserts every `replay.reason` emitted anywhere in the fixture corpus is a member of the single
    §4.2 list, that no row shape carries a private sub-enum, and that ranks 0, 4a, 4b and `null`
    never appear on an `unknown` row while ranks 1–3 all do across the corpus. A test that expects
    a five-token `unknown`-row enum fails this criterion.
25b. **The `switched` stage is modelled as a pinned-destination arm (§13.3a).** With a checkout
    transaction parked at `Stage: switched` on an `onto` row (`LastBaseSHA != NewBaseSHA`) whose
    `entry.Base` ref has since been moved to a different commit: `tws sync <f> --plan --continue`
    publishes `destination.sha` equal to the **persisted** `NewBaseSHA` (not the ref's current
    resolution) and `replay.upstream_sha` equal to the **persisted `LastBaseSHA`** — the recorded
    cutoff, never the destination — with `replay.range` spelled over that upstream; the guarded
    `--continue` executes `git rebase --no-fork-point --onto <persisted NewBaseSHA>
    <persisted LastBaseSHA>` in the argv sidecar, **no** `revalidation-mismatch` is raised, and the
    result is byte-identical to the unguarded control. The plain-arm twin (`LastBaseSHA` empty)
    publishes the snapshot destination with `replay.determinacy: snapshot`, passes `entry.Base` in
    the argv, and **does** raise `revalidation-mismatch` when the approved snapshot moved. A
    `Stage: planned` control asserts the shipped re-resolution is unchanged, and a probe-count
    assertion shows the `switched` plan issues **no** `rev-parse` of `entry.Base` on the `onto` arm
    and **exactly one** `rev-parse --verify <persisted NewBaseSHA>^{commit}` existence probe
    (§13.3a rule 6). A companion cell destroys that object (rewrite + reflog expire + prune): the
    plan publishes rank 5.7 `base-ref-missing` on the row with `runnable: false` at exit `0`, the
    guarded resume exits `1` before any rebase with one marker line, `replay.upstream_sha` still
    equals the persisted `LastBaseSHA`, and no new refusal kind appears anywhere in the document.
    The row also publishes `mutation.will_switch_head: false`, because that arm switches nothing.
25c. **The `switched` arm's HEAD identity is enforced on the plan and guarded routes only
    (§13.3a rule 5).** With HEAD on the persisted `entry.Branch`, `--plan --continue` is
    `runnable: true` and the guarded `--continue` completes. With HEAD checked out on a **different**
    branch, and again with a **detached** HEAD, the plan publishes a rank 4 `preflight-refused`
    blocker on that row naming the persisted branch and the measured HEAD, `runnable: false`, exit
    `0`; the guarded `--continue` exits `1` with exactly one `^plan-guard: preflight-refused: ` line
    and **no ref moves**; and the **unguarded** `tws sync <f> --continue` control still performs the
    shipped rebase of whatever HEAD is on, proving the shipped path was not changed. The JIT twin is
    asserted too: moving HEAD between the guard seam and `doRebase` (barrier) refuses before the
    rebase.
26. A stack whose parent has a decoupled `branch:` plans and **executes** in checkout mode using
    `parent.GitBranch()`, matching external; the pre-fix failure is covered by a regression test.
26a. **Decoupled parent with cross-repo metadata.** With a parent entry carrying both a decoupled
    `branch:` and a `repo:` different from the child's, checkout plans and executes the same
    `parent.GitBranch()` base — proving `StackEntry.Repo` is still not consulted and that no
    `sameStackRepo` conjunct was introduced. The shipped scoped local-only arm's argv over the same
    stack is byte-identical to the pre-change behaviour, asserted through the argv sidecar, and the
    external control keeps its `sameStackRepo` behaviour (base falls through to `resolveBase`),
    which the two documents publish as the mirrored D7 divergence.
26b. **D1-b, the declared silent change.** With a decoupled parent (`pr1` → `feat/pr1`) **and** a
    real, divergent Git branch literally named `pr1`, the shipped binary rebases the child onto
    `pr1` while v1 rebases it onto `feat/pr1`; the test asserts both destinations explicitly, that
    the plan document publishes the v1 destination (plan and executor agree), and that the
    `CHANGELOG.md` entry names this cell (§20). No `sync_noflag` golden changes.
27. A guarded external run passes `--onto <full-sha>`; the plan-only and unguarded twins of the same
    run pass `--onto <ref-name>`; the no-flag goldens are unmoved.
27a. A plan/guard route's per-context configuration budget is exactly one
    `config --list --show-scope -z` plus **at most two** `--type=bool --get` reads
    (`rebase.updateRefs`, `rebase.autoStash`); the argv sidecar shows **no** typed read of
    `rebase.rebaseMerges`, and a context configured with `rebase.rebaseMerges = rebase-cousins`
    (and one with `no-rebase-cousins`) is published as `status: valid`, `interpretation: true`,
    with **no** `config_issues[]` row and no rank 5.07 blocker. The push facts add **no** config
    read of their own — the `remote.origin.fetch` decomposition comes out of that same ordered
    inventory, and a failure of that read is published as `MappingReadOK: false` with the rank 5.9
    `probe-failed` blocker of §14.1a rule 5a rather than as a lease — and exactly **one** remote-tracking ref inventory read per distinct push context of an **applicable** `PlanPushFacts`,
    issued by `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` after the route's fetch (§14.1a rule 7) and by nothing
    else, with **zero** such reads where the facts do not apply; a second ref-inventory read, or one recorded before the fetch, fails this criterion.
27b. **The `config --show-scope` capability is gated at 2.26 and refuses below it (§16).** With a
    stubbed `git --version` reporting `2.25.1`, both plan-only and guarded routes exit with a
    document-level rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker (`entry: null`, `runnable: false`) whose detail
    names the capability and the observed version — the plan at exit `0` inside the document, the
    guarded run at exit `1` with one marker line — and the argv sidecar shows **no**
    `config --list --show-scope` process was attempted. The unguarded control over the same stub
    runs to completion with its shipped argv, output and exit code, proving no project-wide minimum
    Git was introduced. The gate is asserted **independently** of the 2.26 merge-backend gate: a
    stub at `2.26.0` satisfies both, and the two capabilities are separate fields whose
    consequences differ (refuse vs. model the apply-backend arm).
27c. **`merge-recreation` and config-enabled collateral require the effective merge backend, and
    configuration never forces it (§4.2, §5, §11.7, §11.8).** In a context with
    `rebase.rebaseMerges = true` **and** an effective merge backend (`rebase.backend` unset on a
    host Git ≥ 2.26, or explicitly `merge`) the row publishes
    `effective_backend: merge`, `replay.determinacy: unknown`, `replay.reason: merge-recreation`,
    `candidate_count: null`, and rank 10 `indeterminate-entry` under an effective limit. In a
    context whose resolved backend is `apply` with no merge-forcing input, a range containing merges
    keeps its ordinary determinacy and a `candidate_count` asserted equal to the number of commits a
    **real** `git rebase` applies-or-drops as an upper bound — merges dropped — with **no**
    `merge-recreation` reason and no rank 10 row. Three cells assert the **withdrawn** config-forcing
    rule directly, each against a real `git rebase`: `rebase.backend = apply` with
    `rebase.rebaseMerges = true`, `rebase.backend = apply` with `rebase.updateRefs = true`, and both
    together — every one publishes `effective_backend: apply` (never `merge`), no
    `merge-recreation`, `collateral_mechanism: none` and a **known empty** `collateral_refs: []`,
    and the real rebase recreates no merge and moves no extra ref. With `rebase.updateRefs = true`
    and an argv that
    omits `--update-refs`: under `effective_backend: merge` the row publishes
    `collateral_mechanism: config`, a non-empty collateral upper bound and the
    `collateral-update-refs-config` warning, and a real `git rebase` really moves the listed ref;
    under `effective_backend: apply` it publishes `collateral_mechanism: none`,
    `collateral_refs: []`, **no** warning, and the real rebase really moves nothing. Where the
    config inventory could not be read, or the 2.26 default-backend capability is unknown, and the
    published argv forces neither, `effective_backend` is `null`, a true
    `rebase_merges.interpretation` yields rank 2f `probe-failed` rather than an assumed arm, and a
    true `rebase.updateRefs` yields `null` collateral facts with
    `summary.entries_with_unknown_collateral` incremented — never `none`, `[]` or `false`. A source
    assertion shows **`--keep-base` appears in no merge-forcing list**, and an argv-classification
    table drives §11.7's seven rows in order, including a `--update-refs` argv over an
    `apply`-configured context (row 1 wins ⇒ `merge`).

**State and timing**

28. A fresh **guarded** new-mode refusal **at or above the guard seam** leaves **no**
    `.sync-state.v2.yaml`, **no** `.sync-run.lock` and **no** legacy sentinel: `setupSyncRunState`
    was never reached (§12.2b). The criterion asserts the absence of **state**, not the absence of
    a fetch: on a fetch-policy route the invocation's single `git fetch` has already run above the
    seam, and the test asserts it ran exactly once rather than pretending it did not. The
    state-ordering half is asserted with it: on a guarded new-mode
    run that *is* admitted, the persisted `Stage` sequence is `initializing` → `rebasing`, with
    `fetching` never written, while the unguarded control over the same fixture writes
    `initializing` → `fetching` → `rebasing`; both runs produce byte-identical stdout; the guarded
    run's `git fetch` precedes its `.sync-run.lock` creation in the recorded process/filesystem
    order; and the guarded run issues **exactly one** `git fetch` for the whole invocation.
28a. **Post-claim revalidation cleanup (§12.2c).** A guarded fresh run — new-mode and legacy —
    whose post-claim revalidation refuses **before any rebase** exits `1`, moves no ref, writes one
    marker line with **no** `state-preserved: ` prefix and no `--continue` suggestion, and leaves
    **no** payload, sentinel or run guard behind (`stateFilesGone`), with any pre-existing
    artefacts untouched. Over the **five** failure cells of §12.2c rule 4a — an injected
    `SyncStageFinalizing` failure at index 0 and at index 1, and a **real** removal failure at each
    of `RemoveSyncRunState`, `RemoveSyncState` and `RemoveSyncRunGuard`, forced through the §23.1
    injected-reader seam where permissions cannot — the invocation instead exits `1` with the
    cleanup failure wrapping the guard refusal, writes a marker that **does** begin
    `state-preserved: `, names the **measured** residue (`{payload, sentinel, guard}` /
    `{sentinel, guard}` / `{guard}`, in that fixed member order) plus the `tws sync <f> --abort`
    recovery, and leaves precisely that residue on disk. A companion assertion proves the removers
    are real: `RemoveSyncRunState`/`RemoveSyncState`/`RemoveSyncRunGuard` return `nil` for an absent
    path, `nil` after removing a present one, and a non-`nil` error for an undeletable one, while
    their shipped `Delete*`/`Release*` wrappers behave identically to their pre-change bodies in all
    three cells. A crash injected immediately before the first revalidation probe leaves
    the run at `initializing`, resumable by `--continue` and clearable by `--abort`.

    **Rule L — every residue this criterion produces carries a *live* guard, and that fact is part
    of the fixture (binding, and inherited by every criterion that recovers a residue).** The five
    failure cells are reached by **returning** an error through the §23.1 injected seam, so they run
    **in the harness process**, and the `.sync-run.lock` inside each measured residue records that
    process's own PID — which is alive by construction while the test is still running. Under the
    shipped ladders that is not a stale guard at all: on cells 2/4/5 `GuardLive` has no self
    conjunct, so the extraction of §12.8b refuses with the live sentence (§25.95), and on cell 1
    §12.8's ladder fails closed on `PID == os.Getpid()` with its own self-PID sentence. Every
    residue-recovery criterion in this specification — §22.28b, §22.28e (i) and §22.24i (ix-a)'s
    named-recovery half — is therefore **split in two**, and neither half may borrow the other's
    expectation:

    | Family | How the residue's guard is made | What `--abort` (and `--continue`) is asserted to do |
    |---|---|---|
    | **live/self** | the residue is used exactly as the in-process failure left it, while the harness process is still running | the **shipped refusal** for that cell and verb, exit `1`, **nothing removed**, the residue byte-identical afterwards (hash-compared) — with the **one declared exception** below |
    | **dead** | either the residue is produced by an **out-of-process** child that has since exited (the process-terminating half of §23.1 seam 8), or the in-process residue's guard is rewritten to a **known-dead** PID by the guard-detaching helper of §23.1 seam 7, leaving every other guard byte unchanged | the success arm: the per-residue, per-route line of the table below at exit `0`, with `stateFilesGone` |

    **The one declared exception is §12.8a's cell-7 arm, and it is exactly one cell.** A `{guard}`
    residue sitting beside a **real** `.sync-state.yaml` is classifier cell 7, where
    `syncCellRefusal` has no live arm at all and the abort calls
    `ReleaseStaleSyncRunGuardWith(…, SyncGuardReleaseOpts{AllowSelfPID: true})`: a **self-recorded**
    guard is therefore *removed* there, at exit `0`, with §12.8a's line — the deliberate divergence
    §12.8a declares and §22.28d asserts beside a cell-1 fixture that still fails closed. A **live
    foreign** guard in that same cell still refuses. Every other cell — 1, 2, 4 and 5 — follows the
    table above without exception.

    **Outside that one cell, no criterion in this specification asserts exit `0`, a cleared residue
    or a successful reclaim
    over a guard that is live or self-recorded**, and none asserts a refusal over a provably dead
    one. A test that produces a residue in-process and then expects `Sync state cleared.` is
    asserting the wrong half of this rule and fails §22.28a and §22.28b together (§25.96). **The
    operator-facing advice is unaffected, and that is the point of the split**: the
    `; recovery state preserved: <residue> — clear it with: tws sync <f> --abort` sentence is read
    by a human whose tws process has already exited, so the guard that sentence's recovery meets is
    dead and the recovery really does clear — the live/self half exists only because a *test* can
    run the recovery while the writing process is still alive, which no operator can.
28b. **`tws sync <f> --abort` recovers every residue, including guard-only cell 1 (§12.8) — over a
    dead guard; over a live or self-recorded one it refuses.** The criterion has two halves, both
    required, over each of the three residue shapes produced by §22.28a and under rule L above.

    **Half 1 — the same-process residue refuses.** Immediately after the in-process failure cell,
    with the harness still running and the guard therefore recording a live self PID, a following
    `tws sync <f> --abort` is asserted to exit `1`, to remove **nothing** and to leave the residue
    byte-identical (hash-compared), with the shipped sentence for that cell:

    | Residue | Cell | Sentence asserted at exit `1` |
    |---|---|---|
    | `{payload, sentinel, guard}` | 5 | the shipped live-guard `--abort` sentence `a scoped sync is running for %q (pid %d); wait for it to exit before --abort`, with `%d` asserted equal to `os.Getpid()` |
    | `{sentinel, guard}` (either route) | 4 | the same sentence, raised by `syncCellLiveGuardRefusal` **above** the §12.8b interception, which is asserted (counter) never to run |
    | `{guard}` | 1 | §12.8's self-PID sentence `sync guard at %s records this process (pid %d); it was not claimed by this invocation — inspect it and remove it manually` |

    The plain and `--continue` verbs over the same three residues are asserted to raise the plain
    twin of the live sentence (cells 4/5) and, over the `{guard}` cell-1 residue, the shipped
    answers that path really produces — `nothing to continue — no sync in progress` for
    `--continue`, and for a **new-mode** plain run (the route that claims) `ClaimSyncRunGuard`'s own
    live refusal `a scoped sync is already running for %q (pid %d, started %s); wait for it or use
    --continue/--abort after it exits` (`internal/sync_run_state.go:194`), while the **legacy** plain
    twin is asserted to behave exactly as it does today, the guard being invisible to it — likewise
    removing nothing in every cell.

    **Half 2 — the dead-guard residue clears.** The same three residues, taken to the **dead**
    family of rule L, are followed by `tws sync <f> --abort`, which exits `0` and leaves **no**
    payload, sentinel or run guard. **The printed line is per residue *and*
    per route, and no blanket literal may be asserted:**

    | Residue | Route that produced it | Classifier cell | Line asserted |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `{payload, sentinel, guard}` | guarded new-mode **and** guarded legacy alike | 5 | the shipped `Sync state cleared.` — a payload is present, so the §12.8b interception (cell 4 only) is never consulted and the shipped cell-5 arm runs |
    | `{sentinel, guard}` | guarded **new-mode** fresh run, whose sentinel is `setupSyncRunState`'s plain shipped `.sync-state.yaml` marker (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:393-401`) — `verdict: not-guarded` | 4 | the shipped `Sync state cleared.`, byte-identical to the pre-feature binary's cell-4 abort |
    | `{sentinel, guard}` | guarded **legacy** fresh run or cell-7 continuation, whose sentinel is the **backup sentinel** of §13.6 rule 2c — `verdict: valid` | 4 | exactly `Sync state cleared; the interrupted guarded setup's backup of the previous sync state was discarded.` (§12.8b, §22.28e (i)) — asserted **not** to be the bare shipped line |
    | `{guard}` | either route | 1 | exactly `Stale sync guard from PID <pid> cleared; no sync state was present.`, with `<pid>` asserted equal to the known-dead PID the fixture recorded and **not** to `os.Getpid()` |

    Both `{sentinel, guard}` rows are asserted **in the same test**, against each other, so a
    collapse into one literal fails this criterion in whichever direction it collapses: asserting
    the bare `Sync state cleared.` for the guarded-legacy residue hides the destruction of a
    recoverable document, and asserting the discard sentence for the new-mode residue claims a
    backup that never existed (§25.92). Where the dead residue is reached by the
    **guard-detaching** helper rather than by an out-of-process child, the rewritten guard is
    additionally asserted to differ from the original in the PID field **only** (token, creation
    timestamp and feature compared field by field), so the fixture is a liveness change and not a
    different document (§23.1 seam 7). The guard-only cell's
    full table is asserted directly: an absent guard keeps the shipped
    `Nothing to abort — no sync in progress.` byte-for-byte at exit `0`; a symlinked guard fails
    closed with the shipped symlink sentence; an unreadable or undecodable guard, a `PID <= 0`
    guard and a self-PID guard each fail closed at exit `1` with their §12.8 sentence and leave the
    file in place; a **live foreign** guard refuses with the shipped
    `a scoped sync is running for %q (pid %d); wait for it to exit before --abort`, byte-equal to
    the cell 2/4/5 abort refusal; and a guard whose bytes change between the read and the
    compare-and-swap refuses with the §12.8 sentence and removes nothing. Every other cell's
    `--abort` output is asserted unchanged, and the `sync_noflag` goldens are unmoved.
28c. **The header divergence is exactly one cell (§12.2b, §17.2).** On a guarded new-mode external
    fresh run, four cells are asserted beside their unguarded controls: (i) **success** — guarded
    and unguarded stdout are **byte-identical**, both printing the `Sync mode:` header before the
    fetch prose; (ii) **claim/setup failure** — with `setupSyncRunState` forced to fail (injected
    `ClaimSyncRunGuard`/sentinel/payload-write failure through the §23.1 seam), the guarded run has
    **already printed** the header and the unguarded twin has **not**, and the test asserts exactly
    that difference and no other stdout difference; (iii) **post-claim revalidation refusal**
    (§12.2c) — the guarded run prints the header and so does the unguarded twin, because its claim
    succeeded, so the two transcripts agree up to the refusal: **no** header divergence is
    asserted, and a test claiming one fails this criterion; (iv) **JIT/rebase failure below the
    claim** — same, no divergence. The legacy route is asserted to print **no** header in any of
    the four cells, and `--plan` is asserted to put the header on **stderr** in all of them
    (§3.6), which is the only other place it moves.
28d. **`tws sync <f> --abort` also clears the legacy-state-plus-guard residue (§12.8a).** Over
    **three** fixtures for the same classifier cell, none hand-built: (α) the shipped-reachable one
    — a real `.sync-state.yaml` beside a `.sync-run.lock`, produced by
    killing a scoped setup at `syncStepHook(SyncStageInitializing, 0)` to leave a guard-only cell 1
    and then running an **unguarded legacy** `tws sync <f>` that fails into `.sync-state.yaml`;
    (β) §13.2a's **crash window 1** on the cell-7 continuation arm, produced by terminating a
    guarded legacy setup at `syncStepHook(SyncStageInitializing, 0)`, where the operator's real
    `.sync-state.yaml` is asserted byte-identical to the pre-run file; and (γ) that arm's `{guard}`
    **rollback residue**, produced by forcing `RemoveSyncRunGuard` to fail after a successful
    conditional restore, where the same file is asserted restored by hash. In all three,
    all eight `Reason` rows are asserted — each row's guard state produced deterministically, the
    dead-foreign and reused-PID rows through §23.1 seam 7's owned-PID and guard-detaching helpers
    (PID field rewritten, every other byte unchanged, §22.28a rule L), so no row depends on the
    accident of which process happened to write the fixture:
    a **dead foreign** guard is removed and the command exits `0` printing exactly
    `Sync state cleared; stale sync guard from PID <pid> cleared.`, with `.sync-state.yaml` gone,
    the guard gone and any in-progress rebase of the recorded `FailedBranch` aborted exactly as the
    shipped arm aborts it; a **self-PID** guard is removed the same way and prints the same line —
    the one declared divergence from §12.8's cell-1 table, asserted **beside** a cell-1 fixture
    that still fails closed on self-PID in the same test, so the divergence is pinned rather than
    drifted; an **absent** guard leaves the shipped cell-7 abort byte-, exit- and process-identical
    to the pre-feature control (`Sync state cleared.`, no extra line); and a **live foreign**,
    **symlinked**, **unreadable/undecodable**, **`PID <= 0`** or **changed-under-CAS** guard each
    exits `1` with the §12.8/§12.8a sentence for that row while leaving **both**
    `.sync-state.yaml` and the guard byte-identical (hash-compared), aborting no rebase and
    removing nothing. Fixtures (β) and (γ) are additionally asserted to be **resumable rather than
    only clearable**: an armed `tws sync <f> --continue` over either one resumes the untouched
    legacy subject through the cell-7 arm, reclaiming or re-claiming nothing it does not own, which
    is what makes window 1 a genuinely lossless window. Two further cells complete it: the arm is asserted to run its inspection
    **before** any removal (a barrier test flips the guard to live between the classifier and the
    inspection and observes the refusal, not a partial clear), and a failure of the legacy removal
    after a successful guard release is asserted to leave plain cell 7, recovered by re-running
    `tws sync <f> --abort`; the vanished-state race is
    asserted too (the legacy file removed between classification and the abort work prints §12.8's
    guard-only sentence at exit `0`, never a false `Sync state cleared`). Every other cell's
    `--abort` output and the `sync_noflag` goldens are
    asserted unchanged, and the composed sentences are asserted to carry **no** `plan-guard: `
    marker.
28e. **Cell 4 over a valid backup sentinel: `--continue` resumes, `--abort` discards and says so,
    a plain run names both verbs (§12.8b).** Over the §13.2a window-2 fixture —
    produced by **terminating** a guarded legacy setup at `syncStepHook(SyncStageInitializing, 1)`,
    never by hand-building files, so its guard records a **dead** child PID — and over the
    `{sentinel, guard}` rollback residue of §22.24i
    (ix-a), which is the same on-disk shape reached by a returned error rather than a crash and is
    therefore taken to the **dead** family of §22.28a rule L first (its in-process guard rewritten
    to a known-dead PID by the §23.1 seam-7 helper, every other byte unchanged); the **live/self**
    half of that rule is asserted for both fixtures too, as the (i-a) cell below:
    (i) **`--abort`** clears the sentinel and any guard, in the shipped order, and prints exactly
    `Sync state cleared; the interrupted guarded setup's backup of the previous sync state was
    discarded.` at exit `0` — asserted byte-exactly, asserted **not** to be the bare shipped
    `Sync state cleared.`, and asserted not to be §12.8's or §12.8a's line. Afterwards

    (i-a) **the same residue with a live or self-recorded guard refuses instead, for all three

    (ii) **plain `tws sync <f>`** exits `1` with exactly
    `a guarded sync was interrupted while recording state for %q; the previous sync state is
    preserved inside %s — use --continue to resume it, or --abort to discard it`, removes nothing,
    writes nothing and moves no ref, with `.sync-state.yaml` byte-identical afterwards;
    (iii) **`--continue`** takes the recovery arm and is asserted by §22.24j (iii)–(iv);
    (iv) **the shipped answers are preserved where they must be** — a **plain** sentinel in the
    same cell keeps the shipped refusal for plain/`--continue` and the shipped `Sync state
    cleared.` for `--abort`, byte-, exit- and process-identical to the pre-feature control; a
    **live foreign** guard beside any of these refuses first with the shipped
    `a scoped sync is running for %q (pid %d); wait for it to exit before --abort` (or its plain
    twin), removing nothing, proving the interception sits below `syncCellLiveGuardRefusal`; and a
    payload appearing under the arm still produces the shipped `scoped sync state appeared at %s
    while aborting; re-run: tws sync %s --abort`;
    (v) **every unverifiable sentinel fails closed for every verb, and names no verb** — the
    `symlink`, `unreadable`,
    `unsupported-version`, `corrupt`, `foreign` and `hash-mismatch` fixtures of §22.24j (ii) are
    each driven through plain, `--continue` and `--abort` and asserted to exit `1` with rule 2c's
    sentence for that verdict, to remove nothing, to write nothing, to leave `.sync-state.yaml` and
    the guard byte-identical (hash-compared) and to carry **no** `plan-guard: ` marker. Each
    verdict's sentence is additionally asserted **byte-identical across the three verbs** and
    asserted to contain neither the substring `--abort` nor `--continue`: `corrupt` is byte-equal to
    `guarded sync setup state at %s is incomplete or invalid; inspect it and remove it manually —
    tws will not guess` and `hash-mismatch` to `guarded sync setup state at %s no longer matches the
    sync state it backed up; inspect it and remove it manually — tws will not guess`. A sentence
    directing the operator to a verb that itself refuses over the same document fails this
    criterion;
    (vi) **the extraction is pure, and it is verb-aware** — a source assertion shows
    `syncCellRefusal`'s first statement
    is `syncCellLiveGuardRefusal(feature, st, verb)`, forwarding the verb it was itself given, and
    that its own bytes, arms and sentences are
    otherwise unchanged, with a table test asserting `syncCellRefusal` returns exactly the shipped
    error for every one of the twelve cells × three verbs. The extraction is additionally asserted
    **directly**, as a unit, over cells 2/4/5 × the three `syncVerb` values × the guard ladder:
    with a **live foreign** guard it returns the shipped `--abort` sentence
    (`a scoped sync is running for %q (pid %d); wait for it to exit before --abort`) for
    `syncVerbAbort` and the shipped **plain twin** for `syncVerbPlain` **and** `syncVerbContinue`,
    each byte-compared against the pre-feature binary's output for the same fixture and verb — the
    two sentences asserted **distinct** from each other, so a collapse into one spelling fails —
    and, over a guard recording **this process's own PID**, it returns those **same** two sentences
    by the same verb split, never `nil`, because the shipped `GuardLive` has no self conjunct
    (`internal/sync_run_state.go:415`) and a pure extraction may not add one; an assertion that the
    extraction returns `nil` for a self-recorded guard fails this criterion (§25.95). It returns
    `nil` for every verb only over an **absent**, **dead**, `PID <= 0`, **unreadable** or
    **symlinked** guard — and over a live guard whose token disagrees with a present payload's
    `OwnerToken`, which the classifier itself downgrades to `GuardLive: false` — leaving those cells
    to `syncCellRefusal`. A companion assertion pins the deliberate divergence in the same test: for
    the self-PID fixture the controlled snapshot's `ExternalPlanState.LiveForeignOwner()` is
    asserted **`false`** (and `Files.RunGuard.Self` `true`, `Alive` `false`), and the `--plan` twin
    is asserted to publish **no** `live-owner-concurrency` token while the executing twin still

    against each other rather than conflated. An end-to-end cell-4 fixture with a live
    foreign guard is driven through all three verbs and asserted to emit the verb's own shipped
    sentence at exit `1`, removing nothing, proving the interception below never sees the document,
    and its **self-PID** twin is asserted to do exactly the same (§12.8b);
    (vii) **the interception owns this document's flag validation, and its sentences are the shipped
    ones** — over the same window-2 fixture: `--continue --only x` (and each of the other five
    mode-trigger flags in turn, and each of the three verbs) is asserted to exit `1` with the

    without them or abort and start a new run` **byte-compared against the shipped gate's own
    output** on a cell-7 fixture, to remove nothing, to write nothing and to carry no
    `plan-guard: ` marker; `--abort --only x` is asserted to refuse the same way and to leave the

    `--continue` and a `--continue --max-replay-total N` whose `N` **equals** the sentinel's

    persisted-payload` on the matching `--plan --continue` document; a `--continue
    --max-replay-total M` with `M` **different** is asserted to refuse at the guard seam with rank 7
