    (viii) **the vanished sentinel is answered as absence, exactly once, over the state the second
    read really finds, and never as a backup verdict (§12.8b's vanished-state row, §13.6 rule 2c
    binding 3a).** With the §23.1 barrier placed
    between `classifySyncState` and the interception, `.sync-state.yaml` is really removed inside
    that window — by a second process, so the removal is a filesystem event and not an injected
    verdict — and all three verbs are driven over the window-2 fixture. The residue that removal
    leaves is `{guard}`, i.e. classifier **cell 1 with a run guard**, so the criterion is asserted
    over **three** guard fixtures and no blanket literal is admitted:

    | Guard surviving the window | `--abort` | plain `tws sync <f>` | `--continue` |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **dead** (the window-2 fixture's own terminated child PID, or a seam-7 detached one) | §12.8's release arm: exit `0`, exactly `Stale sync guard from PID <pid> cleared; no sync state was present.`, the guard gone afterwards and `<pid>` asserted **not** to be `os.Getpid()` | the ordinary fresh run: a claiming route takes the dead guard over through its compare-and-swap and proceeds; the unguarded legacy twin behaves exactly as today | exit `1`, exactly `nothing to continue — no sync in progress` |
    | **live foreign** (an owned sleeping PID, §23.1 seam 7) | exit `1`, exactly `a scoped sync is running for %q (pid %d); wait for it to exit before --abort`, nothing removed, the guard byte-identical | the claiming route refuses with `ClaimSyncRunGuard`'s shipped `a scoped sync is already running for %q (pid %d, started %s); wait for it or use --continue/--abort after it exits` at exit `1`, having written nothing | exit `1`, exactly `nothing to continue — no sync in progress` |
    | **self-recorded** (the harness's own PID, §22.28a rule L) | exit `1`, §12.8's self-PID sentence `sync guard at %s records this process (pid %d); it was not claimed by this invocation — inspect it and remove it manually`, nothing removed | the claiming route refuses with the same live claim sentence, `%d` asserted equal to `os.Getpid()` | exit `1`, exactly `nothing to continue — no sync in progress` |

    A **fourth** fixture removes the guard **and** the sentinel in the same window: only there are
    the ordinary absent-state answers asserted — a plain run byte-identical in stdout to the same
    invocation over an empty feature, `--continue` at exit `1` with `nothing to continue — no sync
    in progress`, and `--abort` at exit `0` with exactly the shipped
    `Nothing to abort — no sync in progress.`, removing nothing. A test that asserts those three
    answers over a residue whose guard survived fails this criterion, in whichever direction it
    collapses. None of the cells emits §12.8b's discard line, §12.8b's plain refusal, or any rule 2c
    fail-closed
    sentence, and none carries a `plan-guard: ` marker — an implementation that answers the vanished
    path with a `valid`, `corrupt` or `not-guarded` verdict fails this criterion. Counters assert
    the invocation performed **exactly one** re-classification and **exactly one**
    `InspectGuardedLegacySentinel` call, with **no** second inspection and **no** retry loop, and a
    fixture that removes and re-creates the file repeatedly inside the window is asserted to
    terminate with one of the ordinary answers rather than to spin. Three companion cells complete

    shipped cell-5 answer for the verb (the second classification wins, whatever it says); the same
    window with a non-`ErrNotExist` **I/O failure** injected at the interception's read (§23.1 seam
    4) is asserted to fail closed with rule 2c's `unreadable` sentence at exit `1`, removing
    nothing, proving absence and unreadability are not merged; and a `--plan` twin of the removal
    cell is asserted to publish a document at exit `0` carrying **no** `state-refused` blocker that
    names a backup sentinel, having written nothing — with its **live foreign** guard variant

    shipped `live-owner-concurrency` machinery of §12.5 rule 4 rather than any sentinel gate.
29. A continuation refusal leaves the payload, the legacy state file and the checkout transaction
    byte-identical (hash-compared before and after) — and, on the external guarded arms, the

30. A live foreign owner suppresses the plan fetch (`freshness: not-refreshed-live-run`) and refuses
    guarded execution with `guard.execute_blocked_by: ["live-owner-concurrency"]` before any fetch,
    checkout or rebase; killing the helper PID releases both.
31. Every native `ClaimSyncRunGuard`, `AcquireCheckoutLock`, `forceAcquireCheckoutLock` and
    `ReclaimSyncRunGuard` refusal is byte-identical to the shipped sentence and carries **no**

**Capability**

32. On a host Git ≥ 2.44 all **six** gates are satisfied and the modelled fetch effect matches a
    real `git fetch`; with a stubbed `git --version` below each gate the modelled effect changes to
    the older behaviour (or, for the two **refusing** gates — `config --show-scope` and
    `--update-refs` — refuses per §22.27b and §22.32b); with an
    unparseable version the plan/guard path refuses with a
    document-level rank 5.9 `probe-failed` while the unguarded run is untouched.
32a. **The version probe has two producers, one position and one skip rule (§16 rules 1a–1b).**
    The argv sidecar is asserted over every controlled route in both modes:
    (i) **exactly one** `git --version` process per controlled invocation that establishes a
    subject — plan-only, guarded fresh and guarded continuation alike — and a source assertion
    shows the only callers of `ProbeGitVersion` are `InspectCheckoutPlan` and
    `InspectExternalPlan`, with **no** call inside `BuildRebasePlan`, either checkout builder, the
    probe layer or any executing route;
    (ii) the recorded process order places that probe **after** the invocation's `stack.yaml` read
    (or, on a continuation, its transaction/payload read) and **before** the first
    `git config --list --show-scope`, the first fetch-effect probe and the first `git fetch`;
    (iii) **zero** `git --version` processes on every rows-less no-subject document — unreadable
    stack, cyclic stack, refused selection, absent/undecodable continuation state, and each gate
    that refuses above the subject reads — each of which is additionally asserted to publish **no**
    rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker for the skipped probe and no capability-dependent field
    (`fetch.repos: []`, unpopulated `repositories[].config.*`);
    (iv) a stubbed unparseable version on a document that **does** have a subject publishes the
    rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker with `entry: null`, `runnable: false`, non-waivable;
    (v) the unguarded control records **zero** `git --version` processes on every route (§17.1).
32b. **The `--update-refs` gate refuses only where the argv needs it, and only above the fetch
    (§16 rule 3b).** With `git --version` stubbed at `2.37.0` (and at `2.38.0` for the passing
    twin), driven through production `Execute()` in both modes:
    (i) **it refuses where the argv carries the option** — an external `scope=all` run over a stack
    whose selected entries are **materialized** (`tws sync <f> --plan` and its guarded
    `--max-replay-total N` twin, on the fresh arm and on a
    `--continue`) publishes a document-level (`entry: null`) rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker whose
    sanitized detail names the capability and the observed version, with `runnable: false` and the
    refusal asserted **non-waivable** by presenting a matching approval token; the plan exits `0`
    with the document, the guarded twin exits `1` with one anchored `^plan-guard: probe-failed: `
    line;
    (i-a) **scope alone does not gate: an all-scope run with no `--update-refs` argv is not
    refused** — an external `scope=all` fixture on the same 2.37 stub whose executed rows are **all
    non-materialized** (each publishing the pass-2 `["rebase", <base.ref>, <git_branch>]` argv of
    §9.3, plus `skipped-updated-ref`/`skipped-archived` rows with `argv: []`) is asserted to publish
    **no** `probe-failed` blocker for this capability, to fetch where its route fetches, to be
    `runnable: true`, and — in its guarded twin — to **execute to completion**, issuing real
    `git rebase` commands none of which carries `--update-refs` (argv sidecar). A rows-less
    push-only `--continue` on the same stub is asserted the same way. A gate that fires on either
    fails this criterion, because scope is not the predicate;
    (i-b) **one qualifying row is enough: the mixed fixture refuses as a whole** — a `scope=all`
    fixture with **both** a materialized pass-1 row and a non-materialized pass-2 row on the 2.37
    stub is asserted to refuse exactly as (i) does, document-level (`entry: null`), with
    `runnable: false` and **no** per-row variant of the blocker, proving the gate is a property of
    the invocation rather than of a row;
    (i-c) **the predicate equals the published argv, in both directions** — over the **whole**
    fixture corpus, in both modes and on both routes, a table test asserts the biconditional of §16
    rule 3b: `CapRebaseUpdateRefs` is required **iff** the document that invocation would publish
    contains at least one `entries[].argv` or `argv_alternatives` member whose elements include the
    literal `--update-refs`. The gate's own early, pre-fetch evaluation is asserted to agree with
    that document for every fixture, so the projection can never drift from the argv it projects;
    (ii) **it is raised above the fetch and above every mutation** — the argv sidecar records
    **zero** `git fetch`, `git rebase`, `git checkout`, `git push` and `git config --list
    --show-scope` processes for that invocation, the document publishes `fetch.attempted: false`,
    `fetch.outcome: skipped`, `fetch.repos: []` and `freshness: not-refreshed-no-plan-subject`
    (§11.2 cause 2), and the guarded twin leaves no payload, sentinel, guard, lock or transaction
    behind (`stateFilesGone`) and moves no ref;
    (iii) **no backend or collateral claim survives the refusal** — the same document is asserted to
    publish `effective_backend: null` (§11.7 row 2, the inventory was never read), `null` collateral
    facts with `summary.entries_with_unknown_collateral` incremented, and **no**
    `collateral_mechanism: argv`, no `merge` verdict and no known-empty `collateral_refs: []`;
    (iii-a) **backend and collateral follow the actual argv on an ungated run too** — the (i-a)
    all-pass-2 fixture, run on the passing 2.38 twin and on the host Git, is asserted to publish
    `effective_backend` from §11.7's table **without** a row-1 match (no `merge` verdict derived from
    `--update-refs`) and `collateral_mechanism` ∈ `config` \| `none` — never `argv` — on every one
    of its rows, with the mixed (i-b) fixture asserted to publish `argv` on its materialized pass-1
    row and `config`/`none` on its pass-2 row in the **same** document, each asserted against a real
    `git rebase` (§16 rule 8);
    (iv) **it does not fire where the argv omits the option** — a scoped external run (`--only`,
    `--from`), the all-pass-2 `scope=all` run of (i-a) and **every** checkout run (§11.8) on the
    same 2.37 stub publish **no**
    `probe-failed` blocker for this capability, fetch where their route fetches and complete
    normally, proving the gate is argv-derived and not a version floor;
    (v) **the unguarded control is untouched** — `tws sync <f>` with no control flag on the same
    stub records zero `git --version` processes, passes the shipped `--update-refs` argv and is
    byte-, exit- and process-identical to the pre-feature run; **no** test asserts a minimum
    supported Git;
    (vi) **the passing twin really runs** — at `2.38.0` and on the host Git (skipped with a recorded
    reason below 2.38) the same external `scope=all` fixture publishes no such blocker and its
    guarded twin executes a **real** `git rebase --update-refs`, with §11.7 row 1's `merge` verdict
    and §11.8's `collateral_mechanism: argv` asserted against that real command (§16 rule 8).

**Docs and gates**

33. **The documentation gate is file-appropriate, not one grep.** A single corpus grep for flag
    literals over all eight files is withdrawn: `docs/roadmap.md` and
    `docs/engineering-workflow.md` are planning prose, and forcing flag spellings into them would
    make a roadmap entry a flag-reference surface. Two assertions replace it:

    33-i. **Flag/workflow surfaces** — `README.md`, `docs/cheatsheet.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
    `assets/skills/claude/tesseraworkspaces/SKILL.md`,
    `assets/skills/claude/tesseraworkspaces-orchestrator/SKILL.md` and
    `assets/skills/copilot/tws.prompt.md` each contain the literals `--plan`,
    `--max-replay-per-entry`, `--max-replay-total`, `--approve-plan` and `plan-guard:`:

    ```sh
    for f in README.md docs/cheatsheet.md CHANGELOG.md \
             assets/skills/claude/tesseraworkspaces/SKILL.md \
             assets/skills/claude/tesseraworkspaces-orchestrator/SKILL.md \
             assets/skills/copilot/tws.prompt.md; do
      rg -q -- '--plan' "$f" && rg -q -- '--max-replay-per-entry' "$f" \
        && rg -q -- '--max-replay-total' "$f" && rg -q -- '--approve-plan' "$f" \
        && rg -q -- 'plan-guard:' "$f" || { echo "missing in $f"; exit 1; }
    done
    ```

    Every `--plan`/`--approve-plan` workflow printed in those six files additionally carries an
    effective limit on **both** lines (§8.6), asserted by a workflow-block check rather than a bare
    grep.

    33-i-a. **The `CHANGELOG.md` entry discloses all three no-flag recovery cells, by content.**
    The entry is asserted — by a content check over the Unreleased block, not by a bare flag grep —
    to name **each** of §19.4's third, fourth and fifth no-flag behaviour changes, separately and
    unambiguously:

    | Cell | The entry must disclose |
    |---|---|
    | **cell 1**, guard-only (§12.8) | that `tws sync <f> --abort` now clears a stale `.sync-run.lock` that sits beside no sync state, with its own sentence, where it previously reported nothing to abort |
    | **cell 7**, legacy state + guard (§12.8a) | that the same verb now clears **both** artefacts and says so, quoting `Sync state cleared; stale sync guard from PID <pid> cleared.` |
    | **cell 4**, valid **backup sentinel** (§12.8b) | that the residue of an interrupted **guarded legacy setup** is now recoverable: `--continue` **resumes** it, `--abort` clears it and states that **the backed-up previous sync state was discarded** (quoting that sentence), and a plain run names **both** verbs — plus the downgrade note that an older tws release refuses the same residue or discards the backup silently |

    All three rows are asserted **present**; a check that finds cell 1 and cell 7 but not cell 4
    **fails**, because the cell-4 disclosure is the one an operator needs before an `--abort` throws
    away a recoverable document. The rows are matched semantically (case-insensitive, whitespace-
    and emphasis-normalised, keyed on the quoted sentences and on the verbs named), never against a
    sentence this specification dictates verbatim.

    33-ii. **Planning-prose surfaces** — `docs/roadmap.md` and `docs/engineering-workflow.md`
    are asserted **semantically**, by two predicates a human can restate and a test can evaluate,
    never by a byte match against a sentence this specification dictates:

    1. the feature name `rebase plan guard` appears in a **shipped** position — inside the
       "Shipped foundations" list of `docs/roadmap.md` (and the equivalent shipped paragraph of
       `docs/engineering-workflow.md`), and **not** inside the "P1 … backlog" list or a
       "current target" sentence;
    2. `safe reparent/restack` appears as the **named current target**, in the position
       `rebase plan guard` occupied before this change.

    Both are matched case-insensitively, with surrounding whitespace and Markdown emphasis
    normalised, so ordinary prose edits do not break them. These two files are **not** required to
    contain any flag literal, and a flag-literal grep over them MUST NOT be added.
33a. **The negative check is scoped to the prose/asset corpus plus the exact help output, and it
    is not self-defeating.** No documentation or skill claims `--plan` mutates nothing without
    qualification, and none names a ninth warning kind, a `from` scope value, or
    `selection-hazard` as a warning. The check has exactly **two** halves, and no third:

    **(a) Prose and assets — a corpus grep over `docs/` and `assets/` only.** The two repository-root
    Markdown files are included by name, and the entire pattern set is applied to nothing else:

    ```sh
    rg -n --glob '!**/testdata/**' \
       'without mutating anything|scope=from|nine warning' \
       README.md CHANGELOG.md docs/ assets/
    ```

    returns no match. `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/` and `assets/` are the whole §20 corpus;
    the check scans **no** Go tree — not `internal/`, not `cmd/`, not any `_test.go` file — and no
    testdata directory, and a source-wide or repository-wide spelling of it MUST NOT be added.
    The reason is stated as a rule rather than left implicit: **tests legitimately contain every
    banned literal**, as negative fixtures and as the exact expected-value strings of the help
    snapshot, so a grep that scanned them would forbid the very tests that enforce this criterion —
    a self-defeating check. The earlier unglobbed spelling, which would have matched fixture files
    checked into `docs/`/`assets/` testdata, is **withdrawn**.

    **(b) Help output — an exact assertion, not a grep.** `tws sync --help`, captured through
    production `Execute()` (§22.8a), is asserted to contain the five flag help lines and the `Long`
    **byte for byte**, and to contain **none** of the three banned phrases as a substring of the
    captured output. This is an assertion over one string this feature owns, not a scan of the
    tree, so it stays true regardless of what any fixture contains.
33b. **Schema totality, and the descent is bidirectional.** The `--json` document's top-level key
    set and key order equal the
    twenty-five-key list of §4.1 exactly, and the `fetch` and `push` objects equal the closed field
    tables of §4.4a — every member present, every enum value inside its declared domain, every
    tri-state field able to take all three values across the fixture set. **The key-set assertion
    recurses**, in **both** directions, into `fetch.repos[]` rows (8 members), `push.targets[]`
    rows (**10** members: `repo`, `context_id`, `repo_root`, `materialization`, `git_branch`,
    `remote`, `ref`, `force`, `lease`, `scope`) and each row's nested `lease` object (**5**
    members: `mode`, `expectation`, `expected_ref`, `expected_sha`, `expected_sha_freshness`):
    every declared member is asserted **present** in the emitted object *and* every emitted member
    is asserted **declared**, in the declared order, over at least one fixture per route arm
    (`stack-all`, `selected-rebased`, `transaction-plan`). The `lease.expectation` domain is
    asserted **three-valued and closed** — `sha`, `absent`, `unknown` — with at least one fixture
    per value and with every `unknown` row asserted to co-occur with the rank 5.9 `probe-failed`
    blocker of §14.1a rule 5a; a fourth value fails. A member added to `PlanPushTarget` or
    `PlanLease` without amending §4.4a fails; a member removed from either fails; a renamed JSON
    tag fails; and a reflection assertion pins `PlanPushTarget`'s and `PlanLease`'s exported field
    sets and JSON tags to those same lists, so the Go model and the document cannot diverge.

    **`push.targets[].context_id` is asserted nullable, and the array's order is asserted total
    across that `null` (§4.4a, §4.8, §14.1, §14.1a rule 6).** A reflection assertion pins
    `PlanPushTarget.ContextID` to `*string` — a `string` field, a `,omitempty` tag or a
    `json:"context_id"` that cannot encode `null` fails this criterion — and the same assertion is
    made for `PlanPushContext.ContextID` and `PlanPushRemoteFacts.ContextID`, so no carrier behind
    the row reintroduces the withdrawn `""` spelling (§25.104). A source assertion shows **no**
    comparison of any of the three against `""` and **no** map keyed by `""`. Over a fixture whose
    push context cannot be identified while a second, sibling context can, the emitted array is
    asserted to (a) still contain the unresolved row, (b) publish its `context_id` and `repo_root`
    as `null` with every other member of the ten present and non-`null`, (c) carry the
    `{implicit-remote-tracking, unknown, null, null, possibly-stale}` lease beside the rank 5.9
    `probe-failed` row and the entry row's rank 5.1 `repo-unavailable` row, and (d) place that row
    **first**, ahead of the established-id row, under `(context_id [null first], git_branch
    bytewise)`. A two-`null`-row fixture (two unidentifiable contexts, two branches) asserts those
    rows are ordered among themselves by `git_branch` bytewise and are **not** collapsed into one.
    A document that drops the row, sorts it last, coalesces the two `null` rows or emits
    `context_id: ""` fails this criterion, and so does any text or test calling `context_id`
    REQUIRED. The **eighteen** never-null
    arrays of §4.7 are enumerated by path and asserted present, array-typed and non-`null` in every
    fixture — including `entries[].notes[]` on a row with no notes, which is `[]` — and the declared
    non-members (`replay.commits[]`, `collateral_refs[]`, `summary.collateral_refs`, the
    `fetch_effect`/`submodule_recursion`/`local_branch_destinations` nested arrays, `argv[]`,
    `argv_alternatives`) are asserted `null` in at least one fixture each, so the count cannot be
    satisfied by promoting one of them. An added, removed or reordered key fails, and so does an
    array count of seventeen.

    **The `summary` nullability rules are asserted per plannability class, because two of them
    disagree unless plannability is read first (§4.3, §25.43).** Over one fixture per class:
    a `rows` document with **no** `determinacy: unknown` row publishes
    `total_candidates == total_candidates_lower_bound`, both non-`null`, with
    `entries_with_unknown_candidates: 0`; a `rows` document **with** an unknown row publishes
    `total_candidates: null` and a non-`null` lower bound; an `empty` document publishes
    `total_candidates: 0`, `total_candidates_lower_bound: 0` and
    `entries_with_unknown_candidates: 0`; and an **`unavailable`** document publishes
    `total_candidates: null` and `total_candidates_lower_bound: null` **while also** publishing
    `entries_with_unknown_candidates: 0`. A test — or an implementation — deriving
    `total_candidates` from the unknown count alone therefore fails on the last row, which is
    exactly the contradiction this criterion exists to catch.
33c. **Closed token domains (§7.5).** Every token emitted in `push.blocked_by[]` parses into
    `PushBlockedKind` and every token in `restore.blocked_by[]` into `RestoreBlockedKind`; the
    declared domains are exactly `RefusalKinds` plus one and plus three members respectively
    (`len(RefusalKinds) == 30`, `len(pushDomain) == 31`, `len(restoreDomain) == 33`);
    `push-dropped-restoring` is absent from the restore domain and each of the three
    `restore-*` tokens is absent from the push domain; and `RefusalKinds` equals the §7.1 table in
    rank order. Fixtures exercise a `RefusalKind`-derived member on each surface, the
    `restoring`-stage document **whose persisted `intent.push` is `true`** carrying
    `push-dropped-restoring` with `restore.blocked_by: []`, and its `intent.push: false`
    `restoring` twin, whose `push.blocked_by[]` and `restore.blocked_by[]` are both `[]` and which
    carries the token nowhere (§13.3).
33d. **The controlled-path token domain is its own closed type (§4.6, §7.5).**
    `len(ControlledPathBlockers) == 5`, its members equal the §4.6 list in sorted order, every
    token an emitted `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` carries parses back into `ControlledPathBlocker`,
    and the array is asserted sorted, de-duplicated and `[]`-never-`null`, including on a rows-less
    document. `invalid-git-config` and `identity-not-utf8` are asserted **absent** from
    `ControlledPathBlockers` and **present** in `RefusalKinds`, with a fixture showing each
    published as an ordinary `blockers[]` row with `runnable: false` and an empty
    `guard.execute_blocked_by[]`. A compile-level assertion shows `ControlledPathBlocker` is a
    distinct type from `RefusalKind`, `PushBlockedKind` and `RestoreBlockedKind`, and that no
    conversion function produces it. Each of the five members has a fixture reaching it in at least
    one mode. All three fetch-effect members are asserted reachable in **external** mode; in
    checkout mode the two submodule/local-branch members are, while `fetch-context-indeterminate`
    is asserted **unreachable** there, since a single candidate always fetches (§11.1, §11.4,
    §22.13g).
33e. **The `restore` object is total (§14.4).** The `--json` document's `restore` object has exactly
    the ten members of §14.4, in that order, with every enum value inside its declared domain.
    **Every field has its own asserted cells, including its `null` cells:**

    | Field | Asserted cells |
    |---|---|
    | `applies` | `true` on a fresh checkout run with a non-empty built plan, on every checkout continuation that reaches `restoreOriginal`, **and on a `completed`-stage continuation, whose resume calls `finalizeCleanup` alone** — asserted against the real call, not against the stage name; `false` on a fresh checkout run whose built plan is **empty** and on **every** external document, including one whose `blockers[]` is empty — proving it is never derived from `blocked_by[]` emptiness. A `completed`-stage document publishing `applies: false` fails this criterion, as does any document deriving `applies` from "the route calls `restoreOriginal` **and** `finalizeCleanup`" rather than from the declared disjunction (§14.4) |
    | `will_switch_head` | `true` where `target_branch` differs from the branch HEAD is on **immediately before `restoreOriginal`** — asserted by sampling HEAD at that exact point through the `StageRestoring` step hook, **not** from the post-run HEAD, with a companion cell where the run's last rebased row leaves HEAD on a *different* branch than the post-run HEAD would suggest, which a post-run comparison would get wrong; `false` where it provably does not; **`null`** on an `applies: true` document whose HEAD probe was forced to fail, which is asserted to carry the accompanying rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker; `false` on every `applies: false` document; and **`false`** on the `completed`-stage document, which is asserted to issue **zero** `git checkout` processes on its resume |
    | `target_branch` | the logical branch name on all three `applies: true` sources — fresh, restore-reaching continuation and `completed` stage, the last asserted to publish the transaction's recorded `OriginalBranch` rather than `null`; **`null`** where `applies` is `false` **and** where the target could not be established |
    | `target_sha` | full 40-hex (and, on a SHA-256 fixture, 64-hex) equal to the branch's SHA **at snapshot time** — asserted stable after moving the branch mid-run, proving it is not re-read at a seam; **`null`** on an unresolved target, on the rank 4.5 `restore-target-missing` fixture, and on every `applies: false` document |
    | `target_source` | `transaction` on a continuation fixture — including the `completed`-stage one — `probed-head` on a fresh checkout fixture, **`null`** exactly where `applies` is `false`; a fresh run publishing `transaction` fails this criterion |
    | `executable` | `true`, `false` and **`null`** across the fixture set; the `null` cells are exactly the **three** of §14.4 — `restore.applies: false` (asserted on **every** external document, plan and guarded-twin alike, and on the empty-plan fresh checkout run), `summary.plannability: unavailable`, and an `applies: true` document whose target probe failed — each asserted to carry `blocked_by: []` legitimately (§4.7 declared exception). The **`completed`**-stage document is asserted `true` where the finalize preconditions hold and `false` where a projected gate (a foreign live `.checkout-sync.lock` through §13.7 gate j) stops it, in both cells with **no** restore-target token in `blocked_by[]`. A document publishing `executable: false` beside `applies: false` fails this criterion, as does one deriving the value from `blockers[]` |
    | `blocked_by[]` | non-`null` everywhere, token-sorted, de-duplicated, drawn only from `RestoreBlockedKind`, with a fixture for each of `restore-target-missing`, `restore-target-held` and `restore-head-moved` plus one `RefusalKind`-derived member; `[]` on an executable restore, on `applies: false`, and on the unknown cells above; **all three restore-target tokens asserted absent from every `completed`-stage document**, whose route runs no `git checkout`; `push-dropped-restoring` asserted **never** a member |
    | `deletes_transaction` | `true` only on documents whose described run really reaches `finalizeCleanup` (asserted against the real file afterwards on the executing twin) — including the `completed`-stage document, asserted `true` there; `false` on every `applies: false` document and on **every** external document |
    | `releases_lock` | same shape, asserted against the real `.checkout-sync.lock` afterwards, `true` on the `completed`-stage document too; both effect fields are asserted to describe the **success** path only and never a refusal's cleanup (§12.7) |
    | `push_dropped` | `true` **exactly** on the `restoring`-stage fixture whose persisted `intent.push` is `true`, which also emits the `push-dropped-restoring` warning and carries that token in `push.blocked_by[]` while `restore.blocked_by[]` stays `[]`; **`false` on its `intent.push: false` `restoring` twin**, which is asserted in the same test to publish `push.targets: []`, `push.executable: null`, `push.blocked_by: []`, `push.scope: none` and **no** `push-dropped-restoring` warning — a document publishing `executable: false`, the token or `push_dropped: true` on that twin fails this criterion (§13.3, §14.3); and `false` on every other document, including the **`completed`**-stage one, whose `finalizeCleanup` **performs** the pending push (asserted by a real push process on the executing twin) rather than dropping it, and including every external one |

    An added, removed or reordered `restore` key fails this criterion, as does any cell whose
    value falls outside the §14.4 domain. A reflection assertion pins the member count at
    **ten** and the schema version at its declared value, so a revision that answered the
    `completed` cell by adding a `will_restore_original` (or any other) member fails it.

    **The three probed cells are asserted on BOTH arms, and `executable` is asserted total there
    (§14.4's probe-scope table).** A **fresh** checkout run with a non-empty built plan is asserted
    to publish `restore.applies: true`, `restore.executable: true`, `restore.blocked_by: []` and —
    by call counters over the producers — to have really **evaluated** all three cells rather than
    skipped them: one `VerifyGitRef` over `refs/heads/<target>`, one lookup of that context's entry
    in the holder index, and one `restore-head-moved` evaluation that resolves to a known `false`
    because no `OriginalHEAD` is persisted. Three fresh-run cells pin the values: (a) with a real
    **foreign detached** worktree mid `rebase-merge` on the fresh run's own original branch, the
    fresh document is asserted to publish `restore-target-held`, `executable: false` and rank 4.5 —
    proving the fresh arm is not exempt; (b) with only the run's **own** checkout holding that
    branch, the same fixture publishes `blocked_by: []` and `executable: true`, proving the `false`
    comes from **self-exclusion** and not from a skipped probe; (c) `restore-head-moved` is asserted
    **absent** from every fresh document's `blocked_by[]` while the §7.4
    `restore-head-collateral-risk` **warning** is asserted present on the collateral-upper-bound
    fixture with `runnable: true`, so the two are never conflated. The matching **continuation**
    fixtures assert all three tokens reachable and blocking, while the **`completed`**-stage fixture
    is asserted to evaluate **none** of the three (call counters show zero `VerifyGitRef` over the
    target, zero holder lookups for the restore question and no `restore-head-moved` evaluation) and
    to publish `applies: true`, `blocked_by: []` and a finalize-derived `executable`. Finally, a
    table test asserts
    `restore.executable` is **total** over every `applies: true` document in the corpus: exactly one
    of `true` (empty `blocked_by[]`, no probe failure), `false` (non-empty `blocked_by[]`) or `null`
    (probe failure, `blocked_by: []`) — with no document leaving it unset and none publishing
    `false` beside an empty `blocked_by[]` or `true` beside a non-empty one.
33f. **The implicit lease is total, its baseline is measured after the fetch, an unread mapping is a
    probe failure, and a negative refspec
    stales it rather than removing it (§14.1a rules 5a, 7–8, §14.2).** Across the
    fixture set every `push.targets[].lease` is asserted against the closed §4.4a object:
    `mode: implicit-remote-tracking` always; `expectation: sha` with a non-`null` `expected_ref`
    and a 40/64-hex `expected_sha` where the first matching **non-negative** refspec maps the
    branch **and** the mapped remote-tracking ref exists; `expectation: absent` with
    `expected_sha: null` where that ref does not exist (with `expected_ref` still naming it) and
    where the mapping **was read** and no positive refspec maps the branch at all (with
    `expected_ref: null`); `expectation: unknown` with both `expected_ref` and `expected_sha`
    `null` **exactly** where `MappingReadOK` is false; and
    `expected_sha_freshness` non-`null` in **every** cell. All three `expectation` values are
    asserted reachable, and a document publishing a fourth fails this criterion.

    **The unread-mapping cell is asserted as a blocker, not as a lease (§14.1a rule 5a).** With the
    push context's ordered config read made to fail (injected read-fail seam) while everything else
    succeeds, the document is asserted to publish, for that context: the target row **still
    emitted**; its lease exactly
    `{implicit-remote-tracking, unknown, null, null, possibly-stale}`; **one** rank 5.9
    `probe-failed` blocker with `entry: null` whose sanitized `detail` names the `context_id` and
    the verbatim probe error; `runnable: false`; `probe-failed` present in `push.blocked_by[]`; and
    the guarded twin of the same invocation refusing before any rebase. Two documents fail this
    criterion outright: one publishing `expectation: absent` for that cell, and one publishing
    `expected_sha_freshness: fresh` on any row whose `MappingReadOK` or `TrackingReadOK` is false.
    A companion fixture with **two** unreadable contexts asserts exactly two blockers, ordered by
    `context_id` and de-duplicated.

    **The freshness axis is asserted against the closed predicate, cell by cell, and the two cells
    that used to be assumed are now the interesting ones:**

    | Fixture | Asserted `expected_sha_freshness` | What it proves |
    |---|---|---|
    | this invocation fetched the push context, the fetch contacted `origin`, the child exited `0` | `fresh` | the ordinary refreshed baseline (`TrackingPhase: post-fetch`, `MappingReadOK`, `TrackingReadOK`, `FetchedThisRun: true`) |
    | **two linked worktrees of one repository**, one selected and fetched, the other only pushed | `fresh` **on both rows** | the join is the canonical `--git-common-dir`, not `context_id`: one fetch really refreshed both siblings' remote-tracking store (§14.1a rule 8 conjunct iv). A test expecting `possibly-stale` for the unfetched sibling fails this criterion |
    | the selected entry's `branch.<name>.remote` is **`upstream`**, so its successful fetch contacted `upstream` and never `origin` | `possibly-stale` | `FetchedThisRun` names the **push** remote (conjunct iii); a fetch that refreshed `refs/remotes/upstream/**` refreshed no lease baseline |
    | a successful `origin` fetch in a **different** repository/common dir of the same run | `possibly-stale` | conjunct iv again, in the opposite direction |
    | `--no-fetch`, any `--continue`, a §11.2 suppression, a refusing pre-fetch gate | `possibly-stale`, with `TrackingPhase: plan-point` | a real, current, unrefreshed baseline |
    | the fetch child **failed** | `possibly-stale` | conjunct i |
    | the tracking inventory could not be read (`TrackingReadOK: false`) | `absent` + `possibly-stale` | §14.1a rule 5: nothing was read, so nothing is fresh |
    | the mapping could not be read (`MappingReadOK: false`), **even after a successful fetch of that context** | `unknown` + `possibly-stale` + rank 5.9 | §14.1a rules 5a and 8: a fetch cannot make an unread mapping fresh |

    **The measurement order and the measurement *quantifier* are asserted, not assumed.** On a
    fetching run whose push facts **apply**, the argv sidecar shows the
    remote-tracking inventory read **after** the `git fetch` child and **before** the first plan
    probe, `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` is counted at **exactly one** call for that invocation with
    **one** baseline read per applicable push context, and a
    fixture whose remote moves the branch between the mapping phase and the fetch publishes the
    **post-fetch** value — a document publishing the pre-fetch value fails this criterion. On an
    invocation whose facts do **not** apply — `intent.push` false, and separately a rows-less
    `plannability: unavailable` document — the same counter asserts **zero**
    `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` calls, **zero** `MeasurePushRemoteFacts` calls and zero
    remote-tracking reads in the sidecar, with `PlanPushFacts.Phase == "not-applicable"` and
    `push.targets: []`. A test asserting "one call per controlled invocation, unconditionally"
    fails this criterion (§14.1a rule 7). A companion assertion pins the consequence for approval:
    the `push.targets[].lease`
    expectation/ref/SHA are fingerprint members (§8.3), so the token minted by a fetching guarded
    run is asserted equal to the token of a `--plan` of the same state taken after the same fetch,
    and **not** equal to one minted from a pre-fetch baseline.

    The **negative-refspec** cell is
    asserted explicitly, and it is the cell an earlier revision got wrong: with a configured
    `^refs/heads/<branch>` (or an equivalent negative entry) covering the pushed branch **beside**
    a covering positive refspec, the row is exactly
    `{expectation: sha, expected_ref: refs/remotes/origin/<branch>, expected_sha: <the tracking
    ref's current value>, expected_sha_freshness: possibly-stale}` — asserted **even immediately
    after a successful fetch of that context**, because no fetch of that configuration can refresh
    an excluded ref. A document publishing `expectation: absent`, `expected_ref: null` or
    `expected_sha_freshness: fresh` for that cell fails this criterion.

    **Three real `git push --force-with-lease` controls pin the semantics to Git's own behaviour**,
    each run against a real remote with the negative refspec configured and the published row
    captured first:

    | Control | Setup | Asserted result |
    |---|---|---|
    | matching | the remote ref is **at** the value the tracking ref (and therefore `expected_sha`) holds | the push **succeeds** — proving the mapping survived the negative refspec and Git really sent a SHA expectation, not a null OID |
    | stale | the remote ref has moved since the tracking ref was last updated | the push is **rejected** as stale info — proving the `possibly-stale` label names a real hazard |
    | missing | the mapped tracking ref is deleted locally, so the baseline is the null OID, while the remote ref exists | the push is **rejected** — proving the `absent` cell is the stricter reading and not an unprotected force |

    A test that asserts the matching control is rejected, or that models the negative refspec as
    removing the mapping, fails this criterion (§25.32).

    **The producers are asserted directly, not only through documents.** `ResolvePushLease` is
    exercised as a pure function over hand-built `PlanPushRemoteFacts`, with one case per row of
    §14.2's five-step table — `MappingReadOK: false` (asserted to short-circuit: `unknown`, both
    refs `null`, `possibly-stale`, and steps 1–4 never consulted), no mapping, mapping with a
    present tracking ref, mapping with an
    absent one, `TrackingReadOK: false`/`TrackingPhase: unread`, `TrackingPhase` `post-fetch` vs
    `plan-point`, `FetchedThisRun` true/false, and a negative entry beside a
    positive one — asserting it issues **no** Git process (argv sidecar empty), never inspects a
    `PlanFetchOutcome`, and reaches every cell of the §14.2 table without a repository.
    `PushContextRefreshed` is exercised the same way over hand-built `PlanFetchOutcome` values,
    with one case per conjunct of §14.1a rule 8 — un-attempted, attempted-and-failed, `Effect: nil`,
    `Contacted: false`, a remotes list without `origin`, a differing common dir, an empty common
    dir, and the all-conjuncts-satisfied row — asserting `false` for each single-conjunct failure
    and `true` only for the last; and `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` is asserted to conjoin it with
    `TrackingPhase == post-fetch`, `MappingReadOK` and `TrackingReadOK`, with one case per failing
    conjunct yielding `FetchedThisRun: false` over the same satisfied `PushContextRefreshed` input.
33g. **`RebasePlanRequest` and `RebasePlan` are exactly the §9.1a declarations, and the stack is
    sorted once (§9.1a rules 1–4).** Five assertions, all compile-, reflection- or counter-level:
    (i) a construction test builds `internal.RebasePlanRequest{…}` naming **every** field
    explicitly — no elided member, no `…` — so adding a field to §9.1a without updating every
    construction site (§12.2b, §12.2d row 6, §12.3 — including
    `handleGuardedScopedSyncContinue` step 8 — §13.7 rule 1, §13.7a step 8) fails to build,
    and a reflection assertion asserts the struct's field set equals the §9.1a list exactly, with
    no extra member. The **types** of the two members round 10 pinned are asserted by reflection
    too: `Gates` is `[]internal.PlanGateResult` and `PushFacts` is `internal.PlanPushFacts`, with
    compile-level assertions that a `[]internal.PlanBlocker` and a
    `map[string]internal.PlanPushRemoteFacts` are **not** assignable to them (§9.1a rule 5,
    §13.5 rule G, §14.1a rule 9), and a source assertion shows `GateBlockers` is called only
    inside `BuildRebasePlan` and `PushTargets` only once in the tree;
    (ii) a reflection assertion over `internal.RebasePlan` asserts its exported fields are the
    **twenty-five** §4.1 keys, in §4.1 order, with the declared JSON tags, and that marshalling it
    produces exactly that key order — the same list §22.33b checks from the document side, so the
    source model and the projection cannot enumerate different key sets, and no second
    `map[string]any` staging value exists anywhere in the tree (source assertion);
    (iii) a `TopoSort` call counter asserts **exactly one** call per invocation on every controlled
    route in both modes — **zero** on a controlled *checkout* `--continue`, and **one** on a
    controlled *external* `--continue`, which really does rebuild its selection and resume order
    from the current stack (§9.1a rule 3) — and asserts `ExecutionOrder`,
    `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder`,
    `buildCheckoutPlanFrom`, `RemainingRebaseEntries`, `PushTargets`, `ResolvePushContext`,
    `DestinationDeferred`,
    `BuildRebasePlan` and both checkout builders call it **never**, and asserts
    `ExecutionOrder`'s signature takes the precomputed `order []internal.StackEntry` — a signature
    taking a bare `Stack`, or a body calling `TopoSort`, fails this criterion. A companion test
    feeds a deliberately permuted `order` and asserts the produced rows follow **it**, proving the
    argument is consumed rather than re-derived, and a second companion asserts
    `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder` emits `sel.Entries` in that same permuted order (§9.2a rule 2);
    (iv) the **unguarded** counts of §9.1a rule 3a are asserted as the control beside every one of
    them — **two** `TopoSort` calls on an unguarded external new-mode fresh run and on its
    continuation, **two** on an unguarded checkout new-mode fresh run, **one** on each unguarded
    legacy route, **zero** on an unguarded checkout continuation — and a test asserting "one sort
    per invocation" for any of those unguarded rows **fails this criterion**, because that would
    claim a behaviour change on a frozen path;
    (v) a source assertion shows the wrapper/body split is real and unexercised in the wrong
    direction: no controlled route calls `ResolveSyncSelection` or `BuildCheckoutPlan`, and no
    unguarded route calls `ResolveSyncSelectionFromOrder` or `buildCheckoutPlanFrom`.
33h. **The push context and the push projection are single-producer, pure and joinable (§14.1a).**
    (i) `ResolvePushContext` is asserted to reproduce the shipped context rule cell by cell:
    external with `entry.Repo` set ⇒ `repo_root == entry.Repo`, `context_source: entry-repo`;
    external with an empty `Repo` ⇒ the materialized worktree path, `worktree`; checkout ⇒
    `layout.RepoRoot`, `workspace-repo-root`. A non-materialized external entry (archived worktree
    missing, and separately a prunable one) is asserted to produce **no** target at all, matching
    the shipped `os.Stat` skip of `pushEntries`/`pushScoped`, while its `entries[]` row still
    publishes the non-`materialized` value.
    (ii) **The join is asserted, not assumed**: for every materialized row in both modes,
    `push.targets[].context_id` equals that row's `entries[].base_context.context_id` — compared
    over the pointed-to values, with `null == null` an admitted match, so the unresolved-context
    fixture of (iii) joins too — and both
    come from the one measured `PlanContextIdentities` table. A document whose push row carries a
    context id absent from `entries[]` fails this criterion **except** on a document that publishes
    no `entries[]` row at all — the rows-less push-only continuation of §14.1a rule 10d — where the
    join is asserted **vacuous** and the ids are instead asserted to come from that same one
    identity table (§14.1a rule 10e).
    (ii-a) **`PlanContextIdentities` is keyed by `context_id`, and every lookup is direct.** A unit
    test over a real two-repository fixture asserts, for every member, `k == v.ContextID`, that
    `v.ContextID` matches `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` and is never `""`, and that a context whose identity the
    probe could not establish is **absent** from the table rather than stored under `""` — driven
    by forcing the identity probe to fail for one of two contexts and asserting the table has
    exactly one member, that the failed context's published `context_id` is `null` with its rank
    5.1 blocker, and that the surviving context's row is unaffected. Two contexts whose identity
    both fail are asserted to leave the table **empty**, never to collide into a single `""` row.
    A source assertion shows every consumer — `EntryContexts`, `ResolvePushContext`,
    `MeasurePushRemoteFacts`, `BuildPlanHolderIndex` and the §10.3 JIT seam — reads the table as
    the direct map index `ids[id]` and that **no** consumer ranges over it comparing a field to
    find a row; a helper that scans the table, or a map keyed by a repo root, a common dir or a
    display path, fails this criterion. `BuildPlanHolderIndex` is additionally asserted over three
    `need` cells: an id present with a measured `CommonDir` (the inventory is measured and shared
    by common dir), an id present with `CommonDir == ""`, and an id **absent** from `ids` — the
    last two each asserted to yield `Available: false` with `Err` set, **no** `worktree list`
    process, and never another repository's inventory.
    (iii) Every emitted target carries a non-empty `materialization` and either a 64-lower-hex
    `context_id` or `null` **with** the rank 5.1 `repo-unavailable` blocker on the matching entry
    row — the target is asserted **still emitted** in that cell (§14.1a rule 6). The `null` cell is
    asserted **total, not partial**: the same row publishes `repo_root: null`, every remaining
    member of the ten non-`null`, the `expectation: unknown` lease and the rank 5.9 `probe-failed`
    row of §14.1a rule 5a **beside** the rank 5.1 row (both present in `blockers[]`, with
    `refusal.kind: repo-unavailable` winning the §7.2 collapse), `runnable: false`, and
    `probe-failed` in `push.blocked_by[]`. `MeasurePushRemoteFacts` is asserted to record **zero**
    reads for that context and `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` **zero** ref reads for it, while the
    sibling established context records its normal one mapping and one baseline read — so an
    unidentifiable context costs no probe and still produces a total row. A document publishing
    `expectation: absent` there, or omitting either blocker, fails this criterion.
    (iv) `PushTargets` is asserted **pure**: called directly with a hand-built `PlanPushRequest`
    whose `Facts` is a hand-built `PlanPushFacts`,
    it issues zero Git processes and touches no filesystem path (argv sidecar and an injected
    read-fail seam), returns `[]PlanPushTarget` (a compile-level assertion shows no `[]PushTarget`
    type exists in the tree), and emits rows sorted `(context_id [null first], git_branch
    bytewise)` — asserted over a hand-built request mixing `nil` and established ids, whose
    expected order is written out row by row. A reflection
    assertion pins `PlanPushRequest` to its §14.1a field set — **thirteen** members, with `Facts
    PlanPushFacts` as the **only** fact carrier — and `PlanPushFacts` to its **six** members and
    `PlanPushRemoteFacts` to its **ten** (`ContextID` — asserted `*string` — `CommonDir`,
    `RemoteName`, `MappingReadOK`,
    `RemoteExists`, `FetchRefspecs`, `TrackingRefs`, `TrackingReadOK`, `TrackingPhase`,
    `FetchedThisRun`) — so the withdrawn loose
    `Materialization`/`Identities`/`Facts` trio cannot reappear (§14.1a rule 9), and
    `BuildRebasePlan` is asserted to pass `req.PushFacts` through **unchanged** (deep equality
    between the value it was given and the value `PushTargets` received, via an injected seam).
    `PlanPushFacts.Remotes` is asserted to carry **no** entry for a nil-id context and never a `""`
    key, and `PlanPushFacts.Contexts` to be ordered nil-first.
    (v) **Order provenance, stated so it is falsifiable.** The document's rows are canonical —
    `(context_id [null first], git_branch bytewise)` — so row order cannot carry provenance; the
    traversal is asserted
    instead at its two observable ends: `PushTargets` is asserted to iterate `req.Selection.Entries`
    on the `selected-rebased` arm (a source assertion shows it performs **no** sort of its own over
    the selection and calls neither `TopoSort` nor a name lookup back into the stack), and the
    emitted **set** is asserted equal to what the executing `pushScoped` really pushes for the same
    run (rebased-and-validated, minus anchors, minus already-pushed persisted rows), over a fixture
    whose `sel.Entries` order was produced by the invocation's one `TopoSort` (§9.2a rule 2).
    (v-a) **The continuation membership is asserted against a real interrupted run (§14.1a
    rule 10).** Over a scoped run interrupted after entry A was rebased and pushed, entry B was
    rebased and **not** pushed, and entry C is still remaining:
    (a) a `--plan --continue` and the guarded resume of the same state both publish push targets
    for exactly `{B, C}` — B is a target although this invocation will not rebase it, C because the
    resume expects to rebase and validate it, A never because it is in `payload.Pushed`;
    (b) the emitted set is asserted **equal** to what the executing `pushScoped` really pushes on
    that resume, captured from the real `git push` argv sidecar, entry for entry;
    (c) a **rows-less push-only** continuation of the same fixture (C removed from the remaining
    set, so `RemainingRebaseEntries` is empty) publishes `entries[]` rows-less with
    `summary.plannability: empty` **and** a non-empty `push.targets[]` carrying B, with
    `PlanPushFacts.Applies: true`, one mapping measurement and one baseline read for B's context,
    `TrackingPhase: plan-point` and a `possibly-stale` lease, zero `git fetch` processes and the
    §22.12b (iii) rank 4 projection where the completion gate refuses. A document publishing
    `push.targets: []` on that cell fails this criterion;
    (d) a fixture whose payload records the failed entry in **both** `completed` and
    `failed_branch` (a push failure) is asserted to keep that entry as a target — the
    `payloadCompleted` conjunct governs gates e2/e3 and the `[~] resolved` line only, never
    membership (§14.1a rule 10b, §22.14b (iv-b));
    (e) a source assertion shows no consumer orders anything by `payload.Completed` or
    `result.Completed`: the traversal is `sel.Entries` and the emitted order is canonical, so the
    map-ordered completed list can reach neither (§4.8, §14.1a rule 10c).
    (vi) The facts the lease needs are asserted to be measured **once per distinct push context**
    and keyed by `context_id`: a fixture with two entries in two
    different `entry.Repo` clones records exactly two config/ref-inventory read sets, and a fixture
    whose two entries share a context records exactly one. A third fixture, whose one context's
    identity could not be established, records **zero** read sets while still emitting its row — the
    per-context quantifier is "at most one, and none where there is no identity to measure for",
    never "one unconditionally" (§14.1a rules 5a, 7, §22.33h (iii)).
    (vii) **The two phases are asserted as phases, with their quantifiers, not as one
    unconditional measurement.** The mapping half is
    recorded **above** the route's fetch and the baseline half **below** it, in the sidecar's
    process order, on all four fetching routes (external plan, external guarded fresh new-mode,
    external guarded legacy fresh, checkout guarded/plan `--fetch`). On every invocation whose
    `PlanPushFacts.Applies` is **true**, `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` is
    counted at exactly **one** call — including on every non-fetching applicable arm
    (`--no-fetch`, all three continuation arms, a suppressed fetch, a refusing-but-rows-available
    gate), where its published
    `TrackingPhase` is `plan-point` — and `insp.PushFacts.Phase` is asserted `pre-fetch` on every
    **applicable** inspection result. On every invocation whose facts do **not** apply
    (`intent.push` false; a rows-less `plannability: unavailable` document) the same counters
    assert **zero** `MeasurePushRemoteFacts` calls, **zero** `RefreshPushTrackingRefs` calls and
    `Phase == "not-applicable"` on the inspection result, the request and the document's empty
    `push.targets`. A route that handed `insp.PushFacts` to the builder instead of the
    refreshed value fails the builder's own `Applies && Phase == "pre-fetch"` assertion
    (§14.1a rule 7). `MeasurePushRemoteFacts` is asserted to read no ref (argv sidecar shows no
    `for-each-ref`/`rev-parse` of a remote-tracking ref before the fetch) and to set
    `MappingReadOK` false — never a bare `RemoteExists: false` — when its config read is made to
    fail (§14.1a rule 5a, §22.33f).
    (viii) **`push.executable` is asserted three-valued, per cell (§14.3, §4.7).** Across the
    fixture set: `null` with `targets: []`, `blocked_by: []` and `scope: none` on **every**
    document whose `intent.push` is false — a fresh run without `--push`, a `--continue` whose
    payload/transaction persisted `push: false`, a checkout run without it, **and a checkout
    `restoring`-stage document whose transaction persisted `push: false`, which additionally
    carries no `push-dropped-restoring` token or warning and `restore.push_dropped: false`** — in
    **both** modes;
    `null` with `blocked_by: []` on a `summary.plannability: unavailable` document, with and
    without `--push`; `true` on a runnable `--plan --push`; and `false` beside a non-empty
    `blocked_by[]` on a document whose projected gate stops the run before the push and on the
    `restoring` stage **whose persisted `intent.push` is `true`** (`push-dropped-restoring`).
    A document publishing `push.executable: false`
    with `intent.push: false` fails this criterion, as does one publishing a non-empty
    `blocked_by[]` in either `null` cell. The reachability answer is additionally asserted **not**
    derived from `blockers[]` (a document with blockers that do not stop the push keeps
    `executable: true`) and **not** derived from `targets[]` emptiness (an `intent.push: true`
    document with no eligible entry keeps `executable: true` with `targets: []`).
    (ix) **One owner per producer, asserted from the source tree (§14.1a rule 1, §19.1).** A source
    assertion shows each of the six names — `ResolvePushContext`, `MeasurePushRemoteFacts`,
    `RefreshPushTrackingRefs`, `PushContextRefreshed`, `ResolvePushLease`, `PushTargets` — declared
    **exactly once** in package `internal`, and that the single declaration site of every one of
    them is `internal/rebase_planner.go`. The same assertion shows `internal/rebase_plan.go`
    declares **no** `func` of §14.1a (it declares `PlanPushContext`, `PlanPushRemoteFacts`,
    `PlanPushFacts`, `PlanPushRequest`, `PlanPushTarget`, `PlanLease`, `PlanRefspec` and
    `PlanContextIdentities`/`PlanContextIdentity` as types, and `SelectPrimaryRefusal` is asserted
    absent from it by the same rule, §7.2 rule 8), and that `internal/rebase_plan_probe.go`
    declares none of the six names while really holding the config/ref read helpers they call
    (asserted by the call-direction check: the probe file is called *by* the planner file and
    declares no §14.1a symbol). A second declaration, a declaration in the document-model file, or
    a producer moved into the probe file fails this criterion.
33i. **`restore-target-held` has one producer, one inventory and one exclusion (§14.4).** In
    checkout mode, over a real repository with real linked worktrees:
    (i) **held blocks** — with the transaction's `OriginalBranch` checked out in a **second, real**
    worktree of the same repository, `tws sync <f> --plan --continue` publishes
    `restore.applies: true`, `restore.executable: false`, `restore.blocked_by` containing exactly
    `restore-target-held` (sorted, de-duplicated, `RestoreBlockedKind`-typed), a **document-level**
    (`entry: null`) rank 4.5 `restore-blocked` blocker, `runnable: false` and exit `0`; the guarded
    `--continue` refuses at its seam with one anchored `^plan-guard: restore-blocked: ` line, exit
    `1`, moving no ref, and the refusal is asserted **non-waivable** by presenting a matching token
    (§22.19);
    (ii) **the run's own checkout never blocks** — the identical fixture **without** the foreign
    worktree, where that branch is checked out only in the run's own checkout, publishes
    `restore.blocked_by: []` and `restore.executable: true`, and the guarded run completes. The
    exclusion is asserted over three spellings of the same directory — the canonical path, a
    symlinked path and the macOS `/private` spelling — each asserted **not** to block, which is the
    same canonicalisation the row-level holder fact uses;
    (iii) **every other holder blocks, including a prunable and a detached one** — a foreign
    worktree that is
    `prunable`, a detached worktree mid `rebase-merge` on that branch, a detached worktree mid
    `rebase-apply` on it, a detached worktree whose `BISECT_START` names it, and another
    feature's worktree are each asserted to produce the token, so a `Prunable` label is asserted
    **not** to exempt a holder and a detached holder is asserted **not** to be invisible;
    (iii-a) **the holder index itself is asserted directly** — `BuildBranchHolderInventory` is
    exercised as a unit over one real repository with real linked worktrees and asserted to key by
    **short** branch name (`feature/x`, never `refs/heads/feature/x`), to return the
    `checked-out` record for an ordinary worktree, to keep the **prunable** record the shipped
    `BuildWorktreeInventory.ByBranch` map omits, to return `rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply` and
    `bisect` records with `Detached: true` for the three detached fixtures (`head-name` files

    id, to include the run's **own** checkout as an ordinary record (self is excluded by the caller,

    three;
    (iv) **an unavailable inventory is a probe failure, not a held claim** — with
    `git worktree list` forced to fail (the §23.1 Git `PATH` wrapper), the document publishes

    document-level rank 5.9 `probe-failed` blocker, and the guarded twin refuses on **that** rank
    rather than on 4.5;
    (v) **one inventory per repository, reused by every consumer, no second probe** — asserted as a
    formula rather than as the constant `1`:
    (v-a) on a controlled **checkout** invocation, whose run has exactly one context, a call counter
    asserts exactly one
    `BuildBranchHolderInventory` call **at the snapshot point** (and, inside it, exactly one
    `BuildWorktreeInventory` call)
    and the argv sidecar records
    exactly one `worktree list --porcelain` process there, with **all** of the
    row-level `branch_checked_out_at` fact, the rank 5.4 question, §11.8's collateral exclusion and
    the restore question reading that one indexed value. A **plan-only** checkout invocation is

    (v-b) on a controlled **external** invocation over a fixture with **three** rows in **two**
    distinct repositories, the sidecar records exactly **two** snapshot-point
    `worktree list --porcelain` processes — one per distinct canonical common dir, not one per row

    (v-c) a fixture whose two rows sit in **two linked worktrees of one repository** (one common

    (v-d) **applicability is the union of the families, not the row count (§14.4 rule 2)** — three

    `worktree list --porcelain` processes and builds an **empty** index; a **rows-less `restoring`

    holder processes — snapshot plus the pre-`restoreOriginal` refresh of (v-e-2) — and at no row

    (v-e) **JIT refresh is per seam and per common dir; switch rows and collateral rows both

    two-repository fixture, each row that switches **and** each row whose published argv contains

    immediately before its rebase and before the checkout that moves HEAD; a test or assertion
    claiming
    pass 2 issues none fails this criterion (§25.99). A `skipped-*` row, an anchor
    no-op and a **scoped** pass-1 row — which neither switches HEAD nor carries `--update-refs` — are
    each
    asserted to issue **none**; a seam asking two holder questions of one
    common dir (the row fact plus the collateral exclusion) is asserted to issue **one** process and

    (v-e-1) **the holder refresh is load-bearing, and the collateral comparison is total** — over a
    guarded external legacy run whose row publishes a non-empty, known
    `collateral_refs`, a **real** linked worktree that checks one of those refs out is created

    `collateral_refs`, and is asserted to refuse the same way. **Four further cells assert the

    `git rebase` process: (1) a listed ref is **moved** by a real `git update-ref` to another commit
    **inside the same candidate range**, so its membership is unchanged and only `sha` differs — a

    narrow "enters the set" spelling would have let through; (4) the row's collateral array moves

    empty map as "not held". A control cell that changes no tuple at all is asserted to proceed and

    **unguarded** twin of every
    cell is asserted to issue **no JIT seam probe of any kind** — zero
    `worktree list --porcelain` processes and no seam-issued `for-each-ref` or `stack.yaml` reload,
    because it has no seam — and to rebase, proving the frozen path is untouched;
    (v-e-1a) **the switch-class refresh is load-bearing too** — over a guarded **external pass-2**

    point and the row's seam, and the run is asserted to refuse at rank 9 `revalidation-mismatch`
    **before** the rebase and before the checkout (zero `git rebase` and zero row-checkout processes

    and refusing the same way; the run's **own** checkout, re-observed across the canonical,

    (v-e-2) **the restore refresh happens once, immediately before `restoreOriginal`, and only where
    the route really restores** — on a guarded checkout continuation whose `restore.applies` is

    (vi) **rank 5.4 and rank 4.5 coexist** — a fixture where the restore target is **also** a

34. The full gate suite passes:

```sh
gofmt -l internal cmd
go test ./... -count=1
go vet ./...
golangci-lint run ./...
make build
git diff --check
tpatch feature deps --validate-all
```

Focused gates while implementing:

```sh
go test ./internal/ -run 'TestRebasePlan|TestPlanFingerprint|TestPlanSchema|TestRemainingRebaseEntries' -count=1
go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestSyncPlan|TestPlanGuard|TestSyncNoFlag_' -count=1
go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestSyncScoped_|TestCheckoutSyncModes_' -count=1
```

## 23. Test matrix and harnesses

All Git behaviour is tested against **real temporary repositories, real local bare remotes and real
linked worktrees**. Git is never mocked. Race-sensitive behaviour uses deterministic hooks and
barriers, never sleeps.

### 23.1 Harnesses

Reuse and extend — each symbol cited at the file it is really defined in, verified against the
tree:

| Harness symbol | Definition site |
|---|---|
| `scopedFixture` type, `newScopedFixture`, `runSync`, `(*scopedFixture).stateFilesGone` | `internal/cli/sync_scoped_test.go:18-24`, `:26-44`, `:59-65`, `:83-94` |
| `setupGitRepo(t, defaultBranch)` | `internal/cli/new_integration_test.go:135` |
| `createLinearStack(t, repo, feature)` | `internal/cli/sync_continue_integration_test.go:76` |
| `saveTestStack(t, featurePath, entries)` | `internal/cli/checkout_sync_test.go:75` |
| `checkoutModeFixture`, `newModeOpts`, `captureRun` | `internal/cli/checkout_sync_modes_test.go:17`, `:36`, `:51` |
| the Git `PATH` wrapper script and the argv sidecar | `internal/cli/sync_golden_test.go:59-137` (`syncWrapperScript`) and `:195-333` (`newSyncGitWrapper`, `around`, `records`) |
| the frozen no-flag golden suite | the `TestSyncNoFlag_*` functions of `internal/cli/sync_golden_test.go:1450-1600`, over `internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag/**` |
| `syncExecute` | `internal/cli/sync_golden_test.go:1110-1128` |

Three of these were previously cited as a single range of `sync_scoped_test.go`, which is wrong for
`setupGitRepo`, `createLinearStack` and `saveTestStack`: they live in three different files. Every
citation above names the file and the symbol, and a line range only where the symbol's body really
spans it; a symbol whose line moves is still findable by name. `syncExecute` sets `SilenceErrors`
and is explicitly **not** suitable for guard-marker testing — the marker assertions use the
production `cli.Execute()` harness of seam 1 below.

New test-only seams (all REQUIRED):

1. A production entry-point harness invoking `cli.Execute()` (`internal/cli/root.go:16-58`; its
   error/exit-`1` block is `:53-56`).
2. A barrier between the state snapshot and the guard seam.
2a. A barrier between `classifySyncState` and the cell-4 interception of §12.8b, so a second process
   can really create, remove or replace `.sync-state.yaml` inside that window. It is the seam the
   vanished-sentinel assertions of §22.28e (viii) drive, and it injects no verdict: the removal is a
   real filesystem event and the interception's own fresh read is what observes it.
3. A barrier between the reclaimability check and the reclaim compare-and-swap.
4. An injected reader/remover/**restorer**/**writer** that forces non-`ErrNotExist` I/O failures
   where
   permissions cannot — covering both read paths, the three `os.Remove` sites of §12.2c rule 2,
   the `.sync-state.yaml` capture read, the **JIT seam's `stack.yaml` reload** of §25.102 input 3
   (which the same seam also **counts**, so "exactly one reload per seam" and "no reload on a
   switch-only row" are asserted rather than assumed), `SaveGuardedLegacySentinel`,
   `RestoreSyncStateBytes` and
   `RemoveSyncStateIfUnchanged` of §13.2a/§13.6 rule 2c (including their two distinguished
   `ErrSyncStateChanged`/`ErrSyncStateHasPayload` refusals), and
   a document/prose `io.Writer` that fails in the **two** shapes §3.6 row 7 admits: a sole `Write`
   returning `(0, error)` and a sole `Write` returning a short write `(n < len(p), error)`. The
   writer also **counts** its `Write` calls, so the one-write document contract of §3.6 rules 1–2
   is asserted rather than assumed; no Nth-document-write cell exists, because the document is
   offered in one write. Every residue cell of rule 4a, all three guarded-legacy rollback residues
   of §22.24i
   (ix-a) and both §3.6 encoding/writer rows are reachable on every platform through this seam.
5. A fingerprint debug accessor returning the annotated canonical pre-image.
6. A Git `PATH` wrapper able to fail exactly one probe class and to record cwd, argv, environment
   and process count — the seam that fails a JIT seam's single `for-each-ref` for §22.33i
   (v-e-1) cell (7) while leaving every other process intact; and a `git --version` stub for §16.
7. An owned sleeping PID helper for live/dead/reused-PID fixtures, with a **deterministic dead-PID**
   half that every residue-recovery criterion depends on: it spawns a child, records its PID, waits
   for it to exit, and re-checks that the PID is no longer alive, so the value it hands back is
   known-dead rather than assumed-dead. On top of it, one **guard-detaching** helper rewrites an
   existing `.sync-run.lock` so that its recorded PID is that known-dead value and **every other
   byte — token, created timestamp, feature — is unchanged** (asserted field by field after the
   rewrite). It is a test-only fixture normalizer, not a production symbol, it is never called by
   any code under test, and it is the **only** sanctioned way to turn a residue whose guard records
   the running test process into one whose guard is a dead foreign owner (§22.28a rule L, §25.96).
8. `internal.StepHook` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:316`) and `internal.SyncStepHook`
   (`internal/sync_run_state.go:84`) for crash/interruption injection, plus the **two** new
   hook sites — `syncStepHook(SyncStageRebasing, -1)` immediately before the first
   post-claim revalidation probe (§12.2c rule 5) and `syncStepHook(SyncStageInitializing, 3)`
   immediately after the guarded legacy setup's byte capture and above its guard claim
   (§13.2a) — both using the existing hook variable and indices no shipped site uses. **No new
   checkout hook site is added**: parking a transaction at stage `rebased` for the §22.13d (b)
   ancestry-gate assertions uses the **shipped** `StepHook(StageRebased, tx.CurrentIndex)` site
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1148-1149`) — a returning hook there leaves `Stage: rebased` with
   `FailureKind: interruption` persisted, which is exactly the interrupted state the gate is
   projected over, and the fixture then moves the branch off its persisted `NewBaseSHA` with real
   Git commands rather than by editing the transaction. The **finalization** postcondition of
   §22.13n reuses that same shipped site in its **non-returning** form: on a two-or-more-entry plan
   the hook fires on the **last** index, moves an **earlier** entry's branch off its persisted
   `NewBaseSHA` with real Git commands and returns `nil`, so the run proceeds through
   `executeTransaction` into `finalizeTransaction` and fails its whole-plan check deterministically
   — again with **no** new hook site, no new production symbol and no transaction editing (§13.5
   rule F, §19.3). The `conflict`-stage fixtures of §22.13d (c) add no seam either: the conflict is
   produced by a real rebase and resolved with real Git commands. Together with
   the shipped `SyncStageInitializing` artefact indices `0` (guard), `1` (sentinel) and `2`
   (payload) — which the guarded legacy setup fires in the order `3 → 0 → 1 → 2` — they make every
   boundary of §13.2a's four-step order injectable. The harness drives each boundary in **two**
   modes, and the distinction is load-bearing (§13.2a's rollback rule): a hook that **returns an
   error** asserts the rollback path (nothing survives), while a hook that **terminates the
   process** (`os.Exit` in an out-of-process child, or `SIGKILL` of one) asserts the crash windows
   of §22.24i (ix-b). A crash-window assertion driven by a returning hook fails that criterion.
9. The shipped downgrade harness pattern of `internal/cli/sync_downgrade_test.go` (`downgradeTag`),
   retargeted at `v1.2.15`, for the §13.6 fail-closed assertions; when the tagged binary cannot
   be built the frozen replay transcription is used and the substitution is recorded, exactly as
   the shipped suite does.

and `tws status`/`tws doctor`/`tws import` asserted byte-equal to their plain-sentinel behaviour; **cell-7 claim authority** (§22.24i (ix-d)): an armed `--continue` over `{real .sync-state.yaml, guard}` asserted to reach `setupGuardedLegacyRunState`'s `ClaimSyncRunGuard` with `syncCellLiveGuardRefusal` returning `nil` above it, refusing at exit `1` with the shipped claim sentences over live-foreign, self-recorded and `PID <= 0` guards and reclaiming a provably dead one, writing nothing and moving no ref in every refusing cell |
| Guarded checkout continuation | §22.24h: the six-row `--continue` dispatch table (`state_version: 3` flagless ⇒ guarded, v3 + a limit flag ⇒ guarded, v3 + `--plan` ⇒ the plan route, v2/version-less flagless ⇒ the shipped unguarded arms, absent transaction ⇒ the shipped `no transaction to continue: %w`); the flagless v3 resume refusing on the **persisted** limit with one `plan-guard:` line, `origin: persisted-transaction` and the persisted `test_command`, with a supplied conflicting value still rank 7; the unguarded controls byte-, exit- and process-identical with `InspectCheckoutPlan`/`InspectCheckoutPlanState` at zero calls; exactly one `LoadCheckoutTransaction` in the CLI arm and nothing written before `ContinueCheckoutSync`; and `checkoutRecoveryIsGuarded`/`TransactionGuarded` over the full `(route, state_version)` × `{nil, load-error}` table |
| Armed-continuation upgrade | §22.24i: the §13.2a promotion asserted over four subjects (a v2 external payload, a real `.sync-state.yaml`, and a version-less **and** a v2 checkout transaction) — the upgraded document observed from a hook at the invocation's **first Git mutation** with the inherited `route`, the effective limits (including a persisted `0`), unchanged `test_command`/`validation_source` and no token/`guard_enabled`/digest key; re-interruption then a **flagless** `--continue` dispatching guarded and refusing on the persisted limit with no ref moved; `--plan --continue` leaving every byte untouched and the following flagless resume still unguarded; a seam refusal leaving the pre-upgrade subject byte-identical; an unarmed resume byte-, exit- and process-identical to the pre-feature control; `--approve-plan` with both limits absent upgrading nothing; the real `v1.2.15` downgrade sentences over each upgraded subject with no ref moved; the unchanged I20/deferred-I7/header/cell-sentence answers after the upgrade; the forced-save-failure cell (shipped writer sentence, marker-free, zero mutation processes, byte-identical subject, hash-verified restoration of `.sync-state.yaml` and released guard on the cell-7 arm, then a working flagless resume); **the guarded legacy arm's own four-step order driven boundary by boundary** — `SyncStageInitializing` 3/0/1/2, each boundary exercised twice: a **returning** hook asserted to roll back to nothing, and a **process-terminating** hook asserted to leave the declared crash window — with the three windows landing in cells 7-or-1/4/5, the prior document asserted recoverable byte-for-byte (still the file itself in window 1, inside the sentinel in windows 2–3), cell 8 asserted unreachable under this binary, each recovered by its declared arm (§12.8a/§12.8's `--abort` and an armed `--continue` for window 1, §12.3's recovery `--continue` and §12.8b's `--abort` for window 2, the shipped cell-5 arms for window 3) and each replayed under a real `v1.2.15` binary (the shipped cell-7/cell-1 answers with the guard ignored in window 1 — the declared downgrade-concurrency boundary of §22.24i (ix-c) — the shipped cell-4 answers in window 2, fail-closed in window 3, and no ref moved by any refusing verb); **the fallible rollback** asserted in all three residues (`{payload, sentinel, guard}`, `{sentinel, guard}`, `{guard}`) with the exact `; recovery state preserved: … — clear it with: tws sync <f> --abort` suffix, no `plan-guard: ` marker, no 17-byte `state-preserved: ` prefix and a working named recovery; and the source assertion enumerating the **three birth sites and two upgrade writers** as the only version-writing sites, each with one owner file, none called from a plan route, all called below the seam and above the executor |

### 23.3 Portability rules

- Invalid-UTF-8 **repository path** cells are skipped with a recorded reason on macOS HFS+/APFS,
  which rejects those path bytes; branch/ref invalid-byte cells still run.
- Permission-denied regular-file cells use mode `0000` and `t.Skip` with a reason when root or ACLs
  bypass mode bits; the injected-reader fallback then runs.
- Git holder/refusal wording is matched by stable concept or substring, never byte-matched, because
  it is version-dependent.
- Command-scope config fixtures use the inherited Git environment (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`), never a tws-added `-c`.
- `TopoSort` gets a 20,000-iteration randomized ordering test permitting only inter-component
  interleaving to vary; documents and fingerprints stay byte-stable across repeated processes.

## 24. Follow-ups (explicitly not this feature)

1. **Safe reparent/restack** — the next roadmap target; atomic Git + metadata update for a
   single-parent stack.
2. **Portable process birth identity** — record and verify a start time or birth-stable handle,
   then tighten the live-owner predicate; it adds the lock-artefact field **and** its consumer in
   one change (§12.6).
3. **Exact untracked-overwrite simulation** — a verified dry-run two-way `read-tree` probe, with its
   own preconditions (proving it writes neither index nor working tree, on linked worktrees and
   under sparse checkout, against the tree Git will really write). A separate feature, not a switch
   inside this one.
